title: Reps. Gillen, Nehls, Gottheimer and Fong Introduce Bipartisan Legislation to Make Motor Vehicle Collision Fraud a Federal Crime, Lower Car Insurance Premiums
text:
Auto insurance fraud, like staged vehicle accidents, costs consumers an estimated $300 a year in increased premiums.

WASHINGTON, DC — Today, Congresswoman Laura Gillen (D-NY-04) alongside U.S Representatives Troy Nehls (R-TX-22), Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ-05) and Vince Fong (R-CA-20) introduced the bipartisan Stop Auto Fraud Act of 2026 to make motor vehicle collision fraud a federal crime, improve safety for drivers and lower car insurance rates nationwide. The legislation targets insurance fraud schemes in which bad actors deliberately cause, stage or fabricate motor vehicle accidents to file false claims and defraud insurance companies for large cash payouts.

“Long Islanders pay some of the highest car insurance rates in the country and ‘crash for cash’ schemes on our roads are driving rates even higher,” said Rep. Gillen. “When fraudsters stage car wrecks to scam their way to huge payouts, they’re putting lives at risk and forcing responsible drivers to bear the costs. I’m proud to lead this bipartisan bill to hold these criminals accountable, make our roads safer and lower sky-high car insurance costs.”

“Bad actors across the country are deliberately causing, staging and fabricating car wrecks and filing phony insurance claims, and it’s the hardworking American families who end up paying the price with high insurance rates," said Rep. Nehls. "It’s time we put an end to this, make it a federal crime, and hold these fraudsters accountable. I’m proud to co-lead the bipartisan Stop Auto Fraud Act of 2026 with Congresswoman Gillen to crack down on these scams, and put the fines collected into the Highway Trust Fund, which provides the resources to improve our roads, and make our roads safer.”

"Insurance fraudsters send premiums skyrocketing and drive up the cost of living for Jersey families. The fraud rings behind them don't stop at state lines," said Rep. Gottheimer. "That's why I'm proud to work with Reps. Gillen, Nehls, and Fong on this bipartisan bill to make staging or fabricating a crash a federal crime, with fines going straight back into fixing our roads and bridges. We're cracking down on the hucksters and fighting to bring down costs for Jersey families."

"Californians already pay some of the highest car insurance premiums in the nation on top of having one of the highest costs of living,” said Rep. Fong. "Insurance fraud is making it worse. Staged car accidents are a deliberate, organized scam that puts innocent people at risk and drives up premiums for every driver on the road. In the Central Valley, where families depend on their vehicles to get to work, take their kids to school, and run their businesses, these are real costs hitting real people. The Stop Auto Fraud Act makes these schemes a federal crime and gives law enforcement the tools to dismantle the criminal networks behind them."

New Yorkers pay some of the highest car insurance rates in the nation, totaling just over $4,000 annually on average, nearly $1,500 above the national average. Insurance fraud, including staged crashes, further drives up costs for consumers. According to the Insurance Information Institute, staged accidents and related insurance fraud can cost families as much as $300 per year on average.

Insurance carriers reported 38,270 incidents of suspected motor vehicle insurance fraud to the New York State Department of Financial Services in 2023, a 58% increase from 2020. Recently, Florida, Louisiana and New York have enacted laws targeting bad actors who stage elaborate accidents to win payouts from insurance companies or jury awards.

The Stop Auto Fraud Act would make it a federal crime to knowingly stage or fabricate a motor vehicle crash and submit a fraudulent claim. The bill would impose penalties, including possible jail time, for violations. Any collected fines would be paid into the Highway Trust Fund for local and interstate roads, bridges and public mass transit systems.

“Staged vehicle accidents are not harmless property crimes. These are violent offenses that put innocent drivers and pedestrians at risk of injury or worse—all so that fraudsters and their facilitators can cash in. As NICB data and frontline investigations demonstrate, staged accident fraud is on the rise, costly—up to $300 a year in increased premiums—and increasingly organized. And it demands an organized, effective response. NICB applauds Representative Gillen’s Stop Auto Fraud Act of 2026, a bipartisan measure making clear that staged accidents are serious crimes deserving serious consequences,” said Kyle McCollum, Vice President, National Insurance Crime Bureau.

“Auto claims fraud, including intentional crashes, staged accidents, fabricated medical bills, and AI-altered photo evidence, drives up costs throughout the system and ultimately raises auto insurance premiums for everyone,” said Sam Whitfield, Senior Vice President of Federal Government Relations and Political Engagement, American Property Casualty Insurance Association (APCIA). “States that have enacted targeted anti-fraud and staged accident reforms have strengthened enforcement, disrupted organized fraud rings, and helped stabilize auto insurance markets, with some states even experiencing premium reductions. We applaud Representatives Gillen, Nehls, Gottheimer, and Fong for introducing the Stop Auto Fraud Act of 2026, which would establish federal criminal penalties for deliberate staged and phantom auto accidents. By giving law enforcement additional tools to combat organized crime fraud, this legislation addresses a significant driver of rising auto insurance claim costs and helps protect consumers from unnecessary premium increases.”

“Staged crashes and claims connected to them are a particularly malicious form of insurance fraud,” said Jimi Grande, Senior Vice President of Federal & Political Affairs, National Association of Mutual Insurance Companies. “Not only do these fraudsters endanger innocent drivers and communities all across the country, they also cause extensive financial harm. NAMIC applauds Representatives Gillen and Nehls, along with their co-sponsors, for their work to combat scammers and protect all honest road users.”

“The Truck Renting and Leasing Association (TRALA) proudly supports the Stop Auto Fraud Act and appreciates the leadership from Congresswoman Gillen and Congressman Nehls,” said Jake Jacoby, President & CEO, Truck Renting and Leasing Association. “Staged accidents continue to cause havoc with insurance premiums. This legislation will help deter bad actors from attempting to put trucking companies out of business by fabricating accidents, then running crooked legal and medical companies who attempt to profit from this blatant criminal activity.”

"The Trucking Association of New York (TANY) thanks Congresswomen Gillen for taking a strong stand against those who put others at risk using staged accidents for their own financial gain,” said Kendra Hems, President, Trucking Association of New York (TANY). “These are serious crimes and should be treated as such. The Stop Auto Fraud Act does just that and is an important step to reign in fraud and abuse of the insurance system. For the trucking industry, fraudulent and staged claims contribute directly to unsustainable increases in commercial auto insurance costs, putting additional pressure on carriers that are working hard to operate safely and keep our economy moving. We appreciate Congresswoman Gillen’s leadership and look forward to continuing to work with her on the issue."

“Staged crashes and fraudulent insurance claims impose real costs on responsible motorcoach operators and ultimately make it harder to provide safe, affordable transportation,” said Fred Ferguson, President and CEO of the American Bus Association. “The American Bus Association supports the Stop Auto Fraud Act because it gives law enforcement another tool to hold bad actors accountable and protect legitimate transportation businesses from organized fraud. We thank Representatives Gillen and Nehls for working together on this bipartisan effort.”

“On highways across the country, brazen criminals are intentionally colliding with other motorists in an attempt to score a big payday, and commercial trucks are a top target. Their selfish actions put the lives of innocent Americans at risk and contribute to soaring insurance premiums that raise costs for all consumers,” said Alex Rosen, SVP of Legislative Affairs, American Trucking Associations. “We need stronger penalties to deter those who perpetrate these schemes, which is why ATA strongly supports the Stop Auto Fraud Act. The trucking industry commends Reps. Laura Gillen and Troy Nehls for their leadership to make our roads safer and alleviate the financial burden imposed on families and businesses.”

“The Stop Auto Fraud Act of 2026 represents an important step toward protecting motorists, reducing insurance fraud, and improving roadway safety. The Truckload Carriers Association (TCA) strongly supports legislation that would make the submission of a fraudulent insurance claim arising from a staged motor vehicle accident a criminal offense. Staged crashes are not victimless crimes. These deliberate schemes place innocent drivers, passengers, first responders, and other road users at risk of serious injury or death. We commend Representatives Gillen and Nehls for recognizing the growing threat posed by staged vehicle accidents and for advancing a practical, bipartisan solution,” said Jim Mullen, President, Truckload Carriers Association.

“The National Tank Truck Carriers is proud to support the Stop Auto Fraud Act. Tank truck carriers operate in a uniquely high-risk environment, transporting valuable and often hazardous cargoes that make reliable insurance coverage essential to protecting their employees, equipment, customers, and the motoring public. Fraudulent insurance claims undermine the integrity of that system and drive up costs on carriers already managing significant operational risks. NTTC is grateful for the leadership of Representatives Gill and Nehls in combating insurance fraud and protecting responsible motor carriers,” said Ryan Streblow, President & CEO, National Tank Truck Carriers.

The legislation is endorsed by the National Insurance Crime Bureau, American Trucking Associations, American Bus Association, Truck Renting and Leasing Association, American Property Casualty Insurance Association (APCIA), National Association of Mutual Insurance Companies (NAMIC), National Tank Truck Carriers Association, Truckload Carriers Association, Trucking Association of New York, Texas Trucking Association and Southwest Movers Association.

title: RELEASE: House Passes Gottheimer, Foxx Bipartisan Bill to Hold Higher Education Accountable for Hate-Driven BDS Activity that Targets Jewish Students and Professors
text:
Above: Gottheimer speaks on the House floor in favor of the Protect Economic and Academic Freedom Act

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, September 3, the U.S. House of Representatives passed the bipartisan Protect Economic and Academic Freedom Act, authored by U.S. Representatives Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) and Virginia Foxx (NC-5), by a vote of 237-169. The legislation prohibits colleges and universities from receiving federal student aid if they engage in commercial and academic boycotts promoted by the antisemitic and hate-fueled boycott-divest-sanction (BDS) movement. The bill now heads to the U.S. Senate.

See full bill text here.

See Gottheimer’s remarks on the house floor here.

“No student, no professor should be shut out of research, study abroad opportunities, or academic partnerships, or feel unwelcome in the classroom because of where they’re from or what religion they practice. Yet that’s exactly what the boycott-divest-sanction movement seeks to do — targeting one country and one religion: Israel and Judaism,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5). “My bipartisan bill with Congresswoman Foxx is narrow and targeted — it doesn’t touch anyone’s speech, protest, or academic debate. It simply says that if your university takes federal taxpayer dollars, it can’t discriminate against academic partnerships or investments with one country. That’s it. I urge my colleagues on both sides of the aisle to support this bipartisan bill.”

“The antisemitic rot that has corroded college campuses must be eradicated – enough is enough. The safety and security of Jewish students, faculty, and staff should never be threatened under any circumstances. Today, the House sent a clear message: if an institution of higher education chooses to capitulate to the caustic BDS movement, there will be consequences – starting with this bipartisan legislation,” said Congresswoman Virginia Foxx (NC-5).

The Protect Economic and Academic Freedom Act will:

Require colleges and universities to certify that the institution is not engaging in a non-expressive commercial boycott of Israel, or forgo the ability to receive federal student aid.

Define “non-expressive commercial boycott of Israel” to mean a commercial action (including engaging in refusals to deal with Israel and terminating business activities) intended to limit commercial relations with Israel, or persons or entities conducting business in Israel or Israeli-controlled institutions, and is not based on a valid business reason.

Direct the Department of Education to make publicly available a list of all institutions that do not certify.

Require colleges and universities that are recipients of International Education Programs (Title VI) funding to not allow academic boycotts, but instead engage in academic exchange reciprocity.

Congressman Gottheimer has long been a leading voice in Congress against antisemitism. As a member of the House Bipartisan Task Force for Combating Antisemitism, he helped lead the bipartisan Antisemitism Awareness Act to hold campuses accountable for antisemitic harassment, authored the HEAL Act to strengthen Holocaust education, and has helped secure millions in Nonprofit Security Grants to protect synagogues and Jewish institutions across NJ-5. He will keep fighting to root out antisemitism — on college campuses and everywhere else — and to keep Jewish families and communities safe.

Today, Congressman Adam Gray (CA-13) announced the “Delivering for the Valley” tour to highlight over $16 million in federal funding he secured for community projects.

title: Rep. Grijalva Responds to Forest Service Approval of Hermosa Mine Project; Sounds Alarm About FAST-41 Expansion
text:
Washington, D.C. – Congresswoman Adelita S. Grijalva released the following statement after the Coronado National Forest approved South32 Hermosa Inc. Critical Minerals Project Exploration and Mine Plan of Operations, clearing the way for work to begin within the Patagonia Mountains of Southern Arizona, a world-class biodiversity hotspot with an extraordinary range of wildlife and plant species.

Rep. Grijalva previously wrote a letter to Forest Service Chief Tom Schultz highlighting the concerns voiced by local residents, including risks to groundwater, public health, and the region’s fragile environment, as well as frustration with a process lacking transparency and meaningful opportunity for input. She also penned an op-ed in the Patagonia Regional Times outlining her concerns with the project.

Just yesterday, the U.S. House of Representatives passed legislation that would make all mining and mineral processing projects eligible for coverage under FAST-41, an expedited federal permitting process, not just those involving critical minerals. The Hermosa Mine project is the first mining project in the country approved under the FAST-41 process.

“The FAST-41 approval of the Hermosa Mine project sets a dangerous precedent, as exemplified by a rushed review which ignored critical risks to groundwater, public health, and the region’s fragile ecosystem. Once the harm is inflicted, it cannot be undone. Unfortunately, Congress has ignored all the warning signs and chosen to expand this failed program, jeopardizing millions of acres of pristine public lands across the country.”

title: Rep. Grijalva Slams Bill to Fast-Track Mining Permits
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congresswoman Adelita S. Grijalva spoke on the House floor in opposition to H.R. 1501, legislation which passed the House today that would make mining and mineral processing projects eligible for coverage under FAST-41, an expedited federal permitting process.

The bill would also block a Biden Administration proposal that would have narrowed FAST-41 eligibility for mining projects to those involving critical minerals and their supply chains.

Earlier, Rep. Grijalva introduced an amendment that would have required meaningful, robust, and enforceable consultation with potentially impacted Tribal Nations before a mining project could qualify for expedited permitting under FAST-41.

“At a time when we should be strengthening environmental protections, respecting Tribal sovereignty, and ensuring communities have a meaningful voice in decisions that affect their land and water, this bill moves us in the wrong direction,” said Rep. Grijalva.

“I offered an amendment that would have required robust, meaningful, and enforceable consultation with potentially impacted Tribal Nations before a mining project could be eligible for expedited permitting under FAST-41. Tribal Nations deserve a meaningful seat at the table when projects could affect their lands, water, cultural resources, and communities.”

Rep. Grijalva’s opposition to the legislation comes as she continues to raise concerns about proposed mining activity in Southern Arizona. She recently sent a letter to U.S. Forest Service Chief Tom Schultz raising serious concerns about the Hermosa critical minerals project – the first project in the country approved under FAST-41 – and calling for greater consideration of potential impacts on Tribal Nations, local communities, and the region’s natural resources. She also wrote an op-ed in the Patagonia Regional Times following the project’s approval.

You can view her Floor remarks here. The full copy of her remarks is below:

I rise today in opposition to H.R. 1501, the Protecting Domestic Mining Act.

At a time when we should be strengthening environmental protections, respecting Tribal sovereignty, and ensuring communities have a meaningful voice in decisions that affect their land and water, this bill moves us in the wrong direction.

I offered an amendment that would have required robust, meaningful, and enforceable consultation with potentially impacted Tribal Nations before a mining project may be eligible for expedited permitting under FAST-41.

Unfortunately, the Rules Committee refused to make my amendment in order, denying this body the opportunity to even debate and vote on a basic principle: that Tribal Nations deserve a meaningful seat at the table when mining projects threaten their lands, resources, and communities.

My amendment would have ensured that federal agencies uphold the United States’ trust and treaty obligations by engaging in intentional and substantive consultation with Tribal governments. It would have made clear that consultation is not a procedural checkbox, but a meaningful government-to-government dialogue.

It would also have ensured that no mining project could receive expedited permitting treatment unless affected Tribal Nations had been engaged from the earliest possible stages of the project’s development.

This issue has become increasingly relevant in my district with the Hermosa Project in the Patagonia Mountains, southeast of Tucson, Arizona. Its designation as the first critical minerals project under FAST-41 highlights the growing use of expedited permitting frameworks.

While FAST-41 is intended to improve efficiency, mining is among the most environmentally consequential sectors it covers. Expedited timelines must not come at the expense of meaningful public participation or environmental assessment.

We have already seen the consequences of insufficient engagement and analysis.

The Town of Patagonia formally requested a comprehensive groundwater study of the Patagonia Mountains from the Coronado National Forest in both 2020 and 2021, specifically citing concerns related to the proposed Hermosa Project.

Despite these repeated requests — and the support of then-Congressman Raúl M. Grijalva — the study was never completed.

For that exact reason, I sent a letter to the U.S. Forest Service in April to follow up on that same request.

This gap leaves significant uncertainty about potential impacts to groundwater and undermines public confidence in the adequacy of the review process.

When I met with local leaders and community members in Patagonia, they raised serious concerns about their drinking water, their health, and the long-term sustainability of their aquifers.

Those concerns are not abstract; they reflect lived experience and legitimate questions that deserve answers before — not after — decisions are made.

What these experiences make clear is that communities closest to these projects cannot be left to react once decisions are already in motion. They must be engaged from the beginning, with their voices meaningfully incorporated into decision-making.

My amendment does not slow progress — it strengthens it.

By ensuring Tribal Nations and impacted communities have a real seat at the table, we produce more informed and more mindful policy outcomes.

Respecting Tribal sovereignty and listening to affected communities is not optional; it is a fundamental obligation.

For those reasons, I oppose H.R. 1501, and I urge my colleagues to do the same.

title: HEALTH CARE: Harder Announces New Bill to Invest in Food-is-Medicine Programs
text:
Half of all Stockton residents are diabetic or pre-diabetic, one of many chronic diseases made worse by food insecurity

Harder’s bill expands local partnerships focused on tackling high rates of chronic disease through nutrition

WASHINGTON – Today, Rep. Josh Harder (CA-09) announced new legislation to fight high rates of chronic diseases like diabetes in the Valley by investing in nutrition support services and new health care partnerships. Harder’s Partnerships for Better Health Act creates a new grant program at the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), in consultation with the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), to expand access to healthy food and connect people with the support they need to stay healthy.

Chronic disease takes a heavy toll on Valley families:

For the half of Stockton residents who are diabetic or pre-diabetic, managing this kind of challenging chronic disease becomes even harder when health care is sparse, good nutrition is hard to find, and community services are disconnected.

The Valley’s provider shortage also contributes to worsening chronic disease outcomes – San Joaquin County alone has 16 health professional shortage areas, and more than 500,000 new health care workers are needed across the state to meet demand by 2030.

Despite being the fruit and nut basket of the country, one in ten residents of San Joaquin County are struggling with food insecurity – for those with chronic diseases, that means every meal can become part of the fight to keep their condition from getting worse.

“People with chronic diseases like diabetes shouldn’t be struggling with poor nutrition and worse health outcomes in a place that grows a quarter of the nation’s food,” said Rep. Harder. “Washington isn’t doing enough to close the gaps between patients and the amazing local services that work night and day to deliver support. My bill changes that by investing in community partnerships to ensure our neighbors aren’t falling through the cracks and making good quality food a pillar of health care.”

How the Partnerships for Better Health Act improves chronic disease health outcomes in the Valley:

Direct Funding – Provides $15 million annually through 2031 for integrated medical care, nutrition support and education, and social services.

Wrap Around Care – Bridges the gap between patients and the patchwork of providers, advocates, and nonprofits to establish a coordinated, wrap-around system of care in the communities that need it most, like underserved and rural areas.

Fewer Hospitalizations – By investing in prevention and nutrition, this program will ultimately help keep patients out of the emergency room and reduce the mental and financial strain that comes with it.

The Partnerships for Better Health Act would build on successful community partnerships like the Future Well Communities program, launched by Abbott in 2019 in Stockton and run jointly by the Stockton Emergency Food Bank, University of the Pacific, and other leading community organizations including Community Medical Centers, El Concilio, and APSARA to provide integrated care and nutrition services for people with diabetes.

“Food is medicine, but it is also one of the ways we stabilize our community,” said Leonard Hansen, Stockton Emergency Food Bank President and CEO. “Through our work with Abbott, University of the Pacific and our health care partners, we have seen what happens when nutritious food, diabetes education and health care are brought together around the patient. Congressman Harder’s Partnerships for Better Health Act recognizes something we have learned here in Stockton: strong community partnerships can improve health, help prevent chronic disease from becoming a crisis, and give families a better opportunity to thrive.”

“Complex health challenges require bold, innovative solutions, and University of the Pacific is honored to be part of the solution here in Stockton,” said University of the Pacific President Christopher Callahan. “We have seen the impact when higher education, health care providers and community organizations work together to address health disparities. The Partnerships for Better Health Act will build on our proven successes here in Stockton, providing opportunities for communities across the country to create similar solutions for their residents.”

“The work we’ve done in Stockton over the past seven years has had significant impact, and we are optimistic that it can serve as a model for other communities looking for real-world answers to address chronic disease,” said Melissa Brotz, senior vice president, Abbott and president of Abbott Fund, the company’s philanthropic foundation. “When we build sustainable, community-driven partnerships, we can help more families live healthier lives.”

title: Comisionado Residente anuncia más de $2 millones para proteger servicios de agua
text:

title: Comisionado Residente Anuncia Más de $3.4 Millones para Proyectos de Recuperación en Puerto Rico
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — El Comisionado Residente de Puerto Rico, Pablo José Hernández, anunció más de $3.4 millones en fondos de FEMA para proyectos de recuperación y mejoras a infraestructura en varios municipios de Puerto Rico.

“Estos fondos se traducen en carreteras más seguras, instalaciones comunitarias reparadas y recursos para que nuestros municipios puedan continuar recuperándose de los desastres que han afectado a Puerto Rico. Seguiremos trabajando para que los fondos federales lleguen a proyectos que atiendan necesidades concretas de nuestra gente”, expresó el Comisionado Residente.

Los fondos incluyen recursos para reparar carreteras dañadas, restaurar instalaciones deportivas y recreativas, atender infraestructura municipal y continuar trabajos de recuperación relacionados con los huracanes María y Fiona, los terremotos de 2020 y la tormenta tropical Ernesto.

Entre los proyectos que recibirán fondos se encuentran:

$1.38 millones para el Departamento de Transportación y Obras Públicas (DTOP) para reparaciones permanentes en tramos de las carreteras PR-105, PR-406 y PR-1111 en Mayagüez, Añasco y Lares, afectados por la tormenta tropical Ernesto. Los trabajos incluyen reparación de asfalto, drenajes, guardarraíles y medidas para reducir daños futuros por erosión y lluvias.

$894,573 para el Municipio de Guánica para cubrir costos relacionados con la administración de proyectos de Asistencia Pública de FEMA tras los terremotos de 2020.

$298,339 para el Municipio de Ponce para reparar o reemplazar alumbrado, gradas y otros componentes de instalaciones afectadas por el huracán María.

$210,225 para el Departamento de Educación de Puerto Rico para reparar exteriores, interiores, verjas y otros componentes de instalaciones afectadas por el huracán Fiona.

$189,158 para el Municipio de Utuado para trabajos de reparación de superficies, rellenos, terraplenes y muros de gaviones afectados por el huracán María.

$164,327 para el Municipio de Canóvanas para reparar carreteras asfaltadas, cunetas, taludes, tuberías y otros componentes de infraestructura afectados por el huracán María.

$161,645 para el Municipio de Jayuya para reparar superficies de carreteras y terraplenes afectados por el huracán Fiona.

$134,447 para el Municipio de Toa Alta para restaurar una instalación deportiva que incluye un área de juegos, afectada por el huracán María.

Los fondos forman parte de distintos programas de Asistencia Pública de FEMA destinados a reparar infraestructura y atender costos relacionados con la recuperación de desastres en Puerto Rico.

title: Líderes del Congreso se unen al Comisionado Residente para exigir respuestas sobre contrato energético de casi $6 mil millones
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — El Comisionado Residente de Puerto Rico, Pablo José Hernández, junto a cuatro miembros de mayor rango de comités del Congreso enviaron una solicitud de información al Gobierno de Puerto Rico sobre el contrato de $5,900 millones para generación temporera. La solicitud está firmada por la senadora Elizabeth Warren, del Comité de Banca, Vivienda y Asuntos Urbanos del Senado; el senador Martin Heinrich, del Comité de Energía y Recursos Naturales del Senado; el congresista Jared Huffman, del Comité de Recursos Naturales de la Cámara; y el congresista Robert Garcia, del Comité de Fiscalización y Reforma Gubernamental de la Cámara, y el congresista Derek Tran.

Los congresistas exigieron documentos y respuestas al zar de Energía, Josué Colón Ortiz; al presidente de la Oficina de Compras de Terceros, Osvaldo Carlo Linares; y a la directora ejecutiva de la Autoridad de Energía Eléctrica, Mary C. Zapata Acosta. Les dieron hasta el 9 de septiembre de 2026 para responder.

“Mi prioridad es atender lo básico, como agua y luz. Para atender lo básico, tenemos que atender la corrupción”, explicó el Comisionado Residente. “Este escándalo ilustra cómo la corrupción impide que tengamos luz. La Junta canceló el contrato por irregularidades y no tenemos energía temporera. Por ende, se nos está yendo la luz en el verano.”

“El pueblo merece una explicación clara de lo que ocurrió después de que funcionarios del gobierno fueran alertados de que una firma en un contrato público de casi $6 mil millones pudo haber sido utilizada sin autorización: quién lo sabía, qué hicieron y por qué pasaron casi ocho semanas antes de que las alegaciones fueran referidas a las autoridades,” escribieron en la carta.

La solicitud busca determinar:

Quién utilizó o autorizó la firma atribuida a “Jhoby Weaks” y si los funcionarios tuvieron contacto con esa persona.

Cuándo las agencias conocieron que Enchanted Rock negaba haber autorizado la firma, quién fue informado y qué acciones tomaron.

Por qué pasaron casi ocho semanas antes de referir las alegaciones a las autoridades y por qué no se notificó antes a la AEE y a la Junta de Supervisión Fiscal.

El Comisionado Residente y los congresistas también exigieron las comunicaciones, récords e información investigativa relacionada con el caso. La información permitirá evaluar posibles irregularidades o conducta indebida que puedan retrasar proyectos energéticos críticos, así como cualquier acción adicional que corresponda desde el Congreso.

“El respaldo de dos senadores y dos representantes de mayor rango en el Congreso a mi iniciativa es significativo e histórico. Estos serían los presidentes de comités si los demócratas recuperan la mayoría en noviembre. Vamos a investigar qué pasó. Este es solo el comienzo”, advirtió el Comisionado Residente.

###

title: Smith Applauds President Trump’s Approval of Nearly $20 Million in Flood Recovery Aid
text:
SOUTHEAST MISSOURI – Congressman Jason Smith (MO-08) released the following statement praising President Trump’s approval of nearly $20 million in federal assistance to help communities recover from the devastating floods that hit southeast Missouri on July 9th and 10th of this year.

Congressman Smith said, “I saw the damage in Reynolds and Iron Counties firsthand, and pictures don’t do it justice. Families lost everything inside their homes, farmers and small business owners watched decades of hard work wash away in a matter of hours, and the sanctuary of a church that feeds over 100 families is now in ruins. These are good, hardworking people, and this kind of damage is more than any small, rural community can carry on its own.

“I am grateful to President Trump for approving this request, and I want to thank every first responder, volunteer, and local leader who has stepped up for their neighbors through all of this. I’ll always fight to make sure Missourians get the support they need to rebuild in the wake of disaster.”

title: Smith Secures $1.7 Million for Salem Memorial Hospital Through Provision in One, Big, Beautiful Bill
text:
SALEM, Mo. – Salem Memorial Hospital has been awarded approximately $1.7 million through the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), an initiative that Congressman Jason Smith (MO-08) authored and fought for as part of the One, Big, Beautiful Bill. The funding will support major facility and patient-care upgrades at the hospital that has served Smith’s hometown for generations.

Congressman Smith said, “Growing up in Salem, I know exactly what this hospital means to our community. My family has depended on Salem Memorial for generations, and I’ve seen firsthand what it means for a small town when the local hospital stays open and care continues to improve. When a rural hospital closes, that often means an extra hour on the road to receive care, and for many families, that extra hour can be the difference between life and death.

“That’s exactly why I championed the Rural Health Transformation Program. When I was writing the One, Big, Beautiful Bill, I knew we had to include support for rural health care so hospitals like Salem Memorial can get the resources they need to continue serving the families who depend on them — and I did just that. I’m proud to see this funding benefit my hometown, and I will keep fighting to make sure our rural communities have access to quality health care.”

title: LEADER JEFFRIES STATEMENT ON H.R. 4795
text:
UPDATE: Termination of Temporary Protected Status for Haitians and Syrians

On Tuesday, June 25, 2026, the Supreme Court ruled that the Trump administration could move forward with its plans to rip legal status away from nearly 350,000 current Haitian and Syrian Temporary Protected Status (TPS) holders. Following this decision, the Department of Homeland Security announced the termination of TPS for Haitians and Syrians, effective July 27, 2026.

Individuals who have lost TPS may be impacted in different ways, including loss of protection from deportation and loss of work authorization. However, there may be alternative legal pathways to remain and work in the United States. To learn more about what the end of TPS means for you and your family:

All TPS holders regardless of designation should visit the USCIS website for the latest updates on their TPS status.

Visit the NYC Mayor’s Office of Immigration Affairs website to learn more about what the expiration of TPS status means for impacted New Yorkers. Resource documents are available in English, Arabic, French and Haitian Creole.

Contact the Mayor’s Office of Immigrant Affairs (MOIA), whose Legal Support Centers offer free, confidential immigration legal help. Free, safe and confidential immigration legal services are available regardless of your immigration status and in your language by calling the MOIA legal support hotline at 800-354-0365 or visiting nyc.gov/knowyourrights.

title: Kaptur, Blumenthal, Tillis, & Fitzpatrick Urge State Department To Distribute Funding To Organizations Assisting Kidnapped Ukrainian Children
text:
Toledo, OH – Today, Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09), Congressman Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-01), and US Senators Richard Blumenthal (D-CT) and Thom Tillis (R-NC) wrote Secretary of State Marco Rubio urging him to move quickly in awarding $25 Million the State Department has made available to “support the identification, return, rehabilitation, and reintegration of Ukrainian children forcibly transferred to Russia and Russian-occupied territories.”

Although the funding was announced in March, it has not yet been distributed. An estimated 20,000 Ukrainian children have been forcibly transferred to Russia or areas in Ukraine occupied by Russia.

“While we understand the need for rigorous review, thousands of kidnapped Ukrainian children remain separated from their families, and every delay extends the pain and suffering they and their families have already endured,” the members wrote.

The full text of the bipartisan, bicameral letter is available by clicking here, or reading below:

Dear Secretary Rubio,

We write regarding the Department of State’s commitment of $25 Million to support the identification, return, rehabilitation, and reintegration of Ukrainian children forcibly transferred to Russia and Russian-occupied territories. We welcome the Department’s efforts and urge you to move expeditiously to award these funds.

The Department announced available funding opportunities in March 2026. Since then, we have heard directly from organizations working to locate and return Ukrainian children about the continued delay in awarding these funds and the impact it is having on their critical work.

While we understand the need for rigorous review, thousands of kidnapped Ukrainian children remain separated from their families, and every delay extends the pain and suffering they and their families have already endured.

We therefore respectfully urge the Department to promptly complete its review and award the full $25 Million already committed to this important work. Please also provide an update on the anticipated timeline for announcing these awards. Know that Congress stands ready to assist your efforts should you require additional authorities to complete this task.

Thank you for your attention to this matter and your continued commitment to helping bring Ukraine’s stolen children home.

title: Kaptur Statement on Resumption of Brandon Road Project
text:
Toledo, OH — Today, Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09), Ranking Member of the House Appropriations Subcommittee on Energy and Water and Co-Chair of the Bipartisan Congressional Great Lakes Task Force, released the following statement on the status of the work by the US Army Corps of Engineers to construct the invasive carp barrier at the Brandon Road Lock and Dam in Joliet, Illinois.

"I’m pleased work at Brandon Road can start again. This is great news for the Great Lakes, and I thank the Governors who joined me to press the President this week to get it done. With more than a month of critical construction time lost, the Administration still owes Congress and the public an explanation why the stop work order was issued,” said Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09). “Congress authorized this barrier, paid for it, and watched two states put up their own money and their own land to see it built. A project that protects the drinking water, fisheries, and the livelihoods of 30 Million people should never be treated as a bargaining chip. The Army Corps of Engineers should move with great haste to make up the lost ground. I will be watching every step of the way until this project to protect the Great Lakes fisheries is finished.”

Kaptur’s statement follows a month-long delay on the project in which the Trump Administration ordered the Army Corps of Engineers to halt work, giving no reasoning to Congress or to the public. The project, which was authorized and planned in 2024, is designed to prevent invasive carp from reaching the Great Lakes and devastating the region’s $11 Billion fishing and recreation industry.

Congresswoman Kaptur has long been a leading and staunch advocate for the entire Great Lakes region, fighting to protect the vitality of the Lakes and the people, animals, and plants that call them home. On July 31, 2026, Congresswoman Kaptur, along with her fellow co-chairs on the Bipartisan Great Lakes Task Force, sent a letter urging the Trump administration to lift stop-work orders on the project. Congresswoman Kaptur also raised the importance of timely, uninterrupted construction of the Brandon Road Project with the Assistant Secretary of the Army for Civil Works and the Commanding General of the Army Corps of Engineers at an Energy and Water Appropriations Subcommittee Annual Budget Hearing for the Army Corps on April 16, 2026. And she has been following through with communications to Army Corps leadership each time a pause or delay arises as a result of the current Administration’s decision-making needlessly putting the Great Lakes at greater risk of invasive carp penetration.

title: NPR: Tributes to Gloria Steinem are flooding in, from Hollywood to Capitol Hill
text:
Journalist and activist Gloria Steinem dedicated her life to fighting for women’s rights, from reproductive freedom to workplace equality.

Now, after her death at age 92, notable figures from politics to pop culture are offering their remembrances — and personal thanks — to the feminist icon. They’re also vowing to continue her work.

“She pushed open doors not just for herself, but for literally millions of women behind her,” former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton — the first female presidential nominee of a major U.S. political party — wrote in a lengthy Facebook tribute.

Clinton was one of many women in national politics sharing their praise and gratitude for Steinem. Others include former first lady Jill Biden, former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi and House Minority whip Katherine Clark, who said she hung a pair of photos of Steinem and Dorothy Pitman Hughes on her office wall the day she moved in.

“She wasn’t going to be an astronaut, but my goodness, she made it possible for Sally Ride to be an astronaut,” Clinton wrote. “She wasn’t going to play college sports, but she stood behind the women in Congress who passed Title IX and opened up opportunities in sports and academics for girls. And she wasn’t on the Supreme Court when Roe v. Wade was decided, but her voice and her activism was behind that advancement for women’s rights.”

Steinem emerged in the 1960s as a leading face of second-wave feminism. That role was firmly cemented the following decade, when she co-founded both the National Women’s Political Caucus and Ms. magazine.

Steinem helped normalize conversations about workplace sexism, bursting onto the scene in 1963 with an exposé about her undercover stint as a waitress at Hugh Hefner’s New York Playboy Club, and abortion, after sharing her experience getting one abroad in the 1950s. She is credited with helping increase the number of women in elected office and bringing feminism into the mainstream at a time when the law kept women from obtaining credit cards and bank accounts in their own names.

After her death on Wednesday, younger generations of high-profile women took to social media to honor and thank Steinem. Many of their stories were personal.

Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, wrote about working with Steinem to mobilize young voters, making public appearances at interviews and award ceremonies.

“But privately, she was even better than you would imagine- spending Thanksgiving with our family, introducing me to one of my best friends (forever the champion of female friendship), loving our children with her whole heart, counseling me during hard times, and giving extraordinary advice and perspective with a cup of tea and an unrivaled cheekiness and wit,” she wrote, alongside photos including one of Steinem with her young son.

Actress Julianne Moore wrote on Instagram that the time she spent studying Steinem — to play her in the 2020 film The Glorias — was “one of the most edifying of my life.”

“Everything I watched, everything I read, everything I observed about her gave me a template for how I wanted to behave,” Moore wrote. “Her honesty, her tolerance, her patience, and her insistence on humanism and inclusion as she moved through the world offers us all a moral roadmap.”

It wasn’t just women sharing acknowledgments and anecdotes. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., and Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-VT., paid tribute, as did former and current New York City mayors Mike Bloomberg and Zohran Mamdani (Steinem called the city home for more than six decades).

Rep. Jim McGovern, D-Mass., wrote that he first met Steinem while working with Sen. George McGovern (no relation) in the 1970s.

“Later, when I first thought about running for office, she met with me, listened to what I had to say, and told me to run even if the establishment wrote me off,” he added. “She was a bright light to the very end and never stopped fighting for what she believed in.”

Scores of cultural figures — from Oprah Winfrey to Paris Hilton to Stacey Abrams to Billie Jean King — shared heartfelt messages and posts about what Steinem meant to them, and the importance of continuing her work. Several peeled back the curtain on their longtime friendships.

In a lengthy Instagram post, actress and writer Lena Dunham said she first met Steinem as a “lost twenty something,” and gratefully received her advice over the years on “everything from men (can be fun, aren’t required) to activism (it’s a marathon, not a race.).” She said she was one of many such lucky beneficiaries.

“You weren’t just generous with your life force, your vision or your intellect: you were generous with your time, your laughter and even your jewelry (like the time I admired your silver vulva ring and you plucked it off your hand and placed it on mine.),” Dunham wrote.

British actress and activist Jameela Jamil, who called Steinem “a guiding light for me,” wrote about an evening several months ago where the two sat in Steinem’s apartment talking about the world and “our adventures together over the years.”

Jamil said Steinem was worried about the state of the world, women and reproductive rights. Steinem saw the Supreme Court affirm the right to abortion in Roe v. Wade in 1973 and decades later, overturn it, in 2022. She said Steinem told her about her plans, “92 and still fighting.”

“I feel such pain that she left in a moment where it appears the rights she fought for us to have are being rolled back,” Jamil wrote. “She expressed disbelief to me as to how fast the pendulum is swinging back. And it lit a fire in me, to make sure her work and the work of the incredible women before her and around her, was not in vain.”

Steinem told NPR after the reversal of Roe that she didn’t feel her life’s work was being stripped down — and never doubted that the fight would continue.

“I think it’s important to connect the ancient to the new, because otherwise we don’t understand the strong thread of patriarchy and racism that has been with us and continues to be with us,” she said.

Steinem’s second memoir, An Unexpected Life, is set for release later this month.

—

title: Kean Introduces Legislation to Ban Taxpayer Spending on First Class Flights for Members of Congress
text:
(SEPTEMBER 3, 2026) WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congressman Tom Kean, Jr. (NJ-07) introduced the No Taxpayer Funds for Congressional First Class Flights Act (H.R. 10244). This legislation would prohibit the use of official travel funds by Members of Congress for flight accommodations that are not coach class.

“Public service should never be used for personal luxury, and taxpayers should not be footing the bill for Members of Congress to fly first class,” said Congressman Kean. “Every taxpayer dollar should be treated with respect and used responsibly. I am fighting to ensure that politicians put the public first and put an end to any kind of abuse that funds special privileges for elected officials.”

Throughout his time in the House of Representatives, Congressman Kean has been a leader in ethics reform, spearheading efforts to ban members of congress from trading individual stocks. In July, he voted in favor of the Stop Insider Trading Act to ban members of Congress, their spouses, and their dependent children from purchasing publicly traded, individual stocks.

A copy of the bill text is available HERE.

title: Congressman Keith Self Introduces Concurrent Resolution to Denounce Sharia Law
text:
Congressman Keith Self (TX-03) introduced a concurrent resolution denouncing Sharia law and opposing its implementation within the United States.

The resolution reaffirms a fundamental principle: the United States Constitution is the supreme law of the land. No foreign legal or political system should supersede the Constitution or undermine the rights and liberties it protects.

Congressman Self’s resolution comes one week after President Donald Trump acknowledged concerns regarding the implementation of Sharia law in the United States and voiced support for its prohibition.

“The United States Constitution is the supreme law of the land,” said Congressman Self. “We cannot allow Sharia law or any competing legal framework to undermine the liberties generations of Americans have fought and died to protect. I commend President Trump for recognizing the threat posed by Islamic political agendas. Congress must make its position clear: we will defend our Constitution, uphold the rule of law, and put Americans first.”

Read the Daily Signal’s exclusive article on the concurrent resolution here.

Original co-sponsors of the concurrent resolution include Representatives Randy Weber (TX-14), Clay Fuller (GA-14), Buddy Carter (GA-01), Eli Crane (AZ-02), Paul Gosar (AZ-09), Derrick Van Orden (WI-03), Josh Brecheen (OK-02), Barry Moore (AL-01), and Mike Kelly (PA-16).

“‘One Nation, Under God.’ These are words God-fearing Americans live by here on the Texas Gulf Coast,” said Congressman Weber. “That is why I am proud to join Congressman Self’s concurrent resolution denouncing Sharia law and opposing its implementation anywhere in the United States. We cannot stand by and watch while foreign ideologies threaten American democracy, as we are seeing on Ali Akbar Court in Irving, Texas, and in ‘Muslim-only’ communities across the country. Congress must make it clear that Americans will remain safe, free, and governed by the Constitution and the laws and values that made this nation great.”

“The United States Constitution is, and always will be, the supreme law of the land. While religious liberty is fundamental to our nation, no competing legal system should ever supersede our Constitution or the rights and freedoms it guarantees every American. I am proud to join Congressman Self in standing firmly for our Constitution and the rule of law,” said Congressman Carter.

“As someone who served in the Middle East, I’ve seen firsthand the brutal reality of Sharia Law. This is a draconian political system that destroys individual liberty, unravels the fabric of the societies it infiltrates, and stands in direct opposition to the Constitutional rights our Founders envisioned. The American people deserve to know where their representatives stand on this rising threat, and this resolution puts every Member on the record for all to see,” said Congressman Crane. “I applaud Rep. Keith Self for his tireless work as co-chair of the Sharia-Free America Caucus. We will continue working proactively to spare our nation the consequences we’ve already seen play out across Europe.”

“America was founded on the principle that our Constitution—not a religious doctrine or foreign legal system—is the supreme law of the land. No ideology or system of law can supersede the Constitution or the individual liberties it guarantees. I am proud to cosponsor this resolution to reaffirm that our laws are grounded in the Constitution, the rule of law, equal protection, due process, and individual liberty—not Sharia law,” said Congressman Gosar.

“Thank you to Rep. Self for leading a resolution to denounce Sharia Law and preserve America from the spread of radical Islam,” said Congressman Brecheen. “Sharia is an ideology completely at odds with our Republic and has no place in our country. Wake up, America!”

“No foreign system of law should ever be allowed to supersede the Constitution that protects our God-given freedoms. Sharia is used as a system of governance, and it conflicts with the American principles of equal rights, individual liberty, and religious freedom. America has one Constitution, one system of laws, and one standard of justice,” said Congressman Moore. “I’m proud to stand with Congressman Self in making it clear that Sharia has no place as a competing legal authority in the United States and in defending the rule of law and the freedoms that generations of Americans have fought, sacrificed, and prayed to preserve.”

title: Reps. Kelly and Chu Introduce Resolution to Designate September 3 as National Neuroblastoma Awareness Day
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Representatives Mike Kelly (PA-16) and Judy Chu (CA-28) introduced a resolution to designate September 3, 2026, as National Neuroblastoma Awareness Day, recognizing the children and families affected by neuroblastoma and the clinicians and researchers working to develop better treatments and ultimately find a cure.

The resolution was inspired by Mikaela Hong, a La Cañada High School student, neuroblastoma patient and survivor, and founder of the Pediatric Hope Project, who has turned her own experience with neuroblastoma into advocacy for children and families facing pediatric cancer. Hong received Rep. Chu’s 2026 Youth of the Year Award in recognition for her advocacy.

“Establishing an official Neuroblastoma Awareness Day resolution gives lawmakers and communities the opportunity to help elevate public understanding, foster early detection, and offer meaningful support to families navigating this difficult diagnosis,” said Rep. Mike Kelly, Co-Chair of the Congressional Childhood Cancer Caucus. “It is critical to spur the development of safer, more effective treatments and ultimately giving young patients a better chance at a healthy future. As a Co-Chair of both the Congressional Childhood Cancer Caucus and the House Cancer Caucus, I’m proud to support efforts in Congress that advance lifesaving pediatric cancer research and help ensure doctors and researchers have the tools they need to develop better treatments and, ultimately, find cures.”

title: House Homeland Security Democrats Visit Buffalo to Discuss Domestic Extremism Prevention, Meet With 5/14 Families
text:
Delegation Met with Law Enforcement, Local Officials, and Families of 5/14 Victims and Survivors to Examine Emergency Response and Warn Against Trump Administration Cuts to FEMA Preparedness Grants

BUFFALO, N.Y. - Today, at the invitation of Congressman Tim Kennedy (NY-26), Ranking Member of the House Homeland Security Committee’s Emergency Management Subcommittee, a delegation of House Homeland Security Committee Democrats visited Buffalo for a roundtable discussion on emergency management, domestic extremism prevention, and the federal grant programs that support state and local efforts to stop violence before it occurs. Earlier this week, it was revealed that New York State is still awaiting $87 million in FEMA funding for the state’s counterterrorism and homeland security efforts. Kennedy ws joined by Committee Ranking Member Bennie G. Thompson (MS-02), Border Security Subcommittee Ranking Member Lou Correa (CA-46), and Rep. Nellie Pou (NJ-09) for the closed-door roundtable at the Frank E. Merriweather Library. The delegation was joined virtually by New York Attorney General Letitia James.

Joined by Buffalo Police Commissioner Erika Shields, City of Buffalo Emergency Manager Tom Luby, and Dr. Amanda Nickerson, Director of the University at Buffalo’s Alberti Center for Bullying Abuse Prevention, the members heard directly from 5/14 family members and leaders from the 5/14 Foundation, whose perspective centered the roundtable on the racially-motivated mass shooting at Tops Friendly Markets on Jefferson Avenue on May 14, 2022. The shooting, which killed ten people and seriously injured three others, reshaped the community’s understanding of emergency response and long-term recovery. The discussion focused on the emergency response in the shooting’s immediate aftermath, the role that sustained DHS investment can play in preventing domestic extremism through grant programs, and the impact of the Trump Administration’s continued delays and cuts to programs, including the State Homeland Security Grant Program.

Following the roundtable, members of the delegation visited the Tops Supermarket on Jefferson Avenue and the memorial that has been installed on the property honoring those who were lost in the shooting.

“What happened at the Tops on Jefferson Avenue was an act of racist domestic terrorism, and this community has carried that weight every day since,” said Congressman Kennedy. “Standing at that memorial and speaking with family members, advocates, and public safety officials is a reminder of why this work is so important. Our federal government has a responsibility to invest in preventing violence before it happens and to ensure state and local governments can rely on this FEMA funding year after year. Instead, we have seen cuts to the very grant programs that help communities like Buffalo prepare, respond, and heal. I’ll keep fighting to protect that funding and to make sure that Washington never forgets what happened here and in far too many other communities across the nation.”

“I am glad Committee Democrats met with local leaders on the impact of the 2022 domestic terrorism mass shooting in Buffalo. It is clear that this tragedy has left an indelible mark on the Buffalo community. White supremacist extremism has no place in America and, sadly, continues to be a scourge we must work together to eradicate. That means investing in the people and programs that help communities identify threats early, strengthen partnerships with law enforcement and community organizations, and intervene before violence occurs. I thank Congressman Kennedy for hosting us in his district today,” said Ranking Member Bennie G. Thompson.

“Public safety funding is not a political weapon, and Buffalo knows better than most what is at stake,” said New York Attorney General Letitia James. “The federal government is directly undercutting our work to keep our communities safe by withholding critical homeland security funding that our state needs. The best way to honor those whose lives were stolen on 5/14 is by ensuring a horrific attack like this can never happen again. I am grateful to Congressman Kennedy for convening this conversation and fighting in Washington to ensure what happened at Tops is never repeated.”

“We must make sure our first responders and law enforcement have what they need to stop violence before it happens. The Trump Administration needs to stop withholding critical funding for our states now and not after the next tragedy,” said Congressman Lou Correa.

“Time and time again, the American people are seeing the Trump Administration weaponize FEMA funding for their own partisan reasons and political revenge,” said Congresswoman Pou (NJ-09). “The bottom line is that our communities need federal aid, and they should not be punished for whether they live in a red district or a blue one. Withholding over $80 million in assistance is unconscionable, especially when this funding is supposed to be used to combat terrorism and extremism, and provide emergency support.”

“The May 14 mass shooting was a devastating tragedy that continues to profoundly impact members of our community. Beyond the awful effects felt here in Buffalo, this terror attack awakened the nation to the dire threat posed by domestic extremism. But in continuing to withhold $87 million in federal counterterrorism funding to New York State, this administration is demonstrating it has forgotten the painful lessons of May 14 - and that it refuses to prioritize the safety of Americans who live in states that do not politically support this president. I deeply appreciate the visit and support from Representatives Tim Kennedy, Bennie Thompson, Lou Correa, and Nellie Pou, as well as Attorney General Letitia James, and I join their call to restore federal funding to protect New Yorkers from terror attacks. This is not a partisan issue; no Americans should ever suffer what our community did on May 14,” said Councilwoman Zeneta Everhart.

“May 14 was a wound to the soul of our community, and we continue to carry the pain of that terrible day. We must never forget the lives we lost or the lessons that tragedy taught us. As people of faith and as a community, we have a responsibility to protect one another and to stand against hate in all its forms. I commend the work of our elected officials who have continued to stand with Buffalo, to fight for our community, and to make sure the lessons of May 14 are not forgotten. We must continue to come together, look out for one another, and do all we can to ensure that no community ever has to experience this kind of pain again,” said Pastor Mark Blue, Chairman of 5/14 Foundation and President, Buffalo NAACP.

Kennedy and the delegation vowed to continue pressing the Trump Administration to restore full funding to FEMA’s preparedness and prevention grant programs, and to keep working with Buffalo’s law enforcement, emergency management, and community leaders to ensure the lessons of May 14, 2022 translate into stronger protections nationwide.

title: Lawmakers Demand CPSC Stop Invasive Data Collection on Emergency Department Patients
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Rep. Kevin Mullin joined federal lawmakers in calling upon the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) to immediately suspend efforts to pressure some of the nation’s largest hospital systems to hand over the detailed, personally identifiable medical records of every patient who visits their emergency departments.

Recent reporting has revealed that the Commission is directing hospitals to transmit sensitive records—including patient names, birthdates, addresses, and diagnoses—to its private contractor as part of changes to the National Electronic Injury Surveillance System (NEISS). For decades, hospitals across the country have voluntarily participated in NEISS to report injuries involving consumer products, such as kitchen appliances and toys, to help identify products with a pattern of injuring consumers. But now, the Commission is amassing an unprecedented trove of identifiable health data of emergency department patients, regardless of whether an injury involved a consumer product. This sweeping data collection initiative is particularly alarming considering the Trump administration’s broader pattern of amassing Americans’ sensitive data and repurposing it to advance political priorities. In the letter, the lawmakers raised concerns regarding the necessity and legality of this initiative, the adequacy of its privacy protections, and the purposes to which this trove of sensitive data may ultimately be put.

The letter to Peter Feldman, Acting Chairman of the CPSC, was authored by Senators Edward J. Markey (D-Mass.) and Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), along with Representatives Mullin (CA-15) and Jan Schakowsky (IL-09), and cosigned by Senators Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY), Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), Tammy Baldwin (D-Wisc.), Cory Booker (D-N.J.), and Ron Wyden (D-Ore.), and Representatives Debbie Dingell (MI-06), Nanette Barragán (CA-44), and Kelly Morrison (MN-03).

In the letter, the lawmakers wrote, “The Commission is advancing this effort amid a broader pattern of the Trump administration seeking unprecedented access to Americans’ private data. From the Office of Personnel Management’s demand for federal workers’ health information to the Department of Health and Human Services sharing Medicaid enrollee data with the Department of Homeland Security, this administration has repeatedly sought to collect sensitive data from everyday Americans without a semblance of transparency.”

The lawmakers continued, “Against that backdrop, creating a federal repository of identifiable medical records—with no evidence of any limits on how that data may be used, shared, or repurposed—is deeply alarming. Such data collection could easily discourage people in need from seeking care at an emergency department or from being transparent with their medical providers out of fear of federal surveillance or inappropriate use of their information. Even if the Commission uses these records solely to advance consumer protection, creating a federal database of identifiable medical records gives an administration that has repeatedly sought access Americans’ sensitive data another powerful tool for surveillance and misuse.”

title: King-Hinds Announces Passage of Federal Funding Bill with $21.4 Million for CNMI Medicaid
text:
Washington, D.C. – Congresswoman Kimberlyn King-Hinds announced that the Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027 has passed both chambers of Congress and is now headed to the President for signature. The legislation includes $21.4 million in additional federal Medicaid funding for the Northern Mariana Islands.

The legislation increases the CNMI’s fiscal year 2026 Medicaid allotment by $21.4 million and allows the additional funding to remain available until expended. The funding may also be used for eligible services provided during fiscal year 2026 even when the Commonwealth makes payment for those services during fiscal year 2027.

“This is a major step forward for healthcare in the CNMI. An additional $21.4 million in federal Medicaid funding will help strengthen access to care, support our healthcare providers, and provide critical relief following the recent natural disasters.

“This funding addresses an immediate need, but the work does not end here. We must continue advocating for a fair and sustainable long-term Medicaid solution that ensures the CNMI receives the support our community deserves,” King-Hinds said.

“I thank the Senate and House committees for including the CNMI’s Medicaid needs in response to Super Typhoon Sinlaku. I also thank the CNMI Medicaid Agency for its work in supporting this request. We will continue working as Congress takes up the next round of funding discussions in December to address the additional needs of the Medicaid program and other priorities of the Commonwealth.”

A continuing resolution, commonly referred to as a CR, provides temporary funding for federal agencies and programs when Congress has not yet completed the regular annual appropriations process. The legislation continues federal government funding through December 11, 2026, averting a government shutdown while Congress completes work on fiscal year 2027 appropriations.

The continuing resolution also keeps several federal programs important to the Northern Mariana Islands operating through December 11. These include federal highway and transit programs, territorial assistance programs administered by the Department of the Interior, FEMA disaster response and recovery activities, and several veterans health care, housing, transportation, and benefit programs. The legislation passed both chambers of Congress and is now on its way to the President for signature.

title: Krishnamoorthi Continues National Push to Combat Rising Hate Against South Asian Americans at Georgia Event
text:
WASHINGTON — Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL) participated Thursday in the first stop of Indian American Impact’s national listening tour in Norcross, Georgia, where South Asian elected officials, community leaders, and residents gathered to address the rise in hate, harassment, and violence targeting South Asian Americans. The Georgia gathering followed Wednesday’s national roundtable on Capitol Hill and focused on what communities are experiencing and how federal, state, and local leaders can strengthen prevention, reporting, and accountability.

“The rise in hate, harassment, and violence against South Asian Americans demands a response across the country,” Krishnamoorthi said. “After bringing South Asian leaders together in Washington, we are continuing that work here in Georgia with community members and public officials to improve prevention, reporting, and accountability for hate crimes. South Asian Americans have built their lives here, raised their families here, and strengthened communities across this country. We have to stand shoulder to shoulder against hate and violence whenever our communities are targeted.”

The listening session included Krishnamoorthi, Virginia Lieutenant Governor Ghazala Hashmi, Georgia State Senator Sheikh Rahman, Georgia State Representative Akbar Ali, Indian American Impact Executive Director Chintan Patel, SAATH founder Rohan Soni, and community leaders and advocates from across Georgia. Participants discussed what South Asian Americans are seeing and experiencing, how government is responding, and what additional steps could help communities confronting hate and discrimination. The Georgia gathering marked the beginning of Indian American Impact’s national listening tour, which is intended to hear directly from community members about their experiences and what additional steps are needed to confront hate targeting South Asian Americans.

Earlier this year, Krishnamoorthi reintroduced the bipartisan Hate Crimes Commission Act, which would establish a bipartisan commission to examine what is driving hate crimes, including the role of social media and technology, assess barriers to complete reporting, and identify successful prevention and response strategies.

title: Larson Statement on the Death of Gloria Steinem
text: “I am deeply saddened by the passing of Gloria Steinem, a trailblazer who broke barriers for women and championed dignity, equality, and justice for all,” said Larson. “At a time when women could not even own credit cards in their own name, Gloria led a movement that unapologetically demanded equal opportunity for women in all aspects of life. Today, her fight for equal pay, reproductive justice, and equality under the law remains alive and well—especially as we see these fundamental rights come under attack. Her wit, wisdom, and leadership inspired generations, something I saw firsthand with my mother’s commitment and dedication to public service over the years in East Hartford. Gloria’s legacy will continue to guide us forward in the ongoing fight against deadly abortion bans and the discriminatory ‘SAVE Act,’ and to finally ensure the Equal Rights Amendment is rightfully ratified as part of the U.S. Constitution.”

title: Rep. Laurel Lee Introduces Ballots by Election Day Act to Establish Clear Deadline for Federal Elections
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Laurel Lee (FL-15), Chairwoman of the House Administration Subcommittee on Elections and former Florida Secretary of State, introduced the Ballots by Election Day Act, legislation establishing a clear, uniform standard that ballots cast in federal elections must be received by the close of polls on Election Day in order to be counted.

The legislation is the House companion to legislation introduced by Senator Ashley Moody (R-FL). It would require absentee and mail-in ballots in federal elections to be received by the close of polls on Election Day, while preserving existing protections for military and overseas voters under the Uniformed and Overseas Citizens Absentee Voting Act (UOCAVA). The requirement would take effect beginning with federal elections held in 2027.

As Florida’s former Secretary of State, Rep. Lee served as the state’s chief election officer and oversaw the administration of Florida’s elections. Florida already requires most vote-by-mail ballots to be received by 7:00 p.m. on Election Day in order to be counted. The Ballots by Election Day Act would bring that same basic principle to federal elections nationwide: voters should know the deadline, election officials should know the rules, and Election Day should mark the end of voting.

“Having served as Florida’s Secretary of State and overseen elections across our state, I have seen firsthand that clear rules, firm deadlines, and consistent election administration work,”said Rep. Laurel Lee.“Florida has shown that we can provide voters with accessible ways to cast their ballots while maintaining a clear deadline for when those ballots must be received. Election Day should mean election results. When the polls close, voters should have confidence that the voting is over and election officials can move forward with determining the results. The Ballots by Election Day Act applies that commonsense standard to federal elections across the country and provides greater certainty for voters, election officials, and the American people.”

The Ballots by Election Day Act is a simple fix to rebuild trust in elections. The fact that some states allow ballots to pour in for days after an election is absurd. Passing our Ballots by Election Day Act would deliver results before bed,” said Senator Ashley Moody. “I’m happy to see my friend and colleague, Representative Laurel Lee, join me in this fight to bring Florida’s blueprint for elections nationwide.

BACKGROUND:

The Ballots by Election Day Act follows the Supreme Court’s decision in Watson v. Republican National Committee, which determined that current federal law does not establish a nationwide deadline for receiving mail ballots and left the issue for Congress to address.

This bill establishes a clear deadline for when ballots cast for federal office must be received. It provides voters with consistent rules and certainty about when their ballots are due, regardless of where they live. The approach is modeled after Florida, where most vote-by-mail ballots must be received by the close of polls on Election Day.

title: Rep. Nancy Mace Introduces Bill To Kick High-Fructose Corn Syrup Out Of The American Food Supply
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. (Sept. 3, 2026) – Today, Congresswoman Nancy Mace (R-SC) introduced the Removing Excess Additives and Limiting Sugar Act, or the REAL Sugar Act, to bring common sense back to America’s food supply. The legislation bans high-fructose corn syrup in food sold in the United States.

"Americans are tired of being fed highly processed junk and being told it's normal," said Congresswoman Mace. "If we're serious about making America healthy again, we need to take a hard look at what we're putting in our food. The REAL Sugar Act puts American families first and takes on an industry long overdue for accountability."

High-fructose corn syrup hides in foods Americans consume every day, from sodas and sugary beverages to cereal, granola, sauces, flavored yogurt, candy, and ice cream. Excessive consumption of added sugars is linked to weight gain and obesity, type 2 diabetes, and heart disease. It’s time to cut the junk and get back to real food.

The REAL Sugar Act would amend the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to prohibit food containing high-fructose corn syrup from entering interstate commerce. This legislation provides manufacturers with two years to reformulate their products and transition away from high-fructose corn syrup.

The bill would also require the Secretary of Health and Human Services, acting through the Commissioner of Food and Drugs, to report to Congress within three years on industry reformulation efforts, regulations implemented to comply with the legislation, and recommendations for additional Congressional action.

"MAHA means getting back to real food. Americans shouldn't need a chemistry degree to know what they're eating.” Mace added.

The REAL Sugar Act would:

Prohibit food intended for human consumption containing high-fructose corn syrup from entering interstate commerce.

Provide food manufacturers with a two-year transition period to reformulate products.

Require HHS to report to Congress on industry reformulation efforts and regulatory changes.

Require HHS to recommend additional congressional action, if necessary.
