title: NEWS: Sanders, Takano Reintroduce Bill to Move Toward 32-Hour Workweek, Ensure America’s Workers Benefit from AI and Automation
text:
WASHINGTON, Sept. 8 — Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), Ranking Member of the Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions (HELP), and Rep. Mark Takano (D-Calif.) today announced that they will reintroduce legislation to establish a standard 32-hour workweek in America with no loss in pay or benefits. This bill comes as America’s workers have seen massive increases in productivity over the past century and as artificial intelligence, automation and new technologies promise to further increase productivity.

“At a time when artificial intelligence and robotics will radically transform our economy, it is imperative that the financial gains from this new technology benefit working families, not just a handful of billionaires and corporate CEOs. One important way to do that is through a 32-hour workweek with no loss in pay or benefits,” Sanders said. “A 32-hour workweek is not a radical idea. What’s radical is that, despite an explosion in technology and productivity over the last fifty years, millions of workers are working longer hours for lower wages while nearly $80 trillion in wealth has been redistributed from the bottom 90 percent to the top 1 percent. That has got to change. It’s time to reduce the stress level in our country and allow workers and their families to enjoy a better quality of life. It’s time to pass this bill.”

“The 40-hour workweek was established in law nearly 90 years ago,” said Takano. “Since then, cell phones, the internet, and now AI have increased worker productivity, but the profits have been largely concentrated at the top by billionaires and corporations. Work has fundamentally changed. It’s time that labor standards caught up. I’m proud to continue partnering with Senator Sanders in reintroducing this bill to make sure that the gains from historically high productivity are felt by all American workers.”

Today, American workers are more than 400 percent more productive than they were in the 1940s. However, millions of Americans are now working longer hours for lower wages. As of 2019, nearly 40 percent of U.S. workers are on the job at least 50 hours a week, and a staggering 18 percent — or 28.5 million workers — are clocking at least 60 hours a week. In 2024, the average full-time worker in the U.S. now worked almost 43 hours a week. On top of that, today more than 8.5 million Americans work multiple jobs, with more than 4.7 million working a second part-time job on top of a full-time job. Despite working more, Americans are falling behind. Wages are now lower than they were 53 years ago while CEOs make more than 280 times what their workers earn.

According to the American Psychological Association, approximately 80% of workers would be happier and just as productive at work if they worked four days a week.

In 1938, President Franklin D. Roosevelt signed the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) into law establishing the 44-hour workweek through overtime protections — the first broadly applicable federal standard for working hours in the U.S. Just two years later, the FLSA phased-in today’s 40-hour workweek to the American people, which has remained the federal standard ever since. Before these federal labor standards were established, workers — including kids — in the early 19th century were on the job more than 70 hours a week, often in horrendous and dangerous working conditions. In the late 1800s, workers conducted major strikes for an 8-hour workday, coining the historic slogan, “Eight hours for work, eight hours for rest, eight hours for what you will.”

The Thirty-Two Hour Workweek Act is endorsed by: Association of Flight Attendants-CWA (AFA-CWA); The American Federation of Labor and Congress of Industrial Organizations (AFL-CIO); The International Federation of Professional and Technical Engineers (IFPTE); National Employment Law Project (NELP); National Nurses United (NNU), Radio and Machine Workers of America (UE); Service Employees International Union (SEIU); United Auto Workers (UAW); United Food and Commercial Workers (UFCW) and WorkFour.

Read the bill summary here.

title: WATCH: Sen. Schiff Continues Push for Federal Film Tax Incentive, Breaks Down Upcoming Elections on ABC7
text:
Los Angeles, CA – Today, U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) joined ABC7 Los Angeles’ Josh Haskell to discuss his ongoing push to enact a bipartisan federal film tax incentive following President Donald Trump’s Truth Social post last week declaring support for the passage of a federal incentive. Schiff highlighted how federal film tax credits would create thousands of jobs and support local economic growth in California and across the country.

The Senator also broke down efforts to disenfranchise voters which are being enacted ahead of the 2026 midterm election and outlined his agenda for safeguarding elections to ensure every American’s right to vote is protected ahead of the upcoming midterm elections.

View the full interview here.

Key Excerpts:

On the importance of a federal film tax incentive:

This is some rare, good news of bipartisan agreement in Congress. And that is, this is a fabulous industry. It brings a lot of good-paying jobs. It supports the local economy here in Burbank, Glendale. We have so much of the industry, and it’s great for people who work in the industry. But it’s also great for the dry cleaners. It’s great for the caterers and the wardrobe people, and it supports the entire economy. But we’re losing those jobs overseas because other countries have given tax incentives that we haven’t matched. Now, for the first time, there’s a lot of bipartisan interest in this, in getting a federal tax credit done. This is something I’ve been carrying for years and years and years and fighting for. And now we have this rare confluence where the president is for it, Democrats are for it, Republicans are for it. So, we actually have a chance now, finally, to get it done.

On the administration’s voting restriction plans:

[…] They realize I think there’s going to be a major backlash against the tariffs, against the Iran war, against many of the president’s policies that have raised the cost of living for Americans, and they want to basically discourage people from voting. Their hope is to win the election by depriving people of the franchise. So, all around the country, there’s this attack on voting. There’s a case right now before the Supreme Court. If the administration is successful, it will completely upend absentee voting. It will be chaos, which I think they hope for. Here in California, there’s Prop 39, where it may require people to put their Social Security numbers, or some of them, or their driver’s license numbers on their ballots before they mail them. If they forget, their vote doesn’t count. If they use the wrong ID, their vote doesn’t count. This is all designed to take away people’s right to vote.

[…] I’m also concerned, though, apart from these legal efforts or illegal efforts, that you could see interference at polling places on election day. You could see them dispatching the military or ICE as they threatened to do. When you consider that the last big contested election, the president was willing to incite people to attack the Capitol. You really can’t put anything beyond or out of bounds.

On the impact of President Trump’s increasing wealth on Americans:

[…] He has made 2.2 or 2.3 billion dollars in his first year as president. So yeah, there’s a lot that needs to be looked into, and it shouldn’t fall on just Democrats to do it. But Republicans have been unwilling to look at anything the president has done, no matter how corrupt. So yeah, there’ll be investigations, but it’ll be important always to bring it back to what’s the impact of this corruption on people. And I think the impact is that because the president is so focused on making money for himself and his family, he’s not focused on average American families. He’s not focused on their cost of living. He doesn’t care what the tariffs with Canada do to their income and whether they can afford to buy groceries. It’s all about his own wealth. That that needs to be exposed.

On Trump’s trade war with Canada:

I think it’s stupid and destructive. The Canadians have been our strongest allies. They fought side by side with us in every war we’ve been engaged in, and to treat them this way and to engage in this just self-destructive trade war makes no sense at all. Canadians are not our enemies. And it’s I think the Canadians don’t recognize the United States anymore, which is a tragedy. Their government is having to recalibrate its relationship with us after such a productive partnership. It’s just needless and senseless and harmful in raising the cost of living for people.

On the ongoing Iran war:

I don’t think we can afford it at all. And when you break it down, I think I’ve seen some estimates that average families have now had to pay $1,700 to $2,300 more per year that this war has gone on, just in the increased cost of things. And then, of course, the most serious cost is we’ve lost 18 service members. And the cost that those families have borne is just incalculable. So when the president downplays the significance of the war. Well, it may not matter much to him. It may not matter much to his family, but it matters a lot to Americans. And this needs to come to an end.

On the proposed land swap in Yosemite National Park:

It does concern me, and you mentioned investigations earlier. This is something we’re investigating, and that is why this wealthy developer, why this particular proposal, when there are lots of hotel owners and other enterprises that would love to do business in Yosemite and love to have a road of their own. So why does this developer get a road of their own? Why do they get this special easement? It doesn’t make any sense except for the money. You always follow the money. I’m a former prosecutor. You follow the money. And generally, where the money leads with this administration is there’s some corrupt bargain involved. The Forest Service shouldn’t be selling off pieces of a treasure like Yosemite because they’ve got some big donor involved.

title: SCHUMER, AFTER SECURING CONGRESSIONAL GOLD MEDAL TO RECOGNIZE HISTORIC “MIRACLE ON ICE” 1980 OLYMPIC ICE HOCKEY TEAM, VISITS MT VAN HOEVENBERG OLYMPIC SPORTS COMPLEX TO SHOWCASE POTENTIAL FOR FUTURE...
text:
Last Year, Schumer Introduced And Led To Passage Bipartisan Legislation To Celebrate Historic Ice Hockey Game And Honor Olympic U.S. Men’s Ice Hockey Champions With Congressional Gold Medal Recognition – Including One To Be Displayed At New York’s Lake Placid Olympic Center

Senator Reveals His Office Is Participating In Efforts to Explore Potential 2042 NYC-Lake Placid Bid To Have Highest Level Of Competition Featured At New York’s World-Class Facilities

Schumer: Lake Placid Has A Rich Olympic History; We Should Look To Continue That Legacy!

A year after the passage of his legislation honoring the 1980 U.S. Men’s Olympic Hockey Team with a Congressional Gold Medal, U.S. Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer last week visited Mt Van Hoevenberg Olympic Sports Complex to highlight efforts to bring the Winter Olympics back to the North Country. Schumer explained he is involved with new efforts to pursue a bid to host the 2042 Games and said there is no better place than New York State – with its rich sports history and world-class facilities – to host.

“Lake Placid holds a long and special place in Winter Olympic history – having hosted both the 1932 and 1980 Games. Last year, I was proud to sponsor the commemoration of the 1980 ‘Miracle on Ice’ Olympic Ice Hockey Team with the Congressional Gold Medal to be displayed right here in Lake Placid. This historic team, made up of amateur players, sparked an explosion of American pride and patriotism when they defeated the vaunted Soviet Union Red Army Team at the 1980 Winter Olympic Games and then beat Finland in the gold medal game,” said Senator Schumer. “Lake Placid-NYC Games would mean the highest level of competition featured at our world-class facilities, including Lake Placid’s unique alpine and sliding infrastructure. I applaud Governor Hochul’s efforts to look at the feasibility of bringing the Games back here, and I am happy to lend my support to those exploratory efforts. I think Lake Placid just might have more miracles to share with the world.”

Last year, Schumer introduced and helped lead to passage his legislation honoring the 1980 U.S. Men’s Olympic Hockey Team. The team defeated the mighty four-time Olympic champion Soviet Union Team in the semifinal game of the tournament and went on to win a gold medal in a thrilling come-from-behind game against the Finnish National Team. Schumer’s legislation celebrates the team’s historic victory with a Congressional Gold Medal to recognize their extraordinary achievement, including displaying one of the Congressional Gold Medals at the Lake Placid Olympic Center. Also, in 2016, Schumer visited the Olympic Training Center in Lake Placid to launch his successful effort to end the “Victory Tax” that had forced our medal-winning heroes to pay tax to the IRS on the value of their medals and accompanying victory stipends.

Schumer says bringing the Olympics back to Lake Placid and New York would be a once-in-a-generation opportunity to use Lake Placid’s top-notch winter sports infrastructure and New York City’s iconic stadiums for a modern Olympic Games. As New York State considers bidding on the 2042 Winter Olympic Games, Schumer revealed his office is participating in an exploratory committee to evaluate the feasibility of bringing the Winter Olympics back for a joint New York City-Lake Placid-hosted games, and he wants to support these efforts in any way possible.

title: ICYMI: In Light of Recent Findings that Many Veterans Were Defrauded of G.I. Benefits, Shaheen Leads Bipartisan Call for Enhanced Investigation, Greater Coordination Between Departments of Justice and Veterans Affairs
text:
**In separate letters to the Departments of Justice and Veterans Affairs, the bipartisan group of Senators encourage an enhanced response from the Administration to vigorously prosecute fraud against veterans**

(Washington, DC) – U.S. Senators Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), John Cornyn (R-TX) and Maggie Hassan (D-NH) sent a pair of letters calling on the Departments of Justice and Veterans Affairs to enhance their response to recent reporting finding that many veterans were defrauded of their GI Bill benefits by “slapdash” trade schools and education institutions in Texas, California, New Hampshire, Georgia and Florida.

Shaheen, Hassan and Cornyn penned a letter to Department of Veterans Affairs Secretary Doug Collins and Veterans Administration (VA) Inspector General (IG) Cheryl Mason encouraging the Office of the Inspector General (OIG) to launch an enhanced investigation into all unaccredited trade schools where veterans are enrolled to ensure the programs meet all applicable requirements. The bipartisan trio also urged the VA to review its processes for accepting and assessing complaints from students and whistleblowers on potentially fraudulent activity and increase funding and personnel for investigating these cases. The Senators also asked the VA to coordinate with the Department of Justice (DOJ) to refer fraud cases for prosecution.

In a separate letter to U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche, the Senators call on DOJ to strengthen how it investigates, prosecutes and penalizes G.I. Bill fraud and improve coordination with federal, state and local partners to better protect veterans from fraud and abuse. It also calls on DOJ to evaluate its coordination with VA to better target fraud and abuse.

In their letter to the VA, the Senators wrote, in part: “In all, the Washington Post found more than $300 million in fraud at 20 schools that were bilking our veterans. Much of the fraud should have been obvious at first glance. Schools offering courses that cost thousands of dollars but last less than a week should have caused red flags to go up at VA. Moreover, the article raises questions about how the Department processes and refers veterans’ complaints. While these losses to fraud may only represent a small percentage of the VA’s education budget, any loss of funds and adverse impacts to veterans must be swiftly addressed.”

The Senators concluded: “VA has repeatedly said that fraud against veterans is one of its top priorities. It is imperative that we understand how these institutions are allowed to operate and make millions despite multiple oversight measures. Consequently, we call on VA OIG to launch an enhanced investigation into all unaccredited trade schools where veterans are enrolled to ensure the programs meet all applicable requirements. Once any warning sign is identified, VA must act more quickly to disapprove these fraudulent programs from GI Bill eligibility. We also urge the Department and VA OIG to review their processes for accepting and assessing complaints from students and whistleblowers on potentially fraudulent activity and increase funding and personnel for investigating these cases. Finally, we ask that the VA and OIG coordinate with the U.S. Department of Justice and, if appropriate, state attorneys general, to refer more of these cases for prosecution.”

Click HERE to view the full letter to Secretary Collins and Inspector General Mason.

In their letter to the DOJ, the Senators wrote, in part: “In a number of these cases, federal prosecutors failed to press charges, reached settlements for a fraction of the school’s ill-gotten gains or recommended more lenient sentences than even the judge ultimately felt were correct. [...] Fraud against our veterans must be prosecuted vigorously. The Washington Post documented how light the punishment was for the trade schools who charged exorbitant rates for very little education or training. In one case, the settlement that Department of Justice prosecutors struck was rejected by the judge because it was too lenient.”

The Senators concluded: “We urge the Department to reexamine the procedures for U.S. Attorneys to investigate and prosecute alleged G.I. Bill fraud, especially the criteria for settling cases that result in fines constituting a fraction of the overall fraud. We also call on the Department to reconsider how it cooperates with the Department of Veterans Affairs and state educational and law enforcement agencies to better target fraud and abuse of our veterans and the G.I. Bill program.”

Click HERE to view the full letter to Attorney General Blanche.

title: Warner Attends Chesapeake Veterans Affairs Facility Ribbon Cutting, Reaffirms Support for Veterans’ Access to High-Quality Health Care
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Sen. Mark R. Warner (D-VA) attended the ribbon cutting for the new Western Branch outpatient clinic in Chesapeake, a state-of-the-art Community Based Outpatient Clinic (CBOC). The facility spans 27,000 square feet and will have a drive-through pharmacy, primary care, mental health care, and radiology. The clinic will serve more than 10,000 veterans who reside in South Hampton Roads.

HIGH-QUALITY PHOTOS AVAILABLE HERE

“It is my pleasure to be here on a really important day for Hampton Roads veterans. Improving access to care for our veterans must always be a priority, and this brand new, state-of-the-art facility will be a key part of that equation for thousands of veterans in the region,” said Sen. Warner. “Veterans and their families have more than earned access to quality, reliable, and timely health care through years of service and sacrifice, but they have faced unnecessary hurdles to getting that care. I deeply appreciate the men and women who have signed up to work at this facility, and their colleagues nationwide who have devoted their careers to this medical and public service. I will continue fighting to improve access to quality care for our veterans.”

Western Branch CBOC is strategically located in South Hampton Roads to enhance access for veterans who must use either a bridge or tunnel to seek care at Hampton VAHCS, reducing travel times for many.

Sen. Warner has long fought to expand health care access and benefits for Virginia’s nearly 700,000 veterans. Earlier this year, Sen. Warner pressed the administration to significantly boost funding for VA facilities, warning that years of underinvestment will increasingly leave Virginia veterans without the care access they’ve earned. Sen. Warner has specifically focused on the need to modernize and streamline how the VA delivers medical facilities and infrastructure, reduce the disability claim backlog at the VA, ensure the VA is appropriately staffed to improve access to care and benefits, improve women veterans’ access to health care, and he has pushed Congress to approve major VA facilities across the Commonwealth.

title: Warner, Kaine Commend Designation of 9/11 Pentagon Memorial as National Park Service Affiliated Area
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Sens. Mark R. Warner and Tim Kaine (both D-VA), following reports today, commended the official designation of the 9/11 Pentagon Memorial as an affiliated area of the National Park System, a recognition that will help preserve the memory of the 184 people killed at the Pentagon and aboard American Airlines Flight 77 on September 11, 2001, and ensure their stories are passed down to future generations.

“The 9/11 Pentagon Memorial is a solemn tribute to each of the 184 individuals at the Pentagon and aboard Flight 77 who tragically died on September 11, 2001, standing as a lasting reminder of Americans’ loss and resilience on one of our nation’s darkest days,” said the senators. “We’re proud to support efforts that will preserve this memorial for generations to come and ensure that Americans always have a place to honor those we lost, remember their stories, and deepen their understanding of the enduring impact of September 11 on our nation.”

Affiliated areas are nationally significant sites that preserve important cultural or natural resources but are typically owned and operated independently of the National Park Service. Through affiliation, the National Park Service can provide technical assistance and other support to help maintain these important sites. The 9/11 Pentagon Memorial becomes the 33rdaffiliated area in the National Park System.

Sens. Warner and Kaine have long supported the 9/11 Pentagon Memorial and efforts to expand its educational mission, including the establishment of a Visitor Education Center that will tell the story of that day, and of how Americans responded, came together, and moved forward in the aftermath of the tragic September 11 attacks.

title: Wicker, Hyde-Smith, Guest Welcome Over $4 Million For Mississippi Telehealth Efforts
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senators Roger Wicker, R-Miss., and Cindy Hyde-Smith, R-Miss., and U.S. Congressman Michael Guest, R-Miss., celebrated the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services’ decision to award the University of Mississippi Medical Center (UMMC) $4.25 million for a five-year redesignation as a Center of Excellence in Telehealth.

Congress appropriated this funding, which flows through the Telehealth Centers of Excellence program. Wicker, Hyde-Smith, and Guest fought for the funding during the Fiscal Year 2026 appropriations cycle. This program is designed for a five-year window, meaning UMMC will be eligible to receive subsequent awards over the next few years.

“The University of Mississippi Medical Center has been a pioneer in telehealth care, and they will put this funding to work for Mississippi and the nation,” said Senator Roger Wicker. “Telehealth is a lifeline for rural states like ours. This option bridges healthcare divides, bringing providers to senior citizens, busy parents, or those living far from a clinic.”

“As one of two telehealth centers for excellence nationally, UMMC continues to set the pace in expanding telehealth access and its effectiveness as a tool to promote wellness. It’s a pleasure to work with Senator Wicker and Congressman Guest to ensure that federal resources for this good work are maintained,” said Senator Hyde-Smith, who serves on the Senate appropriations subcommittee that funds HHS.

“UMMC has long been a national leader in telehealth. I am proud to represent UMMC in the U.S. House and to advocate for this Telehealth Centers of Excellence program funding. UMMC’s telehealth program will continue to be of great service to Mississippians and serve as a national model, and I am looking forward to the continued research, innovation, and patient-centered care UMMC will provide,”said Congressman Michael Guest.

“We greatly appreciate the ongoing investment in UMMC’s telehealth initiatives that extends our ability to provide high-quality health care to rural and medically underserved areas of our state. Telehealth allows us to monitor patients in rural hospitals, to assist patients with chronic conditions and to help students in need of mental health services,” said Dr. LouAnn Woodward, Vice Chancellor for Health Affairs at the University of Mississippi Medical Center.

Background on the Telehealth Centers of Excellence Program:

The Telehealth Centers of Excellence program supports academic medical centers, like UMMC, as they work to expand telehealth services to rural communities and improve patient outcomes. This funding will help researchers collect data, enhance studies, and provide telehealth training to professionals.

UMMC is one of two federally recognized Telehealth Centers of Excellence in the country. As such, UMMC will serve as a model that medical institutions across the nation can look to as they work to implement telehealth solutions in their states. UMMC’s commitment to telehealth services has made Mississippi a leader in this emerging health care delivery option.

title: Congressman Al Green, the Houston LGBTQ+ Political Caucus, and the Montrose Center will Address the Maltreatment of Transgender Immigrants in ICE Detention Facilities
text:
(Houston, Texas) — On Thursday, September 10, 2026, Congressman Al Green will join Brandon Mack, President of the Houston LGBTQ+ Political Caucus, Avery Belyeu, Chief Executive Officer of The Montrose Center, and Daron Perez, Transwellness Coordinator of The Montrose Center to host a press conference addressing concerns regarding the maltreatment of transgender immigrants in U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detention facilities. The press conference follows Congressman Green’s September 4, 2026, communiqué to U.S. Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, in which he raised concerns about the denial of specialized medical care and the removal of protections for transgender immigrant detainees. A copy of the communiqué is accessible by clicking here.

"ICE detention cannot become a place where transgender people are punished for their identity. When the government takes someone into custody, it assumes responsibility for that person's safety, health, and dignity. We support and stand in solidarity and agreement with Congressman Al Green's demand for answers and accountability. We urge DHS to take immediate and verifiable action,” Brandon Mack, President, Houston LGBTQ+ Political Caucus.

“Transgender individuals who find themselves in the care of our government during immigration proceedings deserve dignity, safety, and basic health care. That means they are not mistreated, are housed in safe accommodations, and are able to access all of their medications. We are grateful to Congressman Green for seeking clarification on how these guarantees are being met,” Avery Belyeu, Chief Executive Officer, The Montrose Center.

Congressman Al Green stated, “Transgender persons deserve to live without fear that their identity will be used as a reason to deny them care, especially health care, safety, or humane treatment while in ICE custody. While many communities have suffered under harmful immigration policies, we must not overlook the particular vulnerabilities faced by transgender immigrants in detention. Government custody must never become a license to discriminate. We must demand humane treatment and necessary medical care, and we must protect transgender lives.”

title: Congressman Biggs Supports ASU’s Bid to Establish New American Defense Center
text:
GILBERT, ARIZONA. – This month, Congressman Andy Biggs (AZ-05) led a letter to Secretary of War Pete Hegseth supporting Arizona State University’s (ASU) application to establish the Applied Research for Manufacturing Operational Readiness (ARMOR) Center at ASU’s Polytechnic campus in Arizona’s Fifth Congressional District. The proposed center would strengthen Arizona’s manufacturing sector and defense industrial base while advancing technologies critical to America’s military readiness.

The U.S. Army is seeking to establish a new national ARMOR Center to accelerate the transition of cutting-edge manufacturing research into capabilities that strengthen military readiness and the American defense industrial base. The center would serve as a trusted government partner, coordinating research and helping move promising technologies into the Army’s Organic Industrial Base, defense contractors, and other manufacturing partners.

ASU’s proposed ARMOR Center would create an end-to-end pipeline to advance technologies from applied research and development through maturation, qualification, scaling, and ultimately deployment into military manufacturing and sustainment operations. Establishing the center at ASU’s Polytechnic campus would further position Arizona as a national leader in advanced manufacturing and defense technology while strengthening the state’s growing defense industrial base.

“Led by institutions and companies like Arizona State University, our state continues to position itself at the forefront of America’s defense industrial base,” said Congressman Biggs. “Throughout my time in Congress, I have been pleased to support projects and initiatives that strengthen our national defense and help safeguard our citizens, freedoms, and interests. ASU is well positioned to lead this important effort, and I am hopeful the administration will select its proposal to establish the ARMOR Center here in Arizona.”

Congressman Eli Crane co-led the letter.

title: ICYMI: Buchanan Warns of Looming National Debt Crisis in Sarasota Herald-Tribune Op-Ed
text:
“Florida families balance their budgets every month. It is about time Washington does the same.”

Op-Ed Details the $40 Trillion National Debt and Buchanan’s Balanced Budget Amendment

WASHINGTON — Congressman Vern Buchanan recently penned an op-ed in the Sarasota Herald-Tribune warning that the national debt, now surpassing $40 trillion, is on pace to leave the next generation with a bill they never agreed to and cannot afford.

“I spent more than 30 years running businesses before I ever set foot on the House floor,” said Buchanan. “In the business world, there is a simple rule that never changes: you cannot spend more than you take in year after year and expect to stay open. Every entrepreneur and small business owner in Florida knows this. So does every family balancing a checkbook. It’s time Washington learned it too.”

Read the full op-ed HERE or below:

The Next Generation Shouldn’t Inherit Washington’s Spending Problem

Congressman Vern Buchanan

I spent more than 30 years running businesses before I ever set foot on the House floor. In the business world, there is a simple rule that never changes: you cannot spend more than you take in year after year and expect to stay open. Every entrepreneur and small business owner in Florida knows this. So does every family balancing a checkbook. It’s time Washington learned it too.

The national debt has surpassed $40 trillion, a number so large it’s difficult to picture. To put it in perspective, that’s more than $300,000 owed for every household in America, a bill no family ever agreed to, and no family should have to afford. The debt now stands at more than 100 percent of the size of our entire economy, a level that warrants extreme concern. Additionally, interest on the debt is growing out of control as it surpasses defense to become the federal governments second largest expense. We’ve borrowed against the future before, but always to win a war or survive a depression, never simply to avoid making a hard choice.

If Washington continues on its current course, with no more wars, no recession and no major new programs, the debt is projected to hit a staggering $64 trillion within the next decade. Add more than $80 trillion in unfunded promises to Social Security and Medicare and the picture becomes even more sobering. These are promises we’ve made to seniors who spent their whole lives paying in, and to young people who haven’t even cast their first vote yet. As representatives of the American people, we are here to serve their best interest, and there is nothing in their interest about handing the next generation a bill this country can’t afford.

In January 2007, the national debt stood at just under $9 trillion. In less than two decades, it has more than quadrupled. Think about that. It took this country more than 230 years, through two world wars, the Great Depression and the Cold War, to reach $9 trillion in debt. It has taken us less than 20 years to add more than $31 trillion more on top of it.

This did not happen under one party or one president. Both sides of the aisle share the blame, and both sides need to be part of the solution. That is why I authored H.J. Res. 3, a constitutional amendment to require a balanced federal budget, as both my first piece of legislation when I arrived in Congress and my first bill to introduce in each Congress since. I believe nothing else we can do in Washington matters much if we do not get our fiscal house in order first.

A balanced budget amendment simply says what every Florida family and every small business already lives by: Congress cannot spend money it does not have without a real plan to pay it back. It would force Washington to set priorities, cut what does not work and stop kicking the hardest decisions down the road to our kids and grandkids. This is not a Republican idea or a Democratic idea. It is widely understood, and it deserves support from members on both sides of the aisle who care about the country the next generation will inherit.

I’ve heard the argument that we can simply tax our way out of this problem. But I don’t believe the answer is to reach deeper into the pockets of the people who are already carrying this country. The math does not support it either. Even the most aggressive tax increases on the wealthiest Americans would not come close to closing deficits of this size, let alone pay for the new spending some in Washington keep proposing. Working families and small businesses didn’t run up this debt, and they shouldn’t be the ones to foot the bill for it. The only honest path forward is to control spending, grow the economy and stop treating the congressional credit card as if it has no limit.

I did not come to Washington to leave behind a bigger problem than the one I found. I came here to run government the way I ran my businesses, with discipline, accountability and an eye on long-term success. Nearly 20 years later, that mission is more urgent than it has ever been.

The debt crisis we are approaching will not announce itself with a single dramatic headline. It will show up in higher interest rates, a weaker dollar, less money for the priorities that matter and fewer opportunities for the next generation. It will reach into the everyday lives of Americans nationwide. We still have time to change course, but that window is closing quickly.

I’m asking my colleagues on both sides of the aisle to join me in getting the national debt under control. Florida families balance their budgets every month. It is about time Washington does the same.

Rep. Vern Buchanan (R-Fla) is the Vice Chairman of the Ways and Means Committee and the chairman of the Health Subcommittee. Prior to serving in Congress, Buchanan was in business for over 30 years and chaired both the Greater Sarasota Chamber of Commerce and Florida Chamber of Commerce.

###

title: Los Representantes García, Ramirez, Quigley y Jackson, Funcionarios Electos Locales y Defensores de los Inmigrantes, Exigen Plena Rendición de Cuentas por la Brutalidad del DHS  y Una Reforma Migratoria Significativa
text:
CHICAGO — Hoy, los miembros del Congreso Jesús “Chuy” García (IL-04), Delia C. Ramirez (IL-03), Mike Quigley (IL-05) y Jonathan Jackson (IL-01) —acompañados por una coalición de funcionarios electos locales, entre ellos la senadora estatal Celina Villanueva, el representante estatal Edgar Gonzalez Jr., la comisionada del condado de Cook Alma Anaya y los concejales Michael Rodriguez y Jessie Fuentes, así como organizaciones defensoras de los inmigrantes como Illinois Coalition for Immigrant and Refugee Rights (ICIRR), Brighton Park Neighborhood Council (BPNC), Organized Communities Against Deportations (OCAD) y The Resurrection Project (TRP) — ofrecieron una conferencia de prensa para marcar un año de resistencia frente a la Operación Midway Blitz.

La coalición instó a tomar medidas en materia de reforma migratoria, incluyendo la exigencia de una votación sobre la Ley Sueño y Promesa (Dream and Promise Act), y reclamó plena rendición de cuentas por parte de las autoridades locales y federales —incluida la Fiscal Estatal del condado de Cook— ante la brutalidad y el terror que las acciones de control migratorio del gobierno federal han infligido a las comunidades de toda la región.

“Hace un año, la administración Trump intentó quebrantarnos y arrebatarnos la dignidad enviando a agentes federales enmascarados a nuestra ciudad mediante la Operación Midway Blitz. Fracasaron; en su lugar, nuestra comunidad se unió, alzó la voz y desafió su abuso de poder”, declaró el Congresista Jesús “Chuy” García. “Un año después, estamos más unidos que nunca. Pero la lucha no ha terminado. Los agentes federales enmascarados siguen operando en nuestros vecindarios, y continuaremos exigiendo que se marchen y que los responsables de sus crímenes rindan cuentas. Y lo que es más importante: seguiremos luchando por una reforma migratoria significativa para que ninguna comunidad tenga que volver a sufrir las consecuencias de nuestro sistema migratorio fallido”.

“Conmemoramos el primer aniversario de Midway Blitz, cuando el Departamento de Seguridad Nacional (DHS) inició una campaña de terror en Chicago. Quienes vivimos ese terror lo tenemos claro: el DHS SIGUE SIENDO la mayor amenaza para nuestra seguridad colectiva”, afirmó la Congresista Delia Ramirez. “Al recuperar la mayoría en el Congreso el próximo año, nuestro dolor, nuestra indignación y nuestras exigencias de justicia deben impulsarnos a una acción que honre a todos aquellos que el DHS nos arrebató; debemos hacer rendir cuentas a CADA fascista que haya permitido la violencia del DHS y se haya beneficiado de ella, así como abolir el ICE y desmantelar el DHS”.

"La 'Operación Midway Blitz' de Donald Trump tenía un único objetivo: aterrorizar a Chicago. Los agentes del ICE y la CBP no fueron tras los peores delincuentes; secuestraron a personas en plena calle, lanzaron gases lacrimógenos contra escuelas primarias y mataron a un padre de dos hijos", declaró el Congresista Mike Quigley. "Lamentablemente, el horror de las políticas migratorias de Trump no terminó con la Operación Midway Blitz. Apenas el mes pasado, asistí a una audiencia de deportación donde vi a niños ante la corte sin sus padres, enfrentándose a una barrera idiomática y teniendo que explicar por qué merecen quedarse en este país. Hay que poner fin a esta crueldad. Estoy más comprometido que nunca a trabajar con mis colegas y con los defensores de derechos para proteger a nuestros vecinos inmigrantes y poner un alto al Departamento de Seguridad Nacional (DHS) de Trump antes de que causen más daño".

"Un año después de la Operación Midway Blitz, recordamos el daño causado por esta operación autoritaria, pero también honramos a los líderes religiosos, organizadores comunitarios, abogados, educadores y ciudadanos de Chicago que dieron un paso al frente para proteger a sus vecinos y defender los valores que fortalecen a nuestra ciudad", afirmó el Congresista Jonathan Jackson. "Seguiré exigiendo que se rindan cuentas por los abusos cometidos contra los inmigrantes y nuestras comunidades. Me uno a mis colegas del Congreso para reiterar nuestra exigencia de una reforma migratoria integral, basada en la convicción fundamental de que toda persona merece dignidad, equidad y el debido proceso".

“Esta semana se cumple el primer aniversario de la Operación Midway Blitz, y los residentes de Chicago aún se encuentran conmocionados por los horrores que nuestras comunidades se han visto obligadas a enfrentar, mientras agentes enmascarados continúan sembrando el caos en toda la ciudad, deteniendo a innumerables residentes y desmantelando familias sin miramientos”, declaró la Senadora Estatal Celina Villanueva. “Desde que se lanzó la operación el pasado mes de septiembre, las comunidades latinas —especialmente aquellas a las que yo represento— han vivido con miedo constante: temor a salir de sus hogares y a enviar a sus hijos a la escuela. Tras un año de agresiones brutales contra manifestantes, patrullajes en las calles, redadas en nuestros vecindarios y daños a nuestros residentes, ya es hora de exigir rendición de cuentas y justicia a esta administración, no solo para los latinos de Illinois, sino también para todos aquellos afectados por estos actos de odio sin sentido”.

“La Operación Midway Blitz no quebrantó a nuestra comunidad; fortaleció nuestra determinación. Durante un año, nuestras familias inmigrantes, vecinos y organizaciones comunitarias se han mantenido unidos frente al miedo y la intimidación. Seguiremos defendiendo a cada familia y protegiendo el espíritu acogedor que define a nuestra comunidad”, afirmó el Concejal del Distrito 22, Michael D. Rodriguez.

“Ya sean las redadas en apartamentos de South Shore, el tiroteo contra Marimar Martínez en Brighton Park o el asesinato de Silverio Villegas González, ha quedado demostrado que ICE NO nos protege; su función es intimidar a las comunidades de color y deportar a tantas personas como sea posible. Los líderes locales y los políticos deben apoyar a los inmigrantes y hacer cumplir las leyes y políticas por las que nuestras comunidades lucharon para convertir a Illinois en un lugar que dé la bienvenida a todos”, afirmó Lawrence Benitio, director ejecutivo del ICIRR.

“La Operación Midway Blitz no ha terminado; todavía sufrimos las consecuencias de ver cómo miles de vecinos fueron arrancados de nuestra comunidad. Familias separadas. Empleos perdidos. Comunidades desestabilizadas. Sin embargo, a pesar de todo, nuestra comunidad sigue dando la cara y luchando. Nos negamos a permitir que se normalice este terror”, declaró Any Huamami, directora de organización del Brighton Park Neighborhood Council.

“Hace un año, por estas fechas, nuestras comunidades sufrían el terror provocado por agentes enmascarados; hubo personas secuestradas sin explicación y familias separadas a la fuerza debido a la campaña de control migratorio de esta administración federal. El año pasado nos demostró que todos corríamos el riesgo de ser detenidos simplemente por nuestra apariencia. Las detenciones ilegales se convirtieron en la norma, pero seguimos aquí denunciando esas acciones y recordando a la gente que ICE continúa operando en nuestras comunidades. Es nuestro deber mantenernos alerta y protegernos mutuamente”, afirmó Antonio Gutiérrez, cofundador y coordinador estratégico de Organized Communities Against Deportations.

“El noroeste de Chicago fue uno de los puntos clave de la Operación Midway Blitz. Los miembros de la comunidad local se unieron para resistir este ataque, formando parte de la red estatal de respuesta rápida coordinada por ICIRR. Nuestra labor no terminó cuando concluyó la Operación Midway Blitz; a la fecha, seguimos presenciando secuestros y agresiones por parte del ICE en nuestros vecindarios. Los miembros de la comunidad seguirán haciendo su parte para mantenernos a salvo. Ya es hora de que los departamentos de policía locales cumplan con su deber e investiguen las acciones de estos agentes para que podamos exigirles responsabilidades. Es lo mínimo que merecen los miembros de nuestra comunidad y los vecinos que sufrieron ataques con gases lacrimógenos y gas pimienta, además de agresiones y violencia por parte del gobierno federal”, declaró el pastor Juan Pablo Herrera, presidente de la junta directiva de PLSNA.

“El miedo que recorrió nuestras comunidades es real, pero este año no estuvo definido por el miedo, sino por la belleza y la resiliencia de nuestra comunidad. La administración Trump se propuso dar un ejemplo con Chicago. En cambio, nosotros dimos el ejemplo: construimos una respuesta coordinada a nivel estatal que ha conectado a decenas de miles de miembros de la comunidad con asistencia legal, así como una red de respuesta rápida que demuestra que los inmigrantes de todo Illinois nunca están solos”, afirmó Eréndira Rendón, vicepresidenta de Justicia para Inmigrantes de The Resurrection Project.

title: Reps. García, Ramirez, Quigley, Jackson, Local Elected Officials and Immigration Advocates Call for Full Accountability for DHS Brutality and Meaningful Immigration Reform
text:
CHICAGO — Today, Congressmembers Jesús “Chuy” García (IL-04), Delia C. Ramirez (IL-03), Mike Quigley (IL-05), and Jonathan Jackson (IL-01), joined by a coalition of local elected officials including State Senator Celina Villanueva, State Representative Edgar Gonzalez Jr, Cook County Commissioner Alma Anaya, Alderperson Michael Rodriguez, Alderperson Jessie Fuentes, and immigration advocacy organizations, including Illinois Coalition for Immigrant and Refugee Rights (ICIRR), Brighton Park Neighborhood Council (BPNC), Organized Communities Against Deportations (OCAD) and The Resurrection Project (TRP), held a press conference to mark one year of resistance to Operation Midway Blitz.

The coalition called for action on immigration reform, including by forcing a vote on the Dream and Promise Act, and demanded full accountability from local and federal authorities, including the Cook County State’s Attorney, for the brutality and terror inflicted by the federal government’s immigration enforcement actions on communities throughout the region.

“A year ago, the Trump administration tried to break us and take away our dignity by sending masked federal agents into our city through Operation Midway Blitz. They failed, and instead our community came together, stood up and challenged their abuse of power,” said Congressman Jesús “Chuy” García. “One year later, we are more united than ever. But the fight is not over. Masked federal agents continue to operate in our neighborhoods, and we will keep demanding that they leave and that those responsible for their crimes be held accountable. Most importantly, we will continue fighting for meaningful immigration reform so that no community has to endure the failures of our broken immigration system again.”

"We are commemorating the one-year anniversary of Midway Blitz, when the Department of Homeland Security began a campaign of terror in Chicago. Those of us who lived through its terror are clear: DHS REMAINS the biggest threat to our collective safety," said Congresswoman Delia Ramirez. "As we regain the majority next year, our grief, our anger, and our calls for justice must move us to action that honors all those stolen from us by DHS, by holding EVERY fascist who has permitted and profited from DHS’s violence accountable, by abolishing ICE, and by dismantling DHS."

"Donald Trump's Operation Midway Blitz had one goal and one goal only: to terrorize Chicago. ICE and CBP agents didn't go after the worst of the worst, they kidnapped people off the streets, tear gassed elementary schools, and killed a father of two," said Congressman Mike Quigley. "Unfortunately, the horror of Trump's immigration policies didn't end with Operation Midway Blitz. Just last month, I attended a deportation hearing where I saw children in court without their parents, facing a language barrier, and being asked to explain why they deserve to stay in this country. This cruelty must be stopped. I'm more committed than ever to working with my colleagues and advocates to protect our immigrant neighbors and stop Trump’s DHS in its tracks before they can do any more harm."

“One year after Operation Midway Blitz, we remember the harm caused by this authoritarian operation, but we also honor the faith leaders, community organizers, attorneys, educators, and ordinary Chicagoans who stepped up to protect their neighbors and defend the values that make our city strong,” said Congressman Jonathan Jackson. “I will continue to demand accountability for the abuses inflicted on immigrants and our communities. I stand with my Congressional colleagues in renewing our call for comprehensive immigration reform rooted in the fundamental belief that every person deserves dignity, equity, and due process.”

“This week marks the one-year anniversary of Operation Midway Blitz, and Chicago residents are still reeling from the horrors our communities have been forced to face, as masked officers continue to wreak havoc across our city by taking countless residents into custody and dismantling families left and right,” said State Senator Celina Villanueva. “Since the operation was launched last September, Latino communities, especially those I represent, have lived in constant fear – afraid of leaving their homes and sending their children to school. After a year of brutalizing protestors, patrolling city streets, raiding our neighborhoods and harming our residents, it is far beyond time to demand accountability and justice from this administration, not only for Latino Illinoisans but also for everyone who has been impacted by these senseless acts of hate.”

“Operation Midway Blitz did not break our community, it strengthened our resolve. For a year, our immigrant families, neighbors, and community organizations have stood together against fear and intimidation. We will continue to defend every family and protect the welcoming spirit that defines our community,” said 22 Ward Alderperson Michael D. Rodriguez.

“Whether it be the apartment raids in South Shore, the shooting of Marimar Martinez in Brighton Park, or the murder of Silverio Villegas González, it’s been proven that ICE does NOT keep us safe - they are designed to intimidate communities of color and deport as many people as possible…Local leaders and politicians must stand with immigrants and enforce the laws and policies our communities fought for to make Illinois a welcoming place for all, said Lawrence Benitio, Executive Director, ICIRR.

“Operation Midway Blitz isn’t over - we’re still reeling from the impact of thousands of neighbors being stripped from our community. Families separated. Jobs lost. Communities destabilized. Yet, through it all, our community keeps showing up and fighting back. We refuse to let this terror be normalized,” said Any Huamami, Director of Organizing, Brighton Park Neighborhood Council.

“On this day, last year our communities were being terrorized by masked agents, kidnapped without explanation, and families have been forcibly broken by this federal administration’s immigration enforcement campaign. Last year showed us we were all at risk of being detained only based on what we look like. Unlawful arrests became the norm, but we are still here exposing those actions and reminding people that ICE is still in our communities. It is our duty to continue to be vigilant and protect each other,” said Antonio Gutierrez, Co-Founder and Strategic Coordinator, Organized Communities Against Deportations.

“Chicago's Northwest Side was one of the concentration points for Operation Midway Blitz. Local community members came together to fight back against this attack on our community as part of the statewide network of rapid responders anchored by ICIRR. Our work did not end when Midway Blitz concluded. We continue to see daily ICE abductions and assaults in our neighborhoods to this day. Community members will continue doing their part to keep us safe. It is now long overdue for police departments locally to do their job, and investigate the actions of these agents, so we can hold them to account. It's the least that our community members and neighbors who were tear gassed, pepper sprayed and faced assault and aggression from the federal government deserve,” said Pastor Juan Pablo Herrera, Board President, PLSNA.

“The fear that swept through our communities is real, but this year wasn’t defined by fear, but by the beauty and resilience of our community. The Trump administration set out to make an example of Chicago. Instead, we led by example—building a statewide coordinated response that has connected tens of thousands of community members to legal support, and a rapid response network that shows that immigrants across Illinois never stand alone, said Eréndira Rendón, Vice President of Immigrant Justice, The Resurrection Project.

title: Rep. Ciscomani Celebrates Grand Opening of the Wildcat Welcome Center at the University of Arizona
text:
Tucson, AZ - U.S. Representative Ciscomani joined the Wildcat community today for the grand opening and ribbon-cutting of the University of Arizona’s new Wildcat Welcome Center, a space dedicated to welcome prospective students and their families to campus.

"It was an honor to join the Wildcat community for this momentous occasion," said Rep. Juan Ciscomani. "The new Wildcat Welcome Center will serve as the gateway for prospective Wildcats and their families, providing an engaging first look at all the University of Arizona has to offer. As the first stop on campus, it will set the stage for countless students’ journeys to becoming Wildcats."

The Wildcat Welcome Center, located inside the Student Union Memorial Center, will serve as the central hub for campus tours, enrollment events, workshops, and student experiences. Future Wildcats and their families will have the opportunity to immerse themselves in the vibrant University of Arizona community and culture. Completed at the outset of the fall semester, the center is now the home base for student ambassador-led campus tours.

As Arizona’s only member of the House Appropriations Committee, Rep. Ciscomani has championed federal investments that strengthen the University of Arizona’s leadership in innovation, research, and workforce development.

Most recently, Rep. Ciscomani championed $2 million for Applied Hypersonics and Directed Energy Integration, which will support workforce development in these critical fields by providing state-of-the-art testing and manufacturing equipment for hypersonics and directed energy research. The investment has already cleared its first major legislative hurdle and remains a priority in the ongoing appropriations process.

"The University of Arizona is preparing the next generation for the jobs and industries of the future, and I am proud to advocate for the federal investments that make this work possible," said Rep. Ciscomani. "From welcoming future Wildcats to advancing groundbreaking research, we are ensuring Arizona remains a leader in innovation and opportunity. As a proud U of A alum, I am committed to keeping our university a premier destination for Arizona students and all those looking to join the Wildcat family."

The Sept. 9 grand opening celebration included remarks from university leaders, appearances by Wilbur and Wilma Wildcat, a performance by the Sunnyside Unified School District Mariachi Band, a ribbon cutting, an open house reception, and student ambassador-led tours.

text:

September 9, 2026

MEDIA CONTACT:

e: jessica.myers@mail.house.gov

c: 202.913.0126

WASHINGTON, DC – U.S. Representatives Yvette D. Clarke (NY-09), Robin Kelly (IL-02), Nanette Barragán (CA-44), and Emily Randall (WA-06) led 49 Members of Congress in sending a letter to Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. and Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz calling for an immediate end to the sharing of Medicaid enrollee data with Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).

Despite a federal preliminary injunction limiting data transfers, CMS continues to share private data belonging to millions of enrollees—including U.S. citizens and lawful residents—beyond court-approved limits. Reports also reveal ICE improperly mishandled the data across internal channels and shared it with third-party analytics contractors like Palantir Technologies.

“The role of HHS should be to protect the health of all those living in this country and provide essential human services, not to be a watchdog for DHS or act as immigration enforcement,” the Members stated in the letter.

title: CORREA, EVANS INTRODUCE BIPARTISAN BILL TO IMPROVE TRANSPARENCY OF SBA SPANISH-LANGUAGE RESOURCES
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Reps. Lou Correa (D-CA-46), Gabe Evans (R-CO-08), Monica De La Cruz (R-TX-15), Henry Cuellar (D-TX-28), Maria Elvira Salazar (R-FL-27), Jim Costa (D-CA-21) and David Valadao (R-CA-22), introduced the bipartisan SBA Spanish Resource Report Act, legislation to give Congress and the public a clearer picture of the Spanish-language resources currently available to entrepreneurs and small business owners through the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA).

This legislation ensures that Congress and Spanish-speaking entrepreneurs are aware of the resources and services that remain available to them through the SBA.

"Hispanic Americans own more than five million businesses across this country, employing nearly three million workers. Everyone in this great nation who’s willing to work hard and contribute deserves a fair shot at the American Dream, and this bill is a step in that direction. The SBA Spanish Resource Act is common-sense legislation that makes sure Spanish-speaking small business owners and entrepreneurs have the resources they need to succeed.” — Congressman Lou Correa (D-CA-46)

“As the grandson of Mexican immigrants and the representative of a district with a prominent Hispanic community, I know the critical role Hispanic small businesses play in our economy. This bill directs an inventory to be conducted of existing Small Business Administration Spanish-language resources to provide greater clarity to Congress and small business owners across our country regarding what resources and services are currently available.” –– Congressman Gabe Evans (R-CO-08)

"Language should never be a barrier to success. With over one million Hispanic-owned small businesses in Texas, I am proud to join bipartisan legislation that expands access and awareness of Spanish-language tools at the SBA. Our small businesses are the backbone of our communities, and I will continue working to ensure Texas main streets thrive.” — Congresswoman Monica De La Cruz (R-TX-15)

“For many small business owners in South Texas, Spanish is the language they use every day with their families, employees, and customers. Federal resources should be accessible to the people they are meant to serve, and this bipartisan bill will help make sure the SBA understands where language gaps may be making it harder for our small businesses to get the information they need.” — Congressman Henry Cuellar (D-TX-28)

“In South Florida, small business happens in both English and Spanish. That is why Congress should know what Spanish-language resources the SBA already offers, how they are being used, and what they cost. I am proud to introduce the SBA Spanish Resource Report Act, to give Congress the information it needs to oversee these resources responsibly and make sure they are serving the small-business owners they are meant to help.” — Congresswoman Maria Elvira Salazar (R-FL-27)

“Across the San Joaquin Valley, small businesses drive our local economy, including thousands of entrepreneurs who conduct business in Spanish. They deserve clear information about the resources available through the SBA. This bipartisan legislation gives Congress the facts we need to identify gaps in the availability of Spanish-language materials and make sure these resources are reaching the communities they are intended to serve.”— Congressman Jim Costa (D-CA-21)

“Small businesses are the backbone of communities across the Central Valley, and every entrepreneur should be able to access the information and resources they need to succeed—no matter what language they speak. In the past, the Small Business Administration has provided some resources in multiple languages, but many of those translations have now been removed altogether. With over 74% of CA-22’s population identifying as Hispanic, there are countless native Spanish-speaking small business owners who rely on accessible information to start, grow, and sustain their businesses. I’m proud to support the bipartisan SBA Spanish Resource Report Act to ensure Congress has the information necessary to understand whether these entrepreneurs have meaningful access to the resources they need to succeed.” — Congressman David Valadao (R-CA-22)

The SBA Spanish Resource Report Act requires the SBA Administrator to provide Congress with a one-time report within 180 days detailing existing Spanish-language resources and services offered through SBA programs. The report must also be made publicly available on the SBA’s website.

Specifically, the report would examine Spanish-language websites, application materials, guidance documents, outreach materials, and customer service resources. It would also review resources available through SBA partners, including Small Business Development Centers, Women’s Business Centers, SCORE chapters, and Veteran Business Outreach Centers.

Where data is available, SBA would also report on how these resources are being used, geographic trends, associated translation and administrative costs, operational considerations, and recommendations for efficiently administering existing Spanish-language services.

Importantly, the bill does not require the SBA to create, expand, reduce, or eliminate any Spanish-language resource or service. Instead, it gives Congress greater transparency into what already exists so lawmakers can make informed decisions based on facts.

Background

In December 2025, SBA removed certain Spanish-language materials from its website, raising concerns about the availability of information for Spanish-speaking entrepreneurs. SBA has continued to provide some Spanish-language resources and services.

Hispanic-owned businesses are an important part of America’s small-business economy. The bipartisan SBA Spanish Resource Report Act seeks to establish a clear, public accounting of the resources SBA currently provides and ensure Congress has the information necessary to conduct effective oversight.

The legislation also requires the SBA Administrator to brief the House and Senate Small Business Committees within 30 days after submitting the report.

Read the full text of the SBA Spanish Resource Report Act here.

title: Rep. Crank Calls on DOJ to Investigate Violent Denver ICE Walk Outs
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. -- Representative Jeff Crank (CO-05) sent a letter to the Department of Justice’s (DOJ) Civil Rights Division requesting an investigation into recent student anti-ICE walkouts in Colorado and involvement from outside organizations.

On Friday, September 4, 2026, videos and reporting showed that student walkouts in Denver, Colorado, turned violent, with assaults on journalists and counterprotests. These incidents have raised serious questions about whether participants were unlawfully prevented from exercising their own constitutional rights.

The growing presence and influence of groups that support defunding federal and state law enforcement and interfere with the enforcement of immigration laws threaten the foundation of American society. The student organization, Colorado Youth Coalition, organized the “Walk Out for ICE Out,” and has aligned itself with the messaging from these outside organizations. The event gained significant traction through social media, leading to a reported 200 high schools participating in the walkout.

Reports from the Denver Police Department detailed at least five assaults at the Denver demonstration, and three people were transported to the hospital. Additionally, multiple constituents of Colorado’s Fifth Congressional District who were present at the park were physically assaulted and sustained injuries.

Due to the nature of the Denver incident, Representative Crank is requesting the DOJ to investigate whetherthese violent assaults infringed on other constitutional rights and the degree to which outside organizationsassisted in supporting the demonstrations where attacks on journalists and others occurred.

Excerpts from the letter read:

The Constitution protects peaceful assembly, but those protections do not extend to violent conduct. For that reason, I believe a federal investigation is warranted, not only to determine whether individuals unlawfully infringed upon the constitutional rights of journalists, counterprotesters, or other members of the public with acts of assault, but also to determine the extent to which outside organizations participated in organizing, funding, or otherwise influencing the violent demonstrations.

…

Given the scale of the statewide mobilization and the violence that occurred at the Denver demonstration, I believe the DOJ should examine not only the individual incidents but also the extent of participation by outside organizations in the walkout. This should include determining what role outside organizations played in supporting the demonstrations, whether organizers provided guidance on conduct, and whether any individuals or organizations encouraged or facilitated violent conduct that resulted in violations of the civil rights of journalists, counterprotesters, or other members of the public.

I therefore respectfully request that the DOJ review the events of September 4, including available video footage, police reports, witness accounts, and communications from the organizations involved, to determine whether further investigation or federal action is warranted. Thank you for your attention and consideration of this request. If you or your staff have any additional questions, please don’t hesitate to contact my office.

title: Davids Secures Major Federal Award to Recruit, Support Kansas Teachers
text:
Today, U.S. Representative Sharice Davids announced that she secured $8.3 million for the Kansas State Department of Education through the U.S. Department of Education’s Teacher and School Leader Incentive Program (TSL). The program strengthens teacher and school leader recruitment, retention, professional development, and leadership opportunities across the country.

“I went to Kansas public schools and became a first-generation college student, so I know firsthand how much a good teacher and a strong education can change a student’s trajectory,” said Davids. “This new investment will help Kansas continue to build the kind of schools where students can thrive by supporting the teachers and school leaders who show up for our kids every day.”

The TSL program helps schools recruit and keep quality teachers and school leaders. The funding can help schools provide teachers with additional training and coaching, create opportunities for experienced teachers to take on leadership roles, and offer incentives for educators who take on more responsibility. The program also helps schools attract and keep strong educators in low-income and rural communities where they are needed most.

A U.S. Department of Education evaluation of the program’s predecessor found that performance-based incentives led to student achievement gains equivalent to roughly three to four additional weeks of learning. The TSL program has since funded 160 projects serving more than 2,000 schools in 36 states and Washington, D.C.

Last year, Davids spoke out against the Trump Administration’s plan to dismantle the U.S. Department of Education, warning that eliminating the department could put critical education funding and services at risk for students, teachers, and families. She has continued pushing for federal investments that support Kansas classrooms, including securing funding for early education, STEM programs, and apprenticeships.

This award includes $2,903,167 in base funding and $5,483,666 in additional frontloaded funding, bringing the total FY 2026 award to more than $8.3 million. The FY 2026 TSL program is expected to provide approximately $60 million nationwide through competitive grants to eligible state agencies, school districts, and other organizations.

title: Deluzio Highlights $25,000 Investment in Job Training Opportunities for Beaver County Youth
text:
CENTER TOWNSHIP, PA — Today, Congressman Deluzio announced that Beaver County is receiving $25,000 in federal funding to invest in educational and job opportunities for Beaver County youth. The Appalachian Regional Commission (ARC) awarded the funding to Flourish Beaver County to develop a three-year strategic plan for these opportunities.

“Young people throughout Western PA should have every tool at their disposal to get a good education, find a solid job, build their lives, and earn their own slice of the American Dream,” said Congressman Deluzio. “This federal funding is a win for Beaver County youth, and I look forward to seeing all that Flourish Beaver County will do with it.”

“This investment from the Appalachian Regional Commission will help Flourish build the organizational capacity needed to keep young people at the center of our work,” said Jennifer Marino, CEO of Flourish Beaver County. “With a stronger, more sustainable foundation, we can expand our ability to bring school districts, higher education, employers, and community partners together to help Beaver County youth discover their strengths, explore future careers, and access the education and training that can help them thrive. We are grateful to Congressman Deluzio and his team for supporting this work.”

The Appalachian Regional Commission’s READY Appalachia Grant Program awarded the funding to Flourish Beaver County—a nonprofit that invests in support opportunities for Beaver County youth. The initiative helps Appalachian communities, organizations, and individuals obtain the skills, knowledge, and resources necessary to strengthen their local economies

The Trump Administration’s efforts to freeze funding and pause federal grants has created significant uncertainty for grantees, varying by agency and program. As of now, courts have paused many of these freezes. However, Congressman Deluzio’s office will continue to monitor these developments and fight to make sure this congressionally-authorized funding continues going to projects that make life better for Western Pennsylvanians. If you are the recipient of a federal grant and have been notified that this funding is no longer available to you or are experiencing other issues accessing your lawfully appropriated funds, please share your concerns with Congressman Deluzio’s office at PA17Grants@mail.house.gov.
