title: Congresswoman Nancy Mace Issues Statement on One Year Anniversary of Charlie Kirk’s Assassination
text:
CHARLESTON, S.C., (Sept. 10, 2026) – Today, Congresswoman Nancy Mace issued the following statement on the one-year anniversary of the tragic assassination of Charlie Kirk:

"A year ago today, Charlie Kirk was brutally assassinated for doing what he loved: standing up for his faith, his country, and the principles he believed were worth defending.

"Charlie never backed down. He showed up campus after campus, crowd after crowd, and had the hard conversations others were too afraid to have. He understood something many have forgotten: if we want to save this country, we cannot be afraid to speak the truth.

“He was a man of deep faith who dedicated his life to spreading the word of God and fighting for a better America. Above all, he was a devoted husband, a loving father, and a man who lived his faith every day.

"His life was cut far too short, but his mission was not. We owe it to Charlie, his family, and this country to keep going. Speak the truth. Stand for what is right. Never let fear silence us.

"Rest in peace, Charlie. Your legacy will live on."

###

title: MALLIOTAKIS URGES THOSE IN NEED OF 9/11 HEALTH BENEFITS, VICTIMS COMPENSATION FUND TO REACH OUT
text:
STATEN ISLAND, N.Y. — As the nation approaches the 25th anniversary of the September 11 terrorist attacks, Congresswoman Nicole Malliotakis is urging 9/11 responders, survivors, victims’ families and others eligible for assistance through the September 11th Victim Compensation Fund (VCF) or the World Trade Center Health Program (WTCHP) and who are experiencing difficulties with their claims to contact her office for help.

"25 years after the worst terror attack on American soil, we must continue to stand with our first responders and 9/11 community, — not just on September 11, but every day,” said Congresswoman Malliotakis. "We have had success helping constituents cut through bureaucratic red tape, appeal claims, and expedite benefits they have earned. Our office will continue doing everything we can to ensure the heroes, survivors and families of 9/11 are never forgotten and receive the support they deserve."

The VCF provides financial assistance to eligible individuals who suffered physical harm or developed illnesses as a result of the September 11 attacks and their aftermath. The WTCHP provides medical monitoring and treatment at no cost to eligible responders and survivors who have 9/11 related health conditions. Navigating the claims process can be complicated, especially for those facing serious illnesses, extensive documentation requirements, or delays. Congresswoman Malliotakis’ office has helped constituents navigate these challenges and work with federal agencies to resolve their cases.

Examples of cases in which the Congresswoman’s office has provided assistance include:

1. Appeal Approved — A former first responder who worked in the World Trade Center area was denied benefits through the World Trade Center Health Program due to an administrative error. After filing an appeal and waiting nearly a year without a resolution, the constituent contacted our office. We worked to address the issue and help move the appeal forward. The appeal was ultimately approved, allowing the constituent to receive the health benefits they were entitled to.

2. Significant VCF Award — A constituent reached out to our office after experiencing significant delays in receiving a 9/11 Victim Compensation Fund award following the death of a family member. The claim had remained unresolved for an extended period due to outstanding documentation and administrative requirements. Our office worked with the appropriate agencies and the VCF to help resolve the remaining issues and expedite the claim, allowing the family to receive the full award.

3. Significant VCF Award — A constituent who had worked in the World Trade Center area reached out after struggling to resolve a 9/11 Victim Compensation Fund claim following a serious 9/11 related illness. The delay placed additional financial strain on the constituent and their family during a difficult period. Our office worked with the VCF to address the outstanding issues and help move the claim forward. The constituent ultimately received a significant compensation award.

4. Estate Award — A constituent reached out after a 9/11 related estate award became delayed during the required legal review. Although the Victim Compensation Fund award had already been determined, the family was unable to access the funds until the necessary court process was completed. Our office worked with the appropriate parties to help move the matter forward and resolve the outstanding requirements. The necessary approval was ultimately secured, allowing the estate to receive the award and bringing the matter to a close.

5. Significant VCF Award — A constituent reached out after experiencing significant delays in receiving a 9/11 Victim Compensation Fund award following the death of a parent. The family was facing significant financial hardship and needed the claim resolved as quickly as possible. Our office worked with the VCF and the appropriate parties to address the remaining requirements and expedite the process. After repeated follow-up, the necessary approval was secured, allowing the constituent to receive the full award.

title: Rep. Miller Introduces Bill to Rename VA Clinic in Honor of Ohio Korean War Veteran
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. September 1, 2026 — U.S. Representative Max Miller (R-OH-07) introduced legislation today to name the Department of Veterans Affairs Community-Based Outpatient Clinic in Medina County the “Leland John Codding VA Clinic,” honoring a Korean War veteran and lifelong public servant.

“Leland Codding has dedicated his life to serving our country, our veterans, and the people of Medina County,” said Congressman Max Miller. “From his service during the Korean War to his work establishing the Ohio Western Reserve National Cemetery and his decades of service in public safety, Leland embodies duty, sacrifice, and commitment to community. Naming this clinic in his honor is a fitting tribute to a man who has spent his life honoring those who served.”

Codding served in the U.S. Army’s 89th Airborne Artillery Battalion from 1951 to 1952 during the Korean War. He later became an avid volunteer for the Ohio Western Reserve National Cemetery, working alongside fellow veteran Ralph Waite to secure its establishment in Medina County.

Codding also dedicated decades to public safety, joining the Medina Fire Department in 1959 and becoming the city’s first full-time Fire Chief in 1988. He has been a member of American Legion Post 202 since 1957 and has dedicated more than 5,500 hours to the Honor Guard at the Ohio Western Reserve National Cemetery.

The legislation would designate the VA Community-Based Outpatient Clinic at 6374 Alder Lane in Medina, Ohio, as the “Leland John Codding Department of Veterans Affairs Clinic,” recognizing more than 70 years of service to his country, fellow veterans, and community.

“Growing up, when someone would ask me who was my hero, I would always say My Dad. He was and still is my Hero. I never heard him tell someone that he wouldn’t or couldn’t help, not once. He helped neighbors, friends, strangers, and his hometown people, as well as those in other states. He taught us that we are here to serve others and make a difference and he has certainly done that. He has made an impact in our community, and I am so proud to say that he is my Dad. To have the VA Clinic named after him would be an honor that he would not have expected nor would have ever asked for. He is humble but so deserving of being honored for his contributions throughout his life. “It’s unbelievable. I just want him to be honored for all he has done for others just out of love for his fellow man, not expecting anything in return. He is one of a kind in my eyes.” –Sue Boggs, Daughter of Leland John Codding, Firefighter 7 Veterans Advocate

“Naming the new Veterans outpatient clinic after my dad would be a lasting tribute to a man who dedicated his life to helping others. He belonged to so many public safety and veterans’ organizations that our family probably forgot some of them. I remember two instances where he saved fellow first responders. The first one was in the late 1960’s when there was a horrible 4th of July storm. He was on the Ohio State Patrol Auxiliary riding with a Trooper when they were trying to get people out of a flooded area. The Trooper got caught in the current and my dad was able to help him get out. The second time I was home on leave from the Navy and the Medina Fire Department was battling a major fire at the Plasticote paint factory. One of his fellow fire fighters slipped in the burning paint and my dad dragged him out. One last thing. My first job was at the Medina Theater. When I applied for the job with the owner Mr. Petrigala, I told him my name he asked if Leland was my father. I said yes and I remember to this day he said, ” If you’re half the man your father is your hired.” – Larry Codding, Son of Leland John Codding

“Well to me, his son Steve, he is a man who knows no boundaries. He was born at a time when Country and Community meant everything. I will not list all the things he did or organizations he belonged to but here are a couple of things you might not know about him. He used to dive for golf balls at County golf courses to buy diving equipment so that he and a fellow Firefighter could become certified divers. They did this so they could dive for drowning victims because at that time, the County didn’t have any dive teams. The diving equipment eventually was kept and donated to Medina Fire Department. For years and years, he would hook up the speaker system at Spring Grove cemetery for Memorial Day when he was Co-owner of Medina Radio and TV. Also, Medina Radio and TV sponsored and had phone banks at the shop, Medina Radio and TV, for the Jerry Lewis Telethon. He would give up Holidays to ride shotgun as an Auxiliary Ohio State Patrolman. Growing up in Medina, just about everyone knew my dad or the Codding family. To say I’m proud of my father is an understatement, he is one of a kind! He deserves having the Veterans Affairs Outpatient Clinic named in his honor. Being Past Commander of the American Legion in Medina, being instrumental in getting the National Cemetery in the County, being part of the Honor Guard year after year the list goes on and on. I know if he could, he would still be serving the Veterans and the community.” – Steven L. Codding, Son of Leland John Codding

“Federal facilities in America’s communities have a greater impact when they are named for someone who has had a lasting impact on that community. The naming of the VA Community Based Outpatient Clinic (CBOC) in Medina County after Leland Codding will show that our government can reach out to the communities it serves in a special way.”- David Taylor, Colonel US Army Special Forces, Retired

Behind this site stands the Ralph Waite Elementary School, named in honor of Ralph Waite a WWII veteran and a dear friend of Leland Codding. Together, these two men were instrumental in bringing the Ohio Western Reserve National Cemetery to Medina County. Leland and Ralph shared a rare ability: when it came to serving veterans in Medina County and across the State of Ohio, no obstacle was too large. Their partnership, their persistence, and their unwavering commitment shaped the veteran landscape we rely on today. It is most fitting that this new VA CBOC be named after Leland Codding, allowing these two extraordinary advocates to stand beside one another in our community once again one memorialized through the school behind this site, and the other through the clinic that will serve generations of veterans to come. Ed Zackery 1SG, U.S. Army (retired) Director, Medina County Veterans Service Office I am in full support of naming the new Medina VA Clinic in honor of Leland Codding. I worked side by side with Fire Chief Codding as I was in command positions at the Medina Police Department to better serve our residents effectively and efficiently by working collaboratively on fire scenes. Leland was also very involved in local American Legion and would march as Color Guard directly behind me in lead car for the annual Memorial Day parade! He was a dedicated and committed public servant very deserving of this honor!” –Dennis Hanwell, Former Medina Chief of Police and City of Medina Mayor, Retired

title: Rep. McCormick and Chairman Babin Seek Information on Federal Biotechnology Research and Security
text:
Washington, D.C. - House Science, Space, and Technology Committee Chairman Brian Babin and Investigations and Oversight Subcommittee Chairman Rich McCormick sent letters to U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) Secretary Chris Wright, National Institutes of Health (NIH) Director Jay Bhattacharya, and National Science Foundation (NSF) Acting Director Brian Stone requesting information on how their agencies are advancing U.S. leadership in biotechnology research while protecting against biosecurity and research security risks.

In the letters, the Chairmen highlight the growing importance of biotechnology to U.S. economic competitiveness, scientific leadership, national security, healthcare, agriculture, energy, and manufacturing. They also emphasize that rapid advances in biotechnology—including synthetic biology, gene editing, DNA synthesis, automated laboratory technologies, and the convergence of biotechnology and artificial intelligence—present significant opportunities as well as emerging security risks.

“The United States must lead in this area of research to support economic growth and societal benefit while strengthening safeguards against harm caused by negligent or malicious actors,” the Chairmen wrote.

The letters also highlight the National Security Commission on Emerging Biotechnology’s April 2025 report, which concluded that “biotechnology will be a defining strategic technology of the twenty-first century” and warned that the United States risks falling behind global competitors without a coordinated national strategy. The report identified biotechnology as critical to economic competitiveness, national defense, public health, agriculture, energy, and industrial production.

The Chairmen commend the Administration's leadership in this area, including President Trump’s May 5, 2025, Executive Order on Improving the Safety and Security of Biological Research.

As part of their oversight, the Chairmen ask the agencies to identify any significant gaps, vulnerabilities, or emerging threats related to biotechnology; explain whether they have implemented recommendations from the National Security Commission on Emerging Biotechnology; and identify any additional authorities, resources, statutory changes, or policy tools needed to strengthen U.S. biotechnology leadership while protecting national security and biosecurity.

The letters underscore the Committee's interest in ensuring that the United States remains a leader in biotechnology research and innovation while maintaining appropriate safeguards against the misuse of emerging biological capabilities.

title: Congressman Menefee Urges Texans to Check Registration Amid Voter Suspense List Status
text:
HOUSTON, TX — Congressman Christian D. Menefee (TX-18) is urging Texans to check their voter registration and make sure their addresses are up to date ahead of the October 5 registration deadline for the November 3, 2026, election.

Roughly 1.2 million Texans are currently on the voter suspense list, including approximately 300,000 Harris County residents whose addresses could not be verified. Being on the suspense list does not mean a voter has lost their right to vote, but it may mean completing additional paperwork, including a Statement of Residence, when casting a ballot.

With the registration deadline approaching, Menefee is encouraging Texans to take a few minutes now to check their status and address any issues before Election Day.

“I represent the district of Barbara Jordan and Mickey Leland, and generations of Texans fought hard for the right to vote. We should never take that right for granted,” said Rep. Menefee. “My own grandfather had to pay a poll tax just to cast his ballot. A generation later, his grandson gets to serve in the United States Congress. I carry that history with me every day, and it’s why I want to make sure every eligible Texan knows their rights and is ready to make their voice heard.”

The deadline to register to vote or update an address for the November 3 election is October 5, 2026.

“It only takes a few minutes to check your registration, so I’m asking Texans to do it now instead of waiting until Election Day,” Rep. Menefee said. “Regardless of how you vote, your voice matters. We owe it to the generations who fought before us to make sure our voices are heard at the ballot box.”

For voter registration and election information, visit VoteTexas.gov.

title: Moylan Pushes to Restore De Minimis Exemption, Address Guam-Bound Mail Delays
text:
(Hagåtña, Guam) — Congressman Moylan met with U.S. Postal Service officials to address new customs and tariff requirements following changes to the de minimis exemption, as well as ongoing delays involving Guam-bound mail.

Moylan raised concerns with USPS Government Liaison Director Jennifer Selde over the additional costs and steps residents now face when sending goods from Guam to the mainland. Under the new federal requirements, packages containing goods must go through an additional customs process before they can be mailed. The requirements do not apply to ordinary letters or documents.

For affected packages, residents are now required to complete the customs process through Zonos, an online platform where they provide information about the items being mailed and pay any applicable duties. Zonos then provides the QR code needed to mail the package through USPS.

The new process has has become burdensome for Guam residents mailing goods to the mainland, prompting concerns over how the changes are affecting an island community that relies heavily on the Postal Service.

“These changes are creating additional costs and complications for people simply trying to mail goods from Guam to the mainland,” Moylan said. “We are raising those concerns at the federal level while also working to make the requirements easier for our residents to navigate.”

Moylan has taken these issues directly to U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer. The Congressman asked Greer to reinstate the de minimis exemption for Guam and urged USTR to consider Guam’s unique status as a U.S. territory under the new tariff rules. Restoring the exemption would remove the new tariffs on qualifying goods mailed from Guam to the mainland.

In his meeting with USPS, Moylan asked for clearer guidance and greater support for residents navigating Zonos. He specifically requested that the Postal Service explore providing a Zonos kiosk or similar service at Guam post offices, giving residents without smartphones or reliable internet access an alternative way to complete the required steps.

The Congressman also raised reports of Guam-bound packages experiencing extended delays, including mail being held at USPS processing facilities in Oakland, California. He emphasized that unreliable mail service can have serious consequences for residents who depend on USPS for medications, passports, important documents, and other essential items.

title: Mrvan Requests Federal Investigation into NWI Power Outages
text:
Washington, DC – Today, Rep. Frank J. Mrvan sent a letter to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) requesting an investigation into the power outages following the derecho that struck Northwest Indiana on August 11, 2026.

The text of the letter is below and a pdf is available here.

“I write to request that the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC), in coordination with the North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC), conduct a comprehensive federal review of the widespread and prolonged power outages that followed the severe weather event, a derecho, that struck Northwest Indiana on August 11, 2026.

“The derecho brought extraordinary straight-line winds across Northern Indiana, with peak wind gusts reaching approximately 100 to 110 miles per hour across portions of Lake and Porter Counties. The storm caused unprecedented damage and resulted in nearly 375,000 customer outages within Northern Indiana Public Service Company’s (NIPSCO) service territory. Tens of thousands of Northwest Indiana residents remained without electricity for nearly two weeks. This was the largest outage event in NIPSCO’s history and far exceeded the average duration of electricity interruptions associated with major events. The Cities of Gary, Lake Station, and Portage, as well as the Town of Munster, were among the hardest hit communities and the last areas to receive full restoration.

“The consequences of these prolonged outages were significant. Families lost food, homes experienced flooding and subsequent mold growth, businesses lost inventory and revenue, and residents lost access to essential medical equipment and prescription medications. For many constituents, the lack of electricity also meant the loss of reliable access to phones, computers, internet service, and other means of communicating with family members, reporting outages, and applying for emergency assistance.

“Most concerning, vulnerable residents were left without reliable access to medical care and other essential services. For nearly two weeks, too many Northwest Indiana families were literally left in the dark.

“On August 25, 2026, a federal Major Disaster Declaration was approved for Indiana, providing critical assistance as communities begin the long process of recovery. However, federal assistance must address not only the damage caused by this storm, but also what can be learned from the unprecedented duration of the resulting power outages.

“The Indiana Office of Utility Consumer Counselor has petitioned the Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission (IURC) to investigate NIPSCO’s storm restoration practices, and I strongly support that state-level investigation. At the same time, given the scale of this event, I believe a federal review is warranted.

“I respectfully request a joint FERC-NERC investigation to assess what contributed to the prolonged outages and determine whether NIPSCO’s preparation, system performance, and restoration efforts were consistent with applicable reliability requirements and best practices. I also request that the findings include recommendations to improve electric-grid reliability and storm resilience.

“Specifically, I ask that the investigation examine whether NIPSCO and its parent company, NiSource, complied with FERC-approved federal reliability standards and whether any deficiencies in reliability planning, system resilience, or emergency response warrant additional federal action. The review should evaluate the following factors:

Storm preparedness: The short- and long-term preparations NIPSCO undertook before the August 11 derecho, including emergency response planning, staffing, equipment, mutual-aid arrangements, and pre-positioning of resources.

Grid resilience and system design: The performance and resilience of NIPSCO’s distribution and transmission infrastructure in the face of extreme straight-line winds and increasingly severe weather events.

Vegetation management and maintenance: The adequacy and effectiveness of routine maintenance and vegetation-management practices, particularly considering the significant investments NIPSCO has reported making in these areas.

Restoration performance: The causes of the prolonged restoration timeline, including why certain communities remained without power substantially longer than others and whether restoration priorities, resource allocation, communications, and repair practices were appropriate.

Regional comparison: NIPSCO’s restoration performance compared with other electric utilities in Indiana and the surrounding region that experienced outages from the same weather event.

Infrastructure investments: Whether the substantial investments NIPSCO has made in recent years toward infrastructure replacement, grid modernization, reliability, and vegetation management have produced the adequate levels of resilience.

“This last point deserves particular scrutiny. NIPSCO has emphasized that recent rate increases are necessary to support infrastructure upgrades and improve grid reliability. Since 2016, customers have contributed approximately $2.3 billion toward infrastructure replacement, and $81 million towards vegetation management between 2023 and 2025. Given the magnitude of these investments, Northwest Indiana residents deserve to know why they experienced outages of this magnitude and duration, and whether additional investments, preparation, maintenance, or changes in reliability standards could have reduced the impact on families and businesses.

“I appreciate your consideration of this request and your commitment to ensuring the reliability and resilience of our nation’s electric grid. I also request that FERC coordinate, as appropriate, with the IURC, NIPSCO, state emergency-management officials, and other relevant stakeholders to implement the lessons learned from this event. I stand ready to work together to advance transparency and accountability, strengthen our electric infrastructure, and ensure that Northwest Indiana families and businesses can depend on safe, reliable, and affordable power.”

title: ICYMI: Congressmembers Nikema Williams Announces $700,000 in Federal Support for Community Schoolyards
text:
ATLANTA, G.A. — Congresswoman Nikema Williams (GA-05) announced that Atlanta Public Schools has received $700,000 in congressionally directed spending to support future community schoolyard projects in Atlanta.

Congresswoman Williams joined Atlanta Public Schools and Trust for Public Land leaders to celebrate the new federal investment, which will help transform school grounds into vibrant outdoor spaces that support student learning and recreation while expanding neighborhood access to green space beyond the school day.

Congresswoman Nikema Williams said:

“As a proud APS mama, I know how much it means for our children to have places where they can learn, play, explore and just be kids. These projects aren’t just playgrounds and outdoor spaces. They support outdoor education, build climate resilience, connect us to nature and improve park equity — because all children deserve a safe and accessible place to play, no matter their ZIP code or bank account.”

The Schoolyards Program is a national initiative of Trust for Public Land designed to expand community access to schoolyards during non-school hours and increase the percentage of people who live within a 10-minute walk of a park. In Atlanta, the program is implemented in partnership with APS, other non-profit organizations, and city agencies, with additional support from the philanthropic community.

George Dusenbury, Georgia State Director of Trust for Public Lands said:

“Community schoolyards are one of the smartest ways we can expand access to green space in Atlanta neighborhoods. This federal investment will help Atlanta Public Schools create places that support students during the school day and serve families and neighbors after hours, ensuring more Atlantans have safe, high-quality places to play, learn and gather.”

In Atlanta, 18 percent of residents still do not live within a 10-minute walk of a park. Over the past six years, TPL has worked with 14 Atlanta schools to redesign schoolyards so they can serve as parks during non-school hours. The first campus selected for this phase is Crawford W. Long Middle School in the Glenrose Heights neighborhood of South Atlanta. Additional details on sites and timelines will be announced as planning moves forward.

Dr. Bryan Johnson, APS Superintendent said:

“At Atlanta Public Schools, we know schools are more than buildings; they are spaces where lifelong memories are made. This project allows us to welcome all of our neighbors to create memories, friendships, and strong bonds right here on our schoolyards. By transforming these spaces into vibrant, welcoming places for play, learning, and connection, we are strengthening the relationship between our schools and the communities they serve. We are proud to partner with the Trust for Public Land to create schoolyards that are truly for everyone.”

title: Norcross, Pallone, Camden leaders meet to discuss nationwide lithium battery fires
text:
September 10, 2026: EMR USA CEO Joe Balzano (second from left) gives tour of Camden recycling plant to Rep. Norcross, Rep. Pallone, and Mayor Carstarphen (left to right)

CAMDEN — Congressmen Donald Norcross (NJ-01) and Frank Pallone, Jr. (NJ-06) today met with representatives from EMR’s Camden recycling plant and local elected officials to discuss the nationwide issue of lithium battery fires.

Lithium batteries contain more power and charge faster than other batteries, but those efficiencies can also create a fire hazard if exposed to physical damage or excess heat. While these risks require special disposal processes, many consumers are unaware when they are disposing lithium batteries and recycling facilities are often underequipped to identify them in the waste stream. As such, there are an estimated 5,000 fires at recycling plants in the United States each year, with most being ignited by improperly disposed lithium batteries.

Without action the problem will only continue to grow: Lithium batteries are used in a large amount of modern products such as handheld electronics, e-cigarettes, medical devices, and the total amount of lithium consumption nearly quadrupled between just 2010 and 2021. Municipalities from coast to coast, including Camden, are increasingly being forced to respond to large battery fires.

“Lithium batteries aren’t going away, and communities are struggling to safely recycle them across the world. Reducing these fires will take a team effort, and the producers of these batteries need to play a more active role – especially since they know what happens to these batteries at the end of their lifecycle,” Norcross said. “There’s no one silver bullet solution, but my visit with Congressman Pallone and folks on the frontlines here in Camden certainly helps me feel that more people are taking this issue seriously.”

“Lithium-ion batteries shouldn’t be turning recycling facilities into fire hazards. When these batteries end up where they don’t belong, they can put entire communities at risk. I came to Camden with Congressman Norcross to see the problem firsthand and figure out what we can do in Congress to prevent these fires before they start,” said Pallone, the top Democrat on the House Energy and Commerce Committee, which has jurisdiction over the issue.

“Everyone wants to ensure that fires of this magnitude never occur,” Victor Carstarphen, mayor of Camden said. “I commend Congressman Norcross for looking at potential solutions to this issue and for working with local officials to help safeguard against the threat of a future event. Improving federal regulations and requiring standardized labeling of materials would be a positive step forward.”

“Recyclers everywhere are reckoning with the risks that lithium batteries pose to the waste stream, and no one has more stake in preventing these fires than the hardworking men and women staffing these facilities in their own communities,” Joe Balzano, chief executive officer of EMR USA said. “EMR appreciates the leaders who came to Camden today to see the issue up close – and for elevating the need for solutions about what can be done about this national problem.”

Multiple efforts have been launched this Congress to prevent lithium battery fires. In October, Norcross introduced the Battery Fire Prevention Act, which includes measures to boost recycling facilities’ access to battery detectors and create a lithium battery buyback fund. Earlier this month, the House Energy and Commerce Committee also advanced the Battery Recycling for America’s Competitive Economy (BRACE) Act – legislation that would modernize and clarify regulations and safeguards for lithium battery storage and recycling.

title: Rep. Panetta Secures More Than $3.1 Million  in Bipartisan Infrastructure Law Funding  for Monterey and Marina Airports
text:
Monterey, CA – United States Representative Jimmy Panetta (CA-19) announced that he secured $3,144,720 in federal funding from the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law to support infrastructure improvements at Monterey Regional Airport (MRY) and Marina Municipal Airport (OAR). The grants are being awarded as part of the final installment of the Federal Aviation Administration’s (FAA) Airport Infrastructure Grants program.

Monterey Regional Airport will receive $2,662,833 to support construction of the landside circulation in conjunction with its new 62,754-square-foot replacement terminal, which will have five gates and passenger boarding bridges. The funding will support Phase 9 of the project, consisting of construction of relocated parking and utilities.

Marina Municipal Airport will receive $481,887 to reseal 3,483 feet of Runway 11/29 pavement, extending the useful life of the runway and supporting continued safe airport operations.

“I’m proud to have secured more than $3.1 million in federal funding from the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law to strengthen the aviation infrastructure our communities rely on,” said Rep. Panetta. “This federal investment in our home will continue supporting the development of the new terminal at Monterey Regional Airport while making critical runway improvements at Marina Municipal Airport. These projects will enhance safety, create jobs, strengthen our local aviation infrastructure, and help ensure that our airports can continue connecting residents, visitors, and communities throughout California’s 19th Congressional District.”

“This latest federal investment represents another important step in creating a safer, more efficient, and more welcoming experience at Monterey Regional Airport,” said Chris Morello, MRY Executive Director. “Funding for the relocated landside circulation components will help ensure the infrastructure surrounding our new terminal supports passengers from the moment they arrive. We appreciate Congressman Panetta’s continued partnership and commitment to advancing this transformational project for the Monterey region.”

“Marina Municipal Airport is an important transportation and economic asset for the City of Marina and the greater Monterey Bay region. This $481,887 investment from the Federal Aviation Administration will allow us to rehabilitate Runway 11/29, extend the useful life of this critical infrastructure, and ensure the airport continues to safely support its diverse aviation users. This investment is especially important as Marina Municipal Airport continues to evolve as a hub for innovation and Advanced Air Mobility. With Joby Aviation’s significant presence at the airport and continued investment in the development of next-generation electric aircraft, Marina is helping position the Monterey Bay region at the forefront of the emerging Advanced Air Mobility industry. Maintaining and modernizing our core airport infrastructure is essential as we support both the aviation needs of today and the technologies that will shape the future of aviation. We greatly appreciate Congressman Panetta’s continued advocacy for Marina Municipal Airport and his support for federal investments that strengthen aviation infrastructure, encourage innovation, and create new economic opportunities for our community and region,” said Courtney Lindberg, Assistant City Manager, City of Marina and A.J. Lawson, Airport Manager, City of Marina.

The funding for Monterey Regional Airport builds on Rep. Panetta’s continued efforts to secure federal support for the airport’s replacement terminal. Last month, Rep. Panetta announced an additional $2,368,257 in FAA Airport Improvement Program funding to support inspection activities during construction of the new terminal. With Rep. Panetta’s support, Monterey Regional Airport has been awarded over $135 million in total federal funding for modernization, supporting terminal design, tarmac improvements, and other safety upgrades as part of its safety enhancement program.

The airport’s existing terminal opened in 1950. FAA is requiring that the passenger facilities be relocated to accommodate federally required operational safety enhancements to Taxiway A, which connects to the airport’s primary commercial runway. The replacement terminal is designed to be accessible, easier for passengers to navigate, and responsive to the airport’s growing demand. The design also calls for the terminal to be zero-net-energy ready and incorporate sustainable materials and features that are emblematic of the Monterey region.

The Airport Infrastructure Grants program was established through the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law to provide federal investments for airport planning and development, terminal improvements, baggage system upgrades, runway and taxiway rehabilitation, roadway and access improvements, and other safety-related infrastructure needs.

title: Pappas Fights Back on Trump’s Executive Order Limiting Mail-In Voting
text:
In response to President Donald Trump’s Executive Order 14399 seeking to exert control over mail-in ballots ahead of the 2026 midterm elections, Congressman Chris Pappas (NH-01), co-chair of the Congressional Postal Caucus, led 99 members in calling on the Postmaster General to revoke a Postal Service rule codifying the order. In addition to that, Pappas joined a bipartisan coalition in filing an amicus brief to the Supreme Court of the United States in the matter of United States Postal Service, et al., v. State of California, et al., a lawsuit brought by a coalition of State Attorneys General against the U.S. Postal Service.

One-third of Americans are expected to vote by mail in the upcoming midterm elections—a voting practice Donald Trump himself used as recently as August 2026, when the president voted in Florida’s Republican primary. A 2025 Brookings Institution study found an average of just four cases of voter fraud for every 10 million mail-in ballots cast — and that states using universal mail-in voting have among the lowest fraud rates in the country.

Letter to Postmaster General David P. Steiner:

Congressman Chris Pappas (NH-01), Congresswoman Nikki Budzinski (IL-13), and Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08) led 97 colleagues in calling on Postmaster General David P. Steiner to revoke a Postal Service rule that codifies President Trump's Executive Order targeting vote-by-mail.

“The evidence is clear: voting by mail is safe, effective, and helps to ensure everyone is able to execute their constitutional right to vote. USPS has played an essential role in elections for generations – and it is our fear that this final rule risks harming the democratic process and severely damaging USPS’s relationship with the millions of Americans who rely on USPS to deliver ballots every election cycle,” the members wrote.

The lawmakers warn that if the rule survives legal challenge, it would carry real consequences: disrupting operations for tens of thousands of USPS employees, creating new obstacles for tens of millions of voters who rely on mail-in ballots, and further eroding public trust in the electoral process.

Amicus brief to the Supreme Court of the United States in the matter of United States Postal Service, et al., v. State of California, et al.:

Congressman Pappas joined a court filing challenging the legality of President Donald Trump’s Executive Order 14399. The court case challenges a Final Rule issued by the USPS pursuant to Trump’s directive that imposes unconstitutional and unworkable restrictions on mail-in voting, including requiring states to provide a “citizenship verification list” and attempting to give USPS control over who can vote by mail.

In the court filing, the amici curiae argue that the order violates the separation of powers and usurps congressional authorities outlined in Article I of the U.S. Constitution, which gives the states and Congress exclusive authority over election administration.

“As current and former legislators, amici took an oath to uphold and defend the Constitution of the United States—including its guarantee of the separation of powers. Amici have a particular interest in defending the institutional role of the Legislative Branch under Article I of the Constitution and in vindicating the long-settled principle that the Constitution commits ultimate regulatory authority over federal elections to Congress. The Constitution does not contemplate the Executive Branch acting unilaterally to assert power over federal elections. Yet that is what the Order and Final Rule do,” wrote the lawmakers.

title: Congresswoman Brittany Pettersen Solemnly Marks One Year Since Evergreen High School Shooting
text:
EVERGREEN – Congresswoman Brittany Pettersen (C0-07) today solemnly marked the one year anniversary of the tragic Evergreen High School shooting, introducing a bipartisan congressional resolution signed by all members of the Colorado U.S. House delegation honoring the shooting victims, and expressing gratitude to first responders, law enforcement, educators, faculty, and neighbors who acted swiftly to protect students and staff during last year’s shooting. Senator Michael Bennet (D-CO) is leading a companion resolution in the Senate.

“Today, we honor the students, staff, first responders, families, and entire Evergreen community for their extraordinary resilience in the face of the tragedy after the Evergreen High School shooting one year ago today. Their strength, courage, and resilience continue to inspire all of us but also reminds us of the urgent need for change,” said Congresswoman Brittany Pettersen. “Our country’s gun violence epidemic has shattered countless lives and is now the leading cause of death for our kids - a reality none of us should accept. As a mom, I understand the fear so many parents live with when they drop their kids off at school. Today, we stand with the Evergreen community and promise to keep fighting in Congress to ensure our kids are safe at school and in our communities. They deserve so much better.”

“One year ago today, the Evergreen community experienced an unthinkable act of gun violence,” said Senator Michael Bennet. “The fear and trauma that Evergreen High School students, families, educators, and first responders experienced that day have not disappeared. We owe it to them – and all of Colorado – to act and to build a future where no child has to experience this kind of violence at school. I am glad to lead the Colorado Congressional Delegation in this resolution, and will continue to fight against senseless acts of gun violence.”

"It is unacceptable that gun violence has become normal in America. A year ago, Coloradans experienced another tragic school shooting, this time at Evergreen High School, which left two students injured and an entire community traumatized. I'm proud to join my colleagues in recognizing the brave first responders and Evergreen’s resilient survivors and residents, but more must be done. Congressional action to stop gun violence is long overdue—it's past time we pass legislation to protect our kids. Enough is enough," said Congresswoman Diana DeGette (CO-01).

“A year later, our hearts remain with the people of Jefferson County as they continue to heal from the tragic shooting at Evergreen High School. No parent should ever have to receive the kind of call that far too many parents in our country have received—and no child should have to be marched out of their classroom, hide under their desk, or fear gunshots in their school. Enough is enough. We must stand together against senseless acts of gun violence,” said Congressman Joe Neguse (CO-02)

“One year after the tragic shooting at Evergreen High School, our heart is with the students, families, and first responders who faced unimaginable horror that day. As a combat veteran and father of two kids, I refuse to accept that our classrooms should function like war zones. We can honor the resilience of the Evergreen community not just with our thoughts, but by elected officials of both parties acting to pass common-sense gun safety laws to protect our children, communities, and Colorado,” said Congressman Jason Crow (CO-06)

“I continue to pray that God strengthens Evergreen High School and the Jefferson County community. I am honored to join my colleagues on the bipartisan memorial resolution and to keep working with them to direct federal dollars toward more School Resource Officers so we can protect our children against evil acts. My heart remains with everyone in Evergreen.” said Congresswoman Lauren Boebert (CO-04).

“As a father of five, I cannot imagine the fear and heartbreak the Evergreen community experienced that day. One year later, we remember the victims, stand with the students, families, and educators who still carry the weight of what happened, and recognize the first responders who ran toward danger to protect others. I’m proud to join Congresswoman Pettersen and my colleagues in the Colorado delegation in honoring the strength and resilience Evergreen has shown over the past year,” said Congressman Jeff Hurd (CO-03)

"One year ago, the Evergreen community lived through something no community should. We pray God continues to give them comfort, and we thank the deputies and teachers who ran toward danger and saved lives,” said Congressman Jeff Crank (CO-05)

"Today, we remember the students, their families, and an entire community that continues to heal from the horrific act of violence that took place just one year ago at Evergreen High School. We also honor the first responders, law enforcement officers, educators, health care workers, and neighbors who acted without hesitation to protect students and save lives. As a father and former police officer, I’m proud to join the Colorado delegation in making sure their courage is remembered and that the Evergreen community knows Colorado continues to stand with them,” said Congressman Gabe Evans (CO-08)

Specifically, the resolution honors the two victims who were wounded, and recognizes the lasting trauma carried by students, staff, families, and the broader community. It also pays tribute to the first responders, law enforcement officers, educators, school staff, neighbors, and hospital workers who stepped up with courage and compassion in the aftermath.

See the full text of the resolution here.

This resolution comes after, earlier this year, Congresswoman Pettersen introduced three pieces of legislation responding to the tragedy at Evergreen High School last year:

The Evergreen Community Safety Act which requires social media companies to respond to warrants and subpoena requests regarding potential threats of violence within 72 hours.

Bill text is available HERE.

The Community Firearm Safety Act, which creates a permissible use under the Byrne Justice Assistance Grant Program within the Department of Justice (DOJ) to allow grants for localities to procure and distribute safe firearm storage boxes to community members.

Bill text is available HERE.

The Community Risk Training and Response Act, which creates a grant program through the Office of the Attorney General for up to $500,000 for localities to provide technical assistance and training to law enforcement, prosecutors, judges and court staff, healthcare providers, educators, and agencies designated to coordinate Extreme Risk Order Implementation and to develop standardized extreme risk protection order training and curriculum nationwide.

Bill text is available HERE.

Since the Columbine tragedy in 1999, more than 390,000 students in the United States have experienced gun violence at school, killing at least 203 and injuring 441 students, educators, and other individuals on K-12 campuses. Colorado has been touched by gun violence before, with spaces of community such as schools, movie theaters, night clubs, and houses of worship affected.

title: BREAKING: Pressley Leads Nearly 60 Lawmakers Demanding Investigation into Black People Found Hanging, Invokes Legacy of Lynching in America
text:
Letter Comes Amidst Alarming Spike in Possible Modern-Day Lynchings

“Inaction by the federal government is tantamount to complicity. This is part of the legacy of racial terror in the United States, and this neglect has long-term consequences.”

Text of Letter (PDF)

BOSTON – Today, Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley (MA-07) led 59 colleagues in writing to the Department of Justice (DOJ) and Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) demanding a thorough, transparent, and comprehensive federal investigation into the numerous incidents of Black people found hanging across the country. The Congresswoman’s letter follows a series of deaths which raise suspicion of foul play given the role of lynching in American history.

The growing number of Black people found hanging in public is a national crisis. A recent report documented more than 70 modern-day lynchings in the United States between 2000 and 2025. In 2026 alone, there have already been at least 10 reported hangings of Black people. They were as young as 18 years old and lived in different parts of the country, including Mississippi, Michigan, and New York. Many families have publicly questioned the conclusions of local and state investigations.

“Inaction by the federal government is tantamount to complicity. This is part of the legacy of racial terror in the United States, and this neglect has long-term consequences,” the lawmakers continued. “Not only are innocent lives lost, but lynching inflicts deep traumatic and psychological wounds on family members, neighbors, and the entire Black community.”

“Congress enacted the Emmett Till Antilynching Act in 2022 to ensure the DOJ and FBI are empowered to fully investigate suspicious deaths and hold individuals accountable,” the lawmakers continued. “It is incumbent upon you to do just that.”

This letter demands a thorough, transparent, and comprehensive federal investigation into every hanging death of a Black individual across the United States. At a minimum, each investigation, with permission of the decedents’ families, should include an independent autopsy, an audit of local and state law enforcement investigations, review of physical and testimonial evidence, and a final report submitted to Congress explaining the agency’s findings. The letter also calls for robust data collection that tracks the hanging deaths of Black people in a transparent and systematic manner.

Joining Congresswoman Pressley in sending the letter are Representatives Alma Adams, Yassamin Ansari, Becca Balint, Nanette Diaz Barragán, Joyce Beatty, Wesley Bell, Sanford Bishop, Everton Blair, Brendan Boyle, Shontel Brown, Janelle Bynum, André Carson, Troy Carter, Yvette Clarke, Jasmine Crockett, Mark DeSaulnier, Sarah Elfreth, Jesús “Chuy” García, Sylvia García, Jimmy Gomez, Al Green, Adelita Grijalva, Jahana Hayes, Glenn Ivey, Jonathan Jackson, Henry C. “Hank” Johnson, Sydney Kamlager-Dove, Robin Kelly, Ro Khanna, Raja Krishnamoorthi, Summer Lee, Jennifer McClellan, LaMonica McIver, Gregory Meeks, Analilia Mejía, Christian Menefee, Kweisi Mfume, Eleanor Holmes Norton, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Frank Pallone Jr., Mark Pocan, Stacey Plaskett, Delia Ramírez, Terri Sewell, Lateefah Simon, Haley Stevens, Marilyn Strickland, Shri Thanedar, Bennie Thompson, Rashida Tlaib, Ritchie Torres, Lauren Underwood, Nydia M. Velázquez, Debbie Wasserman Schultz, Maxine Waters, Bonnie Watson Coleman, Nikema Williams, and Frederica Wilson.

Full text of the letter is available here.

title: Congressman Riley M. Moore Presents $1 Million for Watson Fire Station Renovation
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, Congressman Riley M. Moore presented a $1 million check to City of Fairmont officials in support of Fairmont’s renovation of the Watson Fire Station.

Congressman Riley M. Moore released the following statement:

“Fairmont’s first responders put their lives on the line every day to protect their neighbors. They deserve a facility that ensures they have the tools and resources necessary to do their jobs safely and effectively. I’m proud to have secured this $1 million in federal funding through my work on the House Appropriations Committee to help modernize the Watson Fire Station and ensure Fairmont’s firefighters and EMS personnel have a safe, efficient, and mission-ready facility for years to come.”

The Watson Fire Station has provided essential fire and EMS services to the Watson neighborhood, Fairmont State University, and the Fairmont Technology Park for nearly 50 years. However, the aging facility no longer meets the operational needs of the Fairmont Fire Department or the growing needs of the surrounding community.

The funding will help the City of Fairmont transform the outdated station into a modern, mission-ready facility. Planned improvements include converting the original apparatus bay into sleeping and living quarters and constructing a new, energy-efficient apparatus bay to house fire vehicles, turnout gear, SCBA equipment, a hose washer and dryer, and other essential infrastructure. The upgrades will improve response capabilities, support staffing needs, ensure compliance with current codes, and allow the department to expand technical rescue and EMS services.

The project represents a significant investment in Fairmont’s public safety infrastructure and will help ensure the Fairmont Fire Department is equipped to continue providing critical services to the community for decades to come.

title: SCHNEIDER JOINS BIPARTISAN GROUP OF OVER 250 CURRENT AND FORMER MEMBERS OF CONGRESS URGING THE SUPREME COURT TO BLOCK TRUMP’S EXECUTIVE ORDER LIMITING VOTING BY MAIL
text:
LINCOLNSHIRE, IL – Congressman Brad Schneider (IL-10) joined a bipartisan group of over 250 current and former Members of Congress in urging the Supreme Court to block President Trump’s executive order that would require states to provide a citizenship verification list to the Department of Homeland Security and give the Postal Service control over who can vote by mail. Millions of Americans utilize mail-in voting including deployed service members, seniors, and disabled Americans. Trump himself voted by mail last month.

“The right to vote is a critical pillar of our democracy,” said Schneider. “Every single American deserves the opportunity to cast their ballot how they wish – whether that is in-person or by mail. This executive order is a blatant attempt to sow doubt in the integrity of our elections and disenfranchise eligible voters.

“Trump’s continued attacks on mail-in voting are un-American and anti-democratic. I’m glad to join a bipartisan group of over 250 current and former lawmakers to urge the Court to stand up for the right to vote and stand against any and all attacks that undermine this sacred right,” Schneider concluded. “We will continue fighting to protect free and fair elections for everyone.”

title: Peters Statement on Reported ICE Activity Near San Diego Schools
text:
San Diego, CA — Today, Representative Scott Peters (CA-50) released the following statement after San Diego Unified School District (SDUSD) and San Diego City College both informed the Congressman's office of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) arrest activity outside their schools within the past week:

"I am deeply troubled by reports that students and parents were detained without warning while trying to attend classes or bring kids to school. Schools are supposed to be a safe place for young people to learn. Yet this Administration exploits the places we trust most—schools, childcare facilities, hospitals, courthouses, and places of worship. President Trump has turned these places into hunting grounds.

“ICE isn’t going after the 'worst of the worst,' as President Trump promised. We saw this at Buona Forchetta, when ICE agents threw the owner against a wall, handcuffed employees, and used flash-bang grenades on bystanders. These people weren't drug lords or violent criminals; they were workers trying to make a living.

“Parents and children should not have to worry about ICE agents waiting outside a classroom or a doctor's office. That's why I led introduction of the Protecting Sensitive Locations Act, which would bar immigration enforcement within 1,000 feet of schools, hospitals, and churches except in true emergencies. I will also continue working with SDUSD and City College to make sure San Diegans have the resources they need to stay informed and protected.

"Until ICE operates responsibly and reasonably to target dangerous criminals instead of hardworking families, I will push for real reforms from ICE and hold them accountable for the fear they have inflicted on my constituents and communities across the country. I urge all state and local elected officials to express their support for the Protecting Sensitive Locations Act and my Stop Excessive Force in Immigration Act so we can deliver commonsense reforms that keep our communities safe."

Background:

Last year, Rep. Peters led the Stop Excessive Force in Immigration Act, a bill to make our communities safer by establishing a stronger standard for Federal immigration agents' use of force. The bill would also restrict use of crowd munitions like tear gas and create greater transparency in enforcement by requiring the use of body cameras and strictly limiting the use of masks. Rep. Peters has pushed Congress to pass these common sense reforms, but they have been blocked by the Republican majority.

title: Congressman Brad Sherman Statement on the North Korea Travel Ban
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. -- Congressman Brad Sherman (CA-32), senior member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, issued the following statement:

“To the dismay of many Korean Americans, Secretary Rubio recently renewed the ban on U.S. citizen travel to North Korea for the 10th consecutive year. About 100,000 Korean Americans still hope to have family reunification meetings with aging relatives in North Korea, and the ban makes it impossible for them to do so. It is time for the State Department to revise its policy so that Korean Americans can have the opportunity to attend funerals or burials in North Korea and to heal the wounds of years-long separations.”

###

title: Brown Announces $20 Million Dollar Grant for GCRTA Platform Renovations Funded by Bipartisan Infrastructure Law
text:
Cleveland, OH – Congresswoman Shontel Brown (OH-11) is proud to announce that the Greater Cleveland Regional Transit Authority (GCRTA) has been awarded a $20 million dollar grant to fund renovations to Green Line light rail platforms. The Department of Transportation has awarded GCRTA with an All Stations Accessibility Program (ASAP) grant. The ASAP grant program was created and funded by the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, which Brown voted for in 2021. Congresswoman Brown also supported GCRTA’s funding request with an official letter of support in April.

“I’m proud to announce more federal funding is coming to Northeast Ohio thanks to the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law. This is a big win for our community: $20 million for our transit system that thousands of Ohioans rely on. I was proud to advocate for this funding because this federal grant will help make GCRTA platforms more accessible, allowing more passengers and their families use the Rapid to get where they need to go. It’s another example of the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law delivering for Northeast Ohio,” said Congresswoman Brown.

“Accessibility is about more than platforms and sidewalks; it represents independence, dignity and ensuring everyone can fully participate in our community. Once this project is complete, every rail station in our system will be ADA accessible, which is a major milestone for our network. For our riders, that translates into improved access to jobs, health care, education and everything Greater Cleveland has to offer. We appreciate the unwavering support of Congresswoman Shontel Brown, as a steadfast supporter of public transportation, through legislative advocacy and measurable action," said India L. Birdsong Terry, GCRTA General Manager and CEO.

The DOT’s ASAP program provides federal competitive grants to assist eligible entities in financing capital projects to upgrade the accessibility of legacy rail fixed guideway public transportation systems for people with disabilities.

title: Rep. Steube, Sen. Moody Urge Army Corps to Preserve Charlotte County Septic-to-Sewer Authorization
text:
WASHINGTON—Representative Greg Steube (R-Fla.) and Senator Ashley Moody (R-Fla.) today sent a joint letter to Assistant Secretary of the Army for Civil Works Adam Telle urging the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers to preserve Charlotte County’s eligibility to seek federal funding for septic-to-sewer conversion projects.

Rep. Steube worked to increase the amount in federal funding that Charlotte County could seek from $3 million to $33 million in 2022 to address nearly 2,600 failing septic systems harming water quality in the Charlotte Harbor National Estuary and the Gulf of America. Federal funds have yet to be dispersed for the project, but the lawmakers say that reflects bureaucratic delay, not a lapse in need. Charlotte County has since completed the Manasota Key Shoreline Protection Study and is now positioned to pursue a roughly $400 million wastewater conversion program, with the county planning to request Congressional support for septic-to-sewer conversions in the upcoming funding cycle.

Rep. Steube and Sen. Moody warn that removing Charlotte County’s eligibility for federal support now would strip the county of its ability to seek funding for this work going forward, undoing years of Congressional effort to address failing septic systems and improve water quality throughout Southwest Florida.

The full letter is attached here.

title: Rep. Haley Stevens Champions Bipartisan Data Science and Literacy Act to Prepare Students for Data-Driven Economy
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Michigan Congresswoman Haley Stevens alongside Reps. Jim Baird (R-IN), Don Beyer (D-VA), and Brian Fitzpatrick (R-PA) introduced the Bipartisan Data Science and Literacy Act, to expand access to data science education and make sure Michigan students have the skills needed to compete in an increasingly data-driven economy.

Data science draws on statistics, computer science, and mathematics to analyze and derive insights from data. Yet many students graduate from high school without these foundational skills, even as nearly one in four jobs requires data science skills.

“Data is powering the technologies and jobs that will define America’s economic future, and our students deserve the skills to lead that future,” said Rep. Haley Stevens. “Whether a student goes on to work on the factory floor, in a research lab, at a small business, or developing the next breakthrough technology, the ability to understand and use data will be increasingly important. This legislation is about making sure Michigan students are ready.”

“Data science education can be the catalyst that launches American scientific leadership into the stratosphere. Introducing children to STEM early gives them a foundation to continually build upon, preparing them to tackle increasingly advanced concepts as they reach higher education and enter the workforce. This is how we compound our scientific knowledge and foster the next generation of American innovation. Start early, build upon that knowledge, and grow our nation’s understanding of STEM,” said Rep. Jim Baird.

“Data is one of the most powerful tools shaping our society today. It helps businesses streamline supply chain operations, public health officials track and prevent disease, and Americans navigate nearly every aspect of modern life. Yet too many students lack access to the education they need to understand and use data effectively. Our bill would provide educators with the resources necessary to expand access to a quality data science education and prepare students for 21st century jobs,” said Rep. Don Beyer.

“Every generation has a responsibility to prepare the next for the world they will inherit. As data becomes foundational across nearly every field, our classrooms must keep pace. This legislation builds on the work we have led here in PA-1 to strengthen career and technical education, expand pathways into high-demand fields, and better connect learning with opportunity. The bipartisan Data Science and Literacy Act will carry that mission forward—equipping more students with the skills to succeed, strengthening our workforce, and ensuring America continues to lead,” said Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick.

The Data Science and Literacy Act establishes a grant program at the U.S. Department of Education to expand access to data science education nationwide. The program would support data science instruction from pre-K through community college, strengthen students’ data literacy, and provide professional development opportunities for educators. The legislation also improves federal data collection and establishes evaluation and reporting requirements to guide future investments.

Specifically, the Data Science and Literacy Act authorizes educational grants for the following purposes:

Curriculum Development: Developing, implementing, and expanding data science curricula and instructional materials.

Student Support: Improving student outcomes in data science education, including targeted support for students historically underrepresented in the field.

Professional Development: Providing evidence-based training and recruitment support for educators to effectively teach data science and related subjects.

Partnerships: Supporting collaboration with community colleges, institutions of higher education, and other relevant organizations to strengthen data science education pathways.

Text of the bill can be found here.

The legislation is backed by Data Science 4 Everyone (DS4E), Alliance for Data Science & AI (ADSA), Alliance for Learning Innovation (ALI), American Mathematical Association of Two-Year Colleges (AMATYC), American Statistical Association (AmStat), Association of Mathematics Teacher Educators (AMTE), Computer Science Teachers Association (CSTA), Digital Promise, INFORMS, Inter-university Consortium for Political and Social Research (ICPSR), National Council of Teachers of Mathematics (NCTM), and National Science Teaching Association (NSTA).

“The average school experience is becoming disconnected from the fast-changing world our students are graduating into,” said Zarek Drozda, Executive Director of Data Science 4 Everyone (DS4E). “The question ‘why am I learning this?’ needs to have a better answer. Engaging in data science activities allows students to connect their academic subjects to the real-world, and learn a toolkit for navigating (and questioning) AI at the same time.”

“ADSA works with more than 100 institutions of higher education, from R1 universities, community colleges, HBCUs, and Hispanic-serving institutions. One thing we hear consistently is that they want to be better partners to the K-12 schools in their regions,” said Dr. Micaela Parker, Founder and Executive Director of Alliance for Data Science and AI (ADSA). “The Data Science and Literacy Act creates that opportunity by putting flexible resources into district, community college, and university partnerships to update curricula for the modern age. This bill reflects how students actually use data: across their whole education, not in a single elective. ADSA is proud to support it.”

“Too often, promising education investments go unmeasured, leaving us guessing about what actually works. The Data Science and Literacy Act gets this right by building evaluation into the bill from the start by directing the Institute of Education Sciences (IES) to rigorously assess grant effectiveness and requiring grantees to continuously monitor their own progress. That commitment to evidence, not just access, is exactly what we want to see in federal education investments,” Sara Schapiro, Executive Director of Alliance for Learning Innovation (ALI). “At the Alliance for Learning Innovation (ALI), we believe every student deserves the tools to make sense of data and put it to work solving real problems. We're proud to endorse this bipartisan legislation and thank Representatives Stevens, Beyer, Kim, and Baird for their leadership in building a stronger STEM pipeline for the next generation."

“H.G. Wells once said ‘Statistical thinking will one day be as necessary for efficient citizenship as the ability to read and write.’ (c. 1903) That day is today. This bill is the right step forward,” said Eddie Tchertchian, President of the American Mathematical Association of Two-Year Colleges (AMATYC).

“The presence of AI in our everyday lives and work has made statistical thinking more critical than ever, so I applaud Representative Stevens and her cosponsors for reintroducing this bill, " said Jeri Mulrow, President of the American Statistical Association (AmStat). “Statistical thinking, a core component of data literacy, is essential for today's students to effectively use AI, critically assess its outputs, and succeed in today's job market.”

“In continuing AMTE efforts to bring diverse mathematics teacher education communities together, our organization continues to support educators, coaches, consultants, specialists, and university and community college faculty to share and disseminate research, teaching, and community partnerships in different educational contexts,” said Farshid Safi, President of Association of Mathematics Teacher Educators (AMTE). “AMTE, intentionally and toward a more comprehensive and inclusive lens, adopts an expansive view of the term mathematics education to include intersections with fields such as data science and statistics education, mathematical modeling, STEM education while partnering with those engaged in early childhood, PK-12, and post-secondary contexts.”

“Data shapes the technologies students use, the decisions they encounter, and the world they will help create. The 2026 CSTA PK–12 Computer Science Standards identify Data & Analysis as a core concept in foundational computer science education, calling on students to use data to solve problems, make discoveries, and express ideas while critically examining its quality, representation, privacy, and impact,” said Bryan Twarek, Head of Research and Innovation of the Computer Science Teachers Association (CSTA). “The Data Science and Literacy Act would invest in the curricula, professional development, and partnerships teachers need to prepare their students to become critical consumers, responsible creators, and informed participants in a world powered by computing.”

“Data literacy is a foundational tool for real-world agency. Preparing students for a changing economy requires updating what and how we teach, moving away from narrow metrics of success to build practical skills across disciplines,” said Jean-Claude Brizard, Chief Executive Officer of Digital Promise. “The Data Science and Literacy Act delivers flexible resources that allow school systems and postsecondary partners to strengthen teacher capacity and create powerful learning experiences for every student. Digital Promise strongly supports this legislation as a crucial investment in long-term economic mobility.”

“Ensuring that data literacy is a foundational aspect of education is a cornerstone of the United States’ long-term economic and national security. Data is everywhere and the ideas and demands to create more of it, and the evermore complex ways to deploy it, are growing more significant by the day,” said Jeff Cohen, Chief External Affairs Officer at INFORMS. “This bill is a key part of addressing the substantial shortfall of STEM-prepared students for the workforce of tomorrow. Operations research, analytics, and the science and technology of decision-making is predicated on the sound and ethical use of data. INFORMS strongly supports the bipartisan Data Science and Literacy Act of 2026 and looks forward to working to ensure its passage and effective implementation.”

“Our students are graduating into a world where the ability to understand, interpret, and use data is no longer optional; it is essential. Science and STEM education provide powerful opportunities for students to develop these skills as they use data to ask questions and make sense of the world around them,” said Brianna Reilly Oliveira, Director of Professional Learning for the National Science Teaching Association. “NSTA strongly supports the Data Science and Literacy Act and its investment in educators and students. By equipping educators with the confidence, tools and strategies to integrate data literacy into science and STEM instruction, we can better prepare all students to thrive in a data-rich world.”

title: Suozzi Introduces Bipartisan Bill to Crack Down on Health Care Fraud
text:
Washington, D.C.—Congressman Tom Suozzi (D-NY) today introduced the bipartisan Health Care Fraud Prevention and Enforcement Act with Congresswoman Claudia Tenney (R-NY) to strengthen the federal government’s efforts to combat waste, fraud, and abuse across government healthcare programs. The legislation would increase funding for the Health Care Fraud and Abuse Control Program (HCFAC), a joint agency program involving the Department of Health and Human Services, Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), Office of Inspector General (OIG), Department of Justice, and FBI. HCFAC coordinates federal, state, and local efforts to identify and prosecute health care fraud across programs including Medicare, Medicaid, and other government health care programs.

“Taxpayers bear the cost of every dollar lost to fraud, ultimately making healthcare more expensive. If we want to lower healthcare costs, we need to start by going after waste, fraud, and abuse wherever it’s happening. HCFAC is a tremendously successful program helping us do just that,” said Congressman Suozzi. “Fighting fraud is not a partisan issue; it’s common sense. The Health Care Fraud Prevention and Enforcement Act is about protecting taxpayers, rooting out fraud, and helping keep health care costs down. I’m proud to introduce this important bill to protect taxpayers and the healthcare programs that so many patients depend on.”

“Every dollar stolen through health care fraud is a dollar taken from taxpayers and the patients who depend on these programs,” said Congresswoman Tenney. “Fraudsters are becoming more sophisticated, and the federal government must have the tools and resources to find them, stop them, and hold them accountable. The Health Care Fraud Prevention and Enforcement Act strengthens the investigators and watchdogs on the front lines of this fight and improves oversight across federal health care programs. Protecting Medicare, Medicaid, and other critical programs from fraud will safeguard taxpayer dollars and help ensure these resources are there for the Americans who truly need them.”

Every dollar lost to fraud costs not only the government, but trickles down to consumers through higher premiums and costs on other health care expenses. HCFAC is a highly effective federal program, returning $3 to taxpayers for every dollar spent. By increasing the funding for this successful and worthwhile program, this legislation fights fraud responsibly, by equipping federal agencies with additional resources to prevent fraudulent payments, hold bad actors accountable, lower costs for patients, and recover taxpayer dollars.

Since 2010, the scope of HCFAC’s work has expanded significantly. Medicare and Medicaid spending has far outpaced inflation, enrollment has skyrocketed, and fraudsters have become savvier. The funding for HCFAC has not kept up. As a result, the network of agencies involved have had to police a broader and more complex system without adequate resources. To address this, the Health Care Fraud Prevention and Enforcement Act would rebase HCFAC’s funding, raising it to $490,000,000 for FY2027, $520,000,000 for FY2028, $57,000,000 for FY2029, and ensuring it continues to increase commensurate with inflation in FY2030 and beyond.
