title: Booker Joins Bipartisan Resolution Honoring Victims, Survivors, and First Responders on 25th Anniversary of 9/11
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – On the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks, U.S. Senator Cory Booker (D-NJ) joined a bipartisan group of colleagues in introducing a Senate resolution honoring the victims, survivors, and first responders of 9/11, as well as the service members who defended the United States in the years that followed.

The resolution pays tribute to the 2,977 people killed in Lower Manhattan, at the Pentagon, and in Shanksville, Pennsylvania. It honors the 343 firefighters, 72 law enforcement officers, and eight emergency medical technicians and paramedics who were killed responding to the attacks; the 55 military personnel killed at the Pentagon; and the passengers and crew of United Airlines Flight 93, who fought back and kept the hijackers from reaching their target in Washington. The resolution also recognizes the charitable foundations, nonprofits, labor and faith-based organizations, and community groups that have spent a quarter century serving survivors and the families of those lost.

"Twenty-five years later, we still carry that day with us — the nearly 3,000 lives lost, and the courage of the firefighters, police officers, and first responders who ran toward danger to save others," said Senator Cory Booker. "New Jersey lost hundreds of our neighbors that morning, and families across our state have carried that grief every day since. This resolution is the Senate's way of saying we have not forgotten — not the victims, not their families, and not the heroes whose sacrifice is a debt we can never fully repay. I'm proud to join Senator Gillibrand and my colleagues on both sides of the aisle in honoring their memory."

The resolution is led by Senator Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY). In addition to Booker, it is cosponsored by Senators Andy Kim (D-NJ), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Chris Murphy (D-CT), Tim Kaine (D-VA), John Fetterman (D-PA), Mark Warner (D-VA), Chuck Grassley (R-IA), and John Boozman (R-AR).

title: U.S. Senator Katie Britt Commemorates 25th Anniversary of 9/11 at Montgomery Fire/Rescue Ceremony Honoring Fallen Firefighters
text:
MONTGOMERY, AL — U.S. Senator Katie Britt (R-Ala.) today spoke at a 9/11 memorial service hosted by Montgomery Fire/Rescue. The event honored the 343 firefighters who made the ultimate sacrifice on September 11, 2001, as well as the 15 Montgomery firefighters who have lost their lives in the line of duty while protecting their community.

Senator Britt’s remarks can be read in full below.

“Thank you so much for that introduction and for the ability and invitation to be here today. To all of you who answer the call each and every day, I’m going to echo the mayor’s comments and say thank you. Thank you for your selflessness. Thank you for your willingness to sacrifice. And I want to say thank you to your families.

“This morning, as I reflected on what happened 25 years ago, I thought about where I was. I was in a class in Mary Alston Hall at the University of Alabama. It’s a large lecture setting. We didn’t have the connectivity that we have now, so people were piecing together what was happening in real time. I remember the helplessness that we felt, the uncertainty, the anger, the confusion as we worked to kind of piece together what happened and went back and got in front of the TV.

“One of the images that I will never forget are the men and women in uniform running towards the danger. I think about how many families lives changed that day. This morning, I got my two children up at 4:30 AM, got them out the door, and to the airport at 5:15. There were so many men and women whose day started just like that 25 years ago, who sent their loved ones out the door and thought they’d have an opportunity to see them again. It wasn’t just their lives that changed our world changed on that day.

“The one thing I hope we all take away from that, though, is the spirit of this nation, of who we are, who we are together. When we stand tall in the face of adversity, there is no mountain too tall for us to climb. There is no challenge too difficult for us to face.

“I think about these 15 helmets in front of us, and the men and women who have lost their lives in this community answering that call. What a tremendous debt of gratitude we owe each and every one of you. As I look in front of us, you have chosen to run towards the danger. You have chosen to operate in the impact zone so that more of us can return home safely to our families, so that our communities can be stronger. And you do that with resiliency and courage and grit and an unwavering dedication to your purpose.

“I had an opportunity to tour the new fire station, and mayor, it is quite nice. Walking around and seeing the facility was really impactful, but what I left with that made an even greater impact was the brotherhood that I felt when I was in that building. There is no doubt that you have each other’s backs. Thank you for doing that. What I left with was an even greater resolve that you have ours.

“I want to say thank you. When the moms and dads were taking their children at night to the men and women who are leaving to go off to work, to what they think will be an ordinary day if something were to occur, we know that you have our back. We know that you will run towards the impact zone, and we know that that courage and that faithfulness that you exhibit is unwavering.

“As we look at what’s ahead both in this community and the state, in the nation. I hope that we will remember the resiliency that we felt that day and then the days after 9/11. I hope that we will take that resiliency, that purpose, that unity, and that fortitude with us today and forever.

“Let us not just remember it here at this event, but let’s also tell the next generation. For those of us who have stories about where we were that day, about what it felt like, about the impact and the way that it changed our world, let’s make sure that the next generation knows that as well. Let’s make sure that they’re committed to the ideals of freedom and liberty. That they’re committed to the ideals and purpose that make this nation so great, and that they’re committed to being a part of answering the call.

“Thank you for what you do. Thank you for your selfless sacrifice. And let us all remember those that are lost and the resiliency that we feel about moving ahead. Thank you.”

title: Lopez Island Food Center Breaks Ground With $1M Cantwell-Supported Federal Investment
text:
Lopez Island Food Center Breaks Ground With $1M Cantwell-Supported Federal Investment

The 6,000-square-foot facility will help local farmers connect directly with food-insecure families & workers, & provide needed infrastructure; Cantwell & Larsen helped secure a $1 million federal grant for the project

EDMONDS, WA – Yesterday, leaders in the San Juan Islands celebrated the groundbreaking of the Lopez Food Center, a 6,000-square-foot facility that once completed will house a food share, job training, storage space and farm stands for local farmers, a commercial kitchen, and more.

The project was funded in part by a $1 million federal grant secured by U.S. Senator Maria Cantwell (D-WA) and U.S. Representative Rick Larsen (D, WA-02) through an FY2026 Congressionally Directed Spending (CDS) request.

“Too many families on Lopez Island struggle with food insecurity while San Juan County farms need access to markets, employees, and infrastructure which are all harder to find on the islands than on the mainland. This 6,000-square-foot community space will connect families in need, local farmers, and community organizations and create new opportunities for workers and businesses," Sen. Cantwell said. "The Lopez Food Center is exactly the kind of grassroots solution we should be investing in, and that’s why Congressman Larsen and I worked to secure $1 million in federal funds toward this groundbreaking."

The project will construct a multi-use building in the "main square" of the island focused on two issues: fighting high levels of food insecurity, which impacts approximately 40% of Lopez Island residents, and increasing economic development opportunities for island farms and restauranters.

Once completed, the center will provide a safe and accessible home for the Lopez Food Share, a food share that currently serves 1,123 low-income adults and children each month. The new space will double the number of people who can be served and allow the food share to create a hot meal program and expand its prepared food offerings.

The center will also provide a space for business development and job training to help tackle the labor shortage that limits the growth of the local food economy in San Juan County, an issue compounded by a shortage of affordable housing. The Lopez Food Center will also provide business incubation spaces for local entrepreneurs, pop-up restaurants, and a commercial kitchen.

title: Capito Statement on 25th Anniversary of 9/11
text:
CHARLESTON, W.Va. – U.S. Senator Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.Va.) today released the following statement on the 25th anniversary of the September 11th terrorist attacks:

“On September 11, 2001, our nation and the world were forever changed. For those of us who lived through this day, the images and the heartbreak are impossible to forget. Today on the 25th anniversary, we remember the nearly 3,000 innocent lives taken from us, and we continue to pray for the families and loved ones who have carried that loss. We honor the first responders who ran toward danger, the brave passengers and crew of Flight 93 who sacrificed their lives to save others, and the many others who stepped up to help our nation.

“We also remember what happened in the face of unimaginable tragedy: The terrorists who sought to tear us apart instead united us more than ever. In the days, months, and now years following 9/11, our country continues to prove our resiliency, strength, and courage. I encourage my fellow West Virginians and Americans to come together and remember the heroes who arose in our darkest hour, and pray for all those who faced unfathomable loss in the wake of the attacks. Our country is strongest when we are united, and we must always remember the American spirit that comforts us, inspires us, and brings us together as one. May we never forget, but always remember.”

This week while in Clarksburg, W.Va., Senator Capito filmed a video at the FBI’s Criminal Justice Information Services (CJIS) Division’s 9/11 Memorial to commemorate the 25th anniversary. Click here to watch the video.

title: Senator Collins Honors Victims and First Responders at 9/11 Memorial Ceremony in Augusta
text:
Click HERE, HERE, HERE, HERE, and HERE for individual photos.

AUGUSTA, ME – U.S. Senator Susan Collins delivered remarks today at the Maine Firefighters Memorial in Augusta during a ceremony marking the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks. The ceremony was hosted by the International Association of Fire Fighters Local 1650 in partnership with the Augusta Fire Honor Guard.

“We join together today to remember those whose lives were taken that terrible morning – nearly 3,000 innocent men, women, and children, workers doing their jobs, travelers embarking on trips,” said Senator Collins during her remarks.

“Men and women like Robert and Jacqueline Norton of Lubec, Maine, who boarded Flight 11 to celebrate a son’s wedding in California. At about the same time, Flight 175 took off with Robert Jalbert, a Massachusetts businessman and talented woodworker who grew up in Lewiston. Also on board was James Roux of Portland, on the first leg of a dream trip to climb the Himalayas. Stephen Ward of Gorham had just moved to New York City to work for Cantor Fitzgerald. He was among the 658 employees killed in the North Tower. Navy Commander Robert Schlegel of Gray was settling into his new assignment at the Pentagon. His office was believed to be the point of impact for Flight 77,” she continued.

“On the evening of that terrible day, members of Congress gathered on the steps of the U.S. Capitol. With tears in our eyes and sorrow in our hearts, together we sang, ‘God Bless America.’ The emotions of shock, anger, and grief were joined by determination. That moment remains my most enduring memory. The passage of 25 years has not dimmed our memory or diminished our gratitude. As long as we keep the meaning of this day of remembrance in our hearts, we shall meet the challenges that lie ahead,” Senator Collins concluded.

Following the September 11 attacks, Senator Collins, then Chair of the Senate Governmental Affairs Committee, led the effort with the late Senator Joe Lieberman in authoring theIntelligence Reform and Terrorism Prevention Act of 2004, which implemented the key recommendations of the independent 9/11 Commission. This comprehensive, bipartisan legislation was the most significant restructuring of the American intelligence community in more than half a century, dismantling the “stovepipes” that had left intelligence agencies holding separate pieces of information without a means to connect them. The law established the Director of National Intelligence and the National Counterterrorism Center to close those information-sharing gaps, helping to prevent future terrorist attacks.

###

title: Cortez Masto Honors the 25th Anniversary of September 11, 2001
text:
Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senator Catherine Cortez Masto (D-Nev.) released the following statement in recognition of the 25th anniversary of September 11th, 2001:

“I remember the morning of September 11, 2001, starting off like any other day. I was a federal prosecutor at the time, and I had gone to court that morning in Washington, D.C. for a hearing. I was outside in Judiciary Square, figuring out how to leave the evacuation area, when I heard a loud blast – what I later learned was the sound of the Pentagon crumbling after being hit by Flight 77. Twenty-five years later, I still don’t have words to describe the horror and the pain of that dark day in our nation’s history. And I know so many Americans feel the same.

“On September 11th, 2,977 people were killed in these terrorist attacks. Many more of our first responders lost their lives in the days and years to come as a result of exposure to toxins while they fought to save others at Ground Zero. As we come together to mark 25 years since this tragedy, we are reminded not just of the sadness and fear we all felt as these attacks unfolded, but also of the courage of so many heroes – from those first responders and our men and women in our armed forces, to everyday Americans who stepped up to lend a hand.

“Today, let us keep all of those we lost in our thoughts, let us pray for their families and loved ones, and let us hold true to the words “we will never forget.”

###

title: Duckworth Commemorates 25th Anniversary of 9/11 Attacks with Day of Service
text:
[CHICAGO, IL] — Combat Veteran and U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth, a member of the U.S. Senate Armed Services Committee (SASC) who served in the Reserve Forces for 23 years, today joined volunteers at Chicago Union Station to help pack 520,000 meals that will be donated to the Greater Chicago Food Depository as part of a day of service commemorating the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks. Photos from the event are available on the Senator’s website.

“Twenty-five years ago today, a heinous attack on our country took the lives of nearly 3,000 innocent people and changed the course of countless other American lives,” said Duckworth. “Today, we remember those we lost and reflect on the bravery shown by the first responders who ran toward danger—many of whom never made it home to their families or will forever live with illnesses caused by that day. Our hearts are with their families and loved ones, today and always. As we come together to pack 520,000 meals for local families in need, we honor this day through service and remind ourselves that the strength of our nation is found in how we support and serve one another.”

title: Duckworth, Durbin Join Senate Democrats in Urging Supreme Court to Block Postal Rule Limiting Mail-In Voting
text:
261 Members and former Members file bicameral, bipartisan brief as court order barring Postal Service rule limiting mail voting is being challenged by Trump’s DOJ

[WASHINGTON, D.C.] — U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth (D-IL) and U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, and joined U.S. Senators Alex Padilla (D-CA), Chuck Schumer (D-NY), Gary Peters (D-MI), along with U.S. Representatives Joe Morelle (D-NY-25), Robert Garcia (D-CA-42), Joe Neguse (D-CO-02) and Jamie Raskin (D-MD-08), in leading a bicameral amicus brief challenging the legality of President Trump’s executive order and U.S. Postal Service rule seeking to exert control over mail-in ballots ahead of the 2026 midterm elections.

The group, made up of a bipartisan, bicameral coalition of 261 lawmakers and former lawmakers, filed an amicus brief with the U.S. Supreme Court in the matter of State of California, et al. v. United States Postal Service, et al., a lawsuit brought by a coalition of state attorneys general against the U.S. Postal Service (USPS). The court case challenges a final rule issued by USPS pursuant to President Trump’s directive that imposes unconstitutional and unworkable restrictions on mail-in voting, including requiring states to provide a “citizenship verification list” and attempting to give USPS control over who can vote by mail.

“Donald Trump’s desperate attempts to obstruct voting by mail for every American but himself are unconstitutional and jeopardize our democracy,” said Duckworth. “Trump has already voted by mail twice this year alone. We cannot allow him to illegally intimidate his fellow tens of millions of Americans who cast their ballots by mail. As we approach the 2026 midterms, the Supreme Court must reject these unlawful executive orders and protect Americans’ right to vote this fall.”

“The President is dead set on attacking Americans’ right to vote and undermining our democracy by making baseless claims about ‘rigged’ elections, demanding unreasonable voter registration requirements, restricting mail-in voting, and threatening to unconstitutionally nationalize our elections. But the President cannot nullify our Constitution. The Supreme Court must reject the President’s attempts to chip away at our voting rights,” Durbin said.

Nearly one-third of Americans have voted by mail in recent elections—a voting practice Trump himself used as recently as August 2026, when he voted in Florida’s Republican primary.

In the court filing, the amici curiae argue that President Trump’s Executive Order 4399 and USPS’s final rule violate the separation of powers and usurp congressional authorities outlined in Article I of the U.S. Constitution, which gives the states and Congress exclusive authority over election administration.

“As current and former legislators, amici took an oath to uphold and defend the Constitution of the United States — including its guarantee of the separation of powers,” wrote the lawmakers in the brief. “Amici have a particular interest in defending the institutional role of the Legislative Branch under Article I of the Constitution and in vindicating the long-settled principle that the Constitution commits ultimate regulatory authority over federal elections to Congress. The Constitution does not contemplate the Executive Branch acting unilaterally to assert power over federal elections. Yet that is what the Order and Final Rule do.”

The amici also pointed to a recent federal court ruling blocking USPS from implementing its newly finalized mail ballot rule for the midterm elections, saying the agency lacked the authority to implement the rule and that its actions are “substantively unconstitutional and contrary to law.”

“The district court correctly concluded that Appellees are likely to succeed on the merits of their claims that USPS lacked authority to issue the Final Rule, that the Final Rule unconstitutionally imposes mail-ballot requirements on the States, and that the Final Rule unconstitutionally bars non-compliant State and local election officials from using the USPS to mail ballots at all,” wrote the lawmakers.

The lawmakers concluded by asserting states’ power to administer elections and Congress’s power to make or alter rules regulating elections, which the Supreme Court itself has described as an “override” authority. President Trump’s illegal incursion on this authority is an attempt to disenfranchise people who depend on mail-in ballots to vote.

“The integrity of our constitutional system depends on each branch keeping to its assigned role,” concluded the lawmakers. “The Framers set up a two-part system that gave the States default authority to regulate federal elections subject to Congress’s authority to override the States. The Framers did not provide the President with any authority to interfere in that system, nor has Congress subsequently imbued the President or the Executive Branch with any such authority by statute.”

In addition to Duckworth, Durbin, Padilla, Schumer, and Peters, the amicus brief was joined by the entire Senate Democratic Caucus.

The full brief is available on the Senator’s website.

-30-

title: Durbin Delivers Remarks At National Center For Victims Of Crime’s Annual Training Institute
text:
CHICAGO—Today, U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, delivered brief remarks at the National Center for Victims of Crime’s (NCVC) National Training Institute (NTI), an annual conference providing nearly 800 victim service professionals an opportunity to engage and learn from leaders in the victim advocacy community.

In his remarks, Durbin focused on the need for Congress to hold Big Tech accountable for its failure to protect children and users from harm. Durbin also applauded last month’s landmark settlement requiring Meta to pay more than $17 billion in penalties and make major changes to Facebook and Instagram over claims the company endangers children with addictive social media platforms.

“Parents and grandparents across America feel a pit in their stomachs every time their child logs onto a phone, tablet, or video game console. These parents and grandparents know that the internet has now become a hunting ground for predators, but accountability is finally coming,” Durbin said. “The recent landmark verdicts confirming that social media companies have a duty to protect children using their platforms is a crucial first step. As moment builds in the courts, Congress must do its part to ensure Big Tech is forced to change its behavior.”

Durbin has used his role on the Senate Judiciary Committee to prioritize child safety online through hearings, legislation, and oversight efforts.

On January 31, 2024, while Durbin was serving as Chair, the Committee held a hearing featuring testimony from the CEOs of social media companies Discord, Meta, Snap, TikTok, and X (formerly known as Twitter). This hearing highlighted the ongoing risk to children and the immediate need for Congress to act on the bipartisan bills reported by the Committee.

Durbin and U.S. Senator Josh Hawley (R-MO) joined forces to reintroduce the bipartisan STOP CSAM Act, which would combat online child sexual abuse material. The bill passed the Judiciary Committee unanimously and awaits action on the Senate floor.

In addition, Durbin’s bipartisan Disrupt Explicit Forged Images and Non-Consensual Edits Act of 2024 (DEFIANCE Act) passed the Senate in July 2024 and again in January 2026. The legislation would hold accountable those responsible for the proliferation of nonconsensual, sexually-explicit “deepfake” images and videos. The bill awaits consideration by the House.

Durbin also introduced the Sunset Section 230 Act with the late U.S. Senator Lindsey Graham (R-SC), which would repeal Section 230 two years after the date of enactment so that those harmed online can bring legal action against the companies that caused the harm. The bill awaits consideration by the Senate Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee.

-30-

title: Durbin Statement On The 25th Anniversary Of The 9/11 Terrorist Attacks
text:
CHICAGO – U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL) released the following statement on the 25th anniversary of the terrorist attacks of September 11, 2001:

“Twenty-five years ago today, I vividly recall looking down the National Mall from the Capitol Building and watching as black smoke billowed up from the Pentagon. That image is seared into my mind. But what I also remember about that day was the outpouring of compassion and common purpose that united us.

“Twenty-five years after that devastating day, we still mourn the 2,977 innocent lives lost at the World Trade Center, the Pentagon, and a field in Shanksville, Pennsylvania, including the heroic members of the New York City Fire Department, law enforcement officers, and military personnel.

“Today, as we reflect on how those acts of pure evil forever altered our sense of security and safety, let us also reflect on the importance of remaining faithful to our values and the Constitution while protecting the American people. The victims of 9/11, their loved ones, and the American people deserved justice and accountability long ago.”

Today, Durbin attended the City of Chicago Fire Department’s 9/11 Tribute, marking the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks. The formal memorial tribute at Navy Pier faced east toward New York, Washington, D.C., and Pennsylvania to honor the lives lost and remember the firefighters, paramedics, police officers, and other first responders who made the ultimate sacrifice.

-30-

title: Ernst Marks 25 Years Since September 11: Freedom Is Never Free
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Senator Joni Ernst (R-Iowa), a combat veteran of the Global War on Terrorism, issued the following statement to reflect on the 25th anniversary of September 11, 2001:

“Twenty-five years ago, America’s strength was tested. September 11th changed our nation forever, but it also showed the world the resilience, courage, and unity of the American people,” said Ernst. “A quarter-century later, we remember the innocent lives taken from us and honor the extraordinary Americans who came together in the face of unimaginable tragedy to help our nation heal and rebuild. We must never forget that freedom is never free—it is defended every day by the brave men and women who answer the call to serve. Today, we renew our promise to Never Forget and remain steadfast in protecting the freedoms that keep America a beacon of hope and liberty around the world.”

title: Fetterman Urges U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement to Pay Medical Service Providers
text:
BRADDOCK, PA — Last week, U.S. Senator John Fetterman (D-PA) sent a letter to the Senior Official Performing the Duties of the Director of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), David J. Venturella, to note his concern with the lack of reimbursement to medical service providers for care provided to detainees, and to urge immediate repayment.

“For more than two decades, ICE paid the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to process reimbursement claims for medical services related to immigration detention. This agreement, which came at no cost to the VA, allowed for timely and efficient payment of medical providers and ensured a responsible level of care for detainees and detention center staff. On October 3, 2025, the Veterans Affairs Administration (VA) and ICE abruptly terminated this decades-long contract. This action left ICE with no mechanism to process invoices and pay medical providers serving ICE facilities and detainees,” wrote Senator Fetterman.

In the Commonwealth, Moshannon Valley Emergency Medical Services (MVEMS) is responsible for emergency medical care for over 40,000 Pennsylvanians. This includes nearly 2,000 detainees held at ICE’s Moshannon Valley Processing Center. Since payments ceased, MVEMS is now owed over $230,000.

On January 13, ICE Health Service Corps announced plans to transition claims processing to a new electronic provider portal, with a launch date of April 30. As of now, providers remain unable to submit reimbursement claims for emergency responses initiated through 911 calls and other medical care provided to individuals in ICE custody or at ICE facilities. The continued delays raise serious concerns about access to timely emergency medical care for detainees, guards, custodial staff, administrators, and others at these facilities.

“As MVEMS and medical service providers from across the Commonwealth continue to show up for their communities, ICE must also be a good neighbor. ICE should not and cannot rely on medical service providers like MVEMS to shoulder the financial and operational burden of federal immigration detention operations,” continued the senator.

Read the full text of the letter below and here.

–

Dear Mr. Venturella:

I am concerned about the non-payment of medical service provider invoices for care rendered to individuals in the custody of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), and I demand that ICE immediately pay these bills. This inaction is creating economic hardship for medical service providers across rural Pennsylvania. Refusal to pay for these services hurts our communities and breaks financial obligations.

For more than two decades, ICE paid the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to process reimbursement claims for medical services related to immigration detention. This agreement, which came at no cost to the VA, allowed for timely and efficient payment of medical providers and ensured a responsible level of care for detainees and detention center staff. On October 3, 2025, the Veterans Affairs Administration (VA) and ICE abruptly terminated this decades-long contract. This action left ICE with no mechanism to process invoices and pay medical providers serving ICE facilities and detainees.

On January 13, 2026, ICE Health Service Corps announced it would begin processing claims through a new electronic provider portal. It was the expectation of the Department of Homeland Security and ICE that this portal would launch on April 30, 2026.2 It is now September and providers are still unable to submit reimbursement claims for 911 call-initiated responses and other care provided to individuals in the custody of or physically located at an ICE facility. This raises serious concerns about access to emergency treatment for detainees, guards, custodians, and administrators.

ICE recognizes the danger this lapse in payments to providers creates. In contracting documents signed in October 2025 and made publicly available via the Systems Award Management website in November 2025, ICE states, “It is an absolute emergency for ICE to immediately procure claims processing support because lack of this support will delay critical medical care for [illegal aliens] such as dialysis, prenatal care, oncology, chemotherapy, etc.

While payment delays adversely affect all providers, they are especially harmful to rural health and emergency care providers with limited staff, equipment, and financial reserves. Moshannon Valley Emergency Medical Services (MVEMS) is a rural EMS provider in Philipsburg, PA. MVEMS operates over an almost 800 square mile area and provides EMS service to 41,000 Pennsylvanians. They accomplish this every day with only 10 full-time employees, 35 part-time staff, and five ambulances. They also provide EMS services to the Moshannon Valley Processing Center, which is capable of holding nearly 1,900 detainees. As of August 20, 2025, ICE owes MVEMS $236,124.91 in overdue payments, because of the reimbursement freeze.

As MVEMS and medical service providers from across the Commonwealth continue to show up for their communities, ICE must also be a good neighbor. ICE should not and cannot rely on medical service providers like MVEMS to shoulder the financial and operational burden of federal immigration detention operations.

I request ICE promptly provide my office with the following information:

A detailed accounting of the total amount currently owed by ICE to medical service providers, EMS providers, hospitals, and other health care entities for care provided to individuals in ICE custody.

If unavailable, please provide a detailed estimate of the total amount currently owed based on historical averages adjusted for recent increases in ICE’s enforcement and detention activities.

A statistical impact report addressing how these payment delays have affected detainee medical care and medical and EMS providers.

A detailed update on the status of ICE’s new payment system, including when it will be fully operational, when outstanding claims will be paid, and what steps ICE is taking to prevent future payment disruptions.

I appreciate your attention to this matter, and I hope to receive your response no later than September 15, 2026.

Sincerely,

title: Gillibrand Announces Bipartisan Resolution Commemorating 25th Anniversary of September 11, 2001 Terror Attacks
text:
Today, on the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks, U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand led a bipartisan group of her colleagues in announcing a Senate resolution honoring the victims, first responders, and survivors of 9/11, as well as the service members who defended the United States in the aftermath. The resolution pays tribute to the 2,977 individuals killed in Lower Manhattan, at the Pentagon, and in Shanksville, Pennsylvania. It also honors the 343 firefighters, 72 law enforcement officers, 8 emergency medical technicians and paramedics, and 55 military personnel at the Pentagon who sacrificed their lives responding to the attacks, alongside the passengers and crew of United Airlines Flight 93. The resolution also recognizes the charitable foundations, nonprofit organizations, labor organizations, faith-based organizations, and community groups that have faithfully served survivors and families of victims.

“Twenty-five years ago, our nation experienced tragedy, but in our darkest hour, we saw the extraordinary courage and resilience of the American people,” said Senator Gillibrand.“As we mark 25 years since September 11, 2001, we owe it to the victims, the heroes who ran into the burning towers, and the military personnel who answered the call to serve to ensure their sacrifices are never forgotten. This resolution reaffirms our commitment to standing with survivors and their families, supporting the programs that continue to provide critical care, and vowing to never forget.”

Throughout her time in Congress, Senator Gillibrand has continuously advocated for 9/11first responders and survivors, championing major federal efforts to secure permanent healthcare and financial compensation. She led the passage of the James Zadroga 9/11Health and Compensation Act of 2010 to establish the World Trade Center Health Program (WTCHP) and reopen the Victim Compensation Fund (VCF). She also spearheaded the passage of long-term protections for the 9/11 community with the James Zadroga 9/11Health and Compensation Reauthorization Act to extend the WTCHP through 2090, co-authored the Never Forget the Heroes Act of 2019 to permanently fund the VCF, and led legislative fixes to stabilize the WTCHP’s budget formula, ensuring that over 140,000 enrolled responders and survivors maintain access to specialized care and benefits.

In addition to Senator Gillibrand, the resolution is cosponsored by Senators Andy Kim (D-NJ), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Chris Murphy (D-CT), Tim Kaine (D-VA), John Fetterman (D-PA), Mark Warner (D-VA), Cory Booker (D-NJ), Chuck Grassley (R-IA), and John Boozman (R-AR).

title: Q&A: Upholding Public Trust in Government
text:
Q: What motivates you to hold meetings in every county across Iowa every year?

A: When the Senate’s not in session, I’m home meeting with Iowans. Having dialogue with my constituents is the essence of representative government. As your senator, I bring your ideas and concerns back to Washington, D.C., to solve problems that are making it harder to get ahead and stay ahead. This year I completed my 99 county meetings for the 46th year in a row with more than 100 workers at Sub-Zero in Cedar Rapids. Holding Q&As at hospitals, manufacturing facilities and on the factory floor provides an additional benefit to keep on top of the challenges facing employers and the workforce, as well as learning about our high-quality products and services here in Iowa. I also make it a priority to foster civic engagement with younger generations and enjoy answering questions from students at schools across Iowa.

I’m often asked why I started my annual 99 county meetings. Before I was elected to the U.S. Senate, I was at a local restaurant and overheard someone say that “it must be election time” because politicians were in town. That remark stuck with me. That’s when I decided to hold a meeting in every county, at least once, every year – not every six years. I’m glad my approach to representative government has influenced presidential candidates and other elected officials to hold themselves accountable to the people with face-to-face meetings. Obviously, it’s not possible to meet in person with more than three million Iowans, so I encourage people to share their opinions and concerns by calling my office or sending me an email at https://www.grassley.senate.gov/. Whether I interact in person at a county meeting, by email or in my office on Capitol Hill, feedback from Iowans informs my work at the policymaking tables.

For example, when Iowans told me about a steep price increase for their child’s EpiPen that’s used for emergency treatment for life-threatening allergic reactions, I investigated the situation that led to bipartisan legislation to fix the problem. More recently, I’ve led efforts to fix California’s Prop 12 that’s added a costly burden to Iowa pig farmers’ operations and adversely impacts Iowa’s economy, the number one pork producing state in the nation. I’m also leading a bipartisan push for much-needed reforms in the pharmaceutical industry that’s making it harder for rural pharmacies to keep their doors open. Based on feedback from local employers across Iowa, I supported tax relief to boost the engine of the U.S. economy in the Working Families Tax Cuts Actthat enable small businesses to invest in their operations, create new jobs, raise wages and boost benefits for their employees. As your senator, I remind Iowans that my door is always open.

Q: Why did you cosponsor the Stop Insider Trading Act?

A: My annual 99 county meetings keep my finger on the pulse of Iowans as I work to strengthen public confidence in government. Years ago, Iowans often would ask why Congress doesn’t have to follow the same laws it applies to American society. Prior to 1995, Congress was exempt from a dozen workplace laws. My bipartisan Congressional Accountability Act delivered a reality check to the people who write the laws of the land so that lawmakers walk in the shoes of our constituents.

There’s also growing concern among Americans that elected officeholders enrich themselves while serving in office. Under no circumstances should members of Congress profit from insider information while shaping public policy. Public service is a privilege, not a stepping stone to a fat bank account. Among my efforts to restore public trust in government, I led efforts to improve the Stop Trading on Congressional Knowledge (STOCK) Act enacted during the Obama administration to prohibit members of Congress and federal employees from profiting from nonpublic, insider information. Since its passage, I’ve worked to close loopholes in the law.

Most recently, I’ve cosponsored the Stop Insider Trading Act. This legislation would prohibit members of Congress, their spouses and dependent children from purchasing publicly traded stocks. Moreover, members would be required to file a seven-day public notice prior to the sale of any stock they presently own. Violations of the bill’s requirements would result in stiff penalties and the forfeiture of any gain realized from the transaction. With the support of Iowa Reps. Ashley Hinson, Mariannette Miller-Meeks, Zach Nunn and Randy Feenstra, the House of Representatives passed the bill in July.

Voters place their trust in elected representatives to do what’s right and this bill establishes guardrails to do just that. After 46 years of holding Q&As in every county, every year across the state, it’s an honor and a privilege to listen, learn and advocate on behalf of my fellow Iowans. Without a doubt, common sense runs rampant in Iowa and I’m working as hard as ever to uphold the public trust in government by displacing Washington nonsense with Iowa common sense.

title: ICYMI—Hagerty JoinsThe Scott Jennings Show on Salem News Channel to Discuss Midterms, Iran, Memphis, BLADE Act
text:
DALLAS—On Thursday, United States Senator Bill Hagerty (R-TN), a member of the Senate Foreign Relations, Appropriations, and Banking Committees, joined The Scott Jennings Show on Salem News Channel to discuss the upcoming midterm election, the latest in Iran, the Memphis Safe Task Force, and the BLADE Act.

*Click the photo above or here to watch*

Partial Transcript

Hagerty on the RNC Convention: We have had a great delegation from Tennessee and frankly, great delegations from all over the country. There’s a lot of excitement, a lot of enthusiasm. People loved [President Donald Trump’s] speech last night—a lot of energy there. And frankly, a lot of people that weren’t here, but I’ve heard from across the country that are very pleased to see the energy turnaround. And frankly, to be drawing a contrast finally against Democratic candidates. I think people are tired of reading New York Times headlines running these generic polls, Republicans versus Democrats. And now that we actually see what a Democratic socialist stands for, there’s a huge contrast to be made. I think if you just step back and look at what the Democrats have accomplished this past 18, 20 months, they’ve delivered the two longest government shutdowns in history. What they seem to want to deliver is nothing but chaos, shutdowns, and acrimony. The American public hasn’t seen anything positive coming from the Democrats.

Hagerty on Iran: The Iranian regime is holding on to see what happens on November the third. It certainly worked out well for them back in 2020. Back at that point in time, I was the U.S. ambassador to Japan. I got the Japanese and my colleagues around the world… to stop buying Iranian crude oil… We brought the Iranian economy to a difficult place. It’s even worse right now, but the Iranians held out to see what would happen in the election. Having [former President Joe Biden] in the Oval Office was a gift extraordinaire to the Iranian regime, because immediately the Biden [administration] stopped enforcing all sanctions. Money began to flow by May 2021. We had the 11-day war break out in Israel—you know what happened on October 7th of 2023. Terror breaks out through the entire region because Iran [was] in a position to fund it. We have shut that down now… they’re hanging on by a thread.

Hagerty on the Memphis Safe Task Force: I don’t think you could see a finer contrast in America than the difference between Memphis, Tennessee, and Minneapolis, Minnesota. And the one difference there, the one singular difference is that in Memphis, we worked together. We cooperated; we coordinated.

Hagerty on the creation of the Memphis Safe Task Force: When [FBI Director Kash Patel] called me in December 2024, he said, ‘Sir, the President is about to make his decision on the FBI director, and I would really appreciate your support.’ I said, ‘Kash, I’m happy to support you, but I’m going to need your support in Memphis, too.’ And Kash kept his word to me. We began working on this right after Kash came into office and put together, very quietly, a task force. [The task force] first entered the city working with local police and very quietly came in and took out 154 of the worst of the worst criminals. These are gang members. Through the summer, we took that number up to well over 500, and President Trump is watching our progress all along the way, and said, ‘Okay, we’re going to put the full menu in place.’ Meaning 16, 17 different crime enforcement agencies, including the [U.S. National Guard]… People in Memphis today would tell you, ‘Thank you, thank you, and thank you again, President Trump,’ for doing it. Crime has gone through the floor. Memphis is a great city—now it’s one of the safest cities in America. We’re going to continue working on this. My hat is off to [Memphis Mayor Paul Young], who has cooperated with us, to [Tennessee Governor Bill Lee], who has now taken what were eight state troopers up to 100 in the area. And President Trump has done a magnificent job.

Hagerty on the cooperation of state and federal agencies: It shows what happens when you have cooperation between federal government, state government, local government—cooperation between Republicans and Democrats. It shows that it works in these other cities. We know Chicago has been resistant to this idea… where the Democrats will not cooperate. Violent crime continues to proliferate over Labor Day weekend in Chicago—scores of people were shot and murdered. They just won’t put their people first. They cannot get over the politics. It’s so sad that they’re willing to sacrifice their own citizens to stand on some ideological point that obviously doesn’t work. But again, Memphis stands as a shining example, and my hat is off to [Deputy Chief of Staff Stephen Miller] at the White House, to the president, of course, to Kash Patel, to the [U.S. Department of Justice], and all of the agencies that are there on the ground.

Hagerty on the BLADE Act: My experience in Asia goes back to 1988, when I worked for Boston Consulting Group. They sent me to the region for three years. What I have seen evolve is an industrial policy that the Chinese deploy where they steal our intellectual property. They don’t play by the same set of rules. They use our IP, come in, cut costs, and try to push American companies out of business. They’re doing the same thing in AI. Their distillation models are stealing from us, basically. They’re stealing intellectual property from us. They’re using those to come in and offer a cheap alternative to take over the AI marketplace. We cannot let that happen. We’ve got to lead in this arena. We need to do it responsibly. But the BLADE Act gives us the tools to put in place sanctions to come in and deal directly with those companies that are involved in this illegal distillation, and sanction them in a way that will stop it.

title: Senator Hassan Statement on 25th Anniversary of September 11th, 2001 Terrorist Attack

“September 11th was one of the most terrible days in our country’s history, when 2,977 innocent people were taken from us in a terrorist attack rooted in evil. Every one of those victims had a world all their own. Every one of them was loved and needed.

"The response that day from first responders and the millions of ordinary Americans who sprung to action, donated blood, or decided to serve reminds us that our country can be united in common purpose. Because on 9/11, we remember that, for all our differences and disagreements, we are one country, one people, and one America.

“It’s been 25 years since that terrible day, and we cannot bring back those we lost, but we can become their legacy by living our lives with purpose and meaning. We won’t ever live up fully to the example of courage, bravery, and sacrifice shown by the first responders or the passengers of Flight 93, but it’s incumbent on all of us to try each and every day.”

title: Heinrich Joins Roundtable with New Mexico Voices for Children and W.K. Kellogg Foundation, Tours Presbyterian Kaseman Hospital’s Food Pharmacy, Speaks at ARRAY Technologies’ New Facility Ribbon Cutting, Urges New Mexicans to Raise Their Voices for Roadless Rule
text:
ALBUQUERQUE, N.M. — U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, participated in an event in Albuquerque on improving the well-being of children and families, toured Presbyterian Kaseman Hospital’s food pharmacy, joined a ribbon-cutting ceremony for ARRAY Technologies’ solar manufacturing facility, and spoke in support of protecting the Roadless Rule at a New Mexico Wild community event.

Heinrich began the day participating in a roundtable event hosted in partnership with New Mexico Voices for Children and the W.K. Kellogg Foundation, along with representatives from the UNM School of Medicine, Changing Women Initiative, Future Focused Education, and Breath of My Heart, to discuss New Mexico Voices for Children’s Roadmap Report and policy solutions to improve the well-being of children and families in New Mexico.

U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.) joins a roundtable to discuss policy solutions to improve the well-being of children and families in New Mexico, September 9, 2026.

“I got involved early in the conversation around universal pre-K and early childhood education in New Mexico because we need to invest in our greatest asset: the next generation,” said Heinrich, a member of the U.S. Senate Appropriations Committee. “Right now, we’re seeing the Trump administration walk away from investing in our children and families. We need to be thinking about the future. That’s why I’ve long championed legislation and funded programs that give our children a strong start and ensure they have access to high-quality care. We’ve done some incredible things here in New Mexico over the last few years, but we’re just getting started. I’ll keep pushing to make sure every child in our state has the opportunity to succeed.”

Notably, in 2014, Heinrich was the first member of the New Mexico Congressional Delegation to publicly support unlocking investments from the state’s Land Grant Permanent Fund to sustainably support early childhood education. After the New Mexico Legislature and voters in the state passed the necessary state constitutional amendment to unlock these investments, Heinrich successfully led the effort to secure Congressional authorization of the amendment through his New Mexico Education Enhancement Act, which passed in the Omnibus Appropriations Agreement for Fiscal Year 2023 (FY23).

For more information on the efforts Heinrich has championed to bolster childhood education in New Mexico, click here.

Following the roundtable event, Heinrich toured Presbyterian Kaseman Hospital’s food pharmacy, hearing directly from families who receive the program’s food distribution services about the program’s impact.

U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.) tours Presbyterian Kaseman Hospital’s food pharmacy, September 9, 2026.

While touring the food pharmacy, Heinrich highlighted the need to build on programs like Presbyterian’s that are making nutritious food more accessible to New Mexico families.

“It's time to rebuild our food system in a different way that really serves people's health,” said Heinrich. “We need to thoughtfully look at some of our food deserts in this state and find ways to make fruits and vegetables accessible in those places, while also supporting our local farmers. Presbyterian’s food pharmacy program proves how valuable a fresh fruit and vegetable kind of diet is for New Mexicans, and we should learn from that.”

Last month, Heinrich cosponsored the Accountable Produce is Medicine Act of 2026, which would require the Center for Medicare and Medicaid Innovation (CMMI) to test a new bundled-payment model that integrates Food is Medicine services into chronic disease care. Participating programs would provide eligible Medicare, Medicaid, and CHIP patients with health assessments, care coordination, telehealth and remote monitoring, nutrition counseling, lifestyle support, and healthy, nutrient-dense foods.

In December of 2024, Heinrich introduced the FOOD for Health Act, which aimed to reduce nutrition-related chronic diseases and address food insecurity by supporting the production of nutritious food.

In 2018, Heinrich voted in favor of the 2018 Farm Bill, which established the first federal Produce Prescription Program under the Gus Schumacher Nutrition Incentive Program (GusNIP) program, which provides federal grants to increase the purchase and consumption of fresh fruits and vegetables among low-income households.

Heinrich also joined a ribbon-cutting ceremony to officially open ARRAY Technologies’ Westside Albuquerque facility. The new $50 million facility will triple ARRAY’s solar tracker manufacturing capacity in New Mexico – shortening energy delivery times, lowering costs for consumers, and creating over 300 good-paying jobs in New Mexico.

U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, joins a ribbon-cutting ceremony for ARRAY Technologies’ Solar manufacturing facility, September 9, 2026.

“Array Technologies’ new $50 million facility on Albuquerque’s West Side is a testament to the strength of our workforce and New Mexico’s leadership in unlocking our country’s clean energy future,” said Heinrich, Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee. “This new facility will employ more than 300 New Mexicans and create high-skilled jobs, from welders to tooling and die technicians. It’s proof that when we invest in American-made energy, we’re not just building the technologies that will power our future — we’re creating good-paying jobs, strengthening local economies, and helping lower electricity costs for families and small businesses. And this is just the beginning.”

Heinrich has long supported ARRAY Technologies and investments that have spurred solar development.

In April 2022, Heinrich met with New Mexico solar industry leaders, including ARRAY Technologies, to hear how a solar tariff petition filed with the Department of Commerce would severely harm the state’s solar industry and the hard-working New Mexicans who work in the industry, and later led the charge to prevent the Biden administration from moving forward with the tariffs.

In June 2022, Heinrich delivered keynote remarks at the American Solar Energy Society’s 51st Annual National Solar Conference, SOLAR 2022, hosted at the University of New Mexico, highlighting the importance of accelerating the deployment of residential and utility-scale solar across New Mexico and the nation.

In July 2022, Heinrich passed the CHIPS and Science Act, which invested in domestic solar manufacturing through tax credits and semiconductor funding.

In August 2022, Heinrich helped pass the Inflation Reduction Act, which included the 45X Advanced Manufacturing Production Credit, to subsidize the production of five types of goods: solar energy components, wind energy components, battery components, inverters, and critical minerals.

In April 2024, Heinrich delivered keynote remarks during New Mexico’s first Business-to-Business Electrify New Mexico event, hosted by the Renewable Energy Industries Association of New Mexico, celebrating ARRAY Technologies’ expansion and growth in the state.

In April 2024, Heinrich welcomed U.S. Secretary of Energy Jennifer Granholm to New Mexico to highlight how investments from the Inflation Reduction Act and the CHIPS and Science Act created a manufacturing boom and helped position New Mexico as a national leader in an American-made clean energy future, touring ARRAY Technologies’ manufacturing plant in NE Albuquerque.

In June 2024, Heinrich, as Chairman of the Joint Economic Committee (JEC), hosted a hearing on how investments in clean energy have helped create an economic boom, uplifting ARRAY Technologies for expanding in New Mexico.

Heinrich ended the day speaking in support of the Roadless Rule at a New Mexico Wild community event, emphasizing the importance of fighting to preserve the Roadless Rule. The public now has until October 6 to submit comments on the Trump administration’s proposed plan to rescind the Roadless Rule.

U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, speaks at New Mexico Wild’s event on protecting the Roadless Rule, September 9, 2026.

“Public input makes for better governance. It gets all the facts on the table. It gets people’s opinions on the table, and generally the outcome benefits from that,” said Heinrich, Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee. "We saw that during the public process that led to the Roadless Rule in the late 1990s, when there were tons of people in those hearings — and now, after more than 20 years of management under the Roadless Rule, the comments are 99 percent supportive. And yet, this Forest Service and this administration doesn’t have the decency to hold a single public hearing. Public process is at the heart of good democracy and good governance, and we won’t accept anything less than that.”

Last month, Heinrich released a statement reacting to the Trump administration’s announcement that the U.S. Forest Service (USFS) has filed a proposed rule to rescind the Roadless Rule, calling roadless areas irreplaceable and criticizing the administration for its attack on public lands.

Earlier this summer, Heinrich hosted a press conference on Senate Republicans’ efforts to repeal the Roadless Rule and spoke out against the Trump administration’s efforts to rescind the Roadless Rule.

Additionally, Heinrich wrote an op-ed in Outside News about how the Roadless Rule helps conserve our public lands and prevent wildfires – and how it represents years of input from Americans who have made it clear they want the Roadless Rule to stay in place.

In May, Heinrich and the N.M. Congressional Delegation urged New Mexicans to voice their opposition to the looming Roadless Rule repeal.

In February, Heinrich attended the “Camo at the Capitol Day” rally in the Roundhouse where he stated, “It makes me incredibly proud to be a New Mexican. They’ll never take our public lands from our public hands.”

Last September, Heinrich and the N.M. Congressional Delegation sent a letter to USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins requesting that New Mexico be excluded from the Trump administration’s proposed repeal of the Roadless Rule.

During a U.S. Senate Energy and Natural Resources Public Lands, Forests, and Mining Subcommittee hearing to examine pending legislation, Heinrich brought attention to the Trump administration’s refusal to take public opinion into account prior to repealing the Roadless Rule.

In June 2025, Heinrich released a statement slamming USDA Secretary Rollins’ efforts to rescind the Roadless Rule.

title: Heinrich Statement on the 25th Anniversary of the September 11th Terrorist Attacks
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.) issued the following statement in recognition of the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks.

“Today, we honor and mourn all those who lost their lives at the World Trade Center, in the Pentagon, and in the fields of Western Pennsylvania. We honor the first responders and countless others who risked their lives or made the ultimate sacrifice to help neighbors and strangers in a moment of unfathomable tragedy.

“We remember the way our country came together, through the grief, with determined, united resilience. And we honor the military service members who served in Afghanistan, Iraq, and around the world in the years that followed, and the allies and interpreters who supported their work. We know the sacrifices of our service members, their families, and our allies extended far beyond the battlefield.

“Now, 25 years following the tragic events of September 11, 2001, we say again: We will never forget. We must always strive to carry the spirit of service, unity, and compassion we witnessed in New York, Virginia, and the skies above Pennsylvania on that day and across the country in the weeks that followed. And we will remember the heavy cost of endless wars as we strive to ensure that future generations do not bear the same burdens.”

title: Senator Justice Commemorates 25th Anniversary of September 11
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Senator Jim Justice released the following statement marking the 25th anniversary of September 11, 2001:

“It’s hard to believe twenty-five years have passed since that terrible day that changed our lives forever. Every year when this day comes around, my heart breaks all over again for the families who lost someone they loved—mothers, fathers, sons, daughters, and friends whose chairs at the dinner table have stayed empty far too long. But even in our darkest hour, America showed the world what we’re made of. We saw everyday folks step up in ways that bring tears to your eyes, and first responders run straight into harm’s way without giving it a second thought. That’s who we are. A quarter-century has passed, but our promise remains the same: we will never forget the lives taken from us, and we will never forget the quiet strength and goodness that brought us through. Cathy and I keep all those families in our prayers, and we ask God to watch over our first responders, our troops in uniform, and this great country we all love,” said Senator Jim Justice.

title: Kaine Statement On 25th Anniversary of September 11th Attacks
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Tim Kaine (D-VA), a member of the Senate Armed Services and Foreign Relations Committees, released the following statement in commemoration of the 25th anniversary of the terrorist attacks on September 11, 2001:

“This is a solemn anniversary for all Americans, but it’s especially close to home for the Commonwealth—nearly 200 people died that day at the Pentagon and aboard American Airlines Flight 77, and Virginia, as one of the most military-connected states in the country, had a disproportionate number of her sons and daughters deploy overseas after the attacks. Twenty-five years later, I’m praying for the families of the nearly 3,000 Americans who died, the first responders who heroically put themselves in harm’s way in the aftermath, the thousands of Americans who suffered disability or death because of the dangerous recovery work, the tens of thousands of servicemembers who answered the call and defended our nation in the War on Terror, and the millions of ordinary Americans who pulled together to try and help the nation heal. As Governor of Virginia, I went to the deployments, the homecomings, the funerals, and the wakes of many of our brave servicemembers—and it has made me even more dedicated to, as a U.S. Senator, ensure our veterans, servicemembers, and their families have the resources, health care, and benefits they have earned, to keep our nation secure, and to keep our troops from having to risk their lives unless absolutely necessary.”

title: Kelly Statement on the 25th Anniversary of 9/11
text:
U.S. Senator Mark Kelly (D-AZ) released the following statement on the 25th anniversary of the September 11th attacks on the World Trade Center:

“Twenty-five years ago,nearly 3,000people were killed in an act of terror. Today, we remember those we lost, their families, the first responders who showed extraordinary courage, and the thousands more whose lives were changed forever.

“I piloted the first Space Shuttle mission after 9/11, STS-108. Aboard Space Shuttle Endeavour, our crew carried three flags representing the places where lives were lost that day: an American flag recovered from Ground Zero, an American flag flown over the Pennsylvania State Capitol, and a U.S. Marine Corps Colors flag recovered from the Pentagon. We also carried thousands of smaller American flags and other tributes honoring those we had lost.

“I’llnever forget seeing those flags in orbit with the Earth behind them. Less than three months after the worst attack in history on American soil, carrying those flags was a powerful reminder of what our country had been through and what we stood for.

“In the face of unimaginable loss, Americans came together. We looked out for one another, honored those who served, and showed the world that an attack meant to divide and weaken us would not succeed.

“Twenty-five years later, that spirit of service, courage, and unity stillrepresentsthe best of America. It is something we should never take for granted.

title: Klobuchar, Smith Urge USPS to Reopen Glenville Post Office
text:
MINNESOTA – U.S. Senators Amy Klobuchar (D-MN) and Tina Smith (D-MN) are calling on the United States Postal Service (USPS) Minnesota-North Dakota District Manager to reopen the Post Office in Glenville, Minnesota. The Glenville Post Office closed after a vehicle struck the building on June 28, 2026. Since then, the Postal Service has not resumed operations or announced a reopening day.

“Minnesotans depend on the Postal Service every day,” wrote the Senators. “We urge you and the local postmaster to restore retail postal services to the Glenville community as quickly as possible and communicate clearly with the City of Glenville and postal customers about your timeline and progress in reopening the post office.”

The full letter is available here and below.

Dear District Manager Bye: We write to share concerns that we have received from Minnesota constituents regarding the continued closure of the Glenville Post Office at 220 W. Main Street in Glenville, Minnesota. We urge you and the local postmaster to restore retail postal services to the Glenville community as quickly as possible and communicate clearly with the City of Glenville and postal customers about your timeline and progress in reopening the post office.

The Glenville Post Office closed after a vehicle struck the building on June 28, 2026. More than ten weeks later, the Postal Service has not restored operations at this post office location and our constituents have informed me that the Postal Service has not announced a reopening date or communicated a plan to restore retail postal operations to local residents.

Many Glenville residents depend on their local Post Office every day. Local residents rely on PO boxes to retrieve their mail including prescriptions, Social Security benefits, paychecks, and bills. Post office closures make purchasing stamps, shipping packages, and accessing other retail services less accessible, which can especially impact small business operations that rely on the Postal Service to reach their customers. These postal customers must instead travel to a neighboring community’s post office, which is particularly burdensome for seniors and customers that lack transportation.

Please provide the following information:

What steps is the Postal Service taking to reopen the Glenville Post Office?

What is the expected timeline for restoring post office retail operations in Glenville?

How will the Postal Service ensure clear and frequent communication with Glenville postal customers and City of Glenville officials about the post office’s closure and all efforts to reopen the post office going forward?

Minnesotans depend on the Postal Service every day. We urge you to work with the local postmaster to promptly reopen the Glenville Post Office as soon as possible and keep residents and city officials informed throughout the process.

Thank you for your attention to this important matter.

###

title: Klobuchar Statement on the 25th Anniversary of 9/11
text:
MINNESOTA – U.S. Senator Amy Klobuchar (D-MN) issued the following statement on the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001 attacks:

“This year we mark 25 years since the 9/11 attacks, when nearly 3,000 innocent Americans were killed in an unspeakable act of evil.

We remember all the lives taken and we grieve with the families and friends who lost loved ones in New York, at the Pentagon, and in Shanksville, Pennsylvania. We also honor the courage of the first responders who risked their lives to save others, as well as the countless other acts of heroism and sacrifice we witnessed that day.

We remember the Minnesotans we lost that day: Tom Burnett Jr. from Bloomington, Gordon Aamoth Jr. from Wayzata, Gary Koecheler from St. Paul, and Max Beilke from Alexandria.

Tom, along with his fellow passengers on Flight 93, bravely gave his life to save others. Gordon was a 32-year-old former captain of his high school football team who had a bright future ahead of him, and Gary was a Vietnam War veteran who had been awarded the Bronze Star. They both worked in the South Tower of the World Trade Center. Max died in the Pentagon after dedicating his entire life to our country, serving in Korea and Vietnam, and advocating on behalf of veterans and their families at the Pentagon.

Let us always remember all whose lives were taken on that September day 25 years ago and those whose lives were cut short in the years that followed. We honor their memories by cherishing the values we share as Americans.

Let us carry forward the spirit of courage, generosity, and shared purpose that our country showed in the days that followed. We will never forget.”

title: Lankford Celebrates State’s Largest Federal Transportation Grant with Roosevelt Bridge Groundbreaking
text:
OKLAHOMA CITY, OK — US Senator James Lankford (R-OK) joined Federal Highway Administrator Sean McMaster, Oklahoma Secretary of Transportation and Executive Director of the Oklahoma Department of Transportation Tim Gatz, and state and local leaders in Marshall County on Thursday to celebrate the groundbreaking of the $409 million Roosevelt Bridge Project replacing the more than 80-year-old section of US-70 spanning Lake Texoma between Durant and Kingston.

“After years of working with the Department of Transportation to obtain federal funding, I’m grateful to have secured the largest transportation grant in Oklahoma history for this project,” said Lankford. “This is a historic investment in Southern Oklahoma that will ensure safer, more reliable travel for school buses, truck drivers, families, and tourists that cross Lake Texoma every day.”

The Roosevelt Memorial Bridge over Lake Texoma connects Southern Oklahoma from east to west. Originally built in 1942 under the Roosevelt Administration, the bridge has become functionally obsolete and is at risk of deteriorating and becoming structurally deficient. The bridge carries 12,000 vehicles per day, and while either side is a four-lane highway, the bridge remains two lanes with no shoulders, which leads to bottlenecks and higher collision rates.

“The groundbreaking of the US-70 Roosevelt Bridge replacement project marks a monumental milestone for southeastern Oklahoma and our neighbors in Texas and Arkansas whose lives and economies rely upon this critical corridor,” said Tim Gatz, Oklahoma Secretary of Transportation and Executive Director of the Oklahoma Department of Transportation. “A project of this magnitude would never be possible without the support of our federal delegation, including Senator Lankford, and the $124 million Federal Bridge Investment Program grant that covers roughly 30 percent of this project’s cost. We are also grateful to Governor Stitt, our legislature and many state partners who are helping bring this important project to life.”

In July 2024, Lankford announced the Federal Highway Administration had awarded ODOT $123.85 million in federal funding for the Roosevelt Bridge project, the largest federal transportation grant in Oklahoma history. This is one of 19 projects nationwide awarded a Bridge Investment Program – Large Bridge Project grant. The existing bridge will stay open for travelers during construction, with the new bridge expected to open in Fall of 2029.

title: McConnell on 25th Anniversary of 9/11 Attacks
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senator Mitch McConnell (R-KY) released the following statement today on the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 terrorist attacks on the United States:

“Today, I remember the clouds of dust that filled clear blue skies twenty-five years ago, stealing away fathers, mothers, sons, daughters, brothers, sisters, friends and colleagues. And I remember the faraway battlefields that claimed thousands more in the years that followed.

“My deepest sympathies today are with those Americans for whom the grief of September 11th is not abstract but personal and unrelenting. Time will continue to ease our nation’s shared pain, but it will never fill empty seats at family tables. And so those who continue to carry the heaviest burdens of that day and its aftermath must remain in our prayers.

“But on top of remembrance and sympathy rests another national responsibility every bit as important: to give weight to the words Never Again. From the smoke and rubble of 9/11 came lessons about the fragility of our nation’s security and what it takes to preserve it. We paid for these lessons with thousands of precious American lives. If we are still resolved never again to pay such a price, we must look with clear eyes at a dangerous world and redouble our efforts to outcompete those who would do us harm.”

title: Merkley Statement on 25th Anniversary of September 11 Terrorist Attacks
text:
Washington, D.C. – Oregon’s U.S. Senator Jeff Merkley released the following statement in remembrance of the terrorist attacks on September 11, 2001:

“I will never forget that day 25 years ago: the clear blue morning sky, the billowing black smoke, the clouds of white ash, and everywhere, the confusion and fear. Our nation watched in shock and horror as an unprecedented act of terrorism on Americans was carried out in cold blood. Nearly 3,000 people were taken from us, including courageous first responders who raced toward danger to save others.

“But alongside the devastation, we witnessed extraordinary acts of courage and compassion. Police officers, firefighters, and rescue workers put their lives on the line for strangers. Passengers aboard Flight 93 fought back against the hijackers. Across the country, neighbors reached out to one another, gathering in communities and at candlelight vigils to share their grief and offer comfort. While facing unimaginable tragedy, Americans came together. The divisions that so often separate us fell away as people helped one another simply because help was needed.

“September 11 will always be a solemn day of remembrance. We honor the irreplaceable lives lost, the families and loved ones who continue to carry those losses, and all those whose bravery and service offered hope amid darkness.

“On this anniversary, we hold those memories close and renew our commitment to one another. The spirit of service, community, and common purpose we witnessed that day and the days that followed remains a powerful reminder of what we can accomplish when we come together. May we continue striving to build a country worthy of the sacrifice of those we lost, guided by the enduring values of freedom, equality, justice, and care for our fellow Americans.”

title: Senator Murray’s Statement on the 25th Anniversary of 9/11
text:
Washington, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senator Patty Murray (D-WA) issued the following statement on the 25th anniversary of the attacks on 9/11.

“Today, on the twenty fifth anniversary of September 11th , we remember the innocent lives that were taken from us, and we pause to honor the bravery and selflessness of every single person who stepped up in the face of unthinkable tragedy. We will never forget the loved ones we lost, the courage of our first responders and servicemembers—nor will we forget how our country came together with an outpouring of unity in the aftermath to grieve and heal together. title: WATCH: Sen. Ossoff Commemorates 25th Anniversary of September 11th Terrorist Attacks
