title: Elfreth, Scott, Wittman, Kiggans Celebrate House Passage of Chesapeake Bay WATERS Act
text:
WASHINGTON, DC –Today, Congresswoman Sarah Elfreth (MD-03) and Representatives Bobby Scott (VA-03), Rob Wittman (VA-01), and Jennifer Kiggans (VA-02) secured House of passage of H.R. 6893, the Chesapeake Bay Watershed Advancement for Training, Education, Restoration, and Science (WATERS) Act. This legislation reauthorizes key programs at the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration’s (NOAA) Chesapeake Bay Office (CBO). Senator Mark Warner (D-VA) has introduced companion legislation in the Senate.

NOAA’s CBO provides a variety of services that advance the restoration of the Bay and support local businesses, schools, and coastal resilience. CBO manages the Chesapeake Bay Interpretive Buoy System which collects water quality, meteorological, and oceanographic data used by scientists, fisherman and those recreating on the Bay. CBO also oversees the Chesapeake Bay Watershed Education and Training (B-WET) program, a competitive grant program for environmental education projects that connect students throughout the watershed with the Bay. The Chesapeake Bay WATERS Act authorizes the Chesapeake Bay B-WET program for the first time in the program’s history.

“I am incredibly proud to represent the NOAA Chesapeake Bay Office, which conducts critical scientific research and programming to restore the health and habitat of the whole Chesapeake Bay watershed. I was thrilled to see my colleagues come together on the House floor today to pass the Chesapeake Bay WATERS Act to ensure this office is properly resourced and – for the first time ever – authorize the Bay Watershed Education and Training (B-WET) program to support hands-on outdoor learning for students,” said Congresswoman Elfreth. “If you talk to folks back in Annapolis, they will describe the Bay as ‘transcending politics’ and that it’s ‘like a religion.’ I couldn’t agree more. That is why I will continue to work collaboratively with our partners – Democrat and Republican alike – to ensure the Bay can be enjoyed for generations to come.”

“The Chesapeake Bay is a national treasure and a critical resource for the millions of Americans that live within its watershed,” said Congressman Scott. “NOAA’s Chesapeake Bay Office is essential to ensuring that government, industry, and nonprofits have the technical and scientific information necessary to improve the health of the Bay. This office also oversees the successful Chesapeake B-WET Program that has connected countless students to hands-on, environmental education programming throughout the watershed. Today’s passage of the Chesapeake Bay WATERS Act is a major step towards ensuring that this office can continue supporting the restoration of the Bay and connecting future generations with the environment around them.”

“As a lifelong outdoorsman, vice chairman of the House Committee on Natural Resources, and co-chair of the Chesapeake Bay Watershed Task Force, I am proud to have co-led this bipartisan effort to protect the Chesapeake Bay,” said Congressman Wittman. “The Chesapeake Bay WATERS Act would ensure that the Chesapeake Bay remains healthy for generations to come — protecting our coastal economies and preserving a national treasure. I will continue to advocate for this legislation as it moves to the Senate.”

“The Chesapeake Bay is vital to the coastal communities, local economies, and natural resources we are fortunate to have in Virginia,” said Congresswoman Kiggans. “The Chesapeake Bay WATERS Act ensures NOAA can continue providing the research, restoration support, and educational opportunities needed to keep the Bay healthy and thriving. I’m proud to have worked alongside my colleagues on both sides of the aisle to pass this legislation through the House, and I’ll continue working to see it signed into law.”

“NOAA’s Chesapeake Bay Office is central to the Bay restoration effort, from providing essential water quality monitoring data, to supporting our understanding and management of our fisheries, to fostering a greater appreciation of the Bay through environmental education,” said Anna Killius, Executive Director of the Chesapeake Bay Commission. “Passing the Chesapeake Bay WATERS Act will ensure these critical functions continue and uphold a strong, science-based foundation for the work of the Chesapeake Bay Program partnership.”

“A healthier Chesapeake Bay starts with science, restoration, and education. This legislation does all three by supporting NOAA’s Chesapeake Bay Office and Bay Watershed Education and Training program,” said Keisha Sedlacek, Senior Policy Director for the Chesapeake Bay Foundation. “These programs lead research and restoration work that create cleaner waterways, support fisheries and local economies, and build resiliency to climate change. Education grants allow thousands of kids to learn hands-on outside, building future leaders. We applaud the House and the leadership of Reps. Bobby Scott, Sarah Elfreth, Jen Kiggans, and Rob Wittman for advancing the Chesapeake Bay WATERS Act. We urge swift action from the Senate.”

“The Choose Clean Water Coalition wholeheartedly endorses the Chesapeake WATERS Act, which reauthorizes NOAA’s Chesapeake Bay Office (NCBO),” said Kristin Reilly, Director of the Choose Clean Water Coalition. “Many federal agencies play a critical role in restoring the Chesapeake Bay, and NCBO plays a critical role. They are a leader in restoring the Bay’s oyster population, protecting striped bass and other native species from the onslaught of invasive blue catfish, and helping steward the next generation through outdoor education experiences. It is vital they receive continued support as we enter the next chapter of the Bay restoration effort.”

title: Rep. Estes Introduces Legislation to Prevent Fraudulent IRS Returns
text:
U.S. Representatives Ron Estes (R-Kansas) and Jimmy Panetta (D-California) introduced legislation on Thursday to help prevent the submission of fraudulent IRS returns before they are filed. The legislation verifies that Electronic Filing Identification Numbers (EFIN), which identify who submitted the return to the IRS, are active and authorized in the software before e-file functionality is enabled.

“The EFIN Verification Act of 2026 will reduce the risk of fraudsters using stolen or compromised EFIN numbers to file IRS returns,” said Rep. Estes. “By preventing fraudulent IRS returns from being filed with EFIN verification, this legislation will maintain the integrity of our tax system, prevent scams before they happen, and codify an already-existing IRS program into law.”

“Tax preparation firms play an important role in helping working Americans file their tax returns electronically, but the IRS currently lacks the tools to authenticate their Electronic Filing Identification Numbers. This security gap leaves those numbers vulnerable to theft and misuse by online scammers,” said Rep. Panetta. “I’m proud to co-lead this bipartisan legislation with Rep. Estes to require the IRS to establish an EFIN verification system that will strengthen security, reduce fraud, and protect taxpayers’ hard-earned money.”

title: Rep. Evans, SEPTA Announce $80 Million Federal Grant for Trolley Station ADA Improvements
text:
PHILADELPHIA (September 14, 2026) – Today, U.S. Rep. Dwight Evans (D-PA-3) and the Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Authority (SEPTA) announced that SEPTA has been awarded $80 million in federal All Stations Accessibility Program (ASAP) funding to make three stations in the Center City Trolley Tunnel fully accessible.

“When we invest in our public transit accessibility, we invest in our community,” said Rep Evans. “That’s why I was proud to help establish this vital grant program through President Biden’s historic Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act and fight for SEPTA to receive this critical federal funding. It will increase accessibility at stations throughout Philadelphia- improving the transit experience for all riders."

“Ensuring that every customer can access transit service that is safe, clean and reliable is a core part of SEPTA’s mission,” said SEPTA Board Chair Kenneth E. Lawrence Jr. “Station accessibility projects like those this grant will fund are critically important to that effort. I want to thank our Congressional delegation for establishing this vital program and working to support our application.”

ASAP funding will allow SEPTA to construct accessibility improvements at 22nd Street, 33rd Street and 36th Street T Stations, which are all located in Philadelphia’s 3rd Congressional District, in the Center City Trolley Tunnel. Originally built in 1955, these three stations are only accessible via stairs, preventing individuals with disabilities that require the use of a mobility device, families with strollers, or anyone who is physically unable to use stairs from traveling to and from these destinations. The projects will bring the stations into full compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). Each station will be retrofitted with elevators connecting street level to the underground boarding areas. Raised platforms and other enhancements will also be constructed to accommodate the new fleet of low-floor streetcars that SEPTA is procuring as part of Trolley Modernization.

“Accessibility is critical for SEPTA and our riders,” said SEPTA General Manager Scott A. Sauer. “Across the SEPTA system, we are currently advancing more than a dozen Metro and Regional Rail station accessibility projects that will greatly improve the customer experience. This major ASAP grant will expand our capacity to deliver these critical improvements, and we are grateful for the FTA’s confidence in our program in awarding this grant.”

This is SEPTA’s second ASAP grant. The Authority was previously awarded $56 million to support ADA station improvement projects at five Metro stations. At Erie Station on the B, SEPTA became the first transit agency in the nation to advance to construction on an ASAP-funded project. Last month, SEPTA broke ground on a $44 million ASAP-funded accessibility project at 11th Street Station on the L.

“This investment is a win for every Philadelphia resident who relies on safe, accessible, and modern public transportation,” said Mayor Cherelle L. Parker. “Making the T stations at 22nd, 33rd, and 36th Streets fully accessible is more than an infrastructure upgrade. It’s a commitment to equity, and ensuring Philadelphians can visit family and friends, attend school or get to work. I am proud that with our partners at the Federal Transit Administration and SEPTA, we are building a transit system that serves everyone.”

“This money will make all the difference for our seniors, for Pennsylvanians with disabilities and for anyone who relies on SEPTA,” said U.S. Sen. John Fetterman (D-PA). “I’m proud of the steps SEPTA has already taken to make its system more accessible for all riders, and I’m grateful for the FTA’s support of this important work.”

“This $80 million investment is a major win for SEPTA riders and will help make three of Philadelphia’s trolley stations more accessible for all Pennsylvanians who rely on public transportation,” said U.S. Sen. Dave McCormick (R-PA). “I’m committed to reauthorizing the All Stations Accessibility Program along with Senator Duckworth to ensure this important program continues delivering for communities in Pennsylvania and across the country.”

Evans represents the 3rd Congressional District, which includes Northwest and West Philadelphia and parts of North, South, Southwest and Center City Philadelphia. Evans’ website is evans.house.gov and his social media handle is @RepDwightEvans on Youtube, Bluesky, Facebook, Twitter, Instagram and Threads.

title: Finstad Calls on Department of Justice to Investigate Hennepin County Attorney’s Office Following Recent Minneapolis Shooting
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congressman Brad Finstad (MN-01) led Congressman Pete Stauber (MN-08) and Congresswoman Michelle Fischbach (MN-07) in sending a letter to U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche and the Department of Justice calling for a review of the Hennepin County Attorney’s Office and Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty following the lack of legal action taken prior to the September 2, 2026 shooting in downtown Minneapolis that left two people dead and several others injured, including two law enforcement officers.

The suspected shooter, Carlton Johnson II, had a well-established history of violence, including threatening a resident at his apartment building, brandishing a firearm, and sexually assaulting and threatening a woman. In total, Johnson had accumulated 34 criminal cases in Minnesota, spanning more than a decade. The lack of legal action taken by the Hennepin County Attorney’s Office leading up to the tragic event on September 2nd raises serious concerns about what investigative and prosecutorial procedures were followed.

The letter reads:

“Dear U.S. Attorney General Blanche,

“We are writing to strongly request that the Department of Justice review the circumstances surrounding the Hennepin County Attorney’s Office, particularly Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty, and the lack of legal action taken involving Carlton Johnson II, the suspect of the September 2, 2026, Minneapolis shooting that left two people dead and several others injured, including law enforcement officers.

“Leading up to this tragic event, Hennepin County prosecutors declined to bring charges against Carlton Johnson II after he threatened a resident at the Shoreline Plaza building and brandished a firearm back in June of this year. The office claimed there was “insufficient evidence to prove a charge beyond a reasonable doubt.” In 2023, Johnson sexually assaulted and threatened a woman and in response she filed a restraining order against him. In total, Johnson had accumulated 34 separate criminal cases in the Twin Cities. The blatant lack of legal action taken by the Hennepin County Attorney’s Office that subsequently led to the Minneapolis shooting, raises serious questions about whether appropriate investigative and prosecutorial procedures were followed.

“This is not the first case where the Hennepin County Attorney’s Office, led by Mary Moriarty, poorly exercised their prosecutorial discretion. In 2024, we sent a letter to Governor Tim Walz regarding our concerns about her prosecution of Minnesota State Patrol Trooper Ryan Londregan. Ms. Moriarty weaponized her position against law enforcement and ignored an independent use-of-force expert chosen by her own office, who stated that Trooper Londregan acted as a “reasonable officer” would have. After many months, Ms. Moriarty came to the same conclusion as the experts did and dropped all charges against Trooper Londregan. These cases show a pattern of poor prosecutorial discretion by Ms. Moriarty and undermine confidence in the fair and impartial administration of justice.

“We respectfully request that the Department of Justice review the actions of the Hennepin County Attorney’s Office regarding Carlton Johnson II and his violent past leading up to the Minneapolis shooting. When credible warnings are shown and brought to authorities, it is their responsibility to act, Ms. Moriarty’s dismissal of charges has led to injured law enforcement officers and the loss of Minnesotans.

“Thank you for your attention to this important matter. We look forward to your response and do not hesitate to contact our offices if we can be of further assistance.

“Sincerely,

Brad Finstad, Member of Congress

Pete Stauber, Member of Congress

title: Rep. Fitzgerald Chairs Judiciary Subcommittee Field Hearing on Obamacare Waste, Fraud, & Abuse
text:
CHARLOTTE, NC – Today, Congressman Scott Fitzgerald (WI-05), who serves as Chairman of the House Judiciary Subcommittee on the Administrative State, Regulatory Reform, and Antitrust, held a field hearing in North Carolina titled, “Examining Healthcare Markets: Fraud and Competition.” Rep. Fitzgerald issued the following statement about the hearing:

“I think we can all agree that there is something wrong with the American healthcare system. The price of care is sky high, in part because of the design of, and rampant fraud occurring in, the Obamacare insurance system.

“Obamacare promised affordable healthcare for Americans. But it has not lived up to that promise. The price of Obamacare plans has increased at twice the rate of employer-sponsored plans. Instead of doing something about the artificially inflated prices, the Biden Administration just handed out more subsidies.

“To add insult to injury, because the Obamacare system does not trust Americans to make decisions about their own healthcare coverage, those subsidies go straight into the pockets of insurance companies instead of the American people.

“In the Working Families Tax Cuts bill, Republicans prevented illegal aliens from receiving premium tax credits. We also removed the cap on repayments to the federal government for excessive subsidies and added stricter eligibility verification to ensure people do not receive generous subsidies before their eligibility is determined.

“I also supported the Lower Health Care Premiums for All Americans Act that passed the House late last year. House Republicans recognize that we cannot keep writing blank checks for heavily subsidized programs that continue to drive up costs.

“While we have taken huge steps in the right direction, Congress must build on that progress to protect taxpayers, crack down on fraud, and ensure these subsidies go to people who are actually eligible.

“That’s exactly why we gathered in North Carolina for this field hearing, to gather additional solutions. North Carolina has redefined its healthcare industry through investments in cutting-edge tech and research hubs, as well as a statewide rural health transformation program. As a result, the state has received national rankings in healthcare innovation and quality.”

Watch Congressman Fitzgerald's opening statement from the hearing:

Background: This hearing examined how mergers, certificate of need laws, regulations, vertical integration, and insurance fraud are affecting healthcare access and affordability across the United States. The hearing also reviewed how Obamacare subsidies inflate healthcare costs and create an environment ripe for waste, fraud, and abuse.

title: Rep. Frost: Federal Watchdog Confirms Reports of Inhumane Conditions at “Alligator Alcatraz”
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman Maxwell Alejandro Frost (FL-10) released the following statement after a Department of Homeland Security Inspector General report confirmed that detainees at the now-shuttered “Alligator Alcatraz” were held in outdoor metal cages as small as 16 square feet for extended periods of time:

“Today’s report confirms what we already knew: what happened at Alligator Alcatraz was disgusting, inhumane, and a stain on Florida’s history.

I saw those conditions with my own eyes. I went to Alligator Alcatraz twice, and before both visits, I was specifically told to see “the cage” in the recreation area — including that there had been blood inside it. Both times, I was assured the cages were no longer being used. Now we know that wasn’t true. The federal government’s own watchdog confirmed that people were being held in outdoor metal cages barely larger than a telephone booth, sometimes for nearly two hours.

This does not end with Alligator Alcatraz. People in ICE custody across America are still facing horrific conditions. I will continue conducting oversight at facilities across Florida and demanding answers.”

title: Rep. Fry Calls for Suspension of Federal Gas Tax
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Representative Russell Fry (SC-07) announced that he will introduce legislation to temporarily suspend the federal gas tax and provide immediate relief to American families.

“Whether you’re a parent driving to work, a farmer putting crops in the ground, a rancher feeding livestock, or a small business owner just trying to keep your doors open, you feel the impact of high fuel prices,” said Rep. Fry. “Relief should start where Americans feel it the most—at the pump and in our budgets. Temporarily suspending the federal gas tax will give American families much needed breathing room. I am proud to lead efforts in Congress to provide this relief and put money back in the pockets of American families.”

Under current law, the federal government collects an 18-cent-per-gallon tax on gasoline and a 24-cent-per-gallon tax on diesel fuel. Rep. Fry is drafting and introducing legislation that would temporarily suspend both taxes to provide relief amid rising fuel prices nationwide. President Trump and Energy Secretary Chris Wright are supportive of efforts to lower prices at the pump and have called on Congress to suspend the gas tax temporarily. The legislation is anticipated to be formally introduced in the coming days.

title: Rep. Gillen Presents Five Recovered Service Medals and Decorations Awarded to Late Garden City Veteran to His Family
text:
GARDEN CITY, NY — Congresswoman Laura Gillen (NY-04) presented Nicholas Maggio and his family with five medals and decorations earned by Nicholas’ grandfather, Private Angelo A. Maggio from Garden City, for his service in the U.S. Army in Germany following World War II. The medals and decorations recognize Private Maggio’s honorable service, military proficiency and exemplary conduct during his time in the Army.

"Our veterans have made extraordinary sacrifices in service to our country. Their legacy deserves to be remembered," said Rep. Gillen. "It is my privilege to reunite Nicholas Maggio and his family with his late grandfather's prestigious medals and decorations, which he earned for his exceptional military service after World War II during the occupation of Germany. We owe a debt of gratitude to everyone who has worn the uniform and served our nation. I’m honored to present these medals and work every day on behalf of our veterans and their families."

“Receiving my grandfather’s medals is a meaningful way to honor his life, service, and memory,” said grandson of Angelo Maggio, Nicholas Maggio. “Our family will display them alongside his flag and pass them down to future generations. Two of his grandchildren, my sister Angelina and I, were named after him, and we are proud to carry on his name. I will always remember how he slept in a chair so I could be comfortable when I was afraid, and how he chased our school bus to wave goodbye. These memories reflect the loving, dependable, and devoted person he was. His wisdom, honesty, and strength continue to influence our family. We are deeply grateful to Laura Gillen’s office for helping us recover his medals, which we will treasure for generations to come.”

Born in Pietrapertosa, Italy, Angelo Maggio immigrated to the United States and served in the military from 1954 to 1956, followed by six years in the Army Reserve. In 1970, he settled in Elmhurst, Queens, where he worked and raised his family. Angelo later moved to Garden City in 1998.

When Nicholas reached out for assistance, Rep. Gillen’s office worked closely with him to navigate the National Archives and Records Administration and recover the medals and decorations.

The five commendations awarded to Angelo Maggio included:

Good Conduct Medal: Awarded for exemplary conduct, efficiency and fidelity during a qualifying period of active military service.

Army of Occupation Medal with Germany Clasp: Recognizes qualifying occupation duty in Germany following World War II.

National Defense Service Medal: Awarded for honorable active service during a designated period of national emergency or armed conflict.

Expert Badge with Carbine Bar: Recognizes qualification at the Army’s highest marksmanship level with a carbine rifle.

Sharpshooter Badge with Pistol Bar: Recognizes qualification at the Army’s intermediate marksmanship level with a pistol.

Rep. Gillen’s office is committed to helping residents of New York’s Fourth congressional district navigate federal agencies and access the benefits and services they are owed. Contact Rep. Gillen’s office for assistance with veterans' benefits, replacing or obtaining lost military service medals, Social Security, immigration matters, IRS issues or other issues with federal agencies.

title: PHOTO RELEASE: Following Labor Day, Gottheimer Hosts Roundtable with Local Labor Leaders
text:
Above: Gottheimer meeting with North Jersey labor leaders.

PARAMUS, NJ — U.S. Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) hosted a roundtable with North Jersey labor leaders to discuss his ongoing work to help create jobs, lower costs, and support the hard-working men and women of labor. The roundtable was held at the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers (IBEW) Local 164.

Gottheimer and North Jersey labor leaders discussed affordability, future of AI, next generation of workers, health care costs, rising taxes, and Gottheimer’s continued work in Washington to support Jersey families.

Watch video from his event here.

“I’m proud to stand with North Jersey and our hardworking families,” said Congressman Gottheimer (NJ-5). “Labor unions helped build this state, this country, and create the most competitive workforce in the world. I’ll keep fighting in Washington for better wages, safer working conditions, more job opportunities, and the dignity and respect every worker has earned.”

Gottheimer fighting to support Jersey’s workforce:

Gottheimer helped write, negotiate, and pass the Bipartisan Infrastructure Bill, delivering more than $10 billion to fix Jersey’s crumbling roads and bridges and creating hundreds of thousands of construction and manufacturing jobs — all without increasing the tax burden on our families.

Gottheimer also fought hard for strong Davis-Bacon protections in the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, ensuring that unions can compete for infrastructure contracts and that workers are well-paid.

Gottheimer voted against the One Big Beautiful Bill to protect tens of thousands of good-paying union jobs.

As Co-Chair of the Bipartisan Law Enforcement Caucus, Gottheimer introduced and is fighting to pass the Invest to Protect Act, which makes critical, targeted investments in our local police departments.

Gottheimer has announced the Fight Fires and Fight Cancer Act to stop extremists from recklessly slashing programs that support firefighters’ safety, training, and health care.

Gottheimer introduced and is fighting to pass the bipartisan FIRE Cancer Act to provide federal investments so that all firefighters across America — whether volunteer or professional — can get access to preventative tests, including multi-cancer early detection tests.

As Co-Chair of the bipartisan Problem Solvers Caucus, Gottheimer helped get the Social Security Fairness Act signed into law to ensure workers can get their full public sector pension and Social Security benefits.

Gottheimer helped introduce the bicameral FAMILY Act to guarantee up to 12 weeks of paid leave for workers who have to take leave for serious medical and family events.

Gottheimer helped introduce the Protect America’s Workforce Act, which reverses an Executive Order from the current Administration that would eliminate collective bargaining rights across multiple federal agencies.

Gottheimer supports the Faster Labor Contracts Act, a bipartisan piece of legislation that will speed up the collective bargaining process for newly unionized workers and their employers.

Gottheimer helped introduce the bicameral Public Service Freedom to Negotiate Act, which guarantees the right of public service employees to organize and bargain collectively, regardless of state law.

Gottheimer helped introduce the Tax Fairness for Workers Act, which allows union members to deduct their dues from their taxes.

As Co-Chair of the House Commission on Artificial Intelligence and the Innovation Economy, Gottheimer introduced and is fighting for the bipartisan AI Workforce Training Act to help American workers and businesses prepare for the rapid integration of artificial intelligence across the economy.

title: Rep. Hageman Honors America’s Truck Drivers
text:
Washington, D.C. - Congresswoman Harriet Hageman (R-WY) introduced a resolution supporting the designation of the week of September 13 through September 19, 2026, as “National Truck Driver Appreciation Week.”

Truck drivers move nearly 70% of all freight in the United States, carrying everything from lumber to life-saving medication across the country's highways. Rep. Hageman’s resolution thanks the 3.6 million Americans who drive for hours on end to keep supply chains strong, enabling an unprecedented era of abundance.

“Americans everywhere have truckers to thank for the ability to buy the same goods almost anywhere,” said Rep. Hageman. “They haul our cattle, stock our stores, and serve the small towns that no other form of transportation can reach with year-round deliveries of the raw material of the 21st century. This resolution says thank you and builds on the work I am already doing in Congress to crack down on bad actors compromising opportunities for the American truck driver.”

“OOIDA is proud to represent nearly 150,000 small-business truckers across America who thanklessly serve as the backbone of this country’s supply chain every single day and night. Over 70% of freight in the United States moves exclusively by truck, the majority of which are mom-and-pop operations. We applaud the leadership of Representative Hageman for consistently demonstrating her appreciation for truckers by authoring bills to crack down on unsafe chameleon carriers and to safely bring new truckers into our industry. We believe every trucker in America deserves to have that kind of force behind them and we look forward to continuing to work with Representative Hageman and her like-minded colleagues who fight for truckers every day in Congress, not just this week,” stated Owner-Operator Independent Drivers Association President Todd Spencer.

“Whenever we click ‘add to cart’ or pick up an item from the store shelf, our first impulse should be to feel gratitude for America’s 3.6 million truck drivers who perform the logistical feats necessary to get us the items we want on a daily basis,” said Greg Hodgen, Chairman of American Trucking Associations and CEO of Groendyke Transport, Inc. “National Truck Driver Appreciation Week provides all Americans with the opportunity to give truck drivers the recognition and gratitude they richly deserve. ATA commends Reps. Hageman, Taylor, Figures, and Gillen for leading Congress’ tribute to these hardworking men and women. Truck drivers’ extraordinary dedication, professionalism, attention to detail, and skill are the keys to keeping our roads safe and our country moving.”

“Truck drivers do far more than move freight. They keep Wyoming communities supplied, our energy and agricultural industries working, and our entire economy moving. Recognition will never fully repay the long days, time away from family, and tremendous responsibility these professionals carry, but it matters. On behalf of the Wyoming Trucking Association, I thank Congresswoman Hageman for making sure America’s truck drivers receive the respect and national recognition they have earned,” stated Kevin Hawley, President and CEO, Wyoming Trucking Association.

“National Truck Driver Appreciation Week provides an important opportunity to recognize the professional truck drivers who keep America’s economy and supply chain moving. Rep. Hageman’s resolution highlights the vital contributions of these men and women, as well as their unwavering commitment to safety, reliability, and service each day. NTTC thanks Rep. Hageman for her leadership and joins in honoring America’s truck drivers for their dedication and the essential role they play in our nation,” stated Ryan Streblow, CEO, National Tank Truck Carriers.

“Because of Congresswoman Harriet Hageman’s leadership, Wyoming has been a champion for restoring American safety standards on our roadways and for protecting the wages and jobs of law-abiding, safe American trucking companies and their truck drivers. She truly shows her appreciation each and every day,” stated Shannon Everett, Executive Director, American Truckers United.

“TCA applauds Congresswoman Harriet Hageman for introducing a resolution recognizing America's professional truck drivers during National Truck Driver Appreciation Week. Professional truck drivers are essential to our nation's economy, safely delivering the goods that keep families, businesses, hospitals, and communities running. Their dedication, professionalism, and commitment to safety ensure the strength and resilience of America's supply chain. TCA proudly supports this resolution and thanks Congresswoman Hageman for highlighting the essential contributions of America's professional truck drivers,” stated Dave Heller, Senior Vice President of Safety and Government Affairs, Truckload Carriers Association.

title: REP. HARRIS: FIVE YEARS AFTER THE ADIRIM MANDATORY VACCINE MEMO, PUT HER UNDER OATH
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congressman Andy Harris, M.D., physician and former Naval Reserve medical officer, calls on Chairman James Comer, Chairman Rand Paul, and Chairman Ron Johnson to bring Dr. Terry Adirim in to testify under oath. Five years ago today, September 14, 2021, Dr. Terry Adirim, then acting Assistant Secretary of Defense for Health Affairs, signed the memorandum that told DoD providers they “will” use EUA-labeled product interchangeably with fully approved vaccines to vaccinate the force.¹

Three weeks earlier, on August 24, 2021, Secretary Austin had limited the mandate to vaccines with full FDA licensure, “in accordance with FDA-approved labeling and guidance.”² But because of the subsequent Adirim memorandum, our troops now call September 14 “Reign of Terry” day. Rep. Andy Harris, M.D. (R-Md) said Congress should treat the anniversary the way the force already does: as the anniversary of the day that two-page order left her desk, with serious and dire results.

Harris is a Johns Hopkins-trained anesthesiologist and former Naval Reserve medical officer. In March 2021 he administered COVID shots at clinics in his district. That spring the GOP Doctors Caucus agreed that you should talk to your physician and decide. He said then what he said in April 2023 and is saying again: freedom to choose to be COVID vaccinated, not mandates—and the more than 8,400 troops fired for refusing should have been reinstated.

“I know the difference between a clinical recommendation and an order with a discharge packet attached,” Harris said. “I would never tell a healthy infantryman his career depended on an EUA vial. The record since does not let us pretend it was just ‘following the science.’”

The regulator (the FDA) said should. Her memo said will.¹ It cited no statute, no presidential waiver, no legal analysis—only a footnote to an FDA web page. Under 10 U.S.C. § 1107a, a warrior given an EUA product must be told he can refuse. title: Comisionado Residente anuncia $882,000 de FEMA para atender daños causados por la tormenta Ernesto en Puerto Rico
text:
WASHINGTON D.C. — El Comisionado Residente de Puerto Rico, Pablo José Hernández, anunció la asignación de $882,625.47 en fondos de la Agencia Federal para el Manejo de Emergencias (FEMA) para atender daños y necesidades de emergencia provocados por la tormenta tropical Ernesto.

De los fondos asignados, $299,767.20 serán destinados a la Autoridad de Energía Eléctrica (AEE) para trabajos de medidas de protección de emergencia dirigidos a atender amenazas inmediatas a la salud pública, la seguridad y la propiedad ocasionadas por la tormenta.

Los restantes $582,858.27 serán destinados al Municipio de San Lorenzo para tres proyectos de reparación de infraestructura vial. Estos incluyen:

$234,891.15 para la reparación o reemplazo de subbase, superficie, terraplén y otros componentes viales.

$204,311.73 para la reparación o reemplazo de superficies de carreteras, terraplenes, paseos y componentes relacionados.

$143,655.39 para la reparación o reemplazo de alcantarillas y componentes relacionados de las carreteras.

“Estos fondos permiten atender daños concretos y seguir reconstruyendo nuestra infraestructura. Voy a seguir trabajando para que los recursos federales que Puerto Rico necesita lleguen a nuestras comunidades y se conviertan en obras”, expresó Hernández.

Los fondos corresponden a la declaración federal de desastre FEMA-DR-4850-PR, relacionada con la tormenta tropical Ernesto, y fueron autorizados bajo las secciones 403 y 406 de la Ley Stafford. FEMA obliga los fondos al Gobierno de Puerto Rico, que posteriormente revisa y reembolsa a las entidades que realizan los trabajos elegibles.

La asignación representa recursos federales dirigidos a atender necesidades específicas de infraestructura y emergencia tras el paso de la tormenta Ernesto.

title: Comisionado Residente exige acción de Vivienda Federal ante fondos estancados para la recuperación de la red eléctrica
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — El Comisionado Residente Pablo José Hernández exigió al Departamento de Vivienda y Desarrollo Urbano de Estados Unidos (HUD) a través de una carta, que acelere el desembolso de aproximadamente $1.7 billones en fondos federales destinados a la recuperación y modernización de la red eléctrica de Puerto Rico, mientras decenas de proyectos de generación continúan enfrentando obstáculos financieros, burocráticos y técnicos.

La petición surge tras los hallazgos de la Oficina de Responsabilidad Gubernamental de Estados Unidos (GAO), que encontró que 74% de los fondos de HUD obligados desde 2017 para la recuperación de la red eléctrica de Puerto Rico permanecen sin desembolsar. El informe identificó, entre otros obstáculos, la rotación de personal y congelaciones de contratación que han retrasado la revisión de proyectos, la complejidad del financiamiento y la incertidumbre sobre las entidades involucradas en la recuperación.

Los hallazgos cobran mayor relevancia ante la situación descrita recientemente por El Nuevo Día, que documentó más de 50 proyectos de generación eléctrica que permanecen estancados debido a trabas financieras, burocráticas y técnicas. El reportaje señala que el caso de Power Expectations refleja problemas que durante años han contribuido a atrasar o descarrilar iniciativas de generación en Puerto Rico.

“Como parte de nuestra agenda de priorizar lo básico, estamos poniendo presión para el desembolso de fondos federales para la energía. Desde 2017, Puerto Rico ha enfrentado una crisis energética persistente. No podemos seguir congelados en el tiempo. Puerto Rico necesita generación, una red más fuerte y que los fondos federales asignados comiencen a desembolsarse para comenzar proyectos y producir resultados. Si tenemos dinero disponible y proyectos que llevan años enfrentando obstáculos, el Gobierno tiene la responsabilidad de responder qué está ocurriendo que impide que se haga el trabajo.”, expresó Hernández.

Casi nueve años después del huracán María, la red eléctrica continúa en una condición críticamente frágil. Según la carta enviada por Hernández al secretario de HUD, Scott Turner, Puerto Rico experimentó un déficit energético de 33% en 2025. Entre 2021 y 2024, el consumidor promedio experimentó 27 horas de interrupciones eléctricas al año, mientras que en 2024 la cifra superó las 73 horas.

Hernández solicitó a HUD que explique qué medidas específicas está tomando para acelerar el desembolso de los $1.7 billones restantes, cuál es el calendario para completar el proceso, qué plan de acción ha desarrollado en respuesta a los hallazgos de GAO y cómo garantizará que los fondos ya obligados permanezcan protegidos de una posible rescisión o reasignación.

“El pueblo de Puerto Rico no puede esperar otra década. Cada año que un proyecto se queda detenido es otro año en que nuestras familias, nuestros comercios y nuestros hospitales siguen dependiendo de una red vulnerable e inestable. Tenemos que priorizar lo básico: que haya luz y una infraestructura energética que funcione.”

El Comisionado Residente reiteró que continuará presionando al Gobierno federal para que los recursos destinados a Puerto Rico se traduzcan en obras concretas y en mayor estabilidad para el sistema eléctrico.

title: House Passes Hudson, Knott Bill to Clear Way for New Veterans Home Near Fort Bragg
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, the U.S. House of Representatives passed legislation led by U.S. Representatives Richard Hudson (NC-09), Fort Bragg’s Congressman, and Brad Knott (NC-13) to clear the way for construction of a new state veterans home near Fort Bragg.

“Our veterans sacrificed to take care of us, and we have a responsibility to take care of them,” said Rep. Hudson. “After the Fayetteville State Veterans Home closed, 85 veterans were forced to leave their home and relocate across the state, many far away from their families. Today’s passage brings us one step closer to building a new home near Fort Bragg and bringing that care back to our community.”

"Tens of thousands of veterans call North Carolina’s 13th District home, and they’ve earned care worthy of their service,” said Rep. Knott. "Since the Fayetteville veterans' home closed in 2024, our state's heroes in central North Carolina have been without a home built for their care. I am proud to work with Congressman Hudson on this bill to advance a new veterans' home in Harnett County, which will provide quality, long-term care for those who served our country.”

The legislation transfers 20 acres off installation at Fort Bragg to the State of North Carolina, allowing the state to move forward with the permitting and construction process for the new veterans home.

The former Fayetteville State Veterans Home closed in 2024, displacing 85 veterans, including many with dementia and other disabilities. Hudson has worked with members of the North Carolina congressional delegation and the North Carolina Department of Military and Veterans Affairs to advance plans for a replacement facility, and the legislation is a necessary step in that effort.

Hudson spoke on the House floor ahead of passage, urging his colleagues to support the legislation and highlighting the need to restore a veterans home to the Fayetteville and Fort Bragg community.

Hudson and Knott were joined by Reps. David Rouzer (NC-07), Don Davis (NC-01), Deborah Ross (NC-02), Greg Murphy (NC-03), Valerie Foushee (NC-04), Virginia Foxx (NC-05), Addison McDowell (NC-06), Mark Harris (NC-08), Pat Harrigan (NC-10), Chuck Edwards (NC-11), Alma Adams (NC-12), and Tim Moore (NC-14) in cosponsoring the legislation.

title: Congressman Issa Introduces Digital Asset Inventory and Audit Act to Find and Protect Digital Assets in Federal Custody
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C.– Congressman Darrell Issa (CA-48) recently introduced the Digital Asset Inventory and Audit Act of 2026, legislation to ensure the federal government identifies, secures, and accounts for cryptocurrency and other digital assets that come into its custody.

As federal law enforcement agencies routinely seize computers, phones, and other electronic evidence during investigations, those devices can contain private keys, seed phrases, digital wallets, and other cryptographic information that provide access to digital assets that may be related to criminal activity. What’s missing is a uniform government-wide requirement to identify and account for those assets.

“The federal government cannot protect, recover, or account for assets it does not know it possesses,” said Congressman Issa. “When law enforcement seizes an electronic device, it may also be taking custody of the keys to digital assets that should also be seized. It’s time to recognize and remedy that reality.”

Congressman Lance Gooden (TX-5), an original co-sponsor of H.R. 10317, added “As criminals increasingly use digital assets to move and conceal illicit funds, our law enforcement agencies must keep pace. This bill ensures federal agencies have the tools, standards, and accountability necessary to properly identify and safeguard digital assets in government custody.”

Specifically, the legislation requires federal agencies to identify, secure, and account for digital assets discovered in electronic evidence. It also directs DOJ and NIST to establish government-wide standards for handling those assets and requires regular audits and oversight. The legislation creates no new search or seizure authorities and preserves existing legal and privacy protections.

“The Digital Chamber applauds Reps. Lance Gooden and Darrell Issa for introducing the Digital Asset Inventory and Audit Act of 2026. As digital assets play a growing role in law enforcement investigations and federal asset management, agencies need modern, consistent standards for identifying, securing, and accounting for them. This legislation is an important step toward that goal, and we look forward to working with these Co-Sponsors and Congress to advance it.”

title: Kamlager-Dove to Run for Co-Chair of House Democrats’ Messaging Apparatus
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Rep. Sydney Kamlager-Dove (CA-37) announced her candidacy for Co-Chair of the House Democratic Policy and Communications Committee (DPCC), a key leadership position within the caucus that helps develop messaging and communication strategies for House Democrats.

Rep. Kamlager-Dove announced her intentions in the following letter to colleagues:

Dear Colleague:

As this week will likely be our last together before the critical November elections, I wanted to respectfully ask for your support in serving as Co-Chair of the Democratic Policy and Communications Committee (DPCC). After what I believe will be a historic election for our caucus, Americans will look to House Democrats for leadership through the remaining years of the dreadful Trump presidency. I want to serve as a bridge between leadership and my fellow colleagues as we face the monumental challenges ahead.

My decision to run for DPCC Co-Chair was born from the misery and anguish of the 2024 presidential election. A major lesson from that loss was that our party did not do enough to communicate with voters where they were through the new media landscape of social media, creators, independent journalists, podcasts, and other emerging platforms. So I threw myself into all of it to learn, experiment, and most importantly, break through. After Trump’s illegal actions in his first months in office, I launched Is This Sh*t Legal? to cut through the noise and explain what made those actions illegal, why they mattered, and how Democrats were fighting back. My favorite part of this series was bringing so many of you in and watching your authenticity and passion shine through. I’ve also prioritized building lasting relationships with creators, podcasters, and independent journalists so we’re consistently reaching their audiences and making sure our message is part of the conversation year-round.

What’s important to me as a member of this caucus is ensuring that any progress we make benefits all of us. Because I know our strength and success as a caucus depends on our unity. We cannot create an affordable America or hold Trump accountable as solo actors on a stage. That’s why I have made it a priority to collaborate with so many of you, proudly filming with more than a quarter of our caucus this term–with some members joining me two, three, even four times.

Building on this unity framework, one of my biggest goals, if elected Co-Chair, is to connect the incredible creative talent in my home city of Los Angeles to the Democratic Caucus. Hollywood understands how to tell complicated stories in compelling, accessible ways that meet people where they are. I want to build a stronger bridge between our members and the writers, producers, storytellers, and digital creators who can help us communicate our agenda, connect with voters, and move people to action.

Our caucus has an opportunity to meet this moment with clarity, creativity, and unity. I am ready to bring my experience, relationships, and perspective from Los Angeles to help strengthen how we communicate, collaborate, and deliver for the American people. Above all, I’m committed to being a trusted voice for every member of this caucus and to ensuring that you and your districts are represented when decisions are made and messaging is shaped.

I would be honored to serve alongside each of you as Co-Chair of DPCC, and I respectfully ask for your support as we work together to build a stronger, more effective Democratic Caucus.

Sincerely,

Sydney Kamlager-Dove

Member of Congress

Rep. Kamlager-Dove is in her second term serving California’s 37th Congressional District. She is a member of the House Judiciary Committee and the House Foreign Affairs Committee, where she serves as Ranking Member on the South and Central Asia Subcommittee, and is Whip of the Congressional Black Caucus and Policy Co-Chair of the Democratic Women’s Caucus.

title: Kiggans’ Bill to Ensure Proper Lifeguard Staffing on Public Beaches Passes the House with Bipartisan Support
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congresswoman Jen Kiggans (VA-02) announced the House passage of her bill, H.R. 5063, the Safe Beaches, Safe Swimmers Act, which passed the House by voice. This bill would direct the Secretary of the Interior to work with local governments to ensure there is proper lifeguard coverage in the event of a lifeguard shortage.

Congresswoman Kiggans said, “As the representative of a coastal district, keeping our beaches safe for the families who live here and the millions of people who visit them every year is incredibly important to me. Last summer, communities on Virginia’s Eastern Shore were forced to step up when a federal lifeguard shortage left Chincoteague without the assurance our families deserve. Our local leaders did the right thing, but they should never be left scrambling to solve a federal staffing problem or pay the bill to keep a federal beach safe.

“The Safe Beaches, Safe Swimmers Act provides a commonsense solution by allowing the Department of the Interior to partner with local governments when lifeguard shortages occur and ensuring those communities are reimbursed for the costs they take on. I’m incredibly proud to see this bipartisan bill pass the House today, and I want to thank Mayor Denise Bowden and our local leaders on the Eastern Shore for working with us to turn a challenge we experienced at home into a solution that can help keep families safe at federal beaches across the country.”

“Families visiting America’s vast federal beaches and swimming areas should be able to count on properly staffed shores. H.R. 5063 allows the Department of the Interior to partner with local governments during lifeguard shortages and guarantees those communities are reimbursed for the costs they incur, ensuring federal responsibilities are not shifted to local taxpayers. I commend Rep. Kiggans for developing a practical solution that strengthens visitor safety and supports the coastal communities in Virginia welcoming millions of Americans each year,” said Chairman Bruce Westerman.

Watch Rep. Kiggans’ speech from the House Floor here.

Read Rep. Kiggans’ remarks from the House Floor prior to the bill’s passage as prepared for delivery:

Thank you, Mr. Speaker.

I rise today in support of my bill, H.R. 5063, the Safe Beaches, Safe Swimmers Act.

I have the privilege of representing a district that lives on the beach and the Bay. For families across Coastal Virginia, and the millions of Americans who visit our federal beaches every year, water safety is incredibly important.

Last year, we saw firsthand what can happen when the federal government fails to adequately staff these beaches.

Following a federal hiring freeze, Assateague Island National Seashore was unable to provide its normal lifeguard coverage at the federal beach in Chincoteague, Virginia.

Families continued visiting and swimming, but the lifeguards they had come to rely on were not there.

Our local leaders stepped up. The Town of Chincoteague and Accomack County took on unforeseen costs to make sure lifeguards returned to the beach and families could safely enjoy the water.

But our local governments should never be left scrambling to solve a federal staffing problem on their own.

That is why I introduced the Safe Beaches, Safe Swimmers Act.

My bill provides a commonsense solution. When the Department of the Interior determines that a federal swimming area is facing a lifeguard staffing shortage, it can partner with local governments to provide the necessary coverage. And importantly, when a local government steps up to provide those lifeguards, the federal government will reimburse it for the reasonable costs it incurs.

This applies to designated swimming areas managed by the National Park Service, Fish and Wildlife Service, Bureau of Land Management, and Bureau of Reclamation that are normally monitored by federal lifeguards.

Mr. Speaker, this bill is about public safety, accountability, and giving our communities a solution when Washington falls short.

I am grateful to the local leaders on the Eastern Shore who worked with us after seeing this problem firsthand, and I am proud that we now have an opportunity to make sure communities across the country have another tool to keep their beaches safe.

No family visiting a federal beach should have to wonder whether a lifeguard will be there when an emergency happens.

I urge my colleagues to support the Safe Beaches, Safe Swimmers Act, and I yield back.

The Safe Beaches, Safe Swimmers Act now moves to the Senate for consideration.

Background:

In June 2025, Congresswoman Kiggans questioned Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum in the House Committee on Natural Resources regarding recent federal hiring freezes and whether temporary hires, including lifeguards, would receive an exemption. Watch the Congresswoman’s questioning here and coverage from Shore Daily News here.

Following the hearing, Congresswoman Kiggans sent a letter to Secretary Burgum reaffirming concern for the federal hiring freeze and its impact on the lifeguard shortage. Read her letter here.

In September 2025, Rep. Kiggans introduced the Safe Beaches, Safe Swimmers Act in response to lifeguard shortages on Chincoteague Island and across the Eastern Shore of Virginia in the Summer of 2025. Read her press release here.

Watch Rep. Kiggans’ interview with CBS News following the bill’s introduction here.

title: Kiggans Welcomes Federal Highway Administrator Sean McMaster to Hampton Roads, Highlights Major Hampton Roads Projects
text:
NORFOLK, VA — Congresswoman Jen Kiggans (VA-02) joined Federal Highway Administrator Sean McMaster and local transportation leaders to highlight major infrastructure projects underway in Hampton Roads and discuss continued efforts to improve transportation throughout Coastal Virginia.

Congresswoman Kiggans and Administrator McMaster received a briefing from representatives of the Federal Highway Administration (FHWA), Virginia Department of Transportation (VDOT), and the Hampton Roads Bridge-Tunnel (HRBT) Expansion Project on ongoing work related to the HRBT Expansion and Hampton Roads Express Lanes.

Congresswoman Kiggans said, “Everyone from Hampton Roads knows how critical our tunnels, roads, and bridges are to everyday life. However, transportation infrastructure is more important than just getting from Point A to Point B. Not only does it support operations on our military installations and the movement of goods through the Port of Virginia, but it also keeps our shipyards and ship repair industry moving, connects our local businesses, and helps hardworking families get where they need to go.”

“At nearly $4 billion, the HRBT Expansion project is the largest highway construction undertaking in the Commonwealth’s history, and a great example of what we can accomplish with federal, state, and local collaboration. I’m grateful to Administrator McMaster for coming to Hampton Roads to witness the project firsthand and I look forward to continuing working with the Federal Highway Administration to ensure our region has the safe and reliable infrastructure it needs to thrive,” Kiggans concluded.

The HRBT Expansion Project is widening approximately 10 miles of Interstate 64 between Norfolk and Hampton and constructing two new two-lane bored tunnels alongside the existing tunnels. Once completed, the corridor will expand from four lanes to eight lanes, including six general-purpose lanes and two Express Lanes. The project will help address one of the region’s most significant transportation bottlenecks while improving connectivity for commuters, freight, military personnel, and visitors.

Kiggans’ Work to Secure Transportation Priorities for Hampton Roads:

Since entering Congress, Congresswoman Kiggans has also worked to secure federal funding for transportation priorities throughout Virginia’s Second District, including:

$3 million for Laskin Road Phase I-B in Virginia Beach,

$3.04 million for preliminary engineering and environmental work for the King’s Highway Bridge replacement in Suffolk,

And $1 million for flood-resiliency improvements to Pungo Ferry Road in Virginia Beach.

Through the Transportation Infrastructure Finance and Innovation Act (TIFIA) program, the Hampton Roads Transportation Accountability Commission (HRTAC) applied for a loan of $310 million to finance related express lane projects. By December 2025, the loan had reached the final approval stages, but had yet to receive approval from the U.S. Department of Transportation (USDOT). Following contact from Congresswoman Kiggans’ office, USDOT announced in September 2026 that the loan would proceed, saving local taxpayers roughly $11 million.

Via FY26 federal-aid highway formula funding through FHWA, Virginia received approximately $1.46 billion to support highway construction, bridge improvements, safety, congestion reduction, and other transportation projects across the Commonwealth.

Other FY26 Virginia allocations include:

Approximately $795 million through the National Highway Performance Program,

$387 million through the Surface Transportation Block Grant Program,

And $85 million through the Highway Safety Improvement Program.

title: $7.1M to HSEM to Support Sinlaku Emergency Response
text: Congratulations to the CNMI Office of Homeland Security and Emergency Management on receiving $7,076,132.78 in FEMA grant funding to support emergency protective measures following Super Typhoon Sinlaku. This award is funded at a 100% federal cost share under Section 403 of the Robert T. Stafford Act. The funding will reimburse and support critical emergency response activities carried out between April 12 and July 9, 2026, including personnel costs, contract services, and the operation of the Emergency Operations Center. It also supports the dissemination of critical information to the public, medical care and transportation, and the delivery and distribution of medical supplies. Super Typhoon Sinlaku created an immediate threat to the health and safety of residents across the Commonwealth and required an extensive emergency response. This federal assistance recognizes the significant resources the CNMI deployed during the disaster and helps ensure our local agencies have the support they need to respond effectively.

title: Ensuring Economic Benefits and Protections from Seabed Mining
text:
On September 8, I introduced H.R. 10318, the Pacific Minerals Economic Security Act (PACMESA), to ensure the Northern Mariana Islands and other U.S. Pacific territories directly affected by potential seabed mining receive meaningful economic benefits and a stronger voice in decisions that could impact our communities. PACMESA would direct 50 percent of revenues from covered seabed mining leases to eligible adjacent territorial governments, creating a significant source of revenue for the CNMI if seabed mining occurs offshore. The bill would also strengthen environmental bonding requirements to help ensure companies are financially accountable for potential impacts and expand notification and consultation requirements for territorial governments. Critical minerals are increasingly important to America’s economic competitiveness and national security. If seabed mining occurs offshore our communities, the CNMI should not bear the risks without receiving a meaningful share of the benefits and having a seat at the table. PACMESA provides those protections and helps close important gaps in existing federal law governing hard mineral development on the Outer Continental Shelf.

title: Talking about Connecting Local Business to a Larger Pacific Strategy
text: As the United States seeks to increase both its presence and its influence in the Pacific region, it is critical that our nation’s foreign policy does not overlook one of its most productive assets, its Pacific territories. I firmly believe the territories can be influential voices in our country’s diplomacy with our neighbors, but official diplomacy is only one part of that role. Commerce, investment, transportation, and business relationships also help strengthen America’s presence across the region. Last week, I met with Del Benson and Nathan Benson at the District Office to talk about the role CNMI businesses can play in advancing American interests in the Pacific and the steps we can take, both in the private sector and through the federal government, to help create more opportunities for our local businesses to participate in regional growth. The CNMI sits in the middle of a region that is becoming increasingly important to the United States. We should be thinking seriously about how our businesses, our people, and our location can contribute to that strategy while also creating new opportunities here at home. Thanks Del and Nathan for stopping by and for the great conversation.

title: Talking Constituent Casework with Rotary
text: I came almost straight from the airport to join the Rotary Club of Saipan last week for a conversation about one of the most important services we provide to the people of the Commonwealth, congressional casework. Since January 3, 2025, we have handled at least 612 formal cases and resolved 377 of them. This year alone, we have received more than 370 new cases and resolved a little more than 210. Immigration represents about 48 percent of our casework, Social Security about 20 percent, and FEMA another 20 percent this year because of disaster-related assistance. The central point of my remarks, and what I want to share with all of you, is simple. If you need assistance with the federal government, reach out. Whether it is Social Security, immigration, FEMA, veterans benefits, passports, or another federal issue, our team is here to help you navigate the process and work toward a resolution. Thank you to Rotary for having me and for giving me the opportunity to talk about this important part of the work we do for you.

title: Their Memory Lives On
text: Last week, our office joined the community for the annual We Will Never Forget ceremony and the 11th Annual Field of Heroes as we remembered the lives lost on September 11, 2001, and honored the first responders, service members, and community servants who continue to serve others every day. Thank you to all of the sponsors, organizers, volunteers, and community servants who come together each year to make this commemoration possible. Twenty-five years later, the promise remains the same. We will never forget.

title: Working Together to Support Our Schools
text: When the economy struggles, government revenues fall. That means austerity, reduced services, and difficult decisions about how limited local resources are used. One of the places where those pressures are felt most directly is in our public school system. The CNMI Public School System educates thousands of our children, and federal funding already supports a significant share of its operating budget. I am grateful that we have been able to protect those federal resources, but with local revenues continuing to shrink, we also need to think creatively about how every available resource can be used to support our schools. That is why I sincerely appreciate PSS Board Chair Maisie Tenorio and PSS Director Donna Flores for coming by and having a frank and productive conversation about needs, opportunities, and how we can develop a shared strategy for leveraging federal and local resources to give our children the strong educational foundation they deserve. Thank you Maisie and Donna for stopping by and for your service to our students!

title: Knott, Hudson Bill to Advance a New Veterans’ Home in Harnett County Passes the House
text:
WASHINGTON D.C. - Congressman Brad Knott (NC-13) issued the following statement after the House passed H.R. 10159, a bill he co-led with Congressman Richard Hudson (NC-09) to transfer land facilitating the construction of a new state veterans' home in Harnett County.

"Tens of thousands of veterans call North Carolina’s 13th District home, and they’ve earned care worthy of their service,” said Congressman Knott. "Since the Fayetteville veterans' home closed in 2024, our state's heroes in central North Carolina have been without a home built for their care. I am proud to work with Congressman Hudson on this bill to advance a new veterans' home in Harnett County, which will provide quality, long-term care for those who served our country."

“Our veterans kept their promise to serve, and we have a responsibility to keep our promise to take care of them,” said Congressman Hudson. “After the Fayetteville State Veterans Home closed, veterans were forced to relocate across the state, many far away from their families. Today’s passage brings us one step closer to building a new home near Fort Bragg and bringing that care back to our community.”

Background:

The North Carolina State Veterans Home in Fayetteville closed in 2024 due to disrepair and health and safety concerns.

H.R. 10159 transfers a 20-acre parcel of land from the Fort Bragg Training Area to the State of North Carolina to build a replacement facility.

The new site sits roughly 15 miles from the original Fayetteville location, along the western access road to Fort Bragg.

Congressmen Knott and Hudson were joined by Reps. David Rouzer (NC-07), Don Davis (NC-01), Deborah Ross (NC-02), Greg Murphy (NC-03), Valerie Foushee (NC-04), Virginia Foxx (NC-05), Addison McDowell (NC-06), Mark Harris (NC-08), Pat Harrigan (NC-10), Chuck Edwards (NC-11), Alma Adams (NC-12), and Tim Moore (NC-14) in cosponsoring the legislation.

title: Congressman Langworthy Announces Nearly $13.6 Million in Federal Aviation Grants for Airports Across New York’s 23rd Congressional District
text:
Washington, D.C.—September 14th… Congressman Nick Langworthy today announced $13,532,819 in federal Airport Improvement Program (AIP) grants from the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) for critical infrastructure improvements at three airports across New York’s 23rd Congressional District.

The grants will support runway and taxiway rehabilitation projects designed to maintain the structural integrity of existing pavement, improve safety and reliability, and extend the useful life of critical airport infrastructure.

“This significant $13.6 million investment will help ensure our airports across the Southern Tier and Western New York have the safe, reliable infrastructure they need to serve our communities and support economic growth,” said Congressman Nick Langworthy. “Strong aviation infrastructure is essential for connecting our communities, supporting local businesses and keeping our region competitive. I’m proud to help bring these federal resources home and will continue working to make sure our region gets its fair share.”

The specific grants include:

$11,080,483 for Elmira/Corning Regional Airport in Elmira, awarded to Chemung County. The funding will support the second phase of construction to rehabilitate 8,000 feet of existing paved Runway 6/24, which has reached the end of its useful life, as well as reconstruct its runway lighting. The project will help maintain the structural integrity of the runway and minimize foreign object debris.

$1,619,172 for Wellsville Municipal/Tarantine Field in Wellsville, awarded to the Town of Wellsville. The funding will support the final construction phase of a project to rehabilitate 5,700 feet of existing paved Taxiway A, maintaining pavement integrity, minimizing foreign object debris and extending its useful life.

$833,164 for Akron/Jesson Field in Akron, awarded to Christian Airmen Inc. The funding will support the final construction phase of a project to rehabilitate 3,268 feet of existing paved Runway 7/25, helping maintain its structural integrity, minimize foreign object debris and extend the runway’s useful life.

The funding was awarded through the Federal Aviation Administration’s FY2026 Airport Improvement Program, which provides federal resources for airport infrastructure projects.

title: McCaul Introduces Legislation to Accelerate Breakthroughs in Pediatric Cancer by Leveraging AI
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, Congressman Michael McCaul (R-Texas) — founder and co-chair of the Congressional Childhood Cancer Caucus — introduced the Ailani Myers Accelerating Innovation in Medicine (AIM) to Cure Kids with Cancer Act with caucus co-chairs Ami Bera, M.D. (D-Calif.) and Mike Kelly (R-Pa.). The legislation, which is named after a brave young cancer patient and advocate, will accelerate the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to improve and transform pediatric cancer research, treatment options, and data storage.

McCaul said, "Since I founded the Childhood Cancer Caucus 17 years ago, advancements in technology have radically expanded the frontiers of healthcare. We owe it to our nation's children to leverage cutting-edge AI to improve their care and treatment options. I'm proud to introduce this bill, which codifies and builds on President Trump's executive order to unlock cures for pediatric cancer patients. By empowering AI to continuously drive research forward, we move one step closer to beating this heartbreaking disease once and for all.

"I'm also proud to have named this bill after Ailani Myers, a beautiful young cancer fighter. Like so many of the children I've met, she is far more courageous than most adults. Even a rare form of Leukemia can't steal her smile! Ailani has fiercely advocated for the childhood cancer community and recently attended the signing of President Trump's executive order accelerating AI use for pediatric cancer cures. It's fitting that this bill carry her name and her legacy forward."

Image

McCaul and Ailani in 2013

“Pediatric cancer remains one of the most heartbreaking diagnoses any family can face, and we have a responsibility to use every tool available to improve outcomes for children,” said Bera. “The bipartisan Accelerating Innovation in Medicine for Kids with Cancer Act would leverage cutting-edge AI and data tools to transform pediatric cancer research, improve clinical trial design and access, and deliver more personalized treatment options for young patients. I am proud to support this effort to accelerate innovation, strengthen the Childhood Kelly Data Initiative, and move us closer to ending cancer as we know it.”

“Congress should always consider new, initiative ways not only to treat cancer, but to defeat cancer. This legislation would leverage artificial intelligence to strengthen patient care and patient outcomes,” said Kelly.“I’m proud to sponsor the bipartisan Accelerating Innovation in Medicine for Kids with Cancer Act as we work to ensure pediatric cancer patients and their families have every tool at their disposal to receive the care and cures they deserve.”

The Ailani Myers AIM to Cure Kids with Cancer Act would:

Codify and strengthen the National Cancer Institute’s Childhood Cancer Data Initiative, authorizing federal support to collect, connect, and share pediatric cancer data;

Establish an AI coordinator to align pediatric cancer efforts across the White House, federal agencies, and private-sector partners; and

Harness AI to accelerate pediatric cancer research and treatment by improving data sharing, strengthening predictive modeling, and modernizing clinical trials.

title: House Passes Chairwoman McClain's Common Cents Act to End Wasteful Penny Production
text:
WASHINGTON— Today, the House passed H.R. 10167, the Common Cents Act, legislation led by House Republican Conference Chairwoman Lisa McClain (R-Mich.), to permanently end production of the penny for general circulation and modernize America’s coinage system.

“Washington has a spending problem, and it shows up in places big and small,” Chairwoman McClain said. “If the federal government is spending nearly four cents to make a penny worth one cent, something is broken. House Republicans are proving that common sense still has a place in government by cutting waste and protecting taxpayer dollars.”

The Common Cents Act ends production of pennies for general circulation while keeping existing pennies legal tender and allowing the U.S. Mint to continue producing collectible coins. It also establishes uniform guidance allowing cash transactions to be rounded to the nearest five cents when exact change is unavailable. Electronic payments and other non-cash transactions will continue to be charged to the exact cent.

The legislation also directs the Federal Reserve to develop a national transition plan for the hundreds of billions of pennies already in circulation and requires Treasury to notify Congress before discontinuing any other circulating coin. It also authorizes a lower-cost nickel composition if testing shows it will reduce production costs without significantly disrupting coin-operated machines.

title: The Ackerson Meadow Land Interchange Act Approved by House of Representatives
text:
September 14, 2026

Washington, D.C. – The Ackerson Meadow Land Interchange Act, H.R. 8454, has passed the House of Representatives by a voice vote. The legislation by Congressman McClintock, H.R. 8454, has companion legislation in the Senate authored by Senator Padilla, S. 288.

The legislation addresses a familiar problem in federal land management in the Sierra Nevada: the checkerboard of boundary lines that makes land management disjointed and inefficient. The legislation consolidates land jurisdictions between the National Park System and the National Forest System and will help to eliminate confusion caused by split jurisdiction.

“Jurisdictional boundaries should not stand in the way of effective land management. H.R. 8454 transfers administrative jurisdiction over federal parcels in Ackerson Meadow, helping establish a more logical and efficient approach to managing and restoring this vital ecosystem,” remarked House Natural Resources Committee Chairman Bruce Westerman. “I commend Rep. McClintock for pursuing a targeted solution that improves government efficiency and advances responsible land management in California.”

Congressman McClintock delivered the following remarks today on the House floor in support of the legislation:

Floor Statement (Video Link)

H.R. 8454

Ackerson Meadow Land Interchange Act

September 14, 2026

Mr. Speaker:

The Ackerson Meadow Land Interchange Act is a simple proposal to transfer administrative jurisdiction over approximately 160 acres of National Forest System land to Yosemite National Park. It would also transfer approximately 170 acres of National Park System land to be a part of the Stanislaus National Forest.

Senator Padilla is carrying identical legislation in the Senate. We don’t agree on much, but we certainly agree on this.

This legislation addresses a familiar problem in federal land management in the Sierra Nevada: the checkerboard of boundary lines that makes land management disjointed and inefficient. This bill simply consolidates land jurisdictions between the National Park System and the National Forest System, without increasing the federal footprint.

At issue is the Ackerson Meadow. This meadow supports livestock grazing operations that have been part of the history and economy of the region. These operations are essential for brush control and fire suppression, maintaining meadow conditions and sustaining the rural economy that depends on the productive use of these lands.

Federal agencies, conservation organizations, and local ranchers have worked together to improve the meadow while maintaining grazing opportunities. Restoration projects have improved wetland conditions, enhanced water storage, improved habitat, and supported continued public uses, including grazing.

The proposed land exchange would make that cooperative approach easier by eliminating the confusion caused by split jurisdiction. Ranchers need to know where their permits apply, where infrastructure can be maintained, and who is responsible for decisions affecting their operations.

The bill also protects existing rights and authorizations. It specifically provides that valid existing rights, including rights-of-way, easements, leases, licenses, and permits, remain protected after the transfer. This ensures that current users, including grazing permit holders, are not unfairly disrupted by a change in administrative jurisdiction.

It also appropriately maintains federal responsibilities for hazardous substance cleanup and other obligations.

This bill reflects a principle that should guide federal land policy, management decisions should be based on the realities of the landscape, not simply the boundaries drawn on a map decades ago.

Our national forests and parks serve many purposes. They preserve wildlife habitat, protect watersheds, provide recreation, and support rural economies. A balanced approach recognizes all of these values.

I urge adoption of this measure and yield back the balance of my time.
