title: Curtis Joins Tillis, Armstrong on Delegation to Ukraine
text:
Senators affirmed support for Ukraine, assessed security conditions and defense capabilities amid continued Russian aggression

KYIV, UKRAINE—U.S. Senator John Curtis (R-UT), member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, joined a Republican congressional delegation with Senators Thom Tillis (R-NC) and Alan Armstrong (R-OK) to Ukraine to affirm American support for the Ukrainian people and assess the security situation amid Russia’s continued war of aggression. The trip marks the first time since the start of the invasion that a congressional delegation visited Kharkiv, a heavily fortified frontline city just miles from the Russian border.

While in Kyiv, the delegation met with U.S. and Ukrainian officials and key stakeholders to receive updates on the war, negotiations, and Ukraine’s rapidly developing defense technologies. Before going to Ukraine, the delegation was joined by Senator Elissa Slotkin (D-MI) in Poland.

Photos from the visit can be downloaded here.

Senator Curtis shared the following comments on his experience:

On Ukraine’s military capabilities:

“Ukraine has gone from a fragment of the Soviet Union to a global symbol of freedom and democracy in the face of authoritarianism. The Ukrainian people are fighting for their sovereignty, but they are also defending values Americans cherish: free speech, free markets, and free people.

“While in Ukraine, we witnessed an extremely capable military on the forefront of innovation in the UAS and counter-UAS space. It was particularly helpful to see how Ukraine is providing these capabilities across Europe and the Middle East.”

On the future of U.S. support for Ukraine:

“It is clear that Putin intends to make the coming winter hard for Ukraine. He will not succeed. The Ukrainians provided us with concrete asks to help them get through the winter, including House passage and the full enactment of the Lindsey Graham Russia Sanctions Act. It’s important to note that the requests made by the Ukrainians require no U.S. taxpayer dollars nor further aid packages. My colleagues and I plan to execute on these requests and get Ukraine the support it needs.”

On what’s at stake:

“A Russian victory threatens more than just Europe. Like Russia, China carries territorial ambitions. There’s no question they’re eyeing Taiwan and seeking to set the stage for an invasion, which is why what happens in Ukraine is directly tied to Taiwan and stability in the Indo-Pacific. President Xi is carefully watching our response to Russia’s war, inferring our posture would be similar to how we would respond if China were to invade Taiwan. If China invades Taiwan, global upheaval will follow, and we would see our economy hit harder in the initial onset than the Great Depression.”

On the lived experience of Ukrainians:

“This delegation made clear that the debate in Washington is about much more than lines on a map. We met Ukrainians defending their families and communities and saw the extraordinary lengths civilians are going to return to normality. Their courage and determination are an inspiration to freedom-loving people everywhere. We refuse to let this be a blueprint for future authoritarian regimes’ aggression.”

Background:

During the visit, the delegation received on-the-ground assessments of the security situation in Poland and Ukraine, updates on the war, NATO, and ongoing peace negotiations. Members also examined developments in unmanned aerial vehicle and counter-UAV systems, areas where Ukraine has developed significant battlefield expertise.

In Poland, Curtis praised the country’s leadership within NATO, including its commitment to spending 5 percent of its GDP on defense and its critical role as a logistical hub supporting Ukraine. Curtis emphasized that continued coordination between the United States, Poland, and other NATO allies is essential to deterring further Russian aggression and maintaining security along NATO’s Eastern Front.

Russia’s continued war in Ukraine has highlighted the many broader implications for U.S. national security and global stability. In his role on the Foreign Relations Committee, Senator Curtis has remained vocal, warning that Vladimir Putin’s ambitions extend beyond Ukraine and that a strong, unified NATO posture is necessary to deter further aggression in Europe.

title: Daines on Fox News: “We Need to Be Gold Medalists in the AI Race”
text:
“The complexity of AI far exceeds the capacity of the government to understand and regulate it”

WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senator Steve Daines today joined Harris Faulkner on Fox News to discuss the latest on artificial intelligence policy and the race against China.

Watch the full exchange HERE.

Daines on the AI race versus China:

Well, I just returned from China a couple of weeks ago. I was in Hangzhou, the city larger than New York City. It’s the home of many of the high-tech companies that are some of the best and brightest of China, including DeepSeek, an AI company. Let’s remember we’re in a global race. It’s imperative the United States wins this race. And for those who assert that we should somehow slow down is nonsense. This is about continuing to move as quickly as possible because we are in a race. The bronze or silver medal is not good enough. We need to be the gold medalists in this race in AI. If you look at China at the moment, they’re doing a much better job of adopting AI. They’re ranked second in the world in adoption by Stanford. The United States is ranked 24th. So we’ve got some superiorities related to the innovation ecosystem we’re building in terms of our frontier models and AI. But think about China. They graduate five to ten times more engineers every year in the United States. So the scale and quality of the innovation ecosystem in China, including AI, is now some of the best. We have a peer competitor, and we’ve got to be very thoughtful as we go forward to make sure that the federal government doesn’t get in the way of ensuring that we beat China in this race.

…There’s this thing called a midterm election, Harris, last time I checked coming up. Early voting is starting here in a couple of weeks. And so this is probably a poor time to be having discourse about this issue. We should probably wait until after the election. It reminds me a bit, Harris, remember the days of the climate change hysteria coming from the left about the world was going to end, the polar ice caps were going to be gone and so forth. All these predictions never came true. I hear a little bit of that right now from some of my colleagues on the left side of the aisle who are creating hysteria and want to create this to be a political issue versus thoughtfulness here in Washington about what is the best path going forward here for the United States.

Daines on AI regulation:

This is the same kind of rhetoric we heard from the left about banning all fossil fuels years ago. Imagine the mess we’d be in had they had their way and how that would have put China in an amazing competitive advantage over the United States if we would have disarmed relates to fossil fuels. Thank God we were the leading oil and gas producer in the world. But I think there’s a similar argument here. I was thinking about AI. There is so much good that can be done. Think about what we can do to collaborate in terms of cures for cancer. There’s some wonderful work going on that truly could deal with one of the, I lost my father to cancer in April. I mean, can you imagine if we had cures for cancer? So that’s something that the power and the good that AI can bring. But we should not be blind to the fact there are some downside risks, you know, bio-terrorism, other things that we need to be very concerned about. And that’s why thoughtful conversation, appropriate guardrails. But any time the government tries to jump in and regulate something, it does not understand. The complexity of AI far exceeds the capacity of government to understand and regulate it. That’s one of the dilemmas we face at this moment. And that’s why it’s going to be very important that some of our best thought leaders, smartest people coming from the private sector with some blend with those in public service come together and work on this issue. But we have no business as a bunch of bureaucrats here in Washington as elected leaders who most don’t even use AI on a daily basis. Why would you want to have those elected leaders being the ones regulating it?

…That’s the right track is bring in our best and brightest. We’ve got some of the best

and brightest, thank God, here in the United States on AI. Those are the folks who will be helping shape the path going forward. I worked in a cloud computing startup. I took the company public. I was an executive for 12 years. There’s a fiduciary responsibility that you have as a tech leader because your name, your brand is on the line every day. Can you imagine if there’s a New York Times, Wall Street Journal article about how your company destroyed part of this economy or humanity because of your technology. Believe me, there’s self-corrective measures in terms of fiduciary accountability to shareholders to make sure that there is some self-governance and self-policing within the private sector. Now, I’m not suggesting it’s the Wild West and laissez-faire, but let’s strike the right balance here of the thought leaders here with appropriate guardrails. Let’s tap it light right now. We cannot go down the left’s call to stop or put a moratorium in AI. That hands this race right to China.

###

title: Daines to FDA: Protect Women’s Health, Release Safety Review of Abortion Pill
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senator Steve Daines today spoke in a Senate Finance Committee hearing with Chris Klomp, nominee to be Deputy Secretary of Health and Human Services. They discussed the FDA’s ongoing safety review of mifepristone as well as Most-Favored Nation drug pricing policies.

Watch the full exchange HERE.

Daines on the dangers of the abortion pill:

Daines: We want to make sure we let the data speak as it relates to mifepristone. What does the data tellus? There was analysis done of 865,000 mifepristone prescriptions compiled from insurance claims. That’s a large data set. They found that nearly 11 percent of women experienced a serious adverse event. And let me define the serious adverse event.In most cases that meant going to the emergency room for some serious condition within 45 days oftaking mifepristone. That’s 22 times higher than the FDA’s long-standing estimate,which is less than 0.5 percent. So a big gap between what we’re seeing in insurance claims andwhat the FDA said when they originally released it. During the Biden administration,I believe they had some reckless COVID-era policies that removed, as you mentioned,the in-person dispensing requirement. And serious questions remain whether onlineprescribers can adequately assess gestational age, rule out an atopic pregnancy,or identify situations involving coercion or abuse without a direct in-person evaluation.Secretary Kennedy has stated the FDA is conducting its own comprehensive study ofmifepristone. I’m encouraged by this and continue to urge the agency to complete its review.in a timely manner. Let the data speak, not politics here up on Capitol Hill.

Klomp: Senator, we strongly agree on this point. We have an obligation always to follow the evidence.

Daines: The hope here is that we take the temperature down on the politics of this sensitive issue and let the data speak, frankly, let the women speak, who are seeing a 22-time higher adverse effect from the use of this drug than what the FDA claimed. Specifically, Mr. Klomp, given that the FDA is legally required to file an official update on the status detailing the progress of the safety review by October 7th of this year that’s coming up do you believe the agency will be able to release the full review before the calendar year ends?

Klomp: I checked in on this with the agency just a couple of days ago. I do believe that we are on target to file that interim update and I do believe that we are on target as a department to produce the finished study and results before the end of the year.

Daines on Most-Favored Nation drug pricing concerns:

Daines: I’d like to turn to the issue of most favored nation drug pricing and the GLOBE and GUARD models under review by the Office of Management and Budget. We greatly appreciate the administration’s efforts to lower drug costs for Americans. I know the folks back home in Montana will be standing on their chairs cheering for that ambition. And I do believe President Trump has done more to achieve this goal than any of his predecessors. With this said, I do have some serious concerns having just come from back from China two weeks ago, looking at the innovation ecosystem going on right now in the biosciences and biotech space. The impact these models could have on the American biotech industry, especially at this moment when China is rapidly closing the innovation gap and seeking to overtake the United States as a global leader in biotech. I’ve heard from a lot of smaller and midsize companies about how these models could have a negative outsized impact on their ability to engage in R&D, attract investment, and pursue complex or uncertain therapies. These are companies who are responsible for more than half of FDA-approved medicines and involve nearly 75 percent of American clinical trials. It truly is the lifeblood of biotech innovation. Mr. Klomp, was the risk to the U.S. innovation base a consideration before GLOBE and GUARD were advanced?

Klomp: Senator, thank you for that question. The president was unequivocal in a joint mandate that he gave our team. Lower prices for Americans at the pharmacy counter by getting other wealthy countries to pay their fair share so that we don’t pay three times what they do for the same drug, same box, same manufacturer. And number two, do not harm American leadership and biotechnology. And so we have worked to do just that.

Daines: The latest I just saw, you talked about the large molecules crossing the 50% threshold first time ever coming out of China. They can do a phase one clinical trial now in half the time at 20 percent of the cost. And so it’s game on, and what we need to do is be able to go faster and be more efficient.

title: After Duckworth Push, DoD Inspector General Releases First Quarterly Iran War Report
text:
[WASHINGTON, D.C.] – Following U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth’s (D-IL) push, the Department of Defense Office of Inspector General (DoD OIG), as the Lead OIG on the war, released its first quarterly watchdog report on Operation Epic Fury after Duckworth called for and then secured Inspector General (IG) oversight of Donald Trump’s costly, illegal war against Iran. The report details how the first four months of this war, ending in June, cost American taxpayers a whopping $33.7 billion dollars—including $22 billion spent on munitions alone and $184 million in damages from Iranian strikes on U.S. diplomatic facilities in the Middle East.

“For the first time in nearly eight months, the American people finally have an official glimpse into the cost of this disastrous war—and it is jaw-dropping. On top of the financial pain being inflicted on middle-class pocketbooks, this report sheds new light on how this illegal war is making all Americans less safe by draining our military resources and hollowing out the diplomatic footprint that we sorely need at full strength to end this war. And make no mistake: this report is still a gross underestimate of the grand total that taxpayers are already on the hook for.

“Our servicemembers are exhausted, our munitions are depleted, our diplomatic capabilities have been wrecked and 18 of our troops will never come home. The American people deserve transparency about how their taxpayer dollars are being spent and how their national security is being weakened by this quagmire that is leaving them worse off.

“No matter how hard the Administration tries to keep us in the dark, I will keep demanding answers, accountability and an end to Trump’s costly war of choice.”

The DoD OIG’s first quarterly report is the first government accounting to pull together, across Federal agencies, the costs, scope and scale of the opening silos of Trump’s disastrous war, which has resulted in the deaths of 18 brave servicemembers. The report illuminates exactly how Donald Trump’s reckless, unjustified war has pushed U.S. military and diplomatic infrastructure to the brink, creating urgent munitions shortfalls, siphoning money intended to cover payroll for our troops and personnel, redirecting resources from the Indo-Pacific and other critical national security priorities and leaving the Trump administration scrambling and dangerously unprepared for future contingencies and emergencies abroad. It confirms that Donald Trump blew at least $33.7 billion dollars in the first four months of his reckless war, a cost that does not include millions in repairs to military and diplomatic facilities that the Department of Defense has not yet quantified and likely undercounts necessary diplomatic repairs, by the State Department’s own admission.

Additionally, following a request from Duckworth and other Senate Democrats, today the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) independently estimated that approximately $38 billion has been spent on Trump’s war through the end of July, with each concurrent month set to rack up another $2-3 billion in spending. That estimate is likely a significant underestimate, as it misses various costs such as damaged facilities or fuel expenditure.

Duckworth has been an outspoken critic of Trump’s illegal, needless war in Iran since it began. She is one of the Senate Six—the original group of Senators who have been forcing votes on War Powers Resolutions that would cease hostilities in Iran, which Republicans have shamefully blocked nine times. Last month, the Senator introduced legislation to stop Trump’s desperate attempt to obscure how long his illegal war against Iran has lasted, dishonor the sacrifice of our troops injured and killed in combat and hide the true cost of his disastrous war from the American people.

Ahead of the Senate’s vote on her own War Powers resolution in April, Duckworth gave impassioned remarks drawing on her personal experience serving in our nation’s last war of choice in the Middle East, imploring Republicans to remember their oaths and vote to help rein in this unhinged President—which they did not.

title: Durbin Grills Director Patel On Record Of Failed Leadership At FBI In Senate Judiciary Committee Oversight Hearing
text:
During the hearing, Director Patel deflected Durbin’s questions by denying that federal agents shot Chicagoan Marimar Martinez; refusing to comment on whether there are investigations into fraud perpetrated by Trump Admin officials; and misrepresenting the change in FBI hiring standards

WASHINGTON – U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, questioned Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) Director Kash Patel in today’s Senate Judiciary Committee hearing conducting oversight of the FBI. During the hearing, Durbin grilled Director Patel on the Trump Administration’s destructive and violent immigration enforcement campaigns; the gutting of FBI hiring standards; his role in covering up the Epstein files; and the perpetration of rampant corruption and fraud within the Trump Administration.

Durbin began by pressing Director Patel about his failure to acknowledge that federal agents acted inappropriately during Operation Midway Blitz and Operation Metro Surge, in which multiple U.S. citizens were shot or killed by federal agents. Rather than follow protocol, Director Patel dismissed the incidents and refused to properly open a federal civil rights investigation.

“One year ago, my home state of Illinois was experiencing the beginning of a ruthless, reckless, deadly campaign orchestrated by this Administration known as ‘Midway Blitz.’ Masked federal agents armed with military grade weapons and unmarked vehicles descended on Chicago and other communities, bashing in car windows, indiscriminately rounding up people, deploying chemical agents, and shooting innocent people,” Durbin began. “A border patrol agent shot U.S. citizen and Chicago native Marimar Martinez five times after sideswiping her vehicle. She survived. After Ms. Martinez was shot, DHS [U.S. Department of Homeland Security] branded her as a domestic terrorist. A border patrol agent bragged about shooting her. And an FBI agent falsely claimed she chased a border patrol agent before she was shot.”

“Director Patel, after the shooting, you took to social media, posted a video of a different collision, that you said supported DHS. He [Patel] said, ‘Attack our law enforcement and this FBI will find you and bring you to justice.’ DHS and FBI have since refused to correct the record. [DOJ dropped] charges against Ms. Martinez, who was shot five times by these agents,” Durbin said.

“In another event, an ICE agent shot and killed Silverio Villegas-Gonzalez shortly after he dropped his children off at school and daycare. Publicly released video footage and the ICE agent’s own statement contradict DHS claims that the ICE agent who shot him was ‘dragged a significant distance’ and ‘feared for his life.’ In the past, the FBI would have swiftly responded to these shootings, gathering evidence and working with the Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division to conduct a civil rights investigation. But not now,” Durbin continued.

“Director Patel, why has the FBI refused to investigate either of these shootings?” Durbin pressed.

Director Patel asserted that the incidents are under investigation. However, the FBI has provided no information about civil rights investigations in either case.

“Do you still stand behind the false statements you made on social media after Marimar Martinez was shot?” Durbin replied.

Director Patel deflected, offering a flimsy explanation that his statements were “clipped together to make it sound like I lied.”

Pushing back on the claims Director Patel made on social media, which he emphasized that he stands by, Durbin responded, “Let me quote what you said: ‘Attack our law enforcement and the FBI will find you and bring you to justice.’ Were you bringing her to justice by shooting her five times?”

“We didn’t shoot her,” Director Patel claimed despite body camera footage from the incident and text messages from the federal immigration agent who shot Ms. Martinez making clear that she was shot five times by the federal agent.

“The federal government did, and you are responsible for determining whether there was any violation of federal rights statutes, and you refuse to do so. Unfortunately giving a blank slate to these agents is not an encouragement for good conduct, and you know that as well as I do,” Durbin said.

Durbin then questioned Director Patel about the FBI’s recent decision to gut hiring standards. In June, the FBI reportedly revised their hiring policy to remove theft from an employer, sex solicitation, and bestiality from the list of automatic hiring disqualifications; however, some of these changes may have been quietly implemented as early as February 2025. Yesterday, Durbin led all Senate Judiciary Committee Democrats in demanding a justification for the degradation of hiring standards, emphasizing that hiring candidates with a history of this conduct makes federal agencies more vulnerable to black mail or counterintelligence exposure.

“According to a memo issued this June, the FBI has lowered its hiring standards by dropping automatic disqualification for applicants who have stolen from prior employers, paid for sex, or engaged in bestiality. In July, you claimed the FBI is ‘losing too many qualified candidates to the rigors and requirements from yesteryear.’ Director Patel, do you believe those who have previously stolen from employers, solicited sex, or engaged in bestiality are qualified candidates the FBI is losing?” Durbin asked.

Director Patel misrepresented the change in hiring standards, arguing that the change was to prevent victims of these acts from being automatically disqualified. Further hedging his track record of purging career FBI officials, Director Patel offered statistics about a recent uptick in hiring; however, Director Patel has purged more than 5,000 nonpartisan career personnel from the agency, including all six former Executive Assistant Directors and at least 18 Special Agents in Charge with little to no explanation.

“What I’m reading to you is that you dropped automatic disqualification for applicants who have been engaged in bestiality. Not victims of bestiality—applicants who have engaged,” Durbin said.

Durbin then grilled Director Patel on his direct involvement in covering up the Epstein files.

“On the Epstein files, do you believe the files contain no meaningful evidence of wrongdoing by others who have not been charged so far?” Durbin asked.

Rather than answer Durbin’s question, Director Patel spoke about the number of pages released of the Epstein files. Notably, the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) Office of Inspector General (OIG) has launched a probe into whether the DOJ properly complied with the Epstein Files Transparency Act, as many of the documents were not released on the timeline laid out by the law.

“He just missed one important point. You may remember it. Congress had to pass a law requiring the disclosure of the Epstein files. We had to wait until a woman was elected to Congress to give us the necessary votes in the House to discharge the bill and force a vote in the House on the release of the Epstein files. This was not volunteered by the Trump Administration. It took a law to force them to do it,” Durbin said.

Durbin concluded by questioning Director Patel about the blatant corruption committed by Trump Administration officials without consequence.

“You’ve touted the Trump Administration and FBI success in cracking down on fraud and corruption. In a press conference in June, you stated, ‘You should take a look at what leadership from the White House and President Trump’s prioritization to go after and combat fraud looks like. Fraud is no longer being tolerated. It’s not being put up with,’” Durbin said.

“Recent reports, Mr. Patel, have revealed that Corey Lewandowski, while he was at the Department of Homeland Security, approached senior officials from Qatar and UAE, offering to represent them on the side [on] issues that fell under DHS purview. Director Patel, was the FBI aware of Corey Lewandowski’s efforts to sell access to government services for personal gain before this report was published?” Durbin asked.

Director Patel denied knowledge of Mr. Lewandowski’s actions.

“Has the FBI initiated any investigation into these allegations regarding Mr. Lewandowski?” Durbin pushed further.

Director Patel deflected the question, asserting that this falls under DHS’ purview.

“You can’t say that the FBI has done any investigation into this allegation?” Durbin replied.

title: “Kash Patel Is The Least Qualified And Most Partisan FBI Director In Our Nation’s History,” Durbin Says In Opening Statement In Senate Judiciary Committee FBI Oversight Hearing
text:
In his opening statement, Durbin criticized Director Patel’s failed leadership, citing his weaponization of the FBI, his involvement in covering up the Epstein files, his misuse of FBI resources, and more

WASHINGTON – U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, delivered an opening statement in today’s Senate Judiciary Committee hearing conducting oversight on the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) featuring testimony from FBI Director Kash Patel. During his remarks, Durbin underscored that Americans are less safe with Kash Patel leading the FBI as he is far more concerned with weaponizing the agency against the President’s perceived political enemies while covering up the wrongdoings of President Trump’s allies. Further, Director Patel’s personal conduct—wasting and exploiting FBI resources and failing to account for when official business ends and personal recreation begins—has shown that he is a liability to national security.

Key Quotes:

“Let me say at the outset, that we just heard again, an introduction by the Chairman [Grassley] that gave reference to Crossfire Hurricane and a lot of things that are in the history of the Department of Justice and the Federal Bureau of Investigation. Over a year ago, all of the Democrats on this Committee said, ‘Stop giving these speeches, and bring the people before us to testify under oath as to what actually happened.’”

“Jack Smith, the special counsel, who is a constant reference point when it comes to this ‘Grand Conspiracy,’ has volunteered for more than a year to appear before this Committee under oath and answer the questions. What more could we ask of him?”

“Perhaps in a few weeks when we have been promised he will show up, they [Republicans] could start by explaining, why did you wait a year if we are talking about a ‘Grand Conspiracy?’ Jack Smith, the special counsel, will be under oath before this committee. Each of us will have a chance to ask pertinent questions to clear it up. For some reason, the decision was made at some level to let this controversy fester rather than bring the person in who could actually answer the questions.”

“Director Robert Mueller led the FBI at this tumultuous time [post-9/11]. He, more than any single individual, was responsible for modernizing the FBI to combat the threats we face in the 21st century. I was proud to work with him on a bipartisan basis… We didn’t always agree, but I always respected him. He was a patriot and a person of honesty and integrity.”

“Modernizing the FBI has not been an easy process. Balancing a growing focus on national security and terrorism prevention efforts with traditional work investigating white-collar crime and corruption has taken a lot of time and effort. Over the years, the FBI, as it gained more authorities, at times in history, misused it. There is still work to be done to earn public trust and ensure the most powerful federal investigative agency in the world only engages in lawful operations.”

“Continuing to meet new threats while tackling these challenges requires steady, committed leadership from someone who understands the stakes and has the humility to lead as a servant of the public, like Bob Mueller. Sadly for the American people, the current director does not meet these standards. Mr. Patel is the least qualified and most partisan FBI Director in our nation’s history. He does not have the judgment, experience, or temperament of Director Mueller.”

“Before he was confirmed, Mr. Patel falsely claimed in public that the FBI ‘was planning January 6 for a year.’ He compiled an enemies list of public servants he called ‘government gangsters’ who he promised to target if he was confirmed as head of the FBI.”

“Despite the warnings of Senate Democrats during his confirmation hearing, our Republican colleagues chose to ignore these facts to prioritize President Trump’s retribution campaign over the safety of Americans. They joined on a partisan basis, confirming Director Patel to lead the FBI.”

“Under Mr. Patel’s failed leadership, decades of efforts to modernize and reform the FBI are being undone, and the Bureau has been reshaped as a political weapon against President Trump’s political enemies and a shield to protect the President and his MAGA loyalists—not the American people. Director Patel has been the central figure pushing the so-called ‘Grand Conspiracy,’ diverting FBI resources to inane debunked conspiracy theories that the ‘deep state’ has been targeting President Trump since his first campaign.”

“Director Patel is also wasting FBI resources to relitigate the 2020 presidential election. How many times have nominees who are judges, respected professionals, professors come before this Committee and refused to acknowledge what every eighth-grader in America knows? President Trump lost the 2020 election to Joe Biden by 7 million votes. That’s simple. It’s obvious. It’s a matter of fact. Yet, these nominees refused to acknowledge that reality because this is part of the great conspiracy theory that Trump never loses anything.”

“To weaponize the FBI against the President’s opponents, Director Patel has overseen a purge of thousands of law enforcement officials. From analysts and agents to the most senior leadership, the Bureau has been deprived of tens of thousands of years of cumulative experience.”

“Director Patel has installed MAGA loyalists as political appointees in key career positions. And he even imposed loyalty tests, requiring FBI officials to undergo polygraphs to say whether they ever criticize him.”

“Thousands of agents have been reassigned from their primary criminal and national security mission to immigration enforcement, with the number of FBI personnel working on immigration matters increasing by over 2,000 percent as of last September.”

“In total, over 9,000 FBI personnel—25 percent of the Bureau—worked on immigration cases between January and September of last year. As part of this shift in resources, the Department of Justice shut down almost 23,000 criminal cases in the first six months of the Trump Administration.”

“To replace the career professionals he purged, Director Patel has gutted hiring standards. Today will be his opportunity under oath to answer some basic questions about the standards being used for new FBI agents. In an interview in July, he claimed the FBI is ‘losing too many qualified candidates to the rigors of the requirements from yesteryear.’ What are those so-called obsolete requirements? According to a memo issued in June, the FBI has removed from its list of automatic hiring disqualifications theft from an employer, sex solicitation, and bestiality.”

“To add insult to injury, Director Patel is trying to take credit for the successful efforts of state and local law enforcement to reduce violent crime. The reality is that violent crime spiked during the COVID-19 pandemic and has been steadily and consistently declining since 2022. Every member of this Committee knows that our state and local police – not the FBI – are primarily responsible for combatting violent crime. Don’t believe me? Look at the data. Cities where the National Guard or other federal forces were not deployed had a 2025 drop in violent crime similar to the cities where they were deployed.”

“It is misleading and offensive for this Administration – which has coddled January 6 rioters by giving them full, unconditional pardons from the President as one of his first acts in office. This Administration has ended the careers of thousands of professional FBI agents because they didn’t meet some political test and blocked hundreds of millions of dollars in grants to local law enforcement– to claim credit for the work of our brave frontline police officers. That is not ‘backing the blue’ by any standard.”

“In fact, the cities where federal forces were deployed experienced widespread abuses of the constitutional rights of their residents—including multiple lethal shootings of American citizens.”

“The FBI is charged with investigating deadly uses of force by federal agents, but it has turned its back on its duties under Director Patel. Instead, the Department of Homeland Security is now the primary investigator of whether its own poorly vetted and trained employees violated the law during the ill-conceived missions.”

“Director Patel has also played a key role in the Trump Administration’s cover up of the Epstein files. Director Patel diverted more than a thousand FBI agents from their critical missions to work on 24-hour shifts reviewing every page of the Epstein files. These personnel were instructed to ‘flag’ any records in which President Trump’s name was mentioned. That review ended in an unsigned memorandum from the Department of Justice and FBI simply claiming, ‘there is no incriminating client list.’ Director Patel has still not responded to our letter from more than a year ago asking about his personal role in this cover-up. But we now know that Director Patel reportedly joined a meeting in the White House Situation Room about how to protect the President from the fallout from this cover up of the Epstein files.”

“Director Patel failed to ensure the Trump Administration actually released, as they were required, everything about Epstein and his co-conspirators. This has come at the expense of the American people, who deserve transparency. And it has also been at the expense of the survivors of Epstein’s abuse, who deserve justice and accountability.”

“So today, we find ourselves in a position where the FBI is expending immense resources to protect President Trump politically and deliver retribution to his enemies—but is diverting resources away from protecting the safety, security, and rights of ordinary Americans and their families.”

“I was proud to be part of bipartisan efforts over the many years to ensure the FBI protected both the security and freedom of the American people. And I’m disappointed that this Committee has stood by since January 2025 as that work has been undone.”

“I look forward to a day – hopefully in the near future – when this Committee will fulfill its duty to hold Director Patel accountable for his leadership.”

title: Washington’s Secret Spending Stops Today!
text:
WASHINGTON – After years of fighting to increase transparency around Washington spending, President Donald Trump signed U.S. Senator Joni Ernst’s (R-Iowa) bipartisan bill, the Stop Secret Spending Act, into law to require public disclosure of previously hidden government expenditures.

Current law requires most federal spending to be publicly reported on USAspending.gov, allowing taxpayers to see who receives federal funds and details about how, where, and why the money is spent. However, a loophole has allowed agencies to withhold thousands of spending arrangements known as Other Transaction Agreements (OTAs) from public disclosure – the Stop Secret Spending Act closes that loophole.

The law also requires the federal government to publish a summary of any spending that remains exempt from public disclosure, including the total amount withheld and the justification for doing so, increasing transparency and accountability across the federal government.

Because bureaucrats couldn’t be trusted to fully enact the original law, the Stop Secret Spending Act includes several safeguards to guarantee full transparency:

Over the next decade, the Inspectors General of government agencies and departments are required to conduct regular reviews to ensure spending information is being provided to taxpayers in a timely, complete, and accurate manner;

The Government Accountability Office will also conduct a review and make recommendations for improvements; and

The Treasury Department must issue an annual report providing the total amount spent on grants, contracts, and other awards not included in USAspending.gov along with the reason that data is not posted for the public.

“Taxpayers deserve the receipts. For years, I’ve fought to drag Washington’s secret spending into the sunlight, and I’m grateful President Trump signed my bill into law,” said Sen. Ernst. “Now, bureaucrats won’t be able to spend Americans’ hard-earned money in the dark.”

“Americans deserve to know how their hard-earned tax dollars are being used. Right now, federal agencies are able to hide billions of dollars in spending from public view through agreements that are not subject to normal government spending disclosure requirements,” said Sen. Hassan. “I’m pleased to see this bipartisan bill to bring more transparency to government spending become law.”

“Waste, fraud, and abuse of taxpayer resources by the federal government remains a concern for all Americans,” said Sen. Peters. “This commonsense legislation will let Americans see how their hard-earned dollars are used, so I’m quite glad that this critical, bipartisan bill has become law.”

“For too long, billions of dollars in federal spending have gone unreported due to a loophole in the disclosure of other transaction agreements,” said Rep. Panetta. “I’m proud that our bipartisan, bicameral Stop Secret Spending Act has been signed into law, closing that gap by ensuring these expenditures are accounted for on USAspending.gov. This is a commonsense step toward strengthening public trust, improving fiscal accountability, and ensuring responsible stewardship of taxpayer dollars.”

“Washington has spent far too long operating behind closed doors, and the American people deserve better. That is why I introduced the Stop Secret Spending Act, and I am proud to see President Trump sign it into law,” said Rep. Moore. “I am grateful to Senator Joni Ernst and Congressman Jimmy Panetta for standing with me in this fight to bring greater transparency and accountability to federal spending. This law closes a loophole that allowed billions of taxpayer dollars to escape public scrutiny and makes clear that American taxpayers have a right to know how their money is being spent. This is an important step toward changing the way Washington does business and putting taxpayers first.”

Background:

Senator Ernst has long advocated for greater transparency in federal spending. She first introduced the bipartisan Stop Secret Spending Act after raising concerns about billions of dollars in undisclosed federal spending through Other Transaction Agreements (OTAs) and has repeatedly pushed the legislation forward.

Over the past five fiscal years (October 1, 2021, through September 14, 2026):

The Department of War has obligated $85 billion for thousands of OTAs, through over 30,000 hard-to-track contracts, of which 1,898 are unclassified contracts of $10-million-or-more (438 $10mil+ contracts in just this fiscal year alone).

The Department of Homeland Security has obligated $52.2 million for over 700 OTAs; and

The Department of the Interior has obligated $858.8 million for over 220 OTAs, with many of these actually paid out for the Department of Health and Human Services’ ARPA-H biomedical research contracts.

In August, the Stop Secret Spending Act passed the U.S. Senate unanimously and was sent to the president’s desk. Ernst has continued working across the aisle to advance the legislation and ensure taxpayers have greater visibility into how their hard-earned dollars are spent.

title: Gallego, Kelly Help Secure Nearly $10 Million in FEMA Reimbursements for Pima County
text:
After years of advocacy, senators help secure funding for Pima County’s efforts to provide shelter to asylum seekers during height of border crisis

WASHINGTON – Today, Senators Ruben Gallego (D-AZ) and Mark Kelly (D-AZ) announced the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) has reimbursed Pima County approximately $6.1 million for eligible costs incurred in fiscal year 2023 and an additional $3.5 million for fiscal year 2024 — nearly $10 million combined.

“Pima County stepped up when the federal government asked them to, and for over two years, they waited for Washington to keep its promise and pay the bill,” said Senator Ruben Gallego. “I wasn’t going to let Arizona communities that did the right thing get left holding the bag. We kept pushing FEMA to do its job, and now Pima County is getting the nearly $10 million it was owed.” “The federal government made a commitment to reimburse Pima Country when the community stepped up to the plate during a difficult time,” said Senator Kelly. “Senator Gallego and I pushed for this long overdue reimbursement, and we won’t give up until every Arizona organization gets paid.”

The reimbursements follow years of advocacy by Senators Gallego and Kelly, who have pressed FEMA to fulfill its commitment to reimburse Pima County and other Arizona non-profit organizations for eligible costs under the federal Shelter and Services Program (SSP). In July, the senators demanded that FEMA process and reimburse all outstanding eligible SSP claims.

Congress created SSP with bipartisan support to provide funding to local governments and service providers for short-term emergency services, including food and shelter, for asylum seekers who had been legally processed by the Department of Homeland Security at a time when the border was in crisis. Pima County and other Arizona non-profits used the funding to provide temporary shelter, food, transportation, and other basic services – preventing hundreds of thousands of asylum seekers from being released onto the streets of Arizona border communities without support.

The Trump administration later froze SSP funding and questioned whether recipients had facilitated illegal immigration. Pima County disputed those allegations and continued seeking reimbursement for eligible expenses.

Gallego and Kelly are also working with World Hunger Ecumenical Arizona Task Force (WHEAT) and other Arizona organizations still awaiting reimbursement under the federal program. The senators will continue pressing FEMA to resolve all outstanding eligible reimbursement requests and ensure Arizona communities and nonprofits receive the funding they are owed.

title: WATCH: Gallego Calls for Senate Committee to Rein-in AI, Celebrates Supreme Court’s Mail-in Voting Decision
text:
WASHINGTON – Last night, on MSNOW’s “The Weeknight,” Senator Ruben Gallego (D-AZ) echoed his call to establish a bipartisan Senate Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence to rein-in the technology — largely in response to a former Anthropic researcher quitting his role and warning of an industrywide rush to build AI systems that can improve themselves and, in turn, destroy humanity — and applauded the Supreme Court’s decision to prevent the U.S. Postal Service (USPS) from implementing President Trump’s executive order restricting vote-by-mail ahead of the midterm elections.

WATCH: MS NOW’s The Weeknight

On getting all stakeholders together to regulate AI: “We need experts to come in and talk to us—the people who are skeptics, the people who want to regulate, and the people who have a vision for AI. The problem that we have right now is that we don’t know enough… We need to be bringing the best minds around us and figure out how to put up guardrails, and how to do it quickly.

“I’m glad that they [the AI companies] are coming out, but can we really trust people that have an interest, a very corporate—corporate interest for them, for whatever outcome, right? They have to respond to corporate shareholders. We have to respond to the American public, right? I have to make sure that whatever outcome that we decide to put together for these guardrails aren’t designed basically to cover their asses for whatever they mess up later, right?

On the first steps a Senate Select Committee would take: “The first thing we would fix is: get the people around you, besides those three [Musk, Dario, Altman], to give you the information you need to know how bad this is and where this is going.

“Step two is: Are we looking too small? You know, this is going to have to end up being an international agreement, right? Where we have to talk to not just China, the European Union, other friends and allies, to make sure that we all are staying together on this. Because if there’s any type of leakage, if any types of these agents go rogue, they’re not going to care if this was created in China. They will go after the United States and go after China later, or at the same time.”

On President Trump dismissing concerns over AI: “This is why I’m very much in favor of putting a commission together that is akin to the 9/11 Commission to come up with the recommendations that we need, to put into text and move fast. And if their president doesn’t want to vote for this, then we have the votes to override that president because it is bad.

“The voter is really scared about what’s happening right now. They’re scared that their jobs are going to be taken, that their lives are going to be taken. What we understand is humanity could be totally gone within a couple of years.”

On the victory in the Supreme Court over mail-in voting decision: “That’s good for the voters. And look, Arizona—80% of voters in Arizona vote by mail. The vote-by-mail system was started by Republicans. It’s safe. It’s secure. We don’t need last-minute chaos going into an election that’s less than 60 days away.

“Let’s continue moving forward. The Postal Service is there to deliver mail. They’re not there to decide who can get ballots or not. That’s the job of the secretaries of state.”

title: Sens. Gillibrand And Welch, Rep. Schneider Introduce Bill To Repeal And Refund President Trump’s Canadian Tariffs
text:
**WATCH: Gillibrand Discusses the BAD DEAL Act on CNN**

Today, U.S. Senators Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY) and Peter Welch (D-VT) formally introduced the Banning Antiquated Duties and Delivering Equitable American Levies (BAD DEAL) Act to repeal all tariffs levied under Section 338 of the Tariff Act and refund Americans for all duties paid under this authority. This includes President Trump’s 50% tariffs on Canada.

Gillibrand previously announced the bill in August, when Rep. Brad Schneider (D-IL-10) introduced companion legislation in the U.S. House of Representatives. Senators Jacky Rosen (D-NV) and Amy Klobuchar (D-MN) also cosponsor the bill.

A trade war with Canada will be detrimental to New York’s economy. Canada is one of New York State’s largest export markets for both goods and services, and the state imports more than $20 billion annually from Canada. Already, New York families have spent over $5,500 more due to President Trump’s tariff chaos and other reckless policies. These new 50% tariffs on Canada are projected to cost businesses and households across the U.S. up to $10 billion annually.

“President Trump and Republicans promised to lower costs and make life more affordable, but they’ve used their total power in Washington to make life more expensive than ever,” said Senator Gillibrand. “Let’s be clear: the latest tariffs against Canada are a bad deal for New York families. I’m proud to introduce this legislation to end these costly tariffs and refund Americans. It’s past time for President Trump to stop the political games, get back to the negotiation table, and make a deal that lowers costs and strengthens our economy.”

“No good will come of this trade war with Canada. The only thing these tariffs will create is economic pain on both sides of the border, especially for Vermont and the other 33 states that rely on Canada as their largest trading partner,” said Senator Welch. “Imposing on-again, off-again tariffs is the opposite of how we should treat our close friends and longtime allies, but it’s endemic to how the Trump Administration operates. I’m proud to join my colleagues in leading the BAD DEAL Act to repeal these reckless tariffs and reclaim Congress’ constitutional role in setting our trade policy.”

“Canada is Illinois’ largest trading partner. The costly tariffs imposed under Section 338 by Trump hurt everyone and help no one,” said Rep. Schneider. “American families are actively struggling to make ends meet and have had enough of President Trump’s trade war. I’m proud to join my colleagues to introduce the BAD DEAL Act to repeal this outdated tariff authority and issue the refunds Americans deserve. We must rein in Trump’s chaotic and cost-raising tariffs now before he damages our relationship with our friends and neighbors for years to come.”

The president’s tariffs have previously been found to be unconstitutional and have already raised costs on New Yorkers. Poll after poll after poll have found that a resounding majority of Americans oppose Trump’s tariffs actions that have raised prices and hurt their families.

Senator Gillibrand has opposed President Trump’s tariffs since the start of his administration and worked tirelessly to get the American people their money back. Last year, she joined 14 of her colleagues in introducing the Small Business RELIEF Act to end Trump’s Tariff Tax and refund small businesses their duties paid. In March, she and her colleagues introduced the Small Business Liberation 2.0 Act to exempt small businesses from another set of Trump-imposed tariffs and refund what they had already paid.

title: Watch: Gillibrand Demands Immediate Action On Artificial Intelligence, Tariffs, And Menopause Care In CNN Interview
text:
***Watch Senator Gillibrand’s Full Interview Here***

Today, in an interview on CNN’s The Situation Room, U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY) called for immediate congressional action on regulating artificial intelligence, repealing President Trump’s 50% tariffs on Canada, and providing sufficient healthcare to the millions of American women going through menopause.

The interview follows Senator Gillibrand introducing the BAD DEAL Act to repeal and refund Trump’s 50% Canadian tariffs, and it comes ahead of the first ever congressional hearing on menopause that Gillibrand, ranking member of the Senate Special Committee on Aging, is holding tomorrow.

Footage of Senator Gillibrand’s interview with Pamela Brown can be found here.

Transcripts of key moments can be found below:

ON THE URGENT NEED FOR CONGRESS TO PLACE GUARDRAILS ON ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE THAT PUT HUMANITY FIRST:

GILLIBRAND: We need urgent engagement now. We need to be able to have rules of the road, we need to be able to have reliable guardrails, and we need to be able to be talking to these AI companies regularly about how to do this well, how to maintain our leadership, how to maintain the ability to cure cancer and cure disease, and have massive breakthroughs. But we also need to make sure we’re investing in America. We need to make sure we are investing the wealth of AI into a jobs guarantee, into healthcare and education. We need to make sure that we have a plan for how we deal with these models that are doing things that even the experts did not expect them able to do so soon. And so we do need that regulatory clarity now, and we need to work with AI companies. And I do not think President Trump is providing any leadership on this. He’s sold the most efficient chips to China, but again, not making sure that we have rules of the road that our own AI companies can ensure that the public is safe.

BROWN: He’s calling these warnings from these AI leaders a conspiracy. I’m wondering, in your view, does Congress have the sense of urgency that is needed right now to meet this moment, given all the warnings we’re hearing from AI leaders?

GILLIBRAND: I think we should begin hearings immediately. I also think we should work on a bipartisan basis to provide the guidelines and oversight that is needed. AI companies have been, many of them have been asking for this level of engagement and regulation. We’ve seen so many of the harms, but we also have so much promise, and so we want to make sure we’re at the forefront of this technology, that we are competitive, that we can cure cancer and cure other diseases, but we also want to make sure it doesn’t harm humanity, and so that means alignment has to be there. These AI models must be aligned with humanity. Humanity has to be the focus. I worked in our defense bill over the last several months to try to put a human in the loop on all systems and to make sure AI couldn’t be used for domestic surveillance. We wanted to make sure that nuclear weapons would have proper human oversight before an AI model could choose a target or push send on a nuclear weapon. We also wanted to make sure there was humans in the loop for any offensive weapons. Like, I fully understand how efficient and capable an AI system will be for defense to shoot down missiles on their way to American cities, but when you’re talking about choosing a target or deciding when to bomb or where to bomb, that should have a human oversight in all circumstances.

ON GILLIBRAND’S BAD DEAL ACT TO REPEAL AND REFUND PRESIDENT TRUMP’S TARIFFS:

BROWN: You and Senator Peter Welch recently introduced this act to repeal the 50% tariffs placed on Canadian goods and refund Americans for all duties paid. How will this legislation practically manage the logistics of refunding Americans, the taxes they’ve already paid. How would this work?

GILLIBRAND: Well, what the bill is that Senator Welch and I have would repeal these tariffs completely. President Trump has created so much chaos in the market because of these tariffs. In Canada, this new 50% tariff is going to raise prices for New Yorkers on food, on clothing, on everyday household goods, and on building materials, which again will increase the rate of housing and how much it costs to get a better apartment to rent or to buy a home. And so we are trying to repeal those tariffs immediately because what President Trump has done is illegal and creating massive chaos in the economy for everyday New Yorkers and everyday Americans.

ON GILLIBRAND HOLDING THE FIRST EVER CONGRESSIONAL HEARING ON MENOPAUSE:

BROWN: Before we let you go, Senator, I want to ask you about you recently making history by convening the first ever congressional hearing on menopause through the Senate Committee on Aging. Tell us why that was so important to you to bring this issue to light.

GILLIBRAND: Well, menopause is what millions of American women go through. 75 million women are either in perimenopause, menopause, or postmenopause in America today, and the inadequate amount of research and analysis and care for these women is literally disgraceful. It’s basic health care for most Americans, and because it is so underresearched and underresourced, a lot of American women don’t know how to best treat their symptoms. The symptoms can be wide-ranging to debilitating, and women have the right to get access to healthcare to make them be able to function in life, to be able to continue to work, continue to thrive, continue to provide for their families. But because of the lack of research, because of the lack of funding, because of the lack of information and availability of treatments, a lot of women needlessly suffer and are unable to live full lives.

title: Grassley Questions Director Patel at Senate Judiciary Committee Oversight Hearing
text:
WASHINGTON – Senate Judiciary Committee Chairman Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa) questioned Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) Director Kash Patel at today’s FBI oversight hearing.

Grassley pressed Patel on the FBI’s work to root out suspected Afghan terrorists that entered the country through the Biden administration’s Operation Allies Welcome program and the FBI’s expansion of counter drone capabilities, as well as the FBI’s efforts to combat whistleblower retaliation and shine light on Operation Round River and the Crossfire Hurricane investigation. Patel thanked Grassley for his Big Tech oversight, which the director confirmed has resulted in “significantly improved” child safety reporting.

Video and a transcript of Grassley and Patel’s exchange follow.

VIDEO

Protecting Kids Online

GRASSLEY: “In April 2026, I wrote to eight major internet companies to ensure NCMEC received enough data to hold online child predators accountable. NCMEC informed me last month that several companies have ‘significantly improved’ their child safety reporting. The FBI has assigned personnel to NCMEC to review online reports.

“What improvements can these companies make so that the FBI can more effectively turn the tables and hunt these predators down?”

PATEL: “These companies… [have] allowed us to gain access to their intelligence and their databases for the first time ever, in a secure fashion, specifically for the role of man-hunting child predators and finding missing and exploited children.

“As I stated in my opening, we have found and located over 11,000 children – that's up 20%. That's never happened before. So, thank you for that jolt in the arm that was needed in the private sector. We're going to continue to expand those engagements and work with Congress...so that this continuous flow of data can come in legally and lawfully, and that law enforcement can use it.”

Oversight of the Afghan Parole Program

GRASSLEY: “The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has produced to my office letters of recommendation for two Afghan evacuees placed in the United States during the Biden administration. Department of Homeland Security has confirmed in writing that the government official who signed the letters was Morgan Killington. According to State Department emails, Killington is not a real person.

“The Afghan evacuee charged with shooting two West Virginia National Guardsmen and the Afghan evacuee charged with funding ISIS-K received those letters of recommendation. Clearly, this is a sign of failed vetting.

“Is the FBI performing ongoing reviews to ensure known or suspected terrorists didn’t slip into the country or otherwise should’ve been barred from entry? What has the FBI found to date?”

PATEL: “We are working with our partners at DHS who lead this mission… the number of known or suspected terrorists encountered at the northern and southern border have dropped, thanks to the [security] of the southern border and thanks to the presence of law enforcement and DHS on the northern border

“We're going to continue to work with our intel partners to reach back through and analyze Operation Allies Welcome after the disastrous withdrawal from Afghanistan, and we’ll continue to vet those individuals to make sure we never have an event, a tragic terrorist attack, like we witnessed here in the heart of Washington, D.C., last year in Thanksgiving.”

Uncovering Prohibited Access Files and Operation Round River

GRASSLEY: “At last year’s oversight hearing, I raised concerns about FBI files being hidden in Prohibited Access and Restricted Access cases. You noted last year that you’d produce records found in these types of cases, which you’ve done a good job of.

“Please update the committee on the steps you’ve taken to ensure these types of records are discoverable and that records can’t be hidden from Congress, the courts and the American people.”

PATEL: “The prohibitive cases, Mr. Chairman, were created just for that purpose – to evade transparency [and] to evade promulgation of FBI records that should be made available under FOIA and constitutional oversight. So, we simply did the following: I eliminated prohibited cases… we will work with your committee to continue producing records for what used to be called prohibitive cases.”

GRASSLEY: “As I noted in my opening statement, I have concerns about how Round River records were stored, managed and classified. Round River was the operation that shut down certain government sources regarding the Biden family with apparently no justification. For example, some records include banner markings with ‘Round River’ as a classification code. This is highly unusual, if not outright improper.

“What steps have you taken to investigate any improper classification of Round River records and hold people accountable?”

PATEL: “Thanks to your referral, Mr. Chairman, and shedding light on this, we looked at the classification processes surrounding this ‘creation’ of a [classification] called Round River. We discovered that there was no FBI policy to substantiate such a classification, and that it was basically made up.

“So now, working with you and your staff, we are committed to continue to produce [records], on top of the nearly 2,000 pages of documents on Round River that we've already produced… We are conducting an internal investigation through the Inspection Division on the individuals who launched and codified this false and fake [classification].”

Combating Whistleblower Retaliation

GRASSLEY: “According to an August 2026 Justice Department Inspector General report, FBI officials during [former FBI Director] Wray's tenure retaliated against an FBI employee named Jacob Mercer. These FBI officials are still employed.

“At your nomination hearing, you committed to ensuring whistleblowers are protected from retaliation. What steps has the FBI taken to hold the retaliators accountable for their violation of law, and if nothing's been done, will you commit to updating the committee on accountability measures?”

PATEL: “That is in the middle of an internal investigation. As soon as I'm able to update the committee, after working with our Department of Justice partners, I will do so.”

Expanding FBI’s Counter Drone Capacity

GRASSLEY: “The Safer Skies Act granted long overdue authority to state and local law enforcement agencies to protect their communities from malicious drones. As of July 1st, the FBI had certified 46 eligible agencies to conduct drone mitigation, training a maximum of 16 officers per month. We can’t get our law enforcement agencies certified to use these authorities fast enough.

“What’s the FBI doing to expand and expedite its counter drone training capacity for eligible state and local law enforcement agencies?”

PATEL: “The FBI, under my leadership, stood up the first ever counter-UAS school, called NCUTC, down at Redstone Arsenal in Huntsville, Alabama, where we've trained hundreds of law enforcement officers…

“What we've asked Congress for is increased funding so that we can triple the size of that school, allowing more state and local officers to come in and work with us, and deploy them like we did during the World Cup on our ground intercept teams to cover 11 separate venues and take down 750 drones. We need more equipment, more tech and more bodies trained.”

Exposing the Weaponized Crossfire Hurricane Investigation

GRASSLEY: “For almost a decade, I’ve exposed political weaponization during Crossfire Hurricane and so have you. President Trump issued an Executive Order in each of his administrations mandating declassification of Crossfire Hurricane records.

“Please describe the steps you’ve taken to ensure full declassification and whether other agencies, like the CIA, have created roadblocks to declassifying all records.”

PATEL: “The Crossfire Hurricane declassification at the FBI, at least what's under my control, Mr. Chairman, has been fully declassified. There is some information in there that I do not control because we do not own it, and we have vigorously worked with our intelligence community partners to declassify that. We've produced the largest amount of Crossfire Hurricane documentation to the Congress ever, and we're going to continue.”

title: Heinrich Leads Fight to Protect State & Tribal Gaming Rights, Votes Against Advancing CLARITY Act
text:
Heinrich to introduce an amendment to protect Indian Gaming Regulatory Act & Tribal-state compacts & prohibit CFTC-registered entities from online sports betting & casino-style gaming

WASHINGTON — U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.) released the following statement after voting against advancing the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act (CLARITY Act), legislation that fails to protect state regulatory authority and Tribal gaming rights from prediction markets’ unlawful online sports and casino-style gaming.

“The legislation we voted on today undermines Tribal sovereignty and states’ police powers. And it directly threatens Tribes’ gaming revenues, which would mean less government services funding across Indian Country. That’s a lose-lose,” said Heinrich. “Giving prediction markets a free pass to sidestep existing law and Tribal sovereignty is wrong, in every conceivable way. That is not to say I oppose digital asset market structure legislation. But what that legislation absolutely must include is commonsense protections for state and Tribal gaming rights, including an Indian Gaming Regulatory Act and Tribal-state compact savings clause and a ban on prediction contracts that function like sports bets or casino games.”

Heinrich plans to introduce an amendment to the CLARITY Act that provides:

An Indian Gaming Regulatory Act (IGRA) and Tribal-state compacts savings clause; and

Prohibitions on Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC)-registered entities from listing prediction contracts that resemble sports bets or casino-style gaming products.

The rapid expansion of sports event contracts and casino-style gaming through prediction markets threatens Tribal gaming revenues and the sovereignty of Tribal nations that rely on gaming to fund essential government services, including health care, public safety, education, housing, and social services. By offering products that function like sports bets while operating outside the regulatory framework governing gaming, prediction markets could divert a significant share of revenue away from Tribal governments.

Under the Indian Gaming Regulatory Act (IGRA) of 1988, gaming on Tribal lands is subject to a carefully negotiated framework that protects Tribal sovereignty and establishes the roles of Tribal, state, and federal governments. Following the Supreme Court’s 2018 decision in Murphy v. National Collegiate Athletic Association, Tribes also began entering the legal sports betting market through agreements with states.

Prediction markets are now attempting to offer sports betting nationwide by classifying sports and event contracts as financial products rather than gambling. These markets operate under the authority of the CFTC, which has asserted jurisdiction over prediction contracts and treated them as financial derivatives rather than sports wagers.

The CLARITY Act could further entrench this loophole. By creating exemptions from federal securities regulation for certain digital asset platforms and decentralized finance infrastructure, the bill could allow prediction markets to expand sports betting and casino-style gaming nationwide without complying with the state- and Tribal-based regulatory frameworks that govern legal gaming.

Without clear protections for Tribal and state gaming rights, prediction markets could compete directly with Tribal gaming while avoiding the laws and agreements designed to protect Tribal sovereignty. Congress should ensure that digital asset market structure legislation does not create a federal pathway for companies to circumvent IGRA, Tribal-state gaming compacts, or state gaming laws.

In addition to the amendment Heinrich plans to introduce, Heinrich cosponsored another amendment to the CLARITY Act that would stop stablecoin companies from offering rewards or interest like a bank does, which could hurt local banks, reduce the money they have available to lend to families and small businesses, and increase the amount of funds in stablecoin accounts that are not insured by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC). The amendment is led by U.S. Senators Jerry Moran (R-Kan.), and Jack Reed (D-R.I.).

In July, Heinrich led a letter urging the leadership of the U.S. Senate Committees on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs; and Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry to regulate prediction markets offering nationwide sports and event wagering. The letter is supported by the Indian Gaming Association (IGA), National Congress of American Indians (NCAI), Santa Ana Pueblo, Sandia Pueblo, Ohkay Owingeh Pueblo, Laguna Pueblo, San Felipe Pueblo, Kewa Pueblo, Cochiti Pueblo, Acoma Pueblo, Jemez Pueblo, Santa Clara Pueblo, Taos Pueblo, Tesuque Pueblo, Zia Pueblo, Isleta Pueblo, Pojoaque Pueblo, and Mescalero Apache Tribe.
