title: Fitzpatrick-Led Effort to Shield Ratepayers from Data Center Costs Passes House
text:
Bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act Passes 417–3, advancing Fitzpatrick’s broader push to make data center growth accountable to families and communities

WASHINGTON, D.C. — After months of pushing for stronger protections around rapidly expanding data center development, Congressman Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-01) marked a major bipartisan breakthrough in that effort as the House passed the Ratepayer Protection Act (H.R. 9340) by an overwhelming 417–3 vote.

The legislation, cosponsored by Fitzpatrick, would help ensure that the extraordinary energy infrastructure costs driven by large-scale data center development are borne by the companies creating that demand—not shifted onto families and small businesses through higher utility bills.

The Ratepayer Protection Act would require state public utility commissions to consider standards ensuring large-load data centers cover the incremental costs of the generation, transmission, and distribution infrastructure needed to serve them, while preserving states’ authority over their electricity markets.

“For months, I’ve been working with residents, local leaders, and colleagues on both sides of the aisle to put communities back at the center of this conversation,” said Fitzpatrick. “Families across Bucks and Montgomery Counties should not be asked to pay higher electric bills to cover the massive infrastructure costs created by some of the largest companies in the world. Today’s vote moves us closer to putting that principle into practice. America can lead in innovation without shifting the cost of that growth onto working families, seniors, and small businesses. Growth should strengthen our communities, not come at their expense. Protect our families, respect our communities, and make sure development happens responsibly—that is the standard we are fighting for.”

BACKGROUND

House passage of the Ratepayer Protection Act advances Fitzpatrick’s broader bipartisan effort to establish clear rules for responsible data center growth—protecting families and small businesses, preserving local control, and strengthening transparency and accountability.

As development accelerates across Pennsylvania and the country, Fitzpatrick has worked with residents and local leaders across Bucks and Montgomery Counties to address concerns surrounding utility costs, grid reliability, water and energy use, infrastructure, environmental impacts, and quality of life.

That effort is grounded in three principles: local control, state guardrails, and federal accountability. Communities should have a meaningful voice over what is built and where. States should maintain strong consumer and environmental protections. And the federal government should address challenges that cross local boundaries, including grid reliability, energy markets, ratepayer protections, and national transparency standards.

Fitzpatrick is advancing that framework on several fronts. The Ratepayer Protection Act addresses who pays, helping ensure families and small businesses are not forced to subsidize the extraordinary infrastructure demands of large-scale data centers. The bipartisan Data Center Transparency Act (H.R. 6984) would bring greater scrutiny to energy and water use, environmental impacts, and effects on utility systems and household costs. And the Data Center Bill of Rights (H.Res. 1471) would strengthen local authority, expand transparency, and give communities a meaningful voice before major projects move forward.

Fitzpatrick is also pressing developers to meet clear standards on labor, worker safety, environmental protection, resource use, infrastructure demands, and project costs—so communities have the information and protections they need from the outset.

Taken together, these efforts are aimed at ensuring innovation moves forward without asking families and communities to bear the costs or surrender their voice in the process.

title: Congresswoman Lizzie Fletcher Votes Against New Trump Tariff Powers
text:
Today, Congresswoman Lizzie Fletcher (TX-07) voted against the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, Senate Amendment to H.R. 5334, because, despite its name, it fails to mandate tough sanctions on and hands the President sweeping new tariff authorities.

“Despite its name, the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 fails to sanction Russia, dramatically expands presidential tariff authorities, and represents a threat to Ukraine, to our separation of powers, and to people across the country—which is why I voted against it.

“For years, the Ukrainian people have demonstrated remarkable courage and perseverance in their fight for democracy and the preservation of their sovereignty. I support Ukraine and stand with its people. I also support tough sanctions that hold Russia, Vladimir Putin, and the corporations and people funding Russia’s war accountable, like the ones proposed by this bill. But this bill does not actually impose these sanctions. It leaves these sanctions entirely up to President Trump’s discretion, making them optional without congressional oversight or court review. Since taking office, President Trump has imposed almost no new sanctions on Russia. The bill does not require President Trump to impose any additional sanctions on Russia, and he has given no reason to support the idea that he will. In fact, his actions have demonstrated the opposite.

“For the past 19 months, President Trump has already had the power to impose every sanction authorized by this bill on Russia but has chosen not to. These sanctions are sorely needed to support our Ukrainian allies—and Democrats proposed several amendments to improve this legislation, including to remove the bill’s new tariff authority, authorize military support for Ukraine, and tighten the language so President Trump would have to impose some of these sanctions—but Republicans failed to allow any of these amendments to be incorporated into the bill.

“Instead, this legislation grants the Trump administration new tariff authority to impose a 100 percent tariff on any country of its choosing—for as long as it wants, with virtually no guardrails and without congressional oversight. Since March 2025, Americans have paid more than $350 billion in tariffs the President has imposed solely at his discretion—a staggering cost that will only grow as a result of this bill. President Trump has already imposed tariffs on nearly every country in the world except for Russia. The Supreme Court ruled against President Trump’s tariffs, and Congress should not surrender its tariff authority to the executive branch.

“Make no mistake: Today’s vote is not simply about Russian sanctions—it’s about giving President Trump unnecessary tariff authority and unconstitutional power at the expense of American workers and families who will bear the cost. Congress must find a way to help Ukraine defend itself against Russia’s war of aggression and hold Russia accountable while protecting the American people from a new tariff authority that President Trump is bound to misuse.”

title: Congressman Flood, Nebraska Delegation Mark Another Successful Year of the Nebraska Breakfast in D.C.
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congressman Mike Flood marked the conclusion of the 2026 Nebraska Breakfast, celebrating the 83-year tradition that brings Nebraskans and the federal delegation together in Washington, D.C.

“In its 83rd year, the Nebraska Breakfast brought a little slice of Nebraska Nice to our nation’s capital,” said Congressman Flood. “Held on Wednesdays when both the House and Senate were in session, this tradition gives all Nebraskans visiting Washington, D.C. a chance to stop by, spend time with their federal delegation, and hear firsthand about our priorities and what’s happening on Capitol Hill. I want to thank everyone who stopped by one of our breakfasts this year and helped keep this great Nebraska tradition alive and well.”

Photos of the last Nebraska Breakfast of 2026 can be found by clicking here.

The Nebraska Breakfast is open to all Nebraskans visiting Washington and provides a unique opportunity to hear directly from the entire Nebraska delegation. The tradition was started by Senator Hugh Butler in 1943 and has continued for more than eight decades.

This year, Congressman Flood’s office hosted the Nebraska Breakfast, continuing a longstanding tradition in which offices in Nebraska’s federal delegation alternate hosting responsibilities every year. Congressman Flood included Nebraska trivia questions at each Breakfast, celebrating communities, innovators, and accomplishments across the state.

title: ICYMI: FAA Accepting Public Comments on Proposed Permanent Mar-a-Lago Flight Restrictions Through October 2
text:
On September 2, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) formally proposed making the current airspace restrictions around Mar-a-Lago permanent. The FAA is accepting public comments on the proposal through October 2, 2026.

HOW TO SUBMIT A PUBLIC COMMENT

Members of the public can submit comments on the FAA’s proposal by clicking here or by:

1. Going to Regulations.gov.

2. Entering FAA-2026-10827-0001 in the search box.

3. Following the instructions to submit a comment.

Comments must be submitted by October 2, 2026.

Congresswoman Lois Frankel (FL-22) recently joined Palm Beach County Commissioner Gregg Weiss, Palm Beach Mayor Danielle Moore, and local residents to raise concerns about the FAA’s proposal and explain how members of the public can make their voices heard through the agency’s formal comment process.

Following the event, Rep. Frankel sent a letter to FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford requesting that the FAA:

Delay action on the proposal to make the restrictions permanent;

Extend the public comment period by 60 days, through December 1, 2026, if the agency moves forward, so residents have adequate time to review the proposal and respond;

Hold a public meeting in Palm Beach County so affected residents can ask questions, provide input, and hear directly from the FAA; and

Establish a clear and expedited process to modify or end the restrictions if security circumstances change, rather than locking the community into restrictions that may no longer be necessary.

title: RELEASE: Bipartisan Members of Congress Found Congressional American Film & TV Production Caucus
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, September 16, 2026, U.S. Representatives Brian Jack (GA-03), Laura Friedman (CA-30), Nathaniel Moran (TX-01), Linda Sánchez (CA-38), Nicole Malliotakis (NY-11), and Tom Suozzi (NY-03) founded the bipartisan Congressional American Film & TV Production Caucus.

The bipartisan Congressional American Film & TV Production Caucus will work to revitalize, strengthen, and expand film production across the United States.

For nearly a century, the United States was the undisputed global leader in film and television production, creating stories that inspired generations of Americans, from Rocky to Top Gun.

However, our nation has lost more than 100,000 film and television production jobs since the industry's 2022 peak, more than a third of the workforce. Last year alone, U.S. production spending fell 20 percent while the U.K. grew 15 percent and Eastern Europe grew 78 percent.

In recent years, individual state incentives have been outpaced by subsidies offered by foreign countries, leading to an exodus of film production overseas out of the country. No single state can outbid a foreign government on its own. America should be competing for this work at the national level, and American crews, small businesses, and local economies should be the ones who benefit.

Last month, President Donald J. Trump voiced his support for a bipartisan legislative approach to revitalizing the American film industry, posting on Truth Social, “Republicans and Democrats [should] get together, and immediately craft Legislation to save the Movie, Television, and Entertainment Business in America. Congress should approve, immediately, a Federal Production Incentive to create Entertainment Jobs in America.”

The Congressional American Film & TV Production Caucus is eager to partner with President Trump and his Administration to educate Members of Congress on the economic and cultural importance of American filmmaking and to propose legislative solutions to address the loss of domestic film production.

Caucus Co-Founder and Co-Chairman Congressman Brian Jack (GA-03)said, “I am honored to co-found and co-chair the Congressional American Film & TV Production Caucus. My Congressional District is home to Trilith Studios, and I proudly represent the craftsmen, electricians, and carpenters who work hard to create movies that inspire generations of Americans. I commend President Trump’s leadership in calling for a legislative solution to bring film production back to the United States, and I look forward to working with him and my colleagues in Congress to achieve this important goal.”

Caucus Co-Founder and Co-Chairwoman Congresswoman Laura Friedman (CA-30) said, “We're launching this caucus to show that bringing film and television production back to the United States isn't a partisan fight. Film and television work is leaving this country because 65 other nations decided to compete for these hundreds of thousands of good-paying jobs. A national film tax credit is how we bring that work home, and this caucus is a key step to build support for it.”

Caucus Co-Founder and Co-Chairman Congressman Nathaniel Moran (TX-01) said, "For too long, we've watched jobs in the film and television industry move overseas to the detriment of local communities across America who were the backbone of American storytelling. The American Film & TV Production Caucus is committed to bringing that production back home—back to our sound stages, our small businesses, our caterers, carpenters, electricians, and camera crews who make this industry run in all of our 50 states. Every production that sets up here ripples out, supporting the businesses around it and pumping money into local communities. We need to keep that going and keep American storytelling in America."

Caucus Co-Founder and Co-Chairwoman Congresswoman Linda Sánchez (CA-38) said, “The film and television industry doesn’t just make the shows and movies we all love. It’s an economic engine that employs 2 million American jobs throughout the United States. I’m proud to help launch this bipartisan caucus to support the workers and small businesses who make this industry run, and to find new ways to maintain those jobs and bring more of them back home.”

Caucus Co-Founder and Co-Chairwoman Congresswoman Nicole Malliotakis (NY-11) said, “I am proud to serve as Co-Chair of the Congressional American Film & TV Production Caucus and work on a bipartisan basis to strengthen film and television production here at home. Productions like Blue Bloods, Boardwalk Empire, Ray Donovan, Gotham, and Fallout have supported jobs and economic activity in my district, and we must ensure those opportunities remain in the United States. This caucus will focus on supporting American workers, strengthening domestic production, and keeping America the global leader in film and television.”

Caucus Co-Founder and Co-Chairman Congressman Tom Suozzi (NY-03) said, “The film industry is an economic engine in New York, contributing tens of billions of dollars to the state’s economy every year. I'm proud to help launch the Congressional American Film and TV Production Caucus to promote film production in the United States and continue advocating for an industry that supports thousands of jobs and enriches the cultural fabric of my district.”

Congressman Nathaniel Moran, Congresswoman Linda Sánchez, Congresswoman Nicole Malliotakis, and Congressman Tom Suozzi are members of the House Committee on Ways and Means, the chief tax-writing committee in Congress.

Congressman Brian Jack serves on the House Committee on Rules, which controls the flow of legislation.

And, Congresswoman Laura Friedman is one of the only credited film producers ever elected to Congress.

Congressional Caucuses, officially known as Congressional Member Organizations, are administered through the House Committee on Administration.

###

title: Congressman Evans Introduces Bill to Increase Northern Colorado's Water Supply
text:
WASHINGTON — Today, Congressman Gabe Evans introduced the Greeley Land Exchange Act, which transfers land owned by the United States Forest Service (USFS) to the City of Greeley for city-owned land located within the Cache la Poudre Wilderness Area.

The Greeley Land Exchange Act would streamline maintenance operations, reduce administrative delays, and enable the city to more easily access and maintain its critical water infrastructure without navigating repeated permitting processes.

Under existing law, the City of Greeley is required to apply for special use permits any time they need to conduct maintenance activities and access the Milton Seaman Reservoir. This reservoir is owned and operated by the City of Greeley, supplying drinking water to more than 120,000 residents and serving as Greeley’s largest, most utilized water storage system. Greeley describes the reservoir as part of its network of mountain reservoirs that capture and store snowmelt and runoff to help provide a dependable water supply.

This land transfer would allow the city to gain ownership of the federally owned parcel, which is immediately adjacent to Milton Seaman Reservoir, making it easier to access and maintain the critical infrastructure serving the community.

This bill comes at a time when Colorado’s communities are experiencing record-low snowpack levels as a result from extreme weather conditions and an increasing demand of water supplies.

“Northern Colorado communities depend on reliable water infrastructure, and maintaining that infrastructure shouldn’t require navigating unnecessary federal red tape every time work needs to be done. The Greeley Land Exchange Act is a commonsense solution that gives Greeley direct access to essential systems at Milton Seaman Reservoir while also benefiting the Forest Service and preserving public access to surrounding federal lands. I'm proud to work alongside local community leaders to drive solutions like this forward to cut unnecessary delays, protect our water, and make government work better for the people it serves.” –– Congressman Gabe Evans

“This land exchange will help Greeley optimize its reservoir operations, while maintaining public access and recreation. The City’s Kelly Flats property is a spectacular site that can be better managed for public access through USFS, so this exchange is really in the public’s best interest.” — Mayor Dale Hall

“Greeley’s long partnership with the USFS on reservoir operations, wildfire recovery and source water protection is greatly appreciated by the city. We are pleased to introduce a land exchange bill that would transfer a beautiful 40-acre property with vast recreational and wilderness value on the Wild and Scenic, Cache la Poudre River at Kelly Flats to the USFS, in exchange for lands adjacent to Greeley’s Milton Seaman Reservoir” — Cole Gustafson, Source of Supply Manager

The bill also mutually benefits the Forest Service by providing direct access for road maintenance and forest health activities, while strengthening wilderness continuity and preserving recreational opportunities for the public.

“Colorado’s public lands are meant to be enjoyed, and preserving access for the people who hike, fish, hunt, and recreate here is incredibly important to us. We appreciate Congressman Evans for listening to Coloradans and working to ensure the Greeley Land Exchange Act protects public access while allowing this land exchange to move forward. This is a solution that keeps these outdoor spaces accessible to Coloradans for generations to come.” –– Sabrina Stoker, Executive Director, Cache la Poudre River National Heritage Area

Under the Greeley Land Exchange Act:

The City of Greeley would convey approximately 40 acres of City-owned land to the federal government, excluding all City-owned water rights, in exchange for approximately 78 acres of National Forest System land administered by the Forest Service.

The federal government would retain a perpetual, non-exclusive easement for public nonmotorized access over the Seaman Reservoir Trail and Wintersteen Trail to adjacent National Forest System land. The United States would also retain access for administrative, emergency, inspection, maintenance, repair, reconstruction, and resource-management purposes.

The City of Greeley would pay the costs associated with completing the exchange, including appraisals, surveys, title work, environmental assessments, and closing expenses.

The exchange is intended to reduce administrative delays surrounding access to Greeley’s water infrastructure while providing the Forest Service with land that can be incorporated into the surrounding National Forest System and protected areas.

title: Congressman Gabe Evans’ Bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act Passes the House
text:
WASHINGTON — Today, Congressman Gabe Evans’ bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act passed the U.S. House of Representatives by an overwhelming vote of 417-3, advancing legislation designed to protect American families and small businesses from bearing the infrastructure costs created by large data centers.

The bill requires that large energy load data centers be responsible for the costs of all new energy infrastructure necessary to serve them. This protects existing ratepayers from having costs shifted to them. The bill also requires that states which currently have no standards specific to data centers are to commence hearings and make state-specific determinations for large-load data centers.”

The House passage follows unanimous approval by the House Energy and Commerce Committee in July, where the bill advanced 52–0.

“Hardworking families should not have to subsidize the energy demands of data centers. America needs the infrastructure to lead the world in AI and outcompete Communist China, but we cannot have that growth at the expense of hardworking families, farmers, seniors, and small businesses. My bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act ensures large data centers pay for the infrastructure they require while giving states the flexibility to determine what works best for their communities. I’m incredibly proud to lead the charge on this pivotal issue, ensure our ratepayers are protected, and keep American innovation moving forward.” –– Congressman Gabe Evans

“Floridians are already dealing with sky-high electric bills. They should not be forced to subsidize the enormous energy demands of the world’s richest corporations. If Big Tech builds a massive AI data center, Big Tech—not hardworking families, farmers or small businesses—should pay for the power and grid upgrades it requires. The bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act is an important first step that can help lower costs for our neighbors back home and empower states to set additional, strict guardrails.” –– Congresswoman Kathy Castor

“When done responsibly, data center development leads to longer term investments and broader infrastructure improvements in the communities where they’re built. The Ratepayer Protection Act helps to safeguard these benefits by ensuring that the companies who are building data centers—and not American families and small businesses—are paying for the electricity they use. U.S. leadership in the race to AI dominance is critical to our economic prosperity and national security, so we need to keep building the needed infrastructure with appropriate accountability measures. I'm grateful to Congressman Evans for his tireless work—on a bipartisan basis—to protect ratepayers while ensuring that America continues to lead the world in innovation.” –– Energy and Commerce Committee Chairman Brett Guthrie

Background

If enacted, the legislation would establish federal standards for state regulators to use when reviewing proposals for new large-load customers with an electricity demand of 100 megawatts or more. The bill suggests:

Recovering the full incremental cost of grid upgrades from the large-load customer through special rate structures or other agreements, ensuring utilities and regular ratepayers are not left paying for infrastructure if a customer later scales back operations or leaves the system.

Requiring financial assurances that large-load customers will pay for the generation, transmission, and other infrastructure necessary to serve their demand, preventing those costs from being shifted onto families and local businesses through higher electricity rates.

The legislation preserves state flexibility by requiring regulators to consider the large-load standard without mandating one specific rate structure. States would retain the authority to determine how the standard should apply within their own utility systems.

The Ratepayer Protection Act builds on the principles of the Ratepayer Protection Pledge, under which major technology companies, utilities, and governors committed to having data center developers pay the energy and infrastructure costs associated with new data center development.

The bill now heads to the Senate for consideration. Sen. Husted (R-OH) is leading the Senate companion.

title: Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez Votes to Support Ukrainian Defense and Sanction Russia
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — Today, Representative Marie Gluesenkamp Perez reaffirmed her commitment to the Ukrainian community in Southwest Washington by voting for a comprehensive package of sanctions targeting Russia and anyone who facilitates sanctions evasion. The Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 is a critical effort to cripple funding for Russia’s War in Ukraine by penalizing countries that buy Russian oil. The bill was voted on in the Senate earlier this year, where it passed 86-11. The bill went on to pass in the House 262-159.

This package includes a number of sanctions, specifically it would:

Imposes blocking and entry (visa) sanctions on specified Russian officials, including Vladimir Putin and senior political and military leaders, oligarchs who haven’t opposed the war or continue to benefit from ties with the Russian government, executives/controlling owners of major Russian energy projects, foreign companies supporting Russia’s defense industrial base or military, and persons engaged in corruption, money laundering, or sanctions evasion for the Russian government.

Imposes sanctions on Russia’s “shadow fleet,” a network of vessels and supporting entities used to transport Russian oil and other goods while concealing ownership or transactions to circumvent sanctions.

Imposes sanctions on the Central Bank of Russia, Sberbank, VTB Bank, Gazprombank, and other covered Russian financial institutions. Foreign financial institutions engaging in significant transactions with sanctioned Russian institutions shall also be sanctioned.

Imposes sanctions on entities in which the Russian government holds a controlling/majority interest or that are otherwise government-affiliated, and restricts U.S. financial institutions from processing specified transactions involving the Russian government, government-owned entities, or Russian officials.

Restricts certain Russian securities from U.S. exchanges; prohibits new U.S. investment in Russia and its energy sector and transfer of U.S.-produced energy or energy products; prohibits purchases of Russian sovereign debt; authorizes restrictions on certain services to Russia; and sanctions certain financial-messaging providers used to circumvent sanctions.

Directs implementation of existing restrictions on Russian uranium imports under 42 U.S.C. §2297h-10a(d), including covered uranium associated with Rosatom or its subsidiaries or successors, and requires sanctions against specified officials and shareholders.

Extends the deadline of the 1996 Iran Sanctions Act from 2026 to 2031.

In addition to steep sanctions the bill would introduce aggressive secondary measures, including up to 500% duties on Russian goods and up to 100% duties on third-party countries that purchase Russian oil/gas or facilitate sanctions evasion.

“I’m proud to represent one of the largest Ukrainian communities in America–people who have lost fathers, mothers, sons and daughters in the fight to defeat fascism.,” said Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez, “I urge the President to move quickly to implement these critical sanctions to ensure that Putin and his people know there is a steep price for their continued disregard for the sanctity of life.”

Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez has continuously worked to support Ukraine in its fight to end the Russian invasion and to support Ukrainian refugees displaced by the conflict. In 2024, she voted to pass HR 813, allocating over $60 billion in funding for Ukrainian defense. More recently in the FY27 Defense Appropriations markup, she spoke in support of the Ukraine Security Assistance Initiative, a provision to strengthen domestic manufacturing capability to support Ukrainian defense. Additionally, Rep Gluesenkamp Perez supports Ukrainians living in Southwest Washington through her casework channels, helping constituents facing issues with federal agencies. To get in touch or learn about how her office can help with federal agencies, please visit her casework page or Ukrainian Language casework page.

title: Golden statement in support of Russia sanctions bill
text:
WASHINGTON — Congressman Jared Golden (ME-02) released the following statement regarding his vote in favor of HR 5334, legislation to impose sanctions against Russia until it ends its war against Ukraine:

“Every barrel of Russian oil sold on the global market is funding for Vladimir Putin’s war of aggression against Ukraine. Russia is successfully evading the existing sanctions imposed by the U.S. and our Western partners. This bill provides new tools to cut off the oil revenue that’s greasing Russia’s war machine, including tariffs on the top buyers of Russian energy and those countries helping the federation evade existing sanctions.

“Under Putin’s rule, Russia has tested the boundaries of international order and safety at a scale not witnessed in generations. It is waging a war of territorial expansion against our democratic ally in Ukraine. It has made its hostile intent toward the United States and other western democracies clear in its words and actions, including its efforts to undermine U.S. elections.

“Passing this bill will weaken Putin’s hand, and will show the Ukrainians fighting to defend their homes that the United States will not abandon them. I’m proud to vote yes.”

The bill passed the House in a bipartisan vote of 262-159, having previously passed in the Senate 86-11. It now goes to the president to be signed into law.

BACKGROUND:

Russia has successfully evaded existing sanctions on its energy products with a “shadow fleet” of tankers conducting ship-to-ship transfers or rerouting to friendly buyers, often using false documents to hide ownership or cargo point-of-origin. According to one estimate, this shadow fleet transported roughly 3.7 billion barrels of oil in 2025.

In addition to direct sanctions on Russian officials, including President Vladimir Putin, the bill targets Russian financial institutions and defense and energy actors. It also sidesteps Russia’s evasion strategies by targeting the buyers of Russian energy products, authorizing the president to impose tariffs on the top five importers of Russian oil and gas and the top five facilitators of sanctions evasion.

Golden has been a consistent champion for the defense of Ukraine’s sovereignty, having voted in favor of every major military and financial aid for the besieged nation since 2022. To overcome partisan gridlock, in 2024 he co-sponsored the Defending Borders, Defending Democracies Act with Congressman Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-01), which paired aid for Ukraine, Israel and Taiwan with funding the restore order at America’s southern border. Elements of the bill were included in a successful bipartisan foreign aid and border security package enacted by the House that year.

title: Goodlander, Harrigan Launch Bipartisan Hydropower Caucus to Lower Energy Costs
text:
Washington, D.C. — Today, Congresswoman Maggie Goodlander (NH-02) and Congressman Pat Harrigan (NC-10) launched the bipartisan Hydropower Caucus, a new forum to bring together Members of Congress with hydropower and marine energy experts across federal agencies, industry, and stakeholder organizations.

The caucus will support and advocate for America’s first renewable energy resource and keep hydropower at the center of congressional work to lower energy costs, strengthen grid reliability, create jobs, and expand American energy production.

“Hydropower is at the heart of lowering energy costs for hardworking Granite Staters and making America the world’s clean energy superpower,” said Congresswoman Maggie Goodlander. “For generations, hydropower has delivered reliable, homegrown energy to communities across New Hampshire and our country. Our bipartisan caucus will bring together the people with the expertise and ideas we need to cut red tape, invest in innovation, and get more affordable American energy online. I’m proud to lead this effort with Congressman Harrigan, and I will keep working across the aisle to lower costs and build an energy future that works for the people we serve.”

“We are asking more of our electric grid every year, while some of the most reliable power in the country is already being generated by infrastructure we built generations ago,” said Congressman Pat Harrigan. “Hydropower works, it’s American, and there is no good reason outdated permitting and licensing should stand in the way of getting more out of it. The Hydropower Caucus gives us a bipartisan forum to work through those barriers, bring the people who actually build and operate these systems to the table, and make sure this proven source of American energy has a much bigger role in meeting the demand ahead.”

The Hydropower Caucus will serve as a venue to inform and educate Members of Congress and their staff and connect them with hydropower and marine energy subject matter experts at federal agencies, in industry, and at related stakeholder organizations. It will convene discussions on the issues facing hydropower and marine energy, including permitting and licensing reform, federal incentive programs, tax policy, research, development, and deployment.

“Hydropower is the nation’s longest tenured electricity generator, providing clean, reliable, and affordable power to homes and businesses for over a century. Hydropower was the backbone of the industrial revolution and, with proper stewardship, will see us through the information age as well. Hydropower has always benefited from strong bipartisan support as a result, which is why we are so proud that the Granite State’s own Congresswoman Maggie Goodlander (D-NH) has stepped forward to co-chair the Congressional Hydropower Caucus with Representative Pat Harrigan of North Carolina (R). New Hampshire, New England, and the Nation as a whole will benefit from Congresswoman Goodlander’s leadership, ensuring hydropower remains a core component of our domestic energy supply deep into the 21st century,” said Brandon Kibbe, Vice President of External Affairs for Great River Hydro.

“We applaud Congresswoman Maggie Goodlander’s leadership in launching the Hydropower Caucus and elevating the role of America’s first renewable energy resource. This caucus will provide an important forum for educating policymakers and advancing thoughtful solutions on licensing, permitting, tax policy, and other issues that are critical to ensuring hydropower continues to deliver reliable, affordable, and carbon-free electricity for New Hampshire and the nation,” said Bob King, President of the Granite State Hydropower Association.

“NHA applauds Representatives Goodlander and Harrigan for launching the bipartisan Hydropower Caucus. Hydropower is America’s first renewable energy resource, operating in 48 states and providing reliable power to nearly 30 million Americans. Yet too few people understand its benefits and the policy challenges it faces. The Hydropower Caucus can help change that by educating lawmakers and stakeholders about the many ways hydropower supports our communities—not only through affordable, reliable electricity, but also through irrigation, flood control, recreation, and good-paying jobs. We thank Representatives Goodlander and Harrigan for their leadership in advancing this important effort,” said Matthew Allen, Senior Director of Legislative Affairs for the National Hydropower Association.

ADDITIONAL BACKGROUND:

Goodlander has made expanding affordable, reliable hydropower and lowering energy costs a central part of her work in Congress:

Cutting red tape to unlock low-cost hydropower: In July, Goodlander introduced legislation alongside Rep. Carol Miller (R-WV), Sen. Steve Daines (R-MT), and Sen. Maggie Hassan (D-NH) making it easier to get reliable, low-cost hydropower projects built faster at existing Army Corps of Engineers dams.

Investing in existing hydropower and healthy rivers: Goodlander helped introduce the bipartisan Maintaining and Enhancing Hydroelectricity and River Restoration Act, H.R. 2160, to extend a 30 percent investment tax credit through 2031 for upgrades at existing hydroelectric facilities, environmental improvements, and removal of obsolete river barriers.

Listening to New Hampshire hydropower leaders: On National Hydropower Day, Goodlander visited Great River Hydro’s Vernon Station in Hinsdaleto see how New Hampshire hydropower is delivering affordable, reliable power. She also visited Essex Hydro Associates in Penacook and met with Granite State Hydropower Association leaders.

Lowering energy bills: Goodlander is helping to lead a number of bipartisan bills designed to bring down energy costs, including the bipartisan Weatherization Enhancement and Readiness Act, to expand support for home energy-efficiency upgrades and help households save money on utility bills while making homes safer and healthier. She has also championed the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP), a mission-critical program for millions of American families. Goodlander joined the New Hampshire delegation in opposing the Trump administration’s attempt to terminate New Hampshire’s $43.5 million Solar for All grant, which would have supported community energy projects and reduced utility bills for low-income households by 20 percent or more.

Cracking down on runaway utility profiteering: Goodlander helped introduce the Lowering Utility Bills Act, legislation to rein in excessive profits by investor-owned electric utilities, gas utilities, and transmission providers by requiring them to use the lowest return on equity within an established range of reasonableness when setting rates. Goodlander is leading the charge to hold Liberty Utilities accountable after the company refused to serve natural gas customers in New Hampshire’s Lakes Region, causing delays and higher costs for new homes in communities already struggling with the housing crisis. She also worked alongside New Hampshire’s Office of the Consumer Advocate to take on Eversource when the utility proposed a 43.4% rate hike, and pressed the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to crack down on utilities’ attempts to overcharge customers on their electric bills.

title: Goodlander, Veteran Members of Congress Pass War Powers Resolution to End Unauthorized War in Iran
text:
Washington, D.C. — Today, the House of Representatives voted for the third time to demand an end to the Trump administration’s unauthorized war with Iran. H. Con. Res. 93, introduced by Congresswoman Maggie Goodlander (NH-02) and eight other veteran members of Congress, would direct the President to remove U.S. Armed Forces from hostilities against Iran unless Congress has declared war or specifically authorized the use of military force.

“The President launched his war in Iran 199 days ago — a war that has cost us the lives of 18 servicemembers and jacked up costs for families all over the country,” said Congresswoman Goodlander. “Enough is enough. This war has to end. I will never stop working to protect our servicemembers and defend the Constitution we all swore to uphold.”

ADDITIONAL BACKGROUND:

Congresswoman Goodlander has helped lead the fight to reassert Congress’s constitutional war powers authority, leading to two previous bipartisan Iran War Powers Resolutions passing the House. In June, Goodlander helped lead H. Con. Res. 86 to passage by a 215-208 vote. The Senate subsequently passed the resolution, marking the first time in the history of the War Powers Resolution that both chambers of Congress directed a President to remove U.S. forces from a conflict through a concurrent resolution. In July, Goodlander cosponsored H. Con. Res. 89, which passed 214-208.

Demanded accountability for the war’s costs and consequences. Goodlander pressed Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth for an accounting of the war’s cost, demanded a public House Armed Services Committee hearing, and joined fellow Democratic veterans in seeking an investigation into force-protection failures after six U.S. servicemembers were killed in Kuwait.

Fought to cut off funding for an unauthorized war. Goodlander joined fellow veterans and national security leaders to introduce the No Funds for Iran War Act, which would prohibit taxpayer funds from supporting military action against Iran without a declaration of war or specific congressional authorization.

title: RELEASE: House Passes Bill First Championed by Gottheimer, AM Radio for Every Vehicle Act
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, September 15, 2026, the House of Representatives passed the “AM Radio for Every Vehicle Act,” supported by Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5), delivering a major win for public safety and moving the country one step closer to guaranteeing that every new car and truck sold in America comes equipped with AM broadcast radio.

Gottheimer, who first announced and introduced the legislation in the 118th Congress to protect public safety and encourage electric vehicle (EV) manufacturers to include AM radio in their cars and trucks, applauded the bill’s passage.

“AM radio is a lifeline. When the power goes out, when the cell towers go down, and when the Internet cuts off during a storm or an emergency, AM radio is often the only way families can get the life-saving information they need,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5). “It’s outrageous that some automakers want to rip out a basic, free feature — one that helps keep people safe — just to pad their own bottom line. I’m proud to have helped lead this bipartisan bill from day one, and today the House stood up for every driver, every first responder, and every family who counts on AM radio when it matters most.”

“For more than 100 years, AM radio stations have provided music, sports, news, and entertainment to listeners across the Garden State and the country. More importantly over the last century, radio has provided a critical lifeline in times of emergency. Ensuring that this free service utilizing the public’s airwaves is readily available in every vehicle sold in the United States by passing the AM Radio For Every Vehicle Act is the right decision for public safety,” said New Jersey Broadcasters Association (NJBA) Executive Director Jordan Walton. “It’s hard to imagine that what started as a conversation over a cup of coffee has evolved into this legislation being passed with overwhelming bipartisan support. New Jersey’s broadcasters thank Rep. Gottheimer, leaders in the House, and all who advanced AM4EVA today.”

More than 50 million Americans listen to AM broadcast radio every month, and it remains one of the most reliable ways to reach the public during emergencies. AM radio is the backbone behind America’s National Public Warning System, which provides emergency-alert and warning information to the public during major natural disasters, extreme weather conditions, chemical incidents, health emergencies, and other domestic threats, often when cellular and Internet networks fail. In the aftermath of 9/11 and Hurricane Sandy, AM broadcast radio provided a crucial lifeline for life-saving information, and for many rural communities it remains a primary source of local news, weather, and emergency alerts.

Despite the clear public safety uses of AM broadcast radio, many manufacturers had stopped including AM broadcast radio in their vehicles because they did not want to spend the minimal funds to ensure public safety during emergencies.

The AM Radio for Every Vehicle Act will require the Department of Transportation to issue a rule mandating that all automakers include AM radio as standard equipment in their vehicles, at no additional cost to consumers.

Since first taking on this back in 2023, Gottheimer pushed manufacturers directly, called on the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration to add AM broadcast radio to the Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards, and helped secure a critical federal investment of $56 million for the Next Generation Warning System to improve the capabilities of public broadcasters to send vital emergency and civil defense warnings.

###

title: RELEASE: House Passes Bipartisan, Gottheimer-Led GUARD Act to Protect Seniors from Financial Fraud and Scammers
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Tuesday, September 15, 2026, the U.S. House of Representatives passed the bipartisan GUARD Act (Guarding Unprotected Aging Retirees from Deception Act, H.R. 2978) legislation that U.S. Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) co-led to protect seniors and their families from the financial fraud and scams costing Americans billions every year.

The GUARD Act was introduced alongside Representatives Zachary Nunn (IA-3) and Scott Fitzgerald (WI-5), and now heads to the Senate.

“Every day, scammers are targeting our seniors — draining the hard-earned savings they spent a lifetime building, often with a single phone call or a fake investment scheme,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5), Co-Chair of the bipartisan Law Enforcement Caucus and member of the House Financial Services Committee. “These criminals don’t play it straight, and too often they hide behind overseas networks that make them nearly impossible to track. The GUARD Act gives our cops and investigators the tools and the resources to hunt these fraudsters down, claw back stolen money, and protect the people who built this country. Protecting our parents and grandparents is just common sense, and I’m proud this bipartisan bill is one step closer to becoming law.”

The GUARD Act empowers state, local, and Tribal law enforcement to fight back against the fraud epidemic targeting older Americans. Specifically, the legislation:

Allows law enforcement to use existing federal grant funds to investigate elder financial fraud, “pig butchering” cryptocurrency investment scams, and general financial fraud — including by hiring analysts and experts and providing specialized training on complex, often transnational financial crimes;

Clarifies that federal law enforcement agencies may assist state, local, and Tribal partners and fusion centers in using blockchain-tracing tools and related technology to follow the money and identify the criminals behind these scams;

Instructs the Treasury Department, FinCEN, and federal partners to report to Congress on the true scale of scams in the United States — including how much Americans are losing each year, how many of these schemes trace back to overseas actors and organized crime, and how effective enforcement efforts have been.

“Iowa retirees spent a lifetime building their savings, and scammers are using increasingly sophisticated technology to steal it out from under them,” said Rep. Nunn (IA-3). “The GUARD Act came directly from an Iowa sheriff’s deputy who told me officers were watching criminals steal the life savings of hardworking Iowans but lacked the tools to track them down and recover the money. Today, the House voted to give state and local law enforcement the resources they need to pursue fraudsters, recover stolen funds, and deliver justice for victims. I urge the Senate to take it up without delay and get these protections to the Iowans who need them.”

“Elder fraud and financial scams are robbing older Americans of their life savings at an alarming rate, and the 4,200 credit unions across the country see that firsthand,” said Kathleen Coulombe, Chief Advocacy Officer, America’s Credit Unions. “America’s Credit Unions strongly supports the GUARD Act and measures like it, which take concrete steps to defend seniors and preserve the savings they spent a lifetime earning. By directing real investigative resources to local law enforcement and providing advanced tools to trace stolen funds, the GUARD Act strengthens our front lines against scammers. We thank Representative Nunn for championing this bill and urge Congress to quickly pass this legislation.”

“The GUARD Act will help provide state and local law enforcement with necessary resources to combat fraud and the organized crime rings that are hurting retirees and communities,” said Rodney Davis, Head of Government Affairs, U.S. Chamber of Commerce. “The U.S. Chamber is proud to support this legislation and thanks Rep. Nunn for his leadership in this critical battle against scammers.”

“The Crypto Council for Innovation supports the bipartisan GUARD Act. Strong consumer protection requires that law enforcement have the tools, training, and resources necessary to identify and pursue illicit activity in digital asset markets,” aid Ji Hun Kim, Chief Executive Officer, Crypto Council for Innovation. “We commend Representatives Nunn, Gottheimer, and Fitzgerald for their leadership and for their bipartisan work on this important legislation.”

“Representative Nunn is a close partner on a number of fraud issues, especially the GUARD Act that directs federal grant money toward local law enforcement for the tools and training they need to fight fraud,” said Iowa AARP. “He’s been a champion in his district and across Washington, D.C., and we’re proud to see the GUARD Act move through the House.”

“Protecting consumers from sophisticated financial crime requires a united front across government, law enforcement, and the private sector,” said Chris Sparks, Head of Card Fraud, Capital One. “By passing the GUARD Act today, the U.S. House of Representatives has taken a decisive step toward filling critical gaps to help stop criminal scammers before they strike. Capital One applauds Representatives Nunn, Fitzgerald, and Gottheimer for this bipartisan achievement in advancing legislation that will safeguard older Americans and reinforce trust in our financial system.”

A “pig butchering” scam is a type of financial fraud where scammers target individuals, commonly retirees, to convince them to invest money in a fake opportunity. The term “pig butchering” refers to the process of “fattening up” a victim with false promises before “butchering” them by stealing their invested funds.

The FBI’s 2025 IC3 report states that total internet crime losses reached $20.9 billion in 2025, a 26% increase over 2024 and the first time the figure surpassed $20 billion. Cryptocurrency-related losses hit a record $11.37 billion across 181,565 complaints, up 22% from 2024. Investment fraud, the category that captures most pig butchering activity, was the single largest loss type at more than $8.6 billion.

The bipartisan GUARD Act is supported by the AARP, the Iowa State Police Association, the Financial Technology Association, Consumer Bankers Association, America’s Credit Union Association, Digital Chamber, National Police Association, Crypto Council for Innovation, and the Iowa Bankers Association.

Gottheimer has been a leading voice for protecting seniors and cracking down on financial fraud and emerging-technology threats.

title: Rep. Grijalva Pleas for Safety of Ahmed Soliman; Arizonan in Danger After Deportation to Equatorial Guinea
text:
Washington, D.C. — Congresswoman Adelita S. Grijalva issued a video statement pleading for the safety of Ahmed Soliman, a 30-year-old Arizonan who has lived in the United States since he was four years old but was deported to Equatorial Guinea, a country he has zero ties to.

A judge determined he could face torture or death if returned to his birth country of Egypt because he is gay, so the Trump administration deported him instead to Equatorial Guinea. According to the Arizona Daily Star, on Friday Ahmed was arrested by local authorities in Equatorial Guinea after he spoke out about the inhumane conditions he and other detainees faced in their confinement – including being threatened at gunpoint – at a decommissioned hotel surrounded by armed guards. His phone was confiscated, cutting off his ability to communicate with the outside world. His current condition is unknown.

title: Ratepayer Protection Act Passes House with Strong Bipartisan Support
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congressman Brett Guthrie (KY-02), Chairman of the House Committee on Energy and Commerce, Congressman Bob Latta (OH-05), Chairman of the Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Energy, and Congressman Gabe Evans (CO-08), applauded House passage of H.R. 9340, the Ratepayer Protection Act, by a vote of 417 to 3. The legislation would require state public utility commissions to consider a strategy to make data centers pay their own way, instead of passing costs onto American consumers.

"When done responsibly, data center development leads to longer term investments and broader infrastructure improvements in the communities where they’re built. The Ratepayer Protection Act helps to safeguard these benefits by ensuring that the companies who are building data centers—and not American families and small businesses—are paying for the electricity they use,” said Chairman Guthrie. “U.S. leadership in the race to AI dominance is critical to our economic prosperity and national security, so we need to keep building the needed infrastructure with appropriate accountability measures. I'm grateful to Congressman Evans for his tireless work—on a bipartisan basis—to protect ratepayers while ensuring that America continues to lead the world in innovation."

"I am proud to vote for the bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act, led by Representative Gabe Evans, which will protect ratepayers from increased electricity costs caused by data centers. Across the country, communities are seeing proposals for new data centers that will bring jobs, investment and new technological capabilities, but also raise important questions about how these facilities will affect local electric grids and the nearby communities,” said Chairman Latta. “One question should have a clear answer: American families should not have to pay higher electricity bills so large technology companies can build and operate data centers. I urge the Senate to swiftly consider this legislation and send it to the President’s desk."

"Hardworking families should not have to subsidize the energy demands of data centers. America needs the infrastructure to lead the world in AI and outcompete Communist China, but we cannot have that growth at the expense of hardworking families, farmers, seniors, and small businesses,” said Congressman Evans. “My bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act ensures large data centers pay for the infrastructure they require while giving states the flexibility to determine what works best for their communities. I’m incredibly proud to lead the charge on this pivotal issue, ensure our ratepayers are protected, and keep American innovation moving forward."

BACKGROUND:

title: Guthrie Committee-Led Bills Pass House to Combat Manufacturing of Illicit Drugs and Protect Americans from Dangerous Substances
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Brett Guthrie (KY-02), Chairman of the House Committee on Energy and Commerce, issued the following statement following the House passage of three Committee-led bills to combat the manufacturing of illicit drugs and to protect Americans from dangerous substances, like fentanyl.

“I am glad to see the House take action to pass three House Energy and Commerce bills to build upon our work of combating illicit drugs that have devastated communities across our nation, especially here in Kentucky,” said Congressman Guthrie. “These bipartisan bills will provide law enforcement additional tools to combat the production of fentanyl and other illicit drugs, protect Americans from dangerous substances, increase access to fentanyl testing, and most importantly save lives.”

Background:

H.R. 1266, Combating Illicit Xylazine Act – This legislation passed the House of Representatives unanimously. If enacted, this bill would place xylazine in Schedule III of the Controlled Substances Act and amend the definition of “ultimate user” to allow xylazine to continue to be lawfully administered for legitimate veterinary purposes. This bill requires a report to Congress on the prevalence and proliferation of xylazine trafficking and misuse in the United States.

H.R. 8005, Stop Pills That Kill Act – This legislation passed the House of Representatives unanimously. If enacted, this bill would seek to prevent the misuse of pill press machines and their critical parts for the illicit manufacture of a controlled substance by strengthening the DEA’s ability to conduct regulatory oversight of pill press machines and their critical parts.

H.R. 2004, Tyler’s Law – This legislation passed the House of Representatives unanimously. If enacted, this bill would direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to complete a study and issue guidance on whether hospital emergency departments should implement fentanyl testing as a routine procedure for patients experiencing an overdose.

title: Congresswoman Gwen Moore Statement on the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026
text:
“I continue to support Ukraine as they fight to protect their country and sovereignty against a brutal Russian invasion. We can and must put economic pressure on the bad actors driving this invasion, including Putin’s cronies and those supporting the Russian oil industry.

This Administration has squandered many opportunities to use existing sanction authorities to press Russia. In fact, after starting a war with Iran, the Trump administration relaxed existing sanctions on Russia, further fueling the Russian war machine. I will oppose this legislation because it does not ensure the Trump administration will take action against Putin’s unchecked war in Ukraine. It also includes an extension of existing Iran sanctions that would easily pass with bipartisan support if brought to the Floor as a stand-alone bill.

Instead of expanding Trump’s tariff powers, the Republican-led Congress should be reining him in. Amid a cost-of-living crisis, Trump’s tariffs have already spiked costs for working families and created chaos for small businesses. Not to mention, the Supreme Court ruled that some of Trump’s tariffs were illegal.

There is a better way to support our ally Ukraine that doesn’t involve emboldening a rogue President, like with the Ukraine Support Act.”

title: Congressman Rogers Votes to Protect Ratepayers, Implement Guardrails for Data Centers
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – U.S. Rep. Harold “Hal” Rogers (KY-05) voted for the Ratepayer Protection Act (H.R. 9340) to ensure that data centers pay their own way for the electricity necessary to power them, not hardworking Americans in rural communities.

“With multiple data center proposals in Southern and Eastern Kentucky, we need proper guardrails in place to make sure no costs are added to the skyrocketing utility bills for families and businesses in our rural region,” said Congressman Rogers. “As AI technology growth continues to boom, we need a strategy in place that locks in benefits for Rural America, while also protecting families and businesses from footing the bill.”

The Ratepayer Protection Act amends the Public Utilities Regulatory Policies Act of 1978 to establish a federal standard relating to the recovery of the full, incremental costs of electric system upgrades necessary to serve large-load customers.

Earlier this year, President Donald Trump introduced the Ratepayer Protection Pledge, committing utilities, data center developers, cooperatives and states not to pass the costs of data centers on to American families and businesses. Several Kentucky utility companies signed the pledge, which now has more than 300 signatures nationwide, covering 80 percent of all power delivered in America.

The bill now advances to the Senate for consideration.

For more information about Congressman Rogers’ work in Washington and at home in Kentucky, visit halrogers.house.gov and follow him on social media.

title: Congressman Rogers Advances Flood Control for Eastern Kentucky in Federal Water Resources Development Act (WRDA)
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – U.S. Rep. Harold “Hal” Rogers (KY-05) advanced flood control projects in Eastern Kentucky through the Water Resources Development Act (WRDA) of 2026 (H.R. 9497), which passed the House on Wednesday.

The nation’s major water resources legislation, WRDA, reauthorizes and modifies water infrastructure projects every year. Congressman Rogers requested flood control and risk management projects for the Kentucky River, Buckhorn Lake and Elkhorn Lake Dam in the 2026 bill, advancing critical studies to help protect families and businesses from devastating floods in Kentucky’s Appalachian region.

“Repeated flooding in the mountains has been a deadly and costly battle for our region for decades. We have largely protected communities from massive floods along the Cumberland River, the Big Sandy River and the Levisa Fork with flood walls, levies, tunnels and bridges. Now, with more flooding in the Kentucky River region, we must concentrate on protecting our people and our communities for future generations,” said Congressman Rogers. “I was proud to secure requests for three more flood control projects in this bill, which will also study risk management for the Confluence community of Leslie County where residents are frequently trapped when excessive water is released from Buckhorn Lake.”

The legislation authorizes the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers to move forward with flood control efforts along the Kentucky River in Beattyville, Kentucky. It will also study the safety of the Elkhorn Lake Dam in Letcher County, water supply storage and flood damage reduction efforts. A study of Buckhorn Lake was also included in the bill to examine sediment management, debris removal and the impact it has in Perry and Leslie Counties.

The bill now advances to the Senate for consideration.

For more information about Congressman Rogers’ work in Washington and at home in Kentucky, visit halrogers.house.gov and follow him on social media.

title: House Passes Legislation Targeting Fraud in Federally Funded Programs
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Legislation cosponsored by Congressman Abraham Hamadeh (AZ-08), the National Fraud Enforcement Division Act of 2026, was passed in the U.S. House of Representatives on Wednesday.

The legislation makes permanent the newly established National Fraud Enforcement Division within the Department of Justice (DOJ). The legislation would establish an Assistant Attorney General, appointed by the President and confirmed by the Senate, to lead DOJ efforts to investigate, prosecute, and prevent fraud within federally funded programs.

“I want to thank my colleagues for passing this critical legislation,” stated Congressman Hamadeh. “The criminals, who have created the need for this enforcement effort, have not only stolen taxpayer dollars, but have victimized the most vulnerable in our society by depleting the resources allocated for their needs.”

“Just this week, a criminal, who is a resident in my district, was charged with fraudulently billing Arizona’s federally funded Medicaid agency, AHCCS, of more than $33 million in one year alone,” stated Congressman Hamadeh. “He specifically targeted AHCCCS enrollees who were covered under the American Indian Health Care Program. He exploited vulnerable people to buy expensive property and luxury items. These federal funds are finite, so not only did he target a vulnerable population, but his thievery also serves to weaken the crucial safety net Americans need for education, medical care, retirement, and more.”

Congressman Hamadeh is one of 4 cosponsors on this crucial legislation alongside Reps. Schmidt (R-KS), Hageman (R-WY), and Fischbach (R-MN).

Background:

Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche announced this year the establishment of the National Fraud Enforcement Division within the Department of Justice, tasked with investigating and prosecuting those who steal or fraudulently misuse taxpayer dollars.

The National Fraud Enforcement Division Act of 2026 would establish a permanent National Fraud Enforcement Division within the Department of Justice.

This division will:

o Streamline federal fraud investigations

o Lead efforts to investigate, prosecute, and remedy fraud

o Oversee fraud investigations across multiple agencies

o Work with other DOJ components to identify common fraud schemes

o Propose future legislative/regulatory reforms to fix vulnerabilities in the system

o Advise the Attorney General on fraud investigations

title: GOLDEN MUSSELS: Harder’s Control and Eradication Bill Advancing in Congress
text:
U.S. Fish and Wildlife signals support for Harder’s bill during legislative hearing earlier today

VIDEO from the hearing is available here

WASHINGTON – Today, Rep. Josh Harder (CA-09) announced that his bill to stop the golden mussel invasion is advancing in Congress. Earlier today, the U.S. House Natural Resources Subcommittee on Water, Wildlife, and Fisheries held a bipartisan hearing on Harder’s Golden Mussel Eradication and Control Act and highlighted the need for halting the mussels’ spread and kickstarting eradication efforts.

“The Service works closely with partners to combat golden mussels – last summer, we conveyed a work group to evaluate immediate and long-term needs,” said Dave Miko, Acting Deputy Director for Operations at the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, during the hearing. “The work group is developing a national control and management plan to guide and coordinate efforts. In January 2025, the Service published a proposed rule that would add golden mussels to the list of injurious wildlife. The service recognizes the importance of addressing invasive species and supports the goals of H.R. 3717.”

Golden mussels are using the Delta as the staging ground for a continental invasion:

The first U.S. sighting of golden mussels occurred near the Port of Stockton in 2024 and the infestation now ranges as far south as San Diego County.

A single female mussel can produce up to one million offspring a year, and in some river systems, they have spread up to 150 miles per year on average.

If left unchecked, the infestation could threaten the water supplies relied upon by 27 million Californians and $50 billion in agriculture.

“Our community is on the front lines of efforts to prevent a continental infestation, but we deserve more than just becoming the nation’s quarantine zone,” said Rep. Harder. “That’s why I introduced legislation to supercharge control efforts and invest in eradication technologies, and I’m grateful to see these solutions gaining support in Congress. Washington should quickly pass this bill into law to halt the golden mussel invasion and kick them out of our waterways once and for all.”

How the Golden Mussel Eradication and Control Act works:

Deploys a rapid response program to monitor, contain, and begin eradicating the current infestation.

Invests in new technology and inspection stations to speed up local eradication efforts.

Increases state, local, and federal coordination through a comprehensive report on best practices and new guidance on golden mussel prevention.

“The golden mussel is the most significant invasive species threat California’s water infrastructure has faced in a generation, and it will not stay isolated to California either,” said Rachel Murphy, General Manager for the Contra Costa Water District (CCWD). “The Golden Mussel Eradication and Control Act gives the country the tools to respond: a lead agency, a focused program, applied research, technical assistance, and a way to share what works. CCWD strongly supports the bill, and thanks Congressman Harder for his leadership in bringing it forward.”
